meta.title: Canon — one canonical home per fact
inputs: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (11 477 lines, read where a conflict needed the text)
meta.id_rule: A fact's id is the inventory id of its home statement (stable); every inventory id maps to exactly one fact or section restatement in by_inventory_id. Conflict ids keep the inventories' ids (MODEL-Cnn, KERNEL-Cnn, CF-PIPE-nn, DETERMINISM-C-n = the inventory's C-n, RENDERING-Cnn, SCOPE-Cnn); conflicts the canon found are CANON-Cnn.

home_rules.rule: §2 owns record types, schemas and the plat's data rules (levels, roles, references, knot profiles, the wing and composition carry, identity parts, the document and snapshot text of §2.9). A type the document declares once in its mechanism section stays there: KernelResult/KernelTx/KernelError (§3), the display-list tables (§8.1), LayerSpec (§8.4), LabelEntity/QuarterNode (§9.1), edit events (§7.1), API types (§11.2), StageDecl (§4.12), Seam/SeamContract (II.1).
§3 owns geometry, numeric policy (the lattice values live in §3.2 (2); §2.2 LatticeSpec names the fields), transactions, indexes, kernel operations and kernel invariants.

§4 owns stage behaviour, stage algorithms and stage parameters, including the mechanism a §12.4 budget assumes; §10 content; PART II stage-2 interfaces; PART III village hooks and the village ladder rows.

§5.2 owns each failure class row — detection, rung order and its test column; a stage section states how a rung is computed. §5.3 owns each invariant's check row (scope, timing); the rule it checks lives at its domain section (kernel invariants in §3.10). §5.4 the report. Exception kept from the document: the F-LABEL rungs live in §9.4 (its heading names the ladder).

§6 owns streams, keys, salts, the concern registry, digests (model and records trees), identity, versions, permalinks, retention and the determinism tests of §6.5 (its heading names them; §13.2 schedules them).

§7 owns edit events, named actions, locks and pins, locality and effective scope (the seam exception included), operators, the lifecycle table, migration, overrides, intent and controls, and the locality oracle of §7.3 item 7.
§8 rendering and styles, §9 labels and furniture (the title is furniture, §9.5), §11 formats, API and host bridge (logHead and bridged load verification are §11.3's).

§12 owns every performance budget it states and its measured law; a budget stated only at its subject section with its own measurement and fallback stays there and §12 points to it where it already does (§6.3 matching, §7.4 undo, §7.8 proxies, §2.9 document size and open-to-editable, §6.4 retention size). §12.4 keeps work counts, times and p50; the mechanism is §4's.

§13 owns every test, fixture and acceptance bar it states and every test a surveyor assigned to it; a test stated both in §13 and elsewhere lives in §13, except where the other section's heading names it (§5.2 test column, §5.3 CI-only rows, §6.5 determinism tests, §7.3 item 7 oracle, §8.3 census, §13.7's thresholds are §13's). Kernel tests stated only in §3 move to §13.1.

§15 maps each row to its home and states no number of its own except a bar that exists nowhere else; §16 places work in milestones and points to the criteria's homes; §17 owns licences and the clean-room chain; D-rows stay in the main document (one short paragraph each, pointing to the home); J-rows move verbatim to docs/ARCHITECTURE-RATIONALE.md with a one-line index row left in the main document.

The one-page summary and each part's plain-words intro may paraphrase but carry only canonical figures; history and round narration leave the normative text (the validation record keeps them); an executed-evidence citation stays as a one-line receipt pointer beside the fact it supports.

An interface lives in the section whose subject it is; a second code copy (§14's copies of TileRasterOpts, LabelPlacer, RasterJob, StageDecl fields) becomes a pointer. §14 keeps the package map, dependency rules, extension points and the interfaces it alone declares (Rng.stream, StreamOpts, Kernel façade, EditEngine, Exporter, ContentProvider, ObstacleSource, RoleIndex).

When a restatement carries a detail its home lacks (a qualifier, a number, a case), the home's editor adds it to the home statement: this is the union of existing statements, not a new fact. canon.json lists the numeric ones per fact under detail_gaps (a heuristic: numbers only; a verifier checks meaning).

facts.statement: Plain-words intro: town stored as one precise plat (every area a face, every line an edge) in integer centimetres; refined in five levels coarse-to-fine; everything else a record with stable id pointing into the plat; every record remembers how it was made (rule, random stream) and its lifecycle (generated, edited, pinned, built, converted, demolished); three layers (underground, ground, sky) exist from the start
Every model length is an integer number of centimetres (i32); world centred on (0,0), +x east, +y north (FTG convention, evidence _critic-ftg.md F1)
facts.values: unit cm, i32; origin (0,0); +x east, +y north

facts.statement: Frames are rectangles (COV-VG-VN-156): a rung declares a frame area A (TOWN 4 km², CITY 25 km², METROPOLIS 64 km² — formerly 2 / 5 / 8 km squares); the blueprint's aspect ∈ [0.5, 2] (default 1) gives width = √(A · aspect), height = √(A / aspect), centred on (0, 0) with +y north; the arena spans the frame plus marginShare on every side; every raster's cols × rows follows width × height.

Ring orientation is orient2d at the ring's lowest-leftmost vertex; no orientation, sliver or degeneracy decision reads the sign of a float sum; area statistics in m² are derived from the exact integer.
Heights are centimetres; stored angles are i32 centidegrees; directions used in geometry are integer vectors
Schema lint refuses any length field without a unit suffix (…Cm, …M)

layer ∈ {underground, ground, sky} is a field on every geometric entity and every display-list item, with z: i32 (order inside layer) and elevationCm: i32 (base elevation: island altitude, sewer negative depth)

Each layer has its own arena (G-R11): ground, underground, one per sky island, keyed by PlatKey; sky/underground geometry never cuts ground faces; cross-layer references (island shadow footprint, sewer outfall) are ids
facts.values: one arena per layer / per sky island

facts.statement: The base populates only the ground layer; underground and sky are schema-complete and empty

LayerSpec { id: Layer; zOrder; elevationCm; visible; castsShadowOnto?: Layer; exportSeparately; occlusion 'opaque'|'ghost'|'offset'; ghostAlpha (default 0.35); offsetPerMetre? (default [0, 0.25] px per m, up the screen, with a tether line to the ground footprint) } (VIS-17).

"layer" unqualified means one of the three model layers; toggleable drawing groups of §8–§9 (labels, cadastral outlines, trees, annotations, thematic overrides) are display-list groups selected by semantic, never a fourth model layer

Every entity has an address id kind:token, prefixed with its arena outside the ground layer (sky2/plot:…, under/tunnel:…), that edits, locks, assignments, pins, labels, households, exports and hosts point at

Two identities per entity (LC-1): an address that everything points at (edits, locks, assignments, pins, labels, households, exports, the host) and a lineage that keys its random streams; they start equal and separate only when an entity is re-derived

In memory, addresses are interned u32 handles (kernel owner and role tables hold them); in the document they are strings; the parent is a field, never parsed from the id; no record outside the kernel stores an arena slot
Cm = integer centimetres; a number becomes an arena coordinate only through snap(), in every build
Level = 0|1|2|3|4: L0 land/water; L1 way skeleton; L2 kerbs, corridors, blocks; L3 plots + residue; L4 footprints + yard parts
PlatKey = {layer, part}: part 0 = the ground or underground arena; parts 1–3 = one arena per sky island
VertexId, HalfEdgeId, FaceId are arena slots: kernel-internal, valid within one batch

Plat record: key, frame (§3.2 (9)), lattice; vertices {x,y,out,level,flags}; halfEdges {origin,next,prev,level per pair}; roles: RoleTable; faces[5]: LevelFaces; index[5]: LevelIndex; indexHome {vertex, edge per pair, face per level}; version bumped by every committed batch
facts.values: 5 per-level face and index arrays; version++ per batch

facts.statement: Vertex flags: pinned (set by pinVertices; cleared when last vertex role row leaves), steiner, split (see split-flag rule), free slot
Vertex birth level is lowered by promotion, raised by demotion
twin(h) = h ^ 1: half-edges allocated in pairs; edge birth level stored per pair (h>>1) and is always the lowest level among its role rows
indexHome: per slot, the static index partition (numbered across the levels) whose build holds the item, −1 if none; written by every build, read to tombstone the item (VK4-5)
LatticeSpec: unitCm 1; minEdgeCm 25; attractCm 26; minFaceAngleCdeg 500 (soft, §3.10); rangeCm 8 388 608 (2^23)
facts.values: unit 1 cm; minEdge 25 cm; attract 26 cm; min face angle 5.00° soft; range 2^23 cm

members.note: field names stay in §2.2 LatticeSpec; the values (unitCm 1, minEdgeCm 25, attractCm 26, minFaceAngleCdeg 500, rangeCm 2^23) are stated once at §3.2 (2) and referenced

notes: MODEL-025: field names stay in §2.2 LatticeSpec; the values (unitCm 1, minEdgeCm 25, attractCm 26, minFaceAngleCdeg 500, rangeCm 2^23) are stated once at §3.2 (2) and referenced

facts.statement: LevelFaces: outer, holesStart, holes, kind (Uint16), owner (interned entity handle), parent (level−1 face containing it; −1 at L0), stage (rank in §4.1 order of the stage whose batch created or last re-owned the face: the kept-content rule §3.3), nextOfOwner, ownerHead: OwnerTable

RoleTable: edgeFirst, vertexFirst (first slot of each set, −1 if none), kind (interned RoleName), entity, level (level of adding batch), ordinal (0 unless registry declares role indexed), nextInSet, nextSameKey, head: RoleHeadTable
Indexed roles (ordinal ≠ 0 allowed) are exactly: knot, attach, anchor, weld, deck_end, gate_end, gate_opening

RoleHeadTable and OwnerTable are typed-array hash tables (VK2-9; J-K22): open addressing, linear probing, capacity power of two at load ≤ 0.5 (doubled and re-inserted in slot order when exceeded), fixed integer hash of key words, deletion by backward shift (no tombstones); lookups only, never iterated, so layout never reaches an output

The generation worker freezes the arena at that version and sends each pool worker one read-only copy — vertex, half-edge, role and face arrays, role-head and owner-head tables (typed arrays, §2.2), the index's home column and every non-empty level's static partitions (L0–L3 at the one-click freeze, L4 still empty; L0–L4 at a freeze after edits) — as transferred ArrayBuffers, so pooled plot lines, S12b's greenery and pooled re-derivations find wall-band, setback, margin-band edges and locked or pinned content by the same indexed queries.
RoleHeadTable {k0 entity handle, k1 = role<<16 | ordinal, first (−1 empty), count}; OwnerTable {owner, head (first FaceId, −1 empty), count}

LevelIndex: static PackedIndex[] partitions (one per arena at L0–L1; one per district + one outside districts at L2–L4); dynamic UniformGrid; tombstones: one Set per static partition of item keys (kind·2^32 + slot; kind = vertex, route edge or face) deleted, moved level or changed since that partition's build; filter that partition's hits only; rebuild empties set; all sets and grids empty at every pool freeze, which first rebuilds dirty partitions
RoleRow = {role, entity, ordinal?}: row a writer adds; its level is always the adding batch's; an anchor contact name is given without an ordinal, which the kernel allocates
RoleKey = {role, entity, ordinal}: a row's identity without its level
FaceRef, ChainRef, EdgeSetRef, VertexRef (and batch-local StretchRef) are the only forms in which an entity, seam contract, edit event or API scope refers to geometry
FaceRef = {owner, level}: view of faces whose owner at that level is the entity
ChainRef = {role, entity}: the ordered edge chain carrying (role, entity) — way spine, wall trace, tunnel
EdgeSetRef = {role, entity, ordinal?}: unordered edges carrying the role — plot frontage, access, party walls, one gate opening
VertexRef = {role, entity, ordinal?}: the vertex carrying the role — junction, tower, gate, entrance, portal, deck end, water gate bank end, weld end
StretchRef = {chain, from, to} (VertexRef or LatticePoint ends): chain edges between two vertices; batch-local argument of removeEdges and retypeEdges, never stored in an entity record
LatticePoint = {x: Cm, y: Cm}: arena position, only in log events (with a VertexSig), view state, label placements and a StretchRef's ends — never in an entity record
VertexSig = {v: vertex's own (role,entity,ordinal) rows sorted; e: structural (role,entity) rows of incident edges sorted, deduplicated}

ChainProfile<T> = {knotRole, values[i] for the chain vertex carrying (knotRole, entity, i), interp linear|step}: a value varying along a chain, never an array indexed by chain vertices; knot roles include width_knot, base_knot, invert_knot, bank_knot, shore_class_knot
Everything with a boundary is a face; everything linear is an edge chain
L0 faces: land components, sea, lakes, river reaches, islets, ponds, moats — land and water only; terrain contours and drainage lines are raster products of §2.3, never plat edges or faces

restated_at: §2.3 Terrain is not in the plat

facts.statement: Arena outer ring (frame + context margin §3.2 (9)) is one L0 chain carrying structural role margin on the arena's Terrain entity, written first by S1 before any water; a sea or river reaching it shares its stretch (VK3-8)
facts.values: role margin; written by S1 first

facts.statement: L1 faces: coarse blocks between way spines and wall strips S7 cuts beside each trace; L1 edges: way spines (centrelines), wall lines, wall-strip setback and glacis lines (role setback), shorelines inherited from L0, map border (frame rectangle, role border on Terrain, written first by S3's L1 batch after S3's L0 batch), settlement perimeter (district_bound chain), district boundaries
District boundaries are always L1 edges (a spine, a wall line, a reservation boundary, a shore or the perimeter; VP2-9), so every finer face lies inside one district
places: §2.9 chunks (district boundaries always L1) (restated, per MODEL-048)

facts.statement: L2 refines each L1 face into one half-corridor strip along each spine edge (road reserve on that side, width = way half-width), one junction wedge at each corner, and the remaining built block(s), built by corridorUnion (§3.7); every L2 face nests in exactly one L1 face
Corridor entity = FaceRef of the half-corridor faces on both sides of its spine; Junction = FaceRef of wedges around its vertex; Square = a corridor face of class square (K-1 repair; G-R11)

Wall bands, glacis, tower and gatehouse footprints use bandUnion with the band role: the wall chain (already L1) splits the band, so a band is a FaceRef of per-side L3 parts and never straddles its L1 edge.

members.note: §2.2 rule 1 keeps only which level holds wall bands

notes: MODEL-051: §2.2 rule 1 keeps only which level holds wall bands

facts.statement: L3 faces: plots, courts, yards, greens, alleys-as-faces, wall-band/setback/glacis parts, margin-band parts along the perimeter and other shared non-spine district boundaries (§3.3 pool step 3), hinterland furlongs, lots, woods, driveways, trails (boundaries L3 edges carrying field_bound; hedgerow = green_line role on such an edge; a track along one = same edge with both roles, §4.9)
L4 faces: building footprints (and wing sub-faces when stage 3 exists) plus yard sub-areas
Districts, blocks, merged plots and water bodies are multi-face FaceRefs, never single face ids (P-1 avoided)

J-K1: one arena per PlatKey; the five levels are views of it: all levels in one vertex-and-half-edge arena, every edge carries its birth level; level-n subdivision = edges of level ≤ n; each level-n face is exactly the union of level-(n+1) faces inside it

Invariant: nesting — every face of level n + 1 has exactly one parent at level n and each of its boundary edges is of level n + 1 or a sub-edge of a level-≤ n edge — hard, batch-local, touched faces and re-parented kept faces, by index, never by coordinates.
Face walk at level n follows next and, around each vertex, skips edges of level > n (O(degree))
A level's face records inside a parent face are materialised when the first edge of that level is inserted there; until then the parent face is its own child
A shared boundary is one edge seen by every finer level (kerb, plot line, party wall); a warp moves it once; two row houses share one wall edge
Ground, underground and each sky island are separate arenas and never share topology; cross-arena links are entity ids

Finer levels never move coarser geometry: a level-n batch creates vertices and edges of level n only (else E_LEVEL); stated exceptions: clearing finer content, promotion, demotion and warp moves (§3.3, §3.6)

Where a level-n batch needs a vertex on a coarser edge, splitThrough inserts a level-n Steiner vertex at the lattice point chosen by §3.6's placement rule near the exact foot and routes the coarser edge through it; the route moves by at most half a lattice diagonal
places: §2.2 rule 3 hot pixel sentence (restated, per MODEL-062)

facts.statement: 61 % of 5–60 m edges have no interior lattice point at all (GEO-1)
The coarser edge's endpoints, birth level, faces and own-level roles never change under a finer split; a finer batch may add roles of its own level (a plot's frontage on a kerb)

Level-n route of an edge = chain through its vertices of level ≤ n; every level-n query, level-n digest (§6.2) and level-n stage reads that route, so no level-n result depends on whether/when a finer level was derived (lazy per-district stages included)
J-K32 / K4-1: a route can change under finer vertices without moving them — a same-level split, promotion, demotion or dissolution adds/removes a route vertex and moves nothing

Placement bound: every vertex placed, re-seated or slid onto a coarser edge lies within the hot pixel of that edge's route when placed; a later same-level change of the route moves no finer vertex and may leave one farther off (measured ≈ 1.25 cm after one change, ≈ 1.5 cm after several), which no invariant or stage reads and the index boxes cover (VK4-2).
facts.values: ≈ 1.25 cm after one change; ≈ 1.5 cm after several

facts.statement: Promotion: a coarser batch ending a chain on a route that already carries a finer vertex beside it (a neighbour plot-line end where II.1 (3)'s neighbour step lands its corridor_split edge; a close-up's kept fabric beside a new L1 junction) attracts onto that vertex and promotes it (birth level lowered to the batch's level), without moving it or touching finer faces; it keeps its split flag; commit record lists every promotion; undo record restores birth levels (§3.6, VK-18)

KernelTx.clearRegion is carried by a coarse batch inserted into finished fabric and its preparation batches; clearFiner then acts only on faces meeting it. KernelTx.prepared lists the vertices earlier batches of the same edit or stage placed for this batch's contacts with finer geometry (a kept way's deck_end rows, a re-traced wall run's gate_end rows, anchor contact names at other bank points) — the only finer vertices it may meet (§3.6 candidate (c)).
J-I12: a kept way's straight L1 edge between its two promoted bank vertices becomes the deck span over the new water (deck form settled at integration)

clearFiner (regeneration, undo) and removeEdges remove edges and roles then dissolve each degree-2 vertex that carries split, no vertex role, no pin, and whose two remaining edges carry identical role sets and one birth level
split flag (C-5, VK2-5, VK3-3): marks a vertex whose dissolution restores the edge it was created on exactly; set when created on an existing edge (split foot, crossing, every Steiner vertex)

split flag under moves (VK2-5, VK4-3, J-K26): the step clears the split flag of every vertex it moves, except a Steiner vertex re-seated onto its coarser edge's route and a vertex sliding along a fixed route; it also clears the flag of every flagged unmoved vertex of the same level as a run it split (a same-level split foot or crossing, or a vertex promoted onto that run) when the nearest vertex of that level or coarser beside it along that run moves in the step; a Steiner vertex of a coarser run keeps its flag. The commit record lists these in unflagged and the edit's undo record restores them.
places: §2.2 rule 3 (c) "flag is the whole guard" (restated, per MODEL-074)

facts.statement: J-K28 / VK3-3: levels follow the rows (demotion). A row is always added at the adding batch's level and never coarser than the edge/vertex it is added to; promotion is the one way a vertex becomes coarser; an edge's birth level is always the lowest among its role rows; only a removal can leave a level unjustified

Demotion step (a) edges: removeEdges, clearFiner and retypeEdges' remove finish by giving an edge whose remaining rows are all of levels above its birth level the lowest of them (quay on old shore stretch → L1; a wall on an old bank → L1), keeping L0 land-and-water only

Demotion step (b) flags: a split vertex keeps the flag only while a run it split survives whole (a pair of incident edges of its lowest incident level with identical rows of that level before the batch still exists at one level with identical rows; crossing has two such pairs, T-junction one); else cleared

Demotion step (b) pin: a vertex from which the batch strips its last vertex role row loses its kernel pinned flag (pin guards the feature its role names: gate, junction, portal, deck/gate/weld/anchor end; §3.4 pinVertices) — deck bank vertices F-REDERIVE removes become plain way vertices; a water gate bank vertex on an unchanged shore can dissolve (VK4-1)

Demotion step (c) vertices, in canonical order (lattice y then x), each reading levels earlier ones left: a vertex with no incident edge and no vertex role row of its level or coarser takes the lowest level among incident edges and vertex role rows (none → freed); deck bank vertex with L1 deck_end rows (placed by a preparation batch: carve, outer moat, water edit, §3.3 rule 2) takes way level at once; with L0 rows (placed by an L0 batch: S1 crossing sites, S3 carved channels, S4's or an edit's added deck on standing water, an edit's new site; a deck F-ROUTE's rung sites inside a water operator or carve have L1 rows; VD4-10) keeps L0 with no L0 edge until F-REDERIVE removes deck/deck_end rows (§7.3 (b) 9), then takes way level (VK4-1)

Split restoration (after dissolution): a split vertex whose incident edges of its level or coarser are exactly two, of one level, with identical rows of its level or coarser, carrying no vertex role row of its level or coarser and no pin, and still meeting finer edges or finer vertex role rows, takes the lowest level among those finer edges/rows and keeps its flag

The split flag is the whole guard (VK4-3): it stands only while neither the vertex nor the vertices beside it on its run have moved since it split the run; restoration gives the run's pre-promotion route changed only by same-level vertices added/removed since (K4-1)

A plot-line end or footprint corner that II.1 (3)'s neighbour step promoted to L2 returns to its level when the street is removed (undo, district reroll or any later edit); kerb's L2 route, index and digest equal those before the step

Route restored vertex for vertex on 100 000 of 100 000 random routes (fixall_kernel_r4_checks.out A), and 100 000 of 100 000 for each of one to four later same-level vertices (fixall_kernel_r5_checks.out A); round 4's distance test refused 0.54–0.66 % of restorations

No item changes in place (VK4-5): every item a batch deletes, re-levels or changes — a deleted vertex, edge or face; a promoted or demoted vertex or edge (a demoted edge leaves its old level's item for its new level's); a route edge whose run a vertex of its level joins or leaves (same-level split, promotion, dissolution, demotion) or a move reshapes; a vertex a move displaces; a face whose own-level ring a re-walk or move changes — is tombstoned in the static partition its home entry names (Plat.indexHome, §2.2), the entry then reading −1, and its successor, if any, is inserted in the grid of its current level; an item already in a grid is deleted or replaced there. A static item is therefore exact or filtered; no query sees an item at its old level, place or extent (a promoted-then-demoted plot-line end answers an L2 query not at all and an L3 query once, whatever the rebuild timing).

Invariant: level consistency — every edge's birth level is the lowest among its role rows; no vertex is coarser than every edge and vertex role at it; a vertex finer than an incident edge lies inside that edge's run (its coarser incident edges are exactly two, of one level, with identical rows of that level; VK3-3) — hard, batch-local, the commit record's new, changed, demoted and removed edges and their vertices, and its promoted and demoted vertices.

The doors: insertChain is the only door for new edges; removeEdges and clearFiner the only doors for removing them; insertChain's opts.knots and splitThrough's row the only doors for adding a vertex role row (with retypeEdges' rekey, which moves rows between entities); removeEdges on a VertexRef the door for stripping one (an S8 portal whose lane is removed, §4.6; a tower wallToWay removes, §4.11); warp the only door for moving existing vertices (a moveVertex edit is a warp displacing one vertex resolved by resolveVertexAt; smoothing of committed geometry is a warp whose field the smoother computes). Every other writer is built from these, so planarity, minEdge, clearance and the kept-content rule are properties of this list (§3.10).

insertChain step 5 (re-walk): only faces incident to touched edges are re-walked; face records, owners, parents and stage ranks are updated (a kept face is re-parented into the new face containing it); the commit record lists them.

J-K3: topology by index, references by role. Inside kernel topology keyed by VertexId/HalfEdgeId/FaceId, never object identity or coordinates (2017 shared-Point topology and FTG coincident-intersection bug are the two failures; os-geometry.md §1.1, FTG 153121107)

No record outside the kernel stores arena slots, and no entity record stores a vertex position — except a building's wing rings and its stored stage-3 composition's rings and tower centres (§2.6), whose footprint-boundary points are footprint vertices re-read by §2.6's wing-carrying rule after every change (NP3-1, NP4-2)
facts.values: one stated exception (wing / composition rings, tower centres)

facts.statement: Entity-to-geometry by role/owner tables, examples: Way spine ChainRef(way, wayId); plot FaceRef(plotId,3); junction VertexRef(junction,id); bridge deck ends VertexRef(deck_end, bridgeId, 0|1); water gate bank ends VertexRef(gate_end, gateId, 0|1); castle weld ends VertexRef(weld, castleId, 0|1); open wall end anchors VertexRef(anchor, enceinteId, 0|1); reservation attach points VertexRef(attach, reservationId, i); plot bound gate openings EdgeSetRef(gate_opening, boundId, i)
resolve(ref: FaceRef | ChainRef | EdgeSetRef | VertexRef, key: PlatKey) → Resolved: current slots, stamped with the arena version.

Splits carry roles to both parts, merges union them, attraction merges them onto the surviving edge/vertex, promotion keeps them (except a prepared anchor contact name, which it strips), warp moves the carrying vertex — so a stored reference cannot go stale (GEO-5 (a))

J-K31 / VK3-9: stretches — an operator that removes or hands over part of a chain (carve cut stretch, pruned remainder, kept way's replaced stretch, moved river's old shore stretch, boundary stretch between two bank anchors, way split, partial wallToWay) names it by a StretchRef

StretchRef semantics: chain edges between two of its vertices in chain order for an open chain; for a ring from `from` counter-clockwise to `to` (ring orientation by orient2d at lowest-leftmost vertex, §3.2 (6)); ends name vertices by role or lattice point (unique per lattice point, §3.10); a cut end not yet a vertex is placed first by splitThrough (may give it a vertex role row); resolved within its batch, never stored

A StretchRef resolves at the batch's current state: each end must be a vertex of the chain (named by a vertex role or by its lattice point) and both must lie on one part of it, else E_DEGENERATE with detail 'stretch'; an end finer than the chain is first promoted to the chain's level (W_PROMOTED, listed in the commit record, its split flag cleared), because it becomes an end of the remaining parts.

facts.statement: Chain attributes are knot profiles, never positional arrays (VK-2): way width, wall base elevation, tunnel invert, shore bank kind and shore class are ChainProfiles whose knots are vertices of the entity's own-level route carrying the registry knot role with an ordinal (width_knot, wayId, i)

Profile interpolation: linear by arc length along the route (linear) or held knot to next (step, categorical); constant before first/after last knot of an open chain; a ring interpolates cyclically; a multi-ring chain carries ≥ 1 knot per ring and never interpolates across rings
A constant attribute is a scalar with no knots; the creating stage places each knot on an existing vertex of its own level or inserts one with splitThrough at its own level
splitThrough, attraction, crossings, promotion and warp never change a profile: a split adds a knot-less vertex; a knot vertex moves with its chain
kerb, bandUnion and every export sample the profile (§3.4, §3.7); the digest hashes its values with the knot rows, so an S8 T-junction cannot shift width elsewhere

J-K23 / VK2-8: cutting a profiled chain (way split, partial wallToWay, carve cut) goes through retypeEdges with rekey (§3.4), which first gives each part a cut knot at every cut vertex carrying the profile sample there: linear = arc-length interpolation kept as exact double (only non-authored knot value; computed with + − × ÷ and Math.sqrt only); step = held value; cut at a knot vertex copies the knot to the other part; a part wholly before the first/after last knot takes the constant as a scalar
Cut knots: 20 000 random ways split between two width knots — largest change 6.8×10⁻¹³ cm, 92 % bit-identical; re-keying knots alone changed a width by up to 8.47 m (fixall_kernel_r3_checks.out B)

home.anchor: drop from the normative text; keep at most a one-line receipt pointer

facts.statement: Removing a stretch of a profiled chain (VK3-9) gives each remaining part a cut knot at the stretch end on its side before the stretch's rows and interior knot rows leave; every remaining sample unchanged

Stretch removal: 20 000 random ways with 2–5 width knots — max change 1.6×10⁻¹² cm vs 8.36 m without; 5 000 profiled rings opened between two anchors — 5.9×10⁻¹² cm vs 25.8 m (fixall_kernel_r4_checks.out C)

home.anchor: drop from the normative text; keep at most a one-line receipt pointer

facts.statement: Join of two chains concatenates knots in chain order and drops a knot at the join vertex only where the joined profile samples identically without it (value equals interpolation of neighbours within 10⁻⁹ cm decided in doubles; step: equals previous knot); an undone split's two cut knots drop, restoring profile bit for bit (20 000 of 20 000, r3 file); differing values stay on the one vertex as two ordinals (a step), as §3.6 step 1's merged knots

Positions in the log (GEO-5 (b)): an event addressing a vertex by position (moveVertex, §7.1) stores its LatticePoint and the vertex's VertexSig at edit time; the edit layer refuses a target with an empty signature (every editable vertex carries a structural or vertex role, §7.1 table)

resolveVertexAt(key, at, sig) (§3.4) on replay maps the signature's entity ids through carry-over (§6.3) and binds: (1) vertex at `at` if its signature contains every recorded row; (2) else nearest vertex whose signature contains every recorded row within the rebind radius — attractCm without vertex roles, else §6.3 anchor radius of its vertex-role kind (junction and pin 1 m, gate and tower 2 m) — ties by lattice position (y then x); (3) else event orphaned and reported (§7.3 item 4); never bound by distance alone
facts.values: radii: attractCm 26 cm; junction/pin 1 m; gate/tower 2 m

facts.statement: Lifecycle moveCourseKnot (VK2-12): created by dragging a river's control knot; read as WaterBody.controls (§2.3), the knot path controls/<ordinal> in editedPaths (implicitly pinned); persisted: water body address, knot ordinal, at, to; regenerate: S1's water operator, moved knot kept by every later re-trace; undo record: replaced scope of the whole chain and the knot's former position; migrate: binds after the water body's address is carried (§6.3): (1) the knot with that ordinal if within the rebind radius of at (half the body's control spacing, §4.2 S1 (3)), (2) else the nearest knot of that body within the radius (ties by ordinal), (3) else orphaned and reported; never another body's knot

places: §7.3 (b) 1 6172 (edited knot within half a control spacing) (restated, per DETERMINISM-474)

facts.statement: Kernel-pinned vertices (gates, junctions, portals) move with everything else under a warp unless held, because a warp is the user's explicit move and every entity names its vertices by role, so a moved gate is still its gate.
places: §3.1 l.2148 (smoothing never moves pinned) (restated, per KERNEL-278)

facts.statement: Refinement is a pure function: L(n+1) = refine_n(level-n view, params, streams), streams keyed from the scope's lineage (§6.1)

Fine levels (L1 cells and below) use tree scoping: every unprotected finer entity under the effective scope is discarded and the refinement stages re-run for those faces - recorded inputs and unchanged rerolls for Regenerate (keep settings), advanced rerolls for New random; sound by over-invalidation; the primary mechanism

Kept content (VK-1, J-K14): every face records the rank of the stage whose batch created it (LevelFaces.stage; rank = the stage's position in §4.1's topological order, fixed per generator version). A batch clears finer content inside its faces only where that content's stage rank ≥ that of rederivesFrom; finer faces an earlier stage made are kept — neither cleared nor re-owned — and their edges and vertices are obstacles: an op that would cross a kept edge, split a kept face or bring new geometry within attractCm of it (other than a finer vertex on a route the chain ends on, which is promoted) returns E_KEPT.
Roles, not a single type: each edge pair and vertex carries a small sorted set of (role, entity, level, ordinal) rows from the role registry (a versioned data table)
Any output reading a role set in order (digest §6.2, a contact name's entity) reads it by the role's rank in the registry then the entity's address id — never by an interned handle

Edge roles: way, kerb, corridor_split, band, wall, wall_gate, shore, bank, border, margin, field_bound, district_bound, plot_line, party_wall, frontage, access, yard_part, claim, reserved (reservation boundary before growth, §4.2 S3), setback (L1 line bounding a wall strip, §4.8), deck, green_line (hedgerows on L3 field boundaries), treatment (plot edge fence/hedge/wall/railing as attribute row), gate_opening (sub-edge of a treated plot edge left open for a gate, indexed per gate), tunnel, invisible
Vertex roles: junction, tower, gate, entrance, portal, attach, anchor, weld, deck_end, gate_end, one knot role per profiled attribute (width_knot, base_knot, invert_knot, bank_knot, shore_class_knot)
Registry marks attach, anchor, weld, deck_end, gate_end, gate_opening and the knot roles indexed (rows carry an ordinal)

deck role: a Bridge's deck span = the way's own L1 edge between the bridge's two deck_end bank vertices, carrying deck beside the way role (ChainRef(deck, bridgeId)); S1 and S3 place bank vertices at L0 on shores, S4 or S5 lays the span through them; a carve's or S1 water operator's preparation batch places them on a kept way and water's L0 batch promotes them; a site no way uses keeps two bank vertices and no span (Bridge.state = site); a deck where no site stands on already-standing water (F-ROUTE extra bridge, drawn bridge) gets bank vertices from one L0 batch of two same-level shore splits, nothing cleared, before the way's L1 batch; inside S1's water operator or a carve F-ROUTE's extra-bridge rung only sites its deck (§4.2 S1 (5); NP3-4, VD4-10); so no L0 edge crosses water and no deck splits a water body's L0 faces (LC-7, J-I12)
Avenue and street-tree rows are Greenery.along records, not edges (§2.7)
A way's class, width profile and surface are attributes of the Way entity, not its edges (FTG's 14 wire types generalised)
A wall chain may be open, its ends anchored on typed vertices (shore, cliff, castle)

J-K29 / VK3-2: anchor row marks the end of an open chain resting on a coarser feature (open wall ends (anchor, enceinteId, 0|1)) or serves as a contact name: a bank point a coarse insertion's preparation batch places on a finer edge that is neither a kept way nor a re-traced wall run (perimeter/district-boundary stretch, wall strip setback/glacis line, map border; §3.3 rule 2), for the water batch to name in KernelTx.prepared

Contact name's entity = first row of the edge's own birth level in role order: district boundary → first district in id order among its district_bound rows; perimeter → first in id order of inner district and hinterland pseudo-district; setback/glacis line → its setback row's entity (enceinte); map border → arena Terrain

A contact name is placed by splitThrough with its row given without an ordinal; the kernel allocates that entity's smallest free anchor ordinal (from 2 on an enceinte) as the op applies, in the batch's canonical op order (§3.4; VK4-6 (b)); the name lives until the coarse batch strips it.
facts.values: anchor ordinals from 2 on an enceinte

facts.statement: Clear-region rule 3 (Contact): the coarse batch splits the finer faces meeting the region (re-walked, keeping their owners until a later batch of the operator re-owns them), lists the prepared vertices in KernelTx.prepared, and may meet finer edges and vertices only there: §3.6 candidate (c) attracts it onto each prepared vertex and promotes it, clearing the vertex's split flag and stripping an anchor contact name. Finer edges at a prepared vertex stay: each kept way's straight L1 edge between its two promoted bank vertices becomes the Bridge's deck span carrying deck beside way; each re-traced run's edge between its gate_end vertices is its water gate; the border's stretch is the closed frame; no L0 edge crosses the water, no deck splits the water body's L0 faces, and the way stays one chain (J-I12). Any other contact with finer geometry is E_LEVEL inside the region and E_KEPT outside it.

Water gate's two bank vertices carry (gate_end, gateId, 0|1), on a re-traced run from the preparation batch on, under a fresh Gate address (as a re-sited deck under a fresh Bridge, §6.3, §7.3 (b) 3), and persist because Gate.banks names them; the wall edge between them lies across the water as a deck span does

The trace never crosses water except at a water gate where a river passes; its two vertices on the river banks carry (gate_end, gate, 0|1) and the Gate names them in banks, as an edit’s re-traced run’s do; both kinds are held under a warp unless fromLevel = 0 (generated gate: trace L1 vertices on the shores; edited gate: L0 after the water’s promotion).

Edge roles are structural (way, wall, wall_gate, shore, bank, border, margin, reserved, setback, deck, tunnel) or partition (the rest); a structural role is never removed by sliver absorption or face merge (§3.6); §5.3 crossing invariant finds deck edges by their role
A vertex carrying any role row of a live entity is never dissolved
Coincident features are one edge with several roles (street on district boundary, quay on shore, wall on bank, track on field boundary) — never two edges and never an overwrite
places: §2.2 rule 1 (track on field boundary) (restated, per MODEL-132)

facts.statement: Transaction execution: a batch is one growth stage, one district's infill, one block's plot subdivision or one edit; the kernel applies ops to a scratch overlay, serves every in-batch query from the level's dynamic grid plus the static partitions, validates batch-local invariants on the touched faces and their one-ring (§3.10), and commits or rejects atomically; local repair (§5) runs inside the transaction on the overlay.

Wing rule 1 — boundary runs are footprint runs: the parts of a wing ring on the footprint boundary are runs of the footprint's rings vertex for vertex (a wing boundary vertex is a footprint vertex identified by its lattice point, §3.10); S11 establishes this at the first carry by inserting the footprint rings through every wing vertex on the wings' union boundary (a collinear one included as a shape vertex that never dissolves) and carrying from the inserted ring to the committed face (ChainInsert.placed, §3.4; a row quad already is its committed ring); between wings inside the footprint a vertex one wing has on another's side is a vertex of both rings; every later carry keeps both properties

Wing rule 2 — carry: (a) each boundary run re-read from the after-rings between its two end vertices in the direction keeping the interior on its left, matched by identity (added boundary vertex joins every wing ring along it, dissolved leaves, moved moves); a wing wholly on the boundary (one-wing house, row quad) is re-read whole from its first corner's vertex; (b) every other wing vertex (inner joint, hidden corner of an overlapping wing) takes mean-value coordinates w.r.t. the before-rings (outer and holes), applied to after-rings with + − × ÷ and sqrt only (§6.5), rounded to the lattice; a shared joint maps to one point

Wing rule 3 — kinds: rect and quad corners name the same corner vertices after the carry and are re-indexed; a rect whose carried ring fails §3.8's convex near-rectangle test (every turn non-negative by exact orient2d, four OBB corners matched by ring vertices within 30 cm, area ≥ 0.97 of OBB) becomes a quad with its four corners and ridgeAxis swapped (rect axis 0 along side 1 = quad axis 1), so the ridge keeps its direction and roof path is re-chosen (§3.8, §8.6); quad and polygon keep their kinds

Wing rule 4 — check: every carried ring simple and CCW; union of wings equals footprint face (integer equality after snapping, the stage-3 contract test); decided by the building's pairing (NP4-6; J-P49): whether every directed wing-ring edge keyed by vertex identity is a footprint-ring edge (each used once) or the reverse of exactly one other wing edge; found once per edit, holds through every halving, recomputed by a batch adding/removing a vertex. Tiers: (i) every wing re-read whole → no union, only rule 3 test on a rect; (ii) pairing holds (tiled L, T, cross, U, templates of tiles) → only simple CCW rings; (iii) pairing fails (overlapping wings) → kernel boolean union on the arrangement (§3.7) against the face

For warp/moveVertex the wing check is part of whole-step validation, which halves the step on failure (§3.6; edit layer's record check as for a held pin, §7.4); runs after the kernel's own checks pass; stops at the first failing building in address order; after any other batch a failing building is re-derived by S11 on its plot (F-REDERIVE, reported)

What the snapshot holds (FTG-21, SCL-11): geometry stored once per arena — every boundary written once with its birth level; faces, twins and parents rebuilt on load (§3.9); every level present so a frozen view needs no pipeline code of its own version; entities as columns (identity, lifecycle, attributes, derivation records, naming records, §2.8); provenance not stored (verification replays rebuild it)

Prosperity, density and greenery fields are not stored at full resolution: an editable document recomputes them from their drivers and the stroke list on load (§4.5, §7.2); the snapshot carries only a Uint8 copy of each field at 32 m (≈40 KB at CITY) for thematic display in a frozen view
Neither digest tree is stored: the snapshot holds the two roots (digest, recordsDigest) and the load recomputes both trees (step 3)
The report records stream keys only for ladder uses (any rung from tier 2 up, retries at attempt > 0 included), not for every stream the town used (SCL-11)

Chunks (NF-D5, VD2-9): the block is written as content-addressed chunks. Per arena, the level-≤ 1 routes are one chunk (every vertex of birth level ≤ 1; every L0–L1 edge as one (origin, destination, birth level) triple between its level-≤ 1 endpoints, with its roles of level ≤ 1 and the L0–L1 face rows — no finer Steiner vertex). Each static-index partition (one per district plus one outside districts) is one chunk holding the vertices born in it, its edges of level ≥ 2 (each district boundary is an L1 edge, so each lies in one partition), the Steiner splits its batches made on L0–L1 edges (each as the coarser edge's route endpoints and the split vertex, by lattice point, with the split vertex's level), the finer roles those batches added to the coarser edges' sub-edges, and its face rows of level ≥ 2.

Every reference to a vertex another chunk holds is its lattice point, never (chunk, index), because a vertex is unique per lattice point in its arena; a vertex on an L1 edge two partitions share (the foot of a wall- or margin-band cross edge) is written in the chunk of the partition with the smaller key and named by lattice point from the other.

Chunk rewrite scope: an edit that renumbers one partition's vertices rewrites that partition's chunk alone; the level-≤ 1 chunk only when it changes a level-≤ 1 route, promotes a vertex into one or demotes a vertex or edge out of one; and, when it changes a level-≤ 1 route edge, also every partition chunk holding a Steiner split on that edge (each split names its route edge by the edge's endpoints, VK4-6 (c)); §2.9's rebased-size test at M2a counts these, its block-group fallback pre-decided.

Formats: canonical .plat container = JSON manifest (schema-validated, human-diffable: versions, docId, nextSeq, base recipe, log, pack data, host content, style, snapshot chunk lists) + binary blocks (chunks by hash) as typed arrays; saving from app or API always writes model; only the CLI's --recipe-only export writes a document without it (test fixtures, files made from links) and it refuses a rebased base (VD4-8)

Compact twin: CBOR with typed-array tags; varint zig-zag int32 cm in world coordinates, the settlement centre in the header, so it is an encoding of the same schema (FTG-21); for embeds and sharing; a decoder is part of the library.
Canonical document = docId, schemaVersion, outputVersion, nextSeq, base, log, packs, hostContent, style, model (when present); view, derived and undo are never canonical
logHead = a 128-bit hash of (document id, edit-log length, hash of the last event), in hex (§2.9; our own term, FTG-22).

View state (FTG-12, LC-16): time, location, favourites, notes and public notes, view pins, layer choices, stylePreset (per-viewer, never writes setStyle, §11.3; N-15), season, weather, frame, map rotation, compass, legend and emblem settings, exportAnchor (§11.1; N-14), and which people a user has looked at live in view, outside every digest; style stays canonical; each key LWW by (Lamport counter, session id), so a viewer never writes the model

Sessions (VD2-4): a session is an authoring identity per document and author, not per app start; @plat/api mints one (128-bit random value in base 32, outside model packages) the first time an author edits a document and reuses it on every later open: an unshared document stores it in view state (view.keys['session'], outside every digest, saved with the file, §2.9), so reloads continue the same undo/redo stacks; a file made without one (CLI, link) mints on first edit; a bridged client takes the session the host assigns in doc.load (§11.3; host keeps one per user and document) and never writes the view key; the session enters the log only as EditBase.session; the fold never reads it
Round trip is a hard test: export → import → export byte-identical over the canonical form (O9 a, O11 c)

The kernel never throws for a geometric reason: every primitive returns a typed result (ok value with warnings, or a typed error code with detail and optional partial) instead of crashing or returning unchecked output.
Every stage of generation changes geometry only through batch transactions that are accepted whole after checking the rules or rejected whole; this is what removes whole-map discard-and-retry.
Build-versus-adopt table: lattice, snapping and attraction are built in-house.
Every coordinate passes snap(), with a finite-and-range check in every build (not only debug).
attractCm, the attraction radius.

Attraction: a new vertex within attractCm of an existing vertex lands on it; within attractCm of an edge it lands on the edge via splitThrough, or on that edge's endpoint when the exact foot lies within attractCm of the endpoint, so no split leaves a sub-edge shorter than minEdge.
A new chain running within attractCm of an existing edge shares that stretch with merged roles (stretch sharing).
Placement rule: every new vertex on an existing edge (a split foot, a stretch's join or leave point, a crossing) is placed at the nearest lattice point that keeps minEdge and clearance.

Crossings are resolved by iterated snap rounding on the 1 cm lattice, at most 3 passes; every pass leaves a planar arrangement, so an unconverged result commits with warning W_SNAP_PASSES instead of failing.
There is no separate weld tolerance: coincidence is lattice-point equality; proximity is handled by attraction.

facts.statement: Exact predicates: orient2d is built (exact in doubles under the §3.2 coordinate bound); incircle is adopted from robust-predicates 3.0.3 (Unlicense), licence confirmed against the public registry, version pinned and re-checked by §17.4's licence checker on every upgrade; pre-decided fallback if a future version fails the checker: an in-house BigInt incircle.
Collinear and cocircular ties are broken deterministically on lattice positions, never on slot ids; no predicate compares a float with == 0.
incircle is never on the topology path.
Ring orientation is decided by orient2d at the lowest-leftmost vertex; areas are exact integers (area2); no topology decision reads the sign of a float sum.
Planar subdivision is built in-house as the core asset, struct-of-arrays with allocation-free hot loops (G-R7; NG profile evidence: Point.new 385–561 k and intersectLines 147–213 k calls dominate).
Every insertion is part of a batch transaction.
Self-touching chains are split into simple runs and inserted run by run.
A face below its class floor is absorbed across a partition edge or kept as typed residue; an edge carrying a structural role is never deleted.
Finer content an earlier stage made is kept, never cleared by a coarser batch.
Polygon booleans are built on the kernel's arrangement (J-K4): overlay operands in a scratch arrangement using insertChain's machinery, label faces by winding number, keep the selected faces.
Clipper2 (BSL-1.0, compiled to WASM, run in Node) and polygon-clipping (MIT) are CI oracles in @plat/testkit only, never shipped.

Booleans take and return integer coordinates under the same attraction, placement, minEdge and clearance rules as every other writer; fill rule declared per call (non-zero or even-odd); an empty result is E_DEGENERATE with detail 'empty'; the oracle comparison is split by whether attraction fired.

Buffers, offsets, insets and bands are built on the arrangement: a buffer is the union of per-segment strips and per-vertex join discs (round joins as chords of ≤ 2 cm sagitta; square ends where declared); a per-edge inset and the kerb are face minus the union of buffers; corridors and wall bands are committed by corridorUnion / bandUnion; a varying half-width is sampled from the chain's knot profile, each segment's strip a trapezoid between its end widths.

The half-plane inset is used only for a uniform inset of a face whose convexity is checked exactly (E_NON_CONVEX otherwise); an inset larger than the inradius returns E_DEGENERATE with detail 'collapsed' and the last non-empty distance.

Straight skeleton is built (J-K5): a wavefront with an event queue in doubles using + − × ÷ √ only; events coalesced within 1 mm of offset time and 1 cm of position; ties by the vertex's index in the canonicalised ring; a work limit counted in events; a post-condition validator on every output; convex near-rectangular footprints take the exact OBB roof instead.
facts.values: coalesce 1 mm offset time, 1 cm position

facts.statement: Straight-skeleton uses: roofs of irregular footprints and label spines (the maximum-clearance spanning tree of the hole-aware skeleton graph).
No permissive, mature JS/TS straight-skeleton library is assumed; CGAL (GPL/LGPL) is rejected.

Skeleton input is pre-cleaned (collinear merge, minimum angle 5°); holes supported; a validator failure or E_WORK_LIMIT takes the typed downgrade — a plain roof (no ridge or hip lines) for roofs, a sampled medial axis for spines — exercised by fixtures; never a crash, never unvalidated output.
OBB, convex hull and largest inscribed rectangle are built: monotone chain + rotating calipers; LIR sampled deterministically over four candidate axes (OBB long axis, frontage normal, ±45°) (G-R13).
GEO-7 contract: OBB / hull / LIR with fewer than 3 distinct points or a collinear hull return E_DEGENERATE (detail 'collinear'), never ok with a zero extent; callers must branch on the typed result.

Delaunay / Voronoi adopted: delaunator (ISC), d3-delaunay (ISC); duplicate points merged first; used only for the routing lattice, site sampling, Lloyd relaxation, field seeds and medial axes — never as the street source.
Poisson-disc / blue noise built: Bridson with k = 50 candidates, all evaluated (the references' measured variant, G-P17).
The tiles are built once, when the product is built, and shipped; nothing samples or ranks at run time.

Trees: placement ≤ 1 µs and drawing ≤ 2 µs per instance; a district-band view with 10 000 visible trees composes in one 16 ms frame from cached tiles and its tiles raster in ≤ 30 ms of tile-worker time (O19 e); the 200 000 trees of a METROPOLIS are never all instantiated — only visible tiles generate instances.

Poisson/stamp domains are clipped to any polygon with holes; empty domains return empty; a ragged wood edge comes from thinning the stamped points by the domain-warped density noise, not from warping the sampler (COV-VG-WC3).
Noise: simplex-noise (MIT) adopted with our seeding; fBm and domain warp built; seeded from sub-streams; octaves and lacunarity are table values (VG's 5-octave field as evidence).
Curves built: Chaikin, centripetal Catmull-Rom → cubic, pinned-vertex Laplacian, Visvalingam–Whyatt, circular fillets.
Smoothing never moves pinned vertices (gates, junctions, portals).

Whole-step validation: a smoothing or warp step is validated as a whole step — edges incident to moved vertices against the index and unmoved vertices against the swept triangles, every edge incident to a moved vertex at least minEdge long, no two vertices on one lattice point, and the clearance invariant — and halved globally on failure.

Visvalingam–Whyatt is topology-preserving: a removal is refused when the new edge would touch or cross another edge of the ring, its face's other rings or a declared obstacle, checked in the index (the simplify service).
Fillets are skipped when legs are shorter than the chord; curve results re-enter through insertChain.

Spatial index: flatbush (ISC) static partitions per level — one per arena at L0–L1, one per district at L2–L4 — rebuilt only at stage end; a uniform grid per level for every change inside a stage and for edits; rbush (MIT) only for the screen-space label collision index.
facts.values: L0–L1 per arena; L2–L4 per district

facts.statement: S10's eager step (0) ends before the pool's freeze and rebuilds the L3 partitions it touched, so the frozen copy holds every item in a static partition.

Each level's index holds that level's items — vertices, whole route edges boxed over the vertices standing on their runs and padded by the hot pixel, faces — so a finer batch's Steiner split never writes a coarser level's index.

Tombstoning: every item a batch deletes, re-levels or changes (a promotion or demotion included) is tombstoned in the partition that holds it and its successor inserted in its level's grid (VK4-5); tombstones are item keys, one set per partition, and filter static-partition hits only.
Every freeze first rebuilds the partitions edits left dirty (§3.3 step 1).

Query order: a level-n query returns level-n items sorted by their canonical key on the level-n route — a vertex of level ≤ n by lattice position (y, then x); an edge by the two endpoints of its level-n route edge, lower (y, x) first; a face by the first two vertices of level ≤ n on its outer ring from the lowest-leftmost such vertex (a ring that visits it twice takes the smaller successor). It is a total order because a directed level-n route edge bounds exactly one level-n face; neither which index holds an item nor whether a finer level exists changes an output (VK-14, VK2-4).

Marching squares / distance transform: d3-contour (ISC) or our own; linear time; VG's createDeflection hot spot avoided by construction; contours extracted per render tile, not in S1, and never plat edges.
Path search built: binary-heap A* / Dijkstra on rasters and on the subdivision graph (the 2017 'A*', a FIFO BFS, is not reproduced); failure returns E_NO_PATH with the closest reached point.
Triangulation for render and fields adopted: earcut (ISC); holes supported; degenerate triangles skipped and reported.
Fields, costs and weights are IEEE doubles; + - x / and Math.sqrt are exact by specification; every other real function goes through dmath (the vetted fdlibm port, D-23)

facts.statement: RNG engine: xoshiro128** per stream (four 32-bit words; period 2^128 - 1; fast in JS, no BigInt)
KernelResult<T> = { ok: true; value; warnings: Warning[] } | { ok: false; code: KernelError; detail: string; partial?: T }.

KernelError codes and meanings: E_OUT_OF_RANGE (snap: non-finite or |coordinate| ≥ 2^23 cm, a caller bug reported with its stream key, never stored); E_DEGENERATE (ratio vanishing denominator; OBB/hull of collinear or < 3 points; empty or collapsed boolean/buffer/inset; StretchRef whose ends are not two distinct vertices of one part of its chain, detail 'stretch'); E_LEVEL (batch wrote another level, added a row coarser than the edge/vertex it lands on, or a clear-region batch met finer geometry inside its region away from prepared contacts); E_LOCKED (would cut/move/delete geometry of a locked or pinned entity — returned to the dry run as a conflict); E_KEPT (insertion or clear would cross, clear or come within attractCm of kept finer content, or in a clear-region batch content outside the region — a stage-domain bug in generation, a conflict in an edit dry run; a move keeps nothing); E_SCOPE (pool district overlay wrote outside its district's face set, or two overlays touched one record); E_STRUCTURAL (merge/removal would delete a structural-role edge); E_NOT_TWO_CROSSINGS (splitFace contact semantics); E_HOLE_CONTACT (connectHole post-condition); E_SELF_INTERSECT (ring requiring a simple polygon crosses itself); E_BELOW_MIN_EDGE (optional chains only, collapse below one edge after decimation); E_BELOW_MIN_ANGLE (optional chains only, face corner below minFaceAngle); E_BELOW_MIN_AREA, E_BELOW_MIN_WIDTH (caller-declared class floor); E_NON_CONVEX; E_NO_PATH; E_WORK_LIMIT (operation-count budget exhausted, never a clock); E_INVARIANT (declared hard invariant failed at commit).

Warning = { code; count; at?: LatticePoint } with codes W_ATTRACTED, W_STRETCH_SHARED, W_WEDGE_ROUTED, W_PLACED (vertex placed away from its nearest lattice point by the placement rule), W_PROMOTED (finer vertex promoted, prepared vertices and stretch ends included), W_SNAP_PASSES, W_ACUTE_CORNER, W_SLIVER_RETYPED, W_STEINER, W_HEIGHT_CLAMPED, W_DOWNGRADE.

Legacy error-code mapping: E_TIMEOUT → E_WORK_LIMIT; E_SNAP_UNSTABLE → warning W_SNAP_PASSES; E_MIN_EDGE → E_BELOW_MIN_EDGE (optional chains only); E_COLLAPSED and E_COLLINEAR → E_DEGENERATE with detail; E_NONMANIFOLD → prevented by contact semantics and the simple-face invariant.
