Integer world: all persisted geometry is integer cm; intermediate rational points (crossings, offsets, circumcentres, skeleton nodes) are computed in doubles and immediately placed on the lattice — by §3.6's placement rule for points on existing edges, by nearest-point rounding otherwise.

Range derivation: METROPOLIS target at aspect 2 is 11.31 km × 5.66 km plus the 30 % margin on every side, so |x| ≤ 0.8 × 11.31 km = 905 097 cm ≈ 2^19.8; the largest arena is METROPOLIS at the population cap 120 000 (153.6 km², §12.2) at aspect 2 — 17.53 km × 8.76 km, |x| ≤ ≈ 1 402 000 cm ≈ 2^20.4.

Range invariant: |x|, |y| < 2^23 cm (83.9 km); hence every coordinate difference < 2^24, every orient2d term < 2^48, the determinant < 2^49, and the sign of orient2d is exact in ordinary doubles with ≈ 6× headroom over the largest arena (≈ 9× at the METROPOLIS target). Every exactness argument rests on this invariant (enforced by snap), never on the frame table, so a rescaled frame (§13.7 O14 (e)) cannot break one.
incircle uses the adaptive predicate and is kept off the topology path.
Tolerances are world lengths, never parameter-space (the reference's DELTA = 1e-6 on line parameters is the anti-pattern).
minEdge — the minimum edge length for every writer.

attractCm = minEdge + lattice slack, so a vertex split onto an edge is placed at least attractCm − 0.71 cm = 25.29 cm from both endpoints (a vertex whose exact foot lies within attractCm of an endpoint moves onto the endpoint instead, §3.6 step 2).
facts.values: 26 cm; ≥ 25.29 cm from endpoints; slack 0.71 cm

facts.statement: Maximum displacement of an incoming vertex by attraction: √2 · attractCm ≈ 36.8 cm (onto an edge's endpoint from beside the edge); a new vertex on an existing edge moves off its nearest lattice point only under the placement rule.

Attraction bench evidence (fixall_kernel_r2_attract.out): over 400 000 vertices dropped in the attraction band of random lattice edges, 0 sub-edges shorter than minEdge, shortest 25.50 cm, largest displacement 36.72 cm; the first-written rule left a sub-minEdge edge in 1.34 % of edge attractions (fixall_verify_kernel_attract_gap.out).
minFaceAngle — the kernel's soft corner floor.

Class floors from the tables: minPlotWidth = 2.5 m; minInteriorAnglePlot = 12° (FTG's sheared quads at p95 22.9° corner deviation stay legal — invariants police validity, not regularity); minCorridor per class.

One minimum-edge rule for every writer (GEO-35): insertChain, booleans, buffers, offsets, smoothing and warp create or move edges only through §3.6's insertion semantics or move validation, and the invariant checks the same minEdge on new and moved edges.
Face-size floors are always a minimum width and a minimum area, never minEdge.
No weld tolerance (J-K2): the earlier 5 cm weld no longer exists; coincidence is lattice-point equality and proximity is attraction.

No float comparisons for topology: equality is index equality; 'same place' is a lattice test; any float that decides a topology operation is quantised first to integer cm or to a 16-bit binary angle.

A distance comparison against attractCm or minEdge on a computed point (an exact foot, a crossing) is made in doubles with + − × ÷ √ only, so it is identical on every IEEE engine; a borderline case may fall either way without breaking any bound, because the 1 cm between attractCm and minEdge exceeds the 0.71 cm of any single rounding.

Nightly cross-platform golden run (Node x86 / arm64, Chromium, Firefox, WebKit; workers on and off; pool sizes 0 and 3): identical model digests per stage, derived-complete digests and placement digests on every engine; from M3a the strict GeoJSON of one golden CITY seed (coast+river) with its trees (§8.10 integer-centimetre instance positions, species, crown diameters, leaf types) byte-identical on every engine, workers on and off (§11.1).
Angles and directions are unit vectors in doubles derived from integer endpoints; growth headings are stored as centidegrees.

Exact area (GEO-32, VK-8, J-K13): area2(ring) returns twice the signed area as an exact integer for every ring snap can produce — shoelace terms on coordinates relative to the ring's bounding-box minimum corner (in [0, 2^24)), each |term| < 2^48; terms summed in a double partial flushed into a BigInt accumulator whenever its magnitude reaches 2^52 (one comparison per term), so every partial stays below 2^52 + 2^48 < 2^53; faces at frame-table sizes never reach the flush (terms < 2^43); the result is returned as an exact double because a simple ring's twice-area is < 2^49; a self-crossing ring (only a boolean operand before overlay) uses area2Big, which returns the BigInt.
facts.values: flush at 2^52; terms < 2^48; ordinary terms < 2^43; twice-area < 2^49

facts.statement: area2 evidence (fixall_kernel_r2_attract.out E): three star rings of radius 2^23 − 2 with same-sign terms are exact under the magnitude flush and inexact under the former fixed 1 024-term flush.

snap(x, y) is the only door by which a number becomes an arena coordinate; in every build it rejects !(Math.abs(v) < 2**23) (one comparison, also catching NaN and ±∞) with E_OUT_OF_RANGE, so NaN, ±∞ and values past 2^31 never reach an Int32Array (which would store 0, 0 and a wrapped value — executed in GEO-7); the null-rect crash class cannot return as a vertex at the origin.

Checked ratios: in model packages a division by a computed value goes through ratio(num, den, kind), which returns E_DEGENERATE when |den| is below the quantity's floor (length 1 cm, area 1 cm², angle 1 centidegree, count 1); a lint rule flags every other division whose divisor is not a non-zero literal.
The range bound of (1) is derived from the largest frame at the extreme aspect, so a non-square town needs no other change.

J-K13: Chose a magnitude-triggered flush at 2⁵² from the range invariant for `area2` over flush intervals derived from the frame table — because it is exact for every ring `snap` admits and ordinary faces never pay a BigInt addition (VK-8) (§3.2).

home.anchor: J-K13 (index row stays in the main document's Judgment calls index; the row names §3.2)

facts.statement: KernelTx { key: PlatKey; level: Level; ops: KernelOp[] (declared form only — independent ops applied in canonical order); expect: Invariant[]; onFail: 'reject' | 'repair' | 'downgrade'; batch: BatchScope; stage: StageId (the stage whose code issues the batch); rederivesFrom: StageId; clearRegion?: Ring[]; prepared?: VertexRef[]; workLimit: number (operations, from the stage's declaration) }.

rederivesFrom is the earliest stage a batch re-derives: equal to stage in generation; the start of the edit's re-derivation for an edit (§7.3); the first stage of §4.1's order for a warp or smoothing batch, which keeps nothing (J-K33).
KernelTx.workLimit is an operation count taken from the stage's declaration.
BatchScope = { kind: 'stage'; stage } | { kind: 'district'; id } | { kind: 'block'; id } | { kind: 'edit'; edit }.

CommitRecord (returned by every commit; kernel-internal slots, never persisted): version, key, level; faces per level ≥ the batch's level {created, changed, removed} — the dirty set; edgesAdded, edgesRemoved, steinerAdded, steinerDissolved; moved (vertices a warp or smoothing moved, Steiner re-seats included — their incident edges are §3.10's 'moved edges', GEO-35); promoted (finer vertices whose birth level this batch lowered — the edit's undo record keeps their lattice points, former levels, flags and stripped anchor names); demoted {vertices, edges (one half-edge per pair)} (undo keeps former levels); unflagged (vertices whose split flag or kernel pin was cleared other than by moving them — a prepared contact's or stretch end's promotion, a broken run, a pin whose last vertex role row left, an unmoved vertex beside which a move displaced its run (VK4-3); undo restores the flags); owners; roles ((role, entity, ordinal) keys); warnings; work.

One level per transaction: a batch creates vertices, edges, owners and roles of its own level only, plus the bounded Steiner vertices, promotions and demotions of §2.2 rule 3; it may clear finer content inside its faces (clearFiner) subject to the kept-content rule; a warp batch moves vertices of every level ≥ its own; anything else is E_LEVEL.

A lane a finer stage would add to a coarser level is a separate, coarser transaction (§4.7), never a side effect of a finer one; a stage writing two levels (S3: carvings at L0, reservations at L1) issues one transaction per level, in the order of §4.1's batch table.

E_KEPT governs insertion and clearing only (VK2-7 (a)); a warp or smoothing batch keeps nothing (rederivesFrom = first stage, J-K33) — what a move may not displace is decided by §3.6's held vertices and whole-step validation; faces a step leaves below a class floor are re-derived afterwards by their own batches with their own stage's rederivesFrom.
places: §3.1 E_KEPT l.2165 ('a move keeps nothing') (restated, per KERNEL-106)

facts.statement: The re-walk re-parents each kept face into the new face that contains it; a kept face never straddles a new edge (crossing it is refused), so nesting holds.

In generation E_KEPT cannot arise on a correct pipeline: a wall's band, setback and glacis parts are L3 content of their own L1 wall-strip faces, cut off by S7 before S8 and built after S9 (§4.7 S10 (0), §4.8); the hinterland's L3 content is built after S9 by its own unit (§4.9); the rule turns a wrong domain into a typed failure the stage property tests catch.
0 E_KEPT on the one-click path over B-CITY (a stage whose domain overlaps an earlier stage's kept content is a pipeline bug).

An E_KEPT conflict (edit would cross or clear finer content an earlier stage made, or content outside a coarse edit's clear region, §3.3) is offered with one resolution: start the re-derivation at the stage that made that content (for a wall's band parts or a margin band's part, S10's step (0) for the touched run's wall strips or the scope's side of the touched stretch; §4.7, §7.3 item 2)

A scope holding wall-strip faces, or faces bordering the settlement perimeter or a shared reservation boundary, re-runs step (0) for its own side's parts after its S8 and S9 (first when re-deriving from S10), before its plots: bandUnion restricted to the scope's faces, cross edges ending on the shared edge by attraction onto the vertices the other side's parts placed, and the scope's plot, alley and furlong lines ending on the re-laid band's inner edge; the other side is never written; Regenerate (keep settings) of a perimeter district or the hinterland (S12 row) lays the same parts at the same lattice points, byte-identical to the one-click result when nothing upstream changed

A batch's faces are the faces it names or creates (K4, VK2-11): a same-level split of an edge those faces share with outside faces (the neighbour step's kerb split beside finished plots and footprints, II.1 (3)) adds that vertex to the outside faces' rings; they are not kept content of the batch, are neither cleared nor re-owned, and each ring equals its prior ring with the vertex removed (the seam exception, §4.6 step 7, §7.3 item 1).
clearFiner never removes kept content and never reports it as a conflict; only locked or pinned content is a conflict (§2.2 rule 6).

Local coarse insertion (NF-P14, NF-P4, LC-7, VK2-3; J-I10, J-I12, J-I13, J-K24): a coarse batch inserted into finished fabric — §4.11's carve of a canal, moat or basin, §4.4's outer moat, S1's water operator re-carving a reach (§7.3 (b)) — runs as a declared sequence of single-level batches sharing one clear region (KernelTx.clearRegion), because under the plain rule one canal would clear a whole L0 land component (the town).

The clear region is the edit's footprint, computed by the operator in its dry run: its new chains buffered by (attractCm + the clearance of the chain's class — for a channel, its bank setback), united with every L1 cell the edit's way rule touches (cells the buffer meets; cells bordering a removed or pruned stretch or a kept way's replaced stretch; cells a re-routed way crosses; for a re-traced wall run, cells bordering the old run or strip-line stretches removed and cells the new strips take — VP2-1, NP3-2); the footprint is exactly the union of those cells, since the buffer lies inside the cells it meets.

Clear-region rule 1 (Clearing): clearFiner in a batch that declares a clear region removes each finer face whose interior meets the region — whole, never part — with the partition edges and vertices no remaining face uses, and nothing else; locked and pinned owners return as conflicts; every finer face not meeting the region is kept, whatever its stage rank. Structural finer edges inside the region (ways, walls, setback and glacis lines, deck spans) are kept unless a preceding batch of the same edit removed them; clearFiner removes partition content only (VD2-1). The coarse batch itself clears nothing; it only splits the finer faces that meet the region.

Clear-region rule 2 (Preparation): one or more finer-level batches issued first in the same edit or stage clear the region and place every point where the coarse chain will meet finer geometry as role-named vertices (VK3-2): on each kept way across the new water, a deck's two bank vertices carrying ('deck_end', bridge, 0 | 1) under a fresh Bridge, the stretch between them one straight edge (the deck span); on each re-traced wall run, its water gate's two bank vertices carrying ('gate_end', gate, 0 | 1) under a fresh Gate (named by the Gate record built afterwards, §2.7); on the border line (which must stay closed), its two bank points as anchor contact names with the border's stretch between them left unchanged across the water (one straight edge, or several where the water takes a frame corner or a vertex an earlier edit left, VK4-6 (a)); on every other crossed finer edge that is no way (settlement-perimeter or district-boundary stretch, wall strip setback or glacis line), its two bank points as anchor contact names with the stretch between them removed.

A coarse chain never shares a finer edge, so a finer edge the new water would run along is cut back by the preparation like any lesser way; a way cut back beyond its bank setback (every lesser way; a quay or landing, extended to the new bank only once the water exists, its end an ordinary Steiner vertex on the L0 bank, §4.11 batch (3)) leaves no contact and needs no prepared vertex.

Every stretch the preparation removes (a cut stretch, a pruned remainder, a kept way's replaced stretch, the stretch between two contact names) is removed through a StretchRef; a way left in two parts is first split by retypeEdges' rekey on its far part, so role consistency (§3.10) holds after the batch.

Carve step (4) re-derivation of R: S6’s operator restricted to R’s cells after the L0 batch — each land face of R takes the district (or hinterland, or wall_strip typing) of the pre-edit L1 cell holding the larger part of its area (ties by id); a boundary removed under water is re-separated by the water; the same larger-part rule settles a boundary stretch removed on land; new strips typed wall_strip; water faces leave the district face sets; then S8–S12b re-derive R’s cells by tree scoping (S8 first), with S10 (0) for faces beside a wall trace, perimeter or shared reservation boundary.

Canal across a CITY district that cuts a lane (remainder pruned) and re-routes a primary: every face outside its §4.11 footprint (channel buffer ∪ every L1 cell its way rule touches) byte-identical except the seam exception; its L0 channel attracts onto exactly its prepared vertices (each promoted, no other finer vertex promoted); each deck carries deck beside way per §2.2 rule 7 — the kept way's own L1 edge, no L0 edge across the channel (J-I12). A course-knot move and a river move across a street grid get the same footprint and contact assertions (§7.3 (b)).

Pre-decided fallback if an M3a fixture cannot be met: the batch clears the finer content of its whole L0 land face and re-derives it (the plain rule); moat: 'all' is then carved only before S5c of the outer stage (where L1 holds only arterials), and an edit carve becomes a declared town-wide re-derivation with the fate report (§7.3).

Two op forms (GEO-11, VK-6, J-K15): a transaction takes exactly one of two forms (declared or callback), fixed by its stage's registration (§4.1, §14); supplying both ops and a callback is a programming error caught by an assertion.

Declared form: KernelTx.ops lists independent ops, none reading another's result (S3's carvings, S4's routed arterials, S7's strip lines and furniture, S9's corridorUnion, S11's per-plot footprints, an edit's inserted feature). Before applying, the kernel sorts them by a stable key — op kind rank, then the owning entity's lineage key (§6.3), then the op's index within that entity's stream path — so the committed arena is a function of the prior arena and the op set, not of issue order. Hot-pixel snap rounding is order-independent; attraction, the one order-sensitive rule, becomes deterministic under the canonical order.
facts.values: sort key: kind rank → lineage key → stream index

restated_at: §3.3 rule 2 (anchor ordinal in canonical op order)

places: §3.3 rule 2 (anchor ordinal in canonical op order) (restated, per KERNEL-126)

facts.statement: Properties (roles and batches): roles preserved on coincident chains (a sliver between a spine and a shore keeps both); a declared batch's result identical under any permutation of its ops; a callback-form stage identical across two runs, a slot renumbering and pool sizes 0–3 (§3.3); clearFiner after refinement restores the coarser level exactly; mandatory chains never rejected for precision; 0 stale references after every batch.

Callback form: tx(tx, fn) hands fn the open overlay; each op applies at once, in issue order, and later ops read its result (S5c's growth queue, S8's bent-cut recursion, S10's plot subdivision). The issue order is deterministic because it is a function of the stage's inputs, its streams (§6.1) and canonically sorted query results — never of slot numbers, worker scheduling or arrival order — and attraction within the sequence follows it.
Callback-form test is issue-order determinism: the stage run twice, on a slot-renumbered arena, and inside the pool at sizes 0–3 gives identical digests; op permutation does not apply.

No output depends on slot numbers: every kernel tie-break uses lattice positions (y, then x), canonical item keys or entity ids, never a VertexId, HalfEdgeId or FaceId, so an arena compacted on save, one grown through a long session and one merged from pool overlays give identical results for the same next edit.
places: §3.1 l.2139 (never on slot ids) (restated, per KERNEL-130)

facts.statement: Slot-renumbering property test: renumber the arena's slots and require identical output.

Work limits instead of clocks (GEO-2): every op charges operation counts to its transaction — points snapped, attraction queries, placement candidates tried, crossings resolved, faces walked, skeleton events — and a transaction exceeding its declared workLimit returns E_WORK_LIMIT; counts are identical on slow and fast machines, so a budget can select a ladder rung without changing what the seed produces.

The commit record is the input of the batch-local invariants (§3.10), index maintenance, the display list's dirty set (§8) and the digest update: at commit the kernel re-hashes the leaves the batch touched (per-level plat digests and entity leaves of §6.2) and the nodes on their paths to the root. It is never persisted (it holds arena slots).

Digest bars (M0 d, decided before any golden is signed): maintenance <= 5 % of each batch's own time at CITY; root finalisation at a stage end <= 5 ms at CITY; full recomputation of the root from leaves <= 150 ms at CITY, records tree included - used by the CI oracle and by every load (§2.9 step 3)

An edit's dry run (§7.1) evaluates the edit's batch-local and stage-end invariants once on the scratch overlay and the commit reuses that result (overlay committed as validated): one validation per edit, not two

Derivation pool overlays (VK-3, J-K16): the per-district stages that run in the pool (S10, S10b, S11, S12b; §4.1) use the same transactions on district overlays, in five steps (frozen base, one overlay per district, scope check, merge, pool size 0).

Pool step 1 (frozen base; VK2-1, VK3-5, VK3-6, J-K25): after the eager S10a and S10's shared-edge step (0) commit — step (0) runs on the generation worker and builds, on both sides at once, the bands around every L1 edge two overlays' face sets share without corridors — step (0) ends as an eager stage does, rebuilding the static L3 partitions its batches touched (L3 is the only level it touches).

At the freeze the generation worker first rebuilds every static partition whose dynamic grid or tombstone set is not empty (none on the one-click path; after edits — an epoch's per-district stages, a Re-derive from a stage at or before S10, a verification replay folding either — the partitions the edits left dirty), then asserts every level's dynamic grid and every partition's tombstone set empty. The rebuild is the stage-end rebuild's code on live items, changes no output, and runs at every pool size, 0 included.
A partition left dirty by edits holds at most max(256, ¼ of its static size) grid items before the forced rebuild.

Freeze rebuild timing (fixall_kernel_r4_bench.out B): ≈ 2 ms for one district's L3 and L4 partitions; ≈ 10 ms for five districts'; ≈ 6 ms for the arena-wide L1 partition with one L2 partition; ≈ 59 ms worst case (every partition of a finished CITY).

The derivation pool uses transferred copies, never SharedArrayBuffer (§3.3), so no embedding host needs cross-origin isolation for generation; the tile worker's optional shared columns (§8.9) remain the only use of shared memory.

Pre-decided fallback if M1's (or M4's epoch-path) memory measurement exceeds the rung's line with these copies: a copy made after edits carries only what a pooled stage may read under the laziness contract (§4.1) — L0–L2 partitions, every L3 partition and the L4 partitions of the districts the pool derives — and then §12.8's pool-shrinking step applies.

Step (0)'s own rebuild covers every L3 item it made — at CITY ≈ 9 000 vertices, edges and faces (both sides of ≈ 6 km of perimeter margin band and of the wall's band, setback, glacis and tower parts; our count) in ≈ 26 partitions — and costs ≈ 2.3 ms at CITY and ≈ 5.8 ms at METROPOLIS by the measured build rate (fixall_kernel_r3_bench.out A), carried by §12.4 in S10 (0)'s row.
facts.values: ≈ 9 000 items; ≈ 6 km; ≈ 26 partitions; ≈ 2.3 ms CITY; ≈ 5.8 ms METROPOLIS

facts.statement: Pool step 2 (one overlay per district): a worker derives each district on a fresh overlay over the frozen base; new vertices, half-edge pairs, face records, role rows and interned entity handles go to the overlay's growable arrays in overlay-local slots numbered above the base's high-water mark (remapped at merge); a change to a base record (a kerb edge split, a face ring re-walked) is a copy-on-write record in the overlay; an item of the frozen partitions the overlay deletes, re-levels or changes is tombstoned in a per-partition set the overlay keeps (the copy's own sets are empty), consumed by the district-end rebuild; a pooled stage changes only its district's L3 and L4 items.
Every district starts from the frozen base alone, never from another district's overlay, so its result is a pure function of the base, its allocation and its own sub-stream, whichever worker runs it.

Pool step 3 (scope check): a district's face set is its L1 faces and every face nested in them; its scope is every face of the set, every edge with a face of the set on both sides, every vertex whose incident faces all lie in the set, and — for a split only — every edge on the set's boundary whose other side no overlay writes (a water face, the arena's outer ring) with the vertex placed on it (so waterfront plot lines may end on their own bank). Any write (split, retype, role row, move, owner change) outside the scope returns E_SCOPE.

The L1 edges two overlays' face sets share are never written in the pool: a shared spine is flanked by corridors whose kerbs each side's lines end on (avenue and street-tree rows are Greenery.along records in the planting district's own half-corridor strips, not roles on the way); a shared wall trace gets its band, setback, glacis, tower and gatehouse parts from step (0) before the freeze; every other shared L1 edge without corridors (the settlement perimeter between districts and hinterland, §4.5; a reservation boundary two districts share) gets a margin band from the same step.

Margin band along the perimeter (it carries no way): S10 step (0) lays it, half-width 2 m on each side (a table value ≥ the residue class minimum width) — backland strip on the district side, headland on the hinterland side — so pooled districts and the hinterland unit never write their shared edge; a regeneration on either side re-lays its own side’s part; an edit that moves the perimeter or changes which face sets share an L1 edge without corridors (drawBoundary, merge/split, outskirtToDistrict, moved channel) re-lays it on both sides and removes it where sharing ends, via S6’s operator.

Hinterland unit = the hinterland pseudo-district’s S10 (furlongs, outside lots, driveways, trails, woods, edge orchards), S10b (outside classes, farm households), S11 (farmstead and outside site plans), S12b (ring supply, ambient scatter, shoreline band); runs on the generation worker while the pool runs districts, on its own overlay over the same frozen arena; its faces are the hinterland’s L2 blocks; merges in lineage order under the pseudo-district’s lineage; from freeze to merge no other writer touches the arena; on the single-worker fallback it runs first, then districts in lineage order.

Each overlay lists the base records it copied; at merge, two overlays that copied the same base record, or a copied base record the live arena changed after the freeze, fail the pool with E_SCOPE — defence in depth that a test asserts never fires.

Pool step 4 (merge): the generation worker applies overlays in district lineage order (§6.3): new records appended through a slot remap table (overlay-local slot → next free arena slot); copy-on-write base records replace their originals; references rewritten through the remap; only that district's faces re-walked to validate rings and parents. The district's L3 and L4 static partitions, built by the worker at district end from the base partition's live items and the overlay's new ones, travel with the overlay, have their item tables remapped and replace the base's partitions with empty tombstone sets (home column updated), so the merged arena needs no index rebuild; added and changed role-head and owner-head keys (kept in overlay tables consulted before the base's) are inserted through the remap; the district's digest leaves (§6.2) travel with it and the root is finalised once after the last overlay.
Merge cost is O(overlay size): the ≈ 200 000 records S10–S12b create at CITY merge within §12.4's 8 ms merge row.

Pool step 5 (pool size 0): the single-worker configuration runs the same overlay-and-merge path inside the generation worker, district by district in lineage order, so pool sizes 0–3 run the same code on the same inputs and give identical digests by construction; the golden suite's pool-size test (§6.5, §13.2) confirms it every run.

Spatial indexes (SCL-2, J-K6): each level has (a) static packed indexes (flatbush) partitioned — one partition per arena at L0–L1; at L2–L4 one per district plus one for everything outside districts (hinterland, margin) — each with a tombstone set; and (b) one dynamic uniform grid with O(1) insert and delete.
facts.values: partitions: per arena L0–L1; per district + 1 outside at L2–L4

facts.statement: Dynamic uniform grid cell sizes (table values).
facts.values: 25 m at L0–L1; 10 m at L2; 5 m at L3–L4

facts.statement: What each level's index holds (VK2-1, VK2-4, K4-1): the items of that level (current birth level) — its vertices; its route edges, each maximal run of that level's sub-edges between two vertices of that level or coarser being one item whatever finer vertices later split it, boxed by the vertices standing on the run when its level's batch writes the item, padded by the 0.71 cm hot pixel, with the handle the half-edge leaving its lower (y, x) endpoint (a split keeps that pair on the part at that end, so the handle never changes); and its face records.

A route-edge item's box holds every finer vertex on it by construction: one placed afterwards lies within the hot pixel of the route edge (§3.6 placement rule (i)); one placed before stands in the box however the route changed since (§2.2 rule 3; J-K32).

Route-box evidence (fixall_kernel_r4_checks.out A): the route edge's endpoints' box, padded alike, missed 38 of 400 753 finer vertices under the placement rule's non-nearest choices; the run's box missed none.

A finer batch that splits a coarser edge with a Steiner vertex writes only its own level's index, never a coarser one (S10's step (0) and every pooled stage touch only L3 and L4 indexes); a promotion or demotion — the coarser batch's own change of a route — moves the vertex or edge to its new level's index and rewrites the route-edge items of the levels whose routes it changes (a promoted vertex makes the route edge it splits two items; a demoted vertex joins its two items into one).

Query procedure: inside a stage every insertion and deletion goes to the grid; a level-n query reads the static partitions of levels ≤ n its box intersects and their grids, drops each static hit whose item key its partition has tombstoned, expands each route-edge hit into the pieces of its level-n route that meet the box, and returns the vertices of level ≤ n, each level-n route edge once (as its sub-edge leaving its lower endpoint) and the level-n faces.

Canonical query key read on the level-n route (VK-14, VK2-4): a vertex by its lattice position (y, then x); an edge by the positions of the two endpoints of its level-n route edge, lower (y, x) first, never by a sub-edge's endpoints; a face by the positions of the first two vertices of level ≤ n on its outer ring — the lowest-leftmost vertex of level ≤ n and the next vertex of level ≤ n counter-clockwise, finer vertices skipped, and where the ring visits that vertex twice the smaller of its two successors; in a mixed result vertices before edges before faces. The key is total (no two vertices share a lattice point; no two level-n route edges share both endpoints; a face's key is one directed level-n route edge, which bounds exactly one level-n face), so neither which structure holds an item nor whether a finer level has been derived changes any answer, and no implementation needs a slot to break a tie.
Face-key evidence (fixall_kernel_r3_checks.out C): the full-ring key reverses two L3 plots once S11 derives L4 in the block; the level-n route key orders them identically before and after.
facts.values: 2 plots reversed under the rejected key

facts.statement: Tombstones (VK-15, VK4-5): item keys kind · 2^32 + slot (kind = vertex, route edge or face), held in one set per static partition — the items deleted, moved to another level or changed since that partition's build; they filter that partition's hits only. New items (a reused slot's next occupant, an item's successor after promotion, demotion or change) live in the dynamic grid, which tombstones never filter, so neither reuse nor a level change can hide them and the stale static copy never answers.
places: §3.1 l.2149 (one set per partition) (restated, per KERNEL-166)

facts.statement: A partition's rebuild indexes the live items that belong to it — every item of its level in its arena at L0–L1; at L2–L4 the items of its district, a vertex on an L1 edge two partitions share going to the smaller key (as §3.9's chunks do) — sets their home entries, removes them from the grid and empties its tombstone set.
The home column costs 2 B per vertex, edge-pair and face slot (≈ 0.5 MB at a finished CITY; ≈ 0.2 MB at the one-click freeze) and lets a batch tombstone an item without searching partitions.

J-K34: Chose to tombstone every item a batch deletes, re-levels or changes — item keys in one set per static partition, found through a per-slot home column — and to insert its successor in the grid, over moving or rewriting items in place — because a packed partition cannot change an item, so a stale copy would answer until its partition happened to be rebuilt and answers would depend on rebuild timing; one …

facts.statement: Static partitions are rebuilt only when a stage ends — an eager stage once after its last batch; S10's eager step (0) once before the pool's freeze; a lazy or pooled per-district stage, the district's own partitions after that district's run — and, during an editing session, when a partition's grid overflow exceeds max(256, ¼ of its static size) (a count, never an idle timer); every pool freeze rebuilds the partitions an editing session left dirty.

facts.statement: flatbush rebuild cost (bench_index.out): 0.24 ms at 1 000 items, 2.3 ms at 8 000, 4.9 ms at 17 000; at CITY about one L3 and one L4 rebuild per stage (≈ 7 ms together) or ≈ 0.2–0.3 ms per district partition, versus 1.9 s (S10) and 13.4 s (S11) for a rebuild per block or per plot commit.
A single plot edit rebuilds at most its district's L3 and L4 partitions (≤ 1 000 items each, ≈ 0.5 ms) inside the 5 ms plot-edit budget.
Index work is fitted against commits × level size (§3.3).
Commit granularity is part of every stage's declaration (§4.1), so the ≈ 48 s hazard of per-insertion commits (and its per-batch twin) cannot arise.

S5 growth (S5a-S5d per stage) 40 ms: ≤ 8 µs per insertion incl. snap, attraction and re-walk (the first M0 measurement); stage 1's boundary and trace from S3; later stages' boundaries are level sets of the one travel-cost field computed at S3 (§4.4), re-settled incrementally where S5b's main roads lower it — no per-stage field; ≈ 5 000 proposals.

facts.statement: @plat/kernel's ops are the only writers of any arena; every write op takes the open KernelTx (declared or callback form) and charges its work count; writer level = tx.level, semantics §3.6.

insertChain(tx, points, roles: RoleRow[], cls: 'mandatory' | 'optional', opts?: { closed?; pinned?: number[]; knots?: { index; role; ordinal; entity? (default: the chain's own entity; another entity for a vertex role such as a bridge's deck_end or a gate's gate_end) }[] — every vertex role row the chain's own vertices take }) → KernelResult<ChainInsert>.

ChainInsert { placed: VertexId[] — one per input point, in input order: the vertex the point became after snapping, attraction and sharing; valid until the next commit (S11's first wing carry reads it, §2.6; NP3-1) }.

splitThrough(tx, at: HalfEdgeId, p, row?: RoleRow) → KernelResult<VertexId>: a vertex on an existing edge placed by §3.6's placement rule, a Steiner vertex when the edge is coarser; the optional row is a vertex role row the placed vertex takes (e.g. a cut end's anchor contact name); an anchor row without an ordinal takes the entity's smallest free anchor ordinal (from 2 on an enceinte), allocated as the op applies (VK4-6 (b)); any other indexed row must carry its ordinal (assertion otherwise).
facts.values: anchor ordinals from 2 on an enceinte

facts.statement: removeEdges(tx, ref: ChainRef | EdgeSetRef | StretchRef | VertexRef) → KernelResult<void>: strips (role, entity) from the ref's edges (a StretchRef's only, after cut knots at its ends) or, for a VertexRef, that vertex role row; deletes edges left with no role; re-levels by the rows and dissolves — demotes edges and vertices the rows no longer justify, and dissolves each degree-2 vertex left with the split flag, no vertex role, no pin and identical role sets and level on its two edges — so removing a lane that ended on a spine restores the spine exactly and removing the street a neighbour step served returns the plot-line end it promoted to its level.

clearFiner(tx, faces: FaceRef, level) → KernelResult<Conflict[]>: removes content finer than level inside the faces whose stage rank ≥ tx.rederivesFrom's — with tx.clearRegion declared, exactly the finer faces whose interior meets the region, whole; kept content stays silently; re-levels and dissolves as removeEdges does; locked or pinned owners are returned, not removed.

retypeEdges(tx, ref: ChainRef | EdgeSetRef | StretchRef, add: RoleRow[], remove: RoleName[], rekey?: { from; to; profiles? }) → KernelResult<{ profiles: { knotRole; from?; to }[] }>: the EVO conversion primitive (wall → way) on role sets; an added row coarser than an edge of the ref is E_LEVEL; remove re-levels as removeEdges does. rekey moves the ref's (role, from) rows, knot rows and vertex roles to to (for a StretchRef, the stretch's, its ends being the cut vertices), renumbering each entity's knots from 0 in chain order; where moved edges meet edges keeping from it first cuts each profile (cut knots), where they meet edges already carrying to it joins them; it returns both entities' new profiles (a scalar where a part has no knots left), which the caller writes into both records in the same edit.
setOwner(tx, faces: FaceId[], owner) → KernelResult<void>.
splitFace(tx, face, cut: Point[] — a bent cut is 2–3 vertices) → KernelResult<[FaceId, FaceId]>, children ordered left of the directed cut first.
connectHole(tx, face, cut) → KernelResult<FaceId>: outer ring → hole slit; same face count, one hole fewer.
mergeFaces(tx, a, b) → KernelResult<FaceId>: deletes shared partition edges only; a structural shared edge returns E_STRUCTURAL.
absorbSliver(tx, face, floor: { minWidthCm; minAreaCm2 }) → KernelResult<FaceId>; never deletes a structural edge.

claimSubFace(tx, claim: { ring } | { areaCm2; within: FaceRef | FaceId[] (as corridorUnion takes: S7b passes a district's coarse faces less its wall_strip faces, §4.5, VP2-3); score: RasterRef }, owner) → KernelResult<FaceRef>; may span several faces (a reservation crossing coarse faces, a precinct, a bailey).
radialSplit(tx, face, apex, raysCdeg: number[]) → KernelResult<FaceId[]>: a fan from a centroid or a vertex (groves, chapter houses).
ringBand(tx, face, widthCm) → KernelResult<{ band: FaceId[]; core: FaceId }>: an inner band around a court (cloister, quadrangle).
corridorUnion(tx, l1Faces: FaceRef | FaceId[]) → KernelResult<BandResult>: L2 half-corridor strips, junction wedges and built blocks for those L1 faces only; kept faces inside them are holes.

bandUnion(tx, chains: { ref; halfWidthCm: Cm | ChainProfile; ends: 'round' | 'square' }[], faces, edgeRole: 'kerb' | 'band', owner) → KernelResult<BandResult>: the axis chain splits the band per side; corners get corridor_split; a profile is sampled per segment end.

warp(tx, field: DisplacementField, fromLevel, region, recordCheck? (the edit layer's check of held point records (§7.4) and carried wings (§2.6); false fails the step's validation)) → KernelResult<MoveReport>: the edit layer computes the field from a WarpStroke or a moveVertex (§7.1), and the smoother from a smoothing pass; held vertices, slides, placement-rule re-seats, whole-step validation (§3.6); keeps nothing (§3.3).

pinVertices(tx, refs: VertexRef[]) → KernelResult<void>: sets the kernel pinned flag (smoothing, simplification and cutting keep the vertex; warp does not); the flag lasts while the vertex carries a vertex role row — the removal that strips its last one clears it (§2.2 rule 3; VK4-1).
Kernel services are read-only and return values, never arena slots that outlive a commit.

resolveVertexAt(key, at: LatticePoint, sig: VertexSig, carry: CarryMap (§6.3's supersedes table: old address → successor)) → { vertex } | { orphaned: true; nearest? }: a log position resolves to a vertex, never by distance alone (§2.2 rule 5).
signature(key, v: VertexRef | LatticePoint) → VertexSig: what an edit stores beside a position.
sampleProfile(p: ChainProfile, owner, key, atCm: Cm | 'perVertex') → number[] | string[]: a knot profile sampled by arc length along the owner's own-level route.
kerb(face: L1, committed or in the open overlay) → KernelResult<Ring[]>: face − ⋃ buffer(spineᵢ, half-widthᵢ), what corridorUnion commits; half-widths sampled from each way's width profile.
booleans(op: 'union' | 'intersection' | 'difference' | 'xor', a, b, fill: 'nonzero' | 'evenodd') → KernelResult<Ring[]>.
buffer(chains: Point[][], halfWidthCm: Cm | Cm[] (per input point of these transient chains), joins: 'round' | 'square' | 'miter', ends: 'round' | 'square' | 'flat') → KernelResult<Ring[]>.
offsetFace(face, perEdgeCm: Cm[]) → KernelResult<Ring[]> = face − ⋃ buffer(edgeᵢ, dᵢ); insetRing(face, dCm) → KernelResult<Ring[]>, uniform, half-plane path only for a face checked convex.
skeleton(rings, use: 'roof' | 'spine' | 'regions') → KernelResult<Skeleton>: validated output (arcs, nodes with offset times, the face of each input edge) or a typed downgrade.
simplify(chain, minSegmentCm, minAngleCdeg, obstacles, pinned) → KernelResult<Point[]>: topology-preserving; refuses a removal that would self-touch, cross an obstacle or move a pinned vertex.
hexLattice(region, spacingCm, jitterCm, rng: Stream) → { points; adjacency: Int32Array }: S4's routing lattice with adjacency by construction.

Geometry services: obb(ring), hull(points), lir(ring, axes), sideRuns(face, turnTolCdeg) → Run[] (maximal boundary runs with chord directions), sampleBoundary(face, stepCm), pointLocate(key, level, p), faceNeighbours(face, level), area2(ring), area2Big(ring), orient(a, b, c).
Each kernel op has documented preconditions, work local to the touched faces, a typed result, a declared operation count and fuzz tests with constructive degeneracies (§13.1).

Older pipeline names map directly: corridorUnion keeps its name and becomes the corridor use of bandUnion; claimSubFace may now span several faces; retypeEdges acts on role sets; bufferChain is buffer; edgeChainBetween is resolve(ChainRef); weld no longer exists (attraction); refine(level) is a stage, not a kernel op.

home.anchor: drop from the normative text; keep at most a one-line receipt pointer

facts.statement: sideRuns gives stages a side notion that survives curved, round-joined kerbs (maximal runs within a cumulative turning tolerance, each with its chord direction), which the bent cut needs (§4.6).

setOwner and retypeEdges are the calls §6.3's succession uses: when a re-derivation hands a carried address to a successor, the same batch re-owns the successor's faces and roles under that address, so geometry and address always move together.

buffer's per-point half-widths apply only to transient chains a caller passes (a stroke being previewed, a skeleton arc); a stored chain's varying width is always a ChainProfile, sampled by kerb and bandUnion.

A chain carrying a profile is inserted with its knots (opts.knots: chain index, knot role and ordinal of each knot vertex); a knot that attraction lands on an existing vertex is carried to that vertex, so the profile keeps its knot.

A chain cut into parts owned by different entities, a ring opened, or two chains joined go through retypeEdges' rekey, which inserts and drops cut knots by §2.2 rule 5 and returns the new profiles; the kernel renumbers each entity's knots in chain order itself (the former ordinalOffset argument is gone).

removeEdges gives each remaining part of a profiled chain a cut knot at the stretch's end on its side before the stretch's rows and interior knot rows leave, so every remaining sample is unchanged; rekey cuts at the two ends as at any cut vertex.

A removal that would leave a linear entity in more parts than it declares fails role consistency at commit (§3.10), so an operator cutting a way in two first hands the far part to a new entity with rekey on that part's StretchRef; a cut end not yet a vertex is placed first by splitThrough with the wanted vertex role row (an anchor contact name given without an ordinal, allocated by the kernel).

A stretch of a way removed between two junctions and a stretch of a ring removed between two anchors: the rest of each chain unchanged and every remaining profile sample within 10⁻⁹ cm; a removal leaving a way in two parts without a rekey is refused by role consistency.

Failure-class map (§3.5): collapsed / intersecting edges on concave shapes (MFCG) are answered by snap rounding + attraction + the clearance invariant, with cuts as splitFace transactions under stated contact semantics validated before commit.

cut() ≠ 2 crossings is E_NOT_TWO_CROSSINGS under exact contact rules (vertex grazes, overlaps and antennae defined; slits are connectHole); cut recursion is bounded by the class band and a depth cap; every rejection is logged.
Null OBB / rect crash class is closed by one OBB contract (collinear or < 3 distinct points → E_DEGENERATE, never zero extent), snap's range check in every build, and ratio() for computed divisors.
Exactly one vertex per lattice point; points within 26 cm of a vertex or edge are attracted onto it; near-coincident stretches are one shared edge with merged roles.

Hourglass / sliver footprints are closed by the invariant suite (simple faces, clearance, class floors in width and area), frontage-first construction, and sliver absorption that never deletes a street, wall or shore edge.
Self-intersecting user strokes: insertChain decimates to minEdge, splits self-touching input into simple runs and validates at the authoring boundary.

Step 8 transaction and ladder (GEO-23): reflex pre-cut before step 1 on faces with a reflex vertex deeper than the band’s plot depth (split perpendicular to the reflex vertex’s longer run; antennae split off at roots); splitFace as a transaction, reject if a child violates minEdge, min angle or class minimum block width; ladder (a) redraw f (≤ 2 more), (b) straight cut on the mean normal, (c) always-succeeding straight cut perpendicular to the longest run through its midpoint clipped to F’s component, (d) substitution — court, green or landmark block from the allocation’s pending claims — only for faces ≤ 2 × the band’s upper block area (larger faces reaching (d) cut by (c) again); no rung restarts anything above F.
Boolean thorns are closed because booleans and buffers are built on the kernel's own arrangement and obey the same attraction, minEdge and clearance as every chain, with no re-snap round trip.

Per-edge-buffer steps and poor concave shrinking are closed by one kerb function, face − ⋃ buffer(spineᵢ, half-widthᵢ), committed by corridorUnion; the half-plane inset only for uniform convex insets.
Skeleton glitches are closed by a stated numeric contract, exact OBB roofs for near-rectangles, a validator on every output and typed downgrades.
Identity-keyed, un-serialisable topology is replaced by indexed arenas, one arena per layer serialised once.
The allocation hot spot is answered by a struct-of-arrays kernel with allocation-free intersection and orientation routines, measured in M0.

Attraction candidates (GEO-3, VK-18, VK2-3, J-K2): insertChain processes each chain in the batch's order (canonical for declared sets, issue order for callback stages) in five steps; its candidates are (a) vertices and edges of level ≤ the batch's level; (b) finer vertices lying on those edges' routes where the chain ends on or joins such a route (a neighbour's plot-line end on the kerb where II.1 (3)'s neighbour step lands its corridor_split edge; a close-up's kept fabric beside a new junction); (c) in a clear-region batch, its prepared vertices (deck_end, gate_end, anchor contact names), each attracted and promoted like (b), their finer edges kept. Nothing finer is a candidate otherwise.

A clear-region batch never shares a finer edge (the preparation cut back every finer edge it would run along), so a carve's L0 channel passes through each kept way's two prepared bank vertices and the way's straight L1 edge between them is the Bridge's deck span without a second edge (J-I12).

A finer (b) or (c) vertex a chain vertex lands on, or a chain segment is routed through, is promoted to the batch's level (W_PROMOTED, in the commit record). A (c) promotion clears the split flag and strips an anchor contact name; a (b) promotion keeps the split flag (the vertex still lies on the edge it split), and removing the promoting chain later returns it to its level by demotion (J-K28).

Kept geometry is an obstacle: a chain that would cross it or come within attractCm of it elsewhere returns E_KEPT; inside a clear region a chain that would cross or come within attractCm of a finer vertex or edge other than its prepared contacts returns E_LEVEL, so a canal bank can never weld onto a plot corner within 26 cm.
A chain is inserted run by run; the part already inserted counts as existing geometry for its later parts, so a chain that doubles back attracts onto itself.

insertChain step 1 (snap and decimate): every point passes snap; consecutive points closer than minEdge are decimated — the later dropped unless pinned or a knot; two pinned or knot points closer than minEdge merge at the first, reported, and a merged knot vertex carries both ordinals (a step in its profile); a chain touching or crossing itself is split into simple runs.

insertChain step 2 (vertex attraction): a chain vertex within attractCm of an existing vertex moves onto it (nearest; ties to the smaller lattice position, y then x); otherwise, within attractCm of an existing edge (nearest; ties by canonical keys), take the exact foot: if the foot lies within attractCm of one of the edge's endpoints the vertex moves onto that endpoint (nearer; ties y then x), otherwise onto the edge at the foot's placement point by splitThrough (a Steiner vertex if the edge is coarser). Chain vertices brought within minEdge of each other merge, later into earlier.

Worked case / fixture: a vertex at (20, 20) beside edge (0, 0)–(1 000, 0) is 28.3 cm from (0, 0) (not vertex-attracted) and 20 cm from the edge; its foot (20, 0) lies 20 cm from (0, 0), so it moves onto (0, 0) instead of splitting off a 20 cm edge.
Incoming vertex displacement bound: at most √2 · attractCm ≈ 36.8 cm (or the step-4 corner bound at an acute tip).

insertChain step 3 (segment and stretch attraction): a segment passing within attractCm of an existing vertex is routed through it; where a segment runs within attractCm of an existing edge over a stretch (a near-parallel approach, or a crossing shallower than minFaceAngle) the stretch is shared — the chain joins, follows and leaves the edge, and the shared edges gain the chain's roles (W_STRETCH_SHARED); a join or leave point within attractCm of an endpoint moves onto it; any other is placed by the placement rule; a stretch whose join and leave points would lie closer than minEdge collapses to one contact point handled by step 2.

insertChain step 4 (crossings): remaining crossings are computed exactly, placed by the placement rule and resolved by iterated snap rounding (≤ 3 passes; each pass planar, so an unconverged result commits with W_SNAP_PASSES; sub-centimetre Steiner re-routes are snap-rounding re-routes with the same guarantee).

Wedge routing: two consecutive crossings closer than minEdge lie on the two arms of an acute corner (the clearance invariant forbids anything else) and are resolved at that corner (W_WEDGE_ROUTED): if the corner is the existing arrangement's, the chain is routed through the corner's vertex; if it is the chain's own, the chain's corner vertex moves onto the edge at the placement point of its foot. The chain moves at most minEdge / (2 tan(θ/2)) — 0.47 m at the 30° junction floor, 1.2 m at the 12° plot floor; an optional chain that would move more than attractCm this way is rejected (E_BELOW_MIN_EDGE).

Placement rule (GEO-3, GEO-35, J-K17): every new vertex on an existing edge (split foot, stretch join or leave point, crossing) is placed at the lattice point nearest its exact position among points that (i) lie within 0.71 cm of the existing edge's route at the edge's own level (one index item), so that edge moves no more than its hot pixel; (ii) lie at least minEdge from the endpoints of the edge being split and, for a crossing, of the crossing segment; (iii) keep every vertex and edge around the split at least minEdge from the new vertex and every edge incident to it (clearance, checked in the index); ties y then x. The search runs outward, never beyond attractCm, charging each candidate to the work count. Snap rounding is the same rule for points on no existing edge (nearest lattice point).
facts.values: hot pixel 0.71 cm; search radius ≤ attractCm

facts.statement: The nearest lattice point fails the placement rule only where a vertex already stands between minEdge and minEdge + 0.71 cm from the edge; a qualifying point then lies a few centimetres (≈ 5 cm) along the edge's hot-pixel band.

Placement evidence (fixall_kernel_r2_attract.out C): 200 000 crossings next to a vertex 25–26 cm from the crossed edge — plain nearest-point rounding leaves 1 361 edges shorter than minEdge; the placement rule leaves none, moves a crossing at most 0.84 cm and keeps it within 0.71 cm of the crossed edge.

If no placement candidate qualifies, the incoming vertex moves onto the nearer endpoint of the edge (a crossing routes its segment through that endpoint), the new segments re-enter step 3, and the step reports W_PLACED; each such re-route lands on an existing vertex, so the loop ends within the work limit.

Existing geometry wins: an incoming chain vertex moves at most √2 · attractCm (or the step-4 corner bound); no existing vertex moves (on insertion); an existing edge moves only by its hot pixel (≤ 0.71 cm) where a vertex is placed on it.

No edge shorter than minEdge can be created: every edge a batch creates is (a) a chain segment between consecutive chain vertices (decimation and merge), (b) a sub-edge of a split edge (placement rule (ii)), (c) a chain segment ending at a split point or crossing ((ii) and the merge rule), or (d) the span between two crossings (resolved at the acute corner, step 4); clearance holds by steps 2–3 for every new vertex and segment and by (iii) for every placed vertex.

Attraction evidence (fixall_kernel_r2_attract.out A–B): 400 000 vertices dropped in the attraction band of random lattice edges → 0 sub-edges shorter than minEdge (shortest 25.50 cm; 5 729 moved onto an endpoint; largest displacement 36.72 cm); first-written rule left one in 1.34 % (history). Re-run of cut endpoints on Chaikin×2 spines with 7.9 m median segments: 6.38 % attracted, displaced p50 12.9 cm and at most 26 cm, shortest resulting edge 25.6 cm. The replaced 5 cm weld rejected the rest, so ≈ 5 % of endpoints and ≈ 10 % of two-ended cuts fell to the ladder (history, GEO-3).

Attraction/move/kept-content fixtures (GEO-3, GEO-5, GEO-35, VK-1–VK-18): vertex at (20, 20) against edge (0, 0)–(1 000, 0) moves onto (0, 0) with no sub-minEdge edge; a chain crossing an edge next to a vertex 25.0–25.7 cm from it; a stretch whose join lies within attractCm of an edge endpoint; warp with fromLevel = 1 over a street ending on a shore (junction slides, step commits); a pinch shortening an edge below minEdge and a step putting two vertices on one lattice point (both halve); a 20 × 10 m rectangle with a 3 × 2 m notch (skeleton path, no roof line outside); star rings of radius 2²³ − 2 (area2 exact); an L1 lane into a face holding kept L3 content of an earlier stage (E_KEPT).

Chain classes: mandatory chains (coast, shore, bank, river, wall trace, arterial, band and kerb edges, plot lines, user-drawn geometry) cannot fail for a precision reason — after attraction and placement the only errors left are E_OUT_OF_RANGE (caller bug), E_LEVEL, E_KEPT (wrong stage domain in generation, edit conflict in the dry run) and E_LOCKED (edit conflict) — and a corner below minFaceAngle commits with W_ACUTE_CORNER.

Optional chains (growth proposals, optional lanes, decorative lines) are also rejected with E_BELOW_MIN_ANGLE, E_BELOW_MIN_EDGE (collapse below one edge) or E_SELF_INTERSECT where the role requires a simple ring; a proposal that cannot be inserted is not a street. The F-NUM ladder of §5.2 applies to optional chains only; mandatory chains never reach it.

Clearance invariant: after every commit, every vertex lies at least minEdge from every edge outside its one-ring (the edges incident to it or to its neighbours); acute corners inside the one-ring are governed by minFaceAngle and the class floors; attraction and the placement rule maintain it for insertions and warp checks it for moves; it is a hard, batch-local invariant.
A setback smaller than minEdge collapses to zero (a front drawn 10 cm behind the kerb lands on the kerb), so a stage wanting a visible setback draws at least minEdge (§4.7).

Roles on shared stretches (GEO-4): when a chain shares an edge (stretch attraction or exact collinear overlap), the edge's role set gains the chain's (role, entity, level) row — never a duplicate edge, never an overwrite (a wall pulled onto a bank carries bank and wall; a quay on a shore carries shore and way).

absorbSliver: a face below its class floor (width or area, never minEdge) merges into the neighbour across its longest shared boundary whose edges carry only partition roles; if every candidate boundary carries a structural role, no edge is deleted and the sliver stays as a face of kind residue owned by the neighbour across its longest boundary (W_SLIVER_RETYPED); a street, wall, shore or border never loses a stretch to sliver repair; mergeFaces across a structural edge returns E_STRUCTURAL.

splitFace contact semantics (GEO-6): a cut is a polyline whose interior lies in the face's open interior and which touches the boundary exactly at its two endpoints, decided by exact orient2d on lattice points, never a parameter-space epsilon. (1) Each endpoint is a boundary vertex or a point on a boundary edge inserted by splitThrough; an endpoint within attractCm of a boundary vertex, or whose foot lies within attractCm of an edge endpoint, lands on that vertex.

splitFace (2): any other contact is E_NOT_TWO_CROSSINGS — passing through or within attractCm of a boundary vertex, grazing a reflex vertex, running within attractCm of a boundary edge anywhere but where it arrives at an endpoint, overlapping a boundary edge, or crossing the boundary more than twice; splitFace never lets attraction bend a cut into a pinch; the stage's ladder picks another cut (§4.6).
splitFace (3): an antenna (a dangling chain inside the face — cul-de-sac spine, dead-end lane) counts as boundary: a cut may end on it (a declared T-junction) and may not cross it.

splitFace (4): a cut from the outer ring to a hole does not split the face; it is connectHole(face, cut), post-condition same face count and one hole fewer (the slit of §4.6); a violation is E_HOLE_CONTACT.

splitFace (5): the two children are returned in canonical order, the face left of the directed cut first, so an anchor exactly on the cut belongs to the left child (the anchor rule's tie-break, §6.3).
splitFace (6): a face's exported area boundary omits its antennae, so a GeoJSON ring never retraces a slit.

Moves (GEO-10, GEO-35, VK-7, GEO-5 (c), VK2-5–VK2-7): warp(field, fromLevel, region) applies a displacement field to every vertex of level ≥ fromLevel inside the region; shared boundaries are single vertices, so streets, blocks, plots and footprints under a brush move together; vertices of level < fromLevel stay fixed (a street warp does not move the coast unless fromLevel = 0). Smoothing of committed geometry is a warp whose field the smoother computes, under the same rules.

A move batch keeps nothing: E_KEPT governs insertion and clearing only; what a move may not displace is decided by the held set and what it may not break by whole-step validation; its rederivesFrom is the first stage of §4.1's order (J-K33).

Held vertices (GEO-5 (c), VK2-7 (b)): before the step the kernel computes the held set — (1) every vertex of the geometry a locked or pinned entity's references resolve to (§7.2): the level-n route vertices of every ring of its FaceRef faces (outer rings and holes), of its ChainRef and EdgeSetRef edges, its VertexRef vertices, and of every finer face nested in its faces; (2) closed downwards by level: both endpoints of every coarser edge carrying a held Steiner vertex are held too; each round adds a strictly coarser level, so the closure ends within four rounds. The field is zero at every held vertex; the dry run lists the held entities.

A bridge's deck_end vertices and a water gate's gate_end vertices are held unless fromLevel = 0 (the crossing is fixed across the water — a deck perpendicular to the flow, a water gate's wall edge bank to bank), whatever level its bank vertices have (L0 for a deck and an edited water gate; L1 Steiner vertices on the shores for a generated gate) (VK4-4, J-K35); with fromLevel = 0 the banks and the crossing move together.

Slides (VK-7, VK2-6, J-K18): a route is fixed when its edge is of level < fromLevel or both its endpoints are held; a vertex of level ≥ fromLevel on a fixed route that is not held (a street ending on a shore, a bridgehead, a riverside junction; a neighbour's footprint corner on a locked plot's line) moves only along that route — its displacement projected onto the route's direction, the projected point kept ≥ attractCm from the route's endpoints and every held vertex on it, and the vertex seated at the lattice point the placement rule chooses ((i) within 0.71 cm of the route, (ii) ≥ minEdge from the route edge's endpoints and its neighbours on the route, (iii) clearance), never the plain nearest lattice point.
warp { key: PlatKey; fromLevel 0 or 1 (1 by default; 0 also moves water and coast); strokes: WarpStroke[] } - one staged warp session committed on Apply
Slide fixture (§13.1): a warp with fromLevel = 1 over a street that ends on a shore moves the junction along the shore and commits.

Re-seats (VK2-6): each Steiner vertex on a moved coarser edge is re-seated at the lattice point the placement rule chooses for its projection onto the moved route, with (i)–(iii) read on the moved geometry (J-K17); where no lattice point within attractCm of the projection qualifies, the step fails validation and halves.

Re-seat evidence (fixall_kernel_r3_checks.out A): over 200 000 re-seats beside a vertex 25.0–25.7 cm from the route, plain nearest rounding breaks minEdge or clearance in 12.9 % and the placement rule in none, moving the vertex at most 4.3 cm along the route and within 0.71 cm of it; constructive case — a kerb warped to (0, 0)–(1 000, 9) past a vertex at (517, 30), 25.35 cm away, with a plot-line end re-seated at that vertex's foot: plain rounding lands 24.999 cm away and fails, the placement rule 25.999 cm and commits.

Order within a step (VK3-4, J-K30): re-seats and slides are placed one at a time in canonical order by each vertex's lattice position before the step (y, then x), each reading already-placed vertices at their placed points and every other moved vertex at its rounded target (for a re-seat or slide, the nearest lattice point to its projected point); whole-step validation then checks the result; the order depends on positions alone, never on slots.

Step-order evidence (fixall_kernel_r4_checks.out B): two Steiner vertices re-seated onto one warped route with projections 25.0–26.5 cm apart get different points under the two orders in 6.8 % of pairs.

Whole-step validation (GEO-10, GEO-35): each target is rounded to the lattice (re-seats and slides by the placement rule, in canonical order) and the whole step is validated — every edge incident to a moved vertex (including edges between two moved vertices and edges at re-seated or sliding Steiner vertices) is at least minEdge long and tested against the index for crossings; every unmoved vertex is tested against the triangles swept by the moved edges; no two vertices on one lattice point; no held vertex moved; the clearance invariant holds; and the edit layer's recordCheck passes (every held point record inside its host face at its clearance, §7.4; every building whose footprint moves valid under §2.6's wing-carrying rule, decided by §2.6 rule 4's tiered test after the kernel's own checks pass, stopping at the first failing building in address order; NP4-2, NP4-6).
On whole-step validation failure the step's strength is halved globally — deterministic, at most 8 halvings, after which the step is a reported no-op.

facts.statement: One geometry engine (GEO-9, DEF-2, J-K4): booleans, buffers, per-edge insets and bands are built on the kernel's own arrangement (insertChain's machinery on a scratch overlay) and no second geometry engine ships; on every host the same TypeScript code produces the same integers.

Boolean algorithm: overlay both operands' rings, label every face with its winding numbers (a breadth-first walk from the unbounded face adding each crossed edge's ring orientation), keep the faces the operation and fill rule select, and remove the edges separating two kept faces.

Buffer construction: union of per-segment strips and per-vertex join discs; round joins as chords of at most 2 cm sagitta (about 27 chords per full circle at a 3 m radius); square ends where declared (gates, bridgeheads); a half-width varying along a stored chain is sampled from its knot profile at each segment's two ends and the strip is the trapezoid between them. The output is produced by the same insertion rules as every chain (attraction, placement, minEdge, clearance; GEO-35) with no re-snap round trip.

The kerb, defined once (GEO-20): for an L1 face F, kerb(F) = F − ⋃ buffer(spineᵢ, half-widthᵢ) over F's bounding spines, each half-width sampled from its way's width profile, round joins on the union's convex side and square ends where declared; the union's concave corners (block corners at junctions) are sharp by construction.

corridorUnion commits exactly the kerb geometry at L2: kerb rings as kerb edges; the spine (already L1) splits the band into two half-corridor strips; a corridor_split edge from each junction vertex to the kerb corner separates the junction wedge; on a side where the spine passes straight through a junction vertex (a T-junction whose street arrives from the other side) there is no kerb corner and no wedge — one corridor_split edge from the vertex to the foot of its perpendicular on that side's kerb separates the half-corridor strips of the spine's two sub-edges (the edge II.1 (3)'s neighbour step inserts alone into a finished neighbour's strip, VK2-11); faces outside the band are the built blocks.

Finer faces an earlier stage made inside F are kept: each must lie wholly inside one resulting L2 face, and a kerb or corridor_split edge that would cross one or come within attractCm of it returns E_KEPT; the one-click order leaves none inside the faces S9 bands (wall band, setback and glacis parts are built after S9 in their own L1 strip faces; a strip ends at the corridor of the way through each gate, so every gate passage stays open).

kerb is also a read-only service on faces of an open transaction's overlay: S8 plans every cut on kerb(F) of the current L1 faces, inserts each accepted lane at L1 in its own district transaction and recurses on the children's kerbs; S9 then commits corridorUnion for those L1 faces with the same function on the same inputs, so the block S8 cut and the block S9 keeps are one face.

corridorUnion takes a set of L1 faces and re-derives only those, which is also how an edit re-derives the corridors around a changed street.

Oracles, not fallbacks (VK-4, J-K19): Clipper2 (compiled to WebAssembly, run in Node) and polygon-clipping are dev dependencies of @plat/testkit only; no product bundle ever loads either; there is no runtime fallback, so no host produces a different model hash and no fallback path needs a budget (SCL-22).

Differential agreement with the CI oracles (Clipper2-WASM in Node, polygon-clipping) on booleans and buffers, split by attraction (§3.7): unattracted cases with equal face counts and symmetric difference ≤ perimeter × 1 cm; attracted cases valid and within perimeter × √2 · attractCm; ≥ 10⁵ unattracted cases per operation.

The skeleton never writes an arena: roof ridges and hips are derived per building and cached by (entity, content revision, roof construction), never by id alone (§8.1 (5), LC-23, N-19), so a setAttr on floors or a re-fitted footprint changes the roof; label spines are derived per face (§9); a skeleton failure can degrade a roof or a label, never the plat.

facts.statement: A stage that wants skeleton-derived topology (e.g. per-frontage regions of a block, §4.7) inserts the validated arcs through insertChain like any other chain, and its downgrade is the stage's own exact construction.

Skeleton numeric contract (GEO-8): event times are computed in doubles with + − × ÷ √ only (no transcendental; identical on every IEEE engine) on coordinates relative to the polygon's bounding-box corner, because exact rational event times are impossible (edges move at unit speed, so times involve √(dx² + dy²)).

Skeleton events closer than 1 mm in offset time and 1 cm in position coalesce into one multi-edge event; ties are broken by the input vertex's index in the ring, canonicalised to start at its lowest-leftmost vertex.
Skeleton work limit: 4 · (n + r) + 64 events for n vertices and r reflex vertices (a correct run needs at most about n + r); exceeding it is E_WORK_LIMIT, a count, never a timeout.

facts.statement: Snapping evidence (GEO-8): after snapping, only 33 % of rotated squares keep a single apex, which is why near-rectangles take the exact OBB path.

OBB roof constructions: a hip roof's ridge ends half the OBB's minor extent in from each short side, with hips from the four matched vertices to the ridge ends; a gable roof's ridge ends where the ridge line meets the footprint's own boundary; a pyramid's apex is the OBB's centre. Every roof line then lies inside the footprint (endpoints inside; a segment between two points of a convex polygon lies inside it), so crossing hip lines (VIS-11) cannot occur.

facts.statement: Notch counter-example (fixall_kernel_r2_attract.out D): a 20 × 10 m rectangle with a 3 × 2 m notch at x = 1–4 m on a long side (area 0.970 of its OBB, four corners present) has a reflex vertex, so it takes the skeleton; under the old test its hip from (0, 0) to ridge end (5, 5) passed through (1.5, 1.5), outside the footprint.

Roofs are taken wing by wing by BaseWing.kind (§2.6, NF-P2): rect wings (rectangles, L / T compositions) are convex and take the exact path; a quad wing (a row house cut to a curved frontage) takes the exact path when it passes the convex near-rectangle test and the validated skeleton (with plain-roof downgrade) otherwise; a quad's gable construction draws the stored ridge — the segment between the arc-length midpoints of the two side chains its ridgeAxis names, sides delimited by BaseWing.corners; no path asserts a party-wall side is straight, so a quad whose bent side fails the test takes the skeleton (VP2-5); polygon wings keep the pyramid, cone and dome constructions.
The skeleton serves quad wings that fail the near-rectangle test, irregular or notched outlines (institution shapes), label spines and stage-3 irregular wings.

facts.statement: Snapshot vertices: live vertices in slot order (slots compacted on save — renumbering is free because nothing outside the kernel stores a slot and no output depends on slots), coordinates as delta + zig-zag varint Int32 pairs, with current birth levels (after promotion or demotion) and flags.
Snapshot edges: one (origin, destination, birth level) triple per edge pair, the level the current one (lowest among the edge's rows); next, prev and twins are not stored.

Snapshot roles: (edge or vertex, role, entity, level, ordinal) rows, entities as document ids — knot, attach, anchor, weld, deck-end, gate-end and gate-opening rows included — so every entity-held vertex and chain profile survives the round trip without a stored position; an edit's anchor contact names never reach a snapshot (the promoting batch strips them).

Snapshot faces: per level, one (boundary half-edge, owner, kind, stage rank) row per face; parents are not stored; the stage rank is persisted because the kept-content rule must decide the same way after a reload.

Chunk load order: the kernel inserts the level-≤ 1 routes, then each partition chunk in partition-key order — its splits first, sorted along each coarser edge by position, then its vertices and edges — resolving lattice-point references through the one-vertex-per-lattice-point index; the rebuild then yields the same arena and per-level digests (they read routes, not slots), and save → load → save holds chunk by chunk.

On load the kernel rebuilds next / prev by sorting each vertex's outgoing edges by exact angle (quadrant, then orient2d), re-walks faces level by level, recovers each face's parent from its boundary edges, and rebuilds the role reverse index and the static index partitions: O(E log d), deterministic.

Pre-decided fallback for §2.9's open-to-editable bar: each L2–L4 static index partition is rebuilt at the first query that reads it instead of at load — output-neutral because every query result is sorted by canonical key.
Kernel round-trip test: save → load → save is byte-identical and the loaded arena passes every hard invariant (§3.10).

Two added snapshot columns — a 2-byte ordinal per role row and a 1-byte stage rank per face — are ≈ 0.45 MB raw at CITY, mostly zero ordinals and repeated ranks that compression removes; the document-size test (§2.9: ≤ 320 B per building at CITY) measures the result at M1.
