facts.statement: Invariant: every coordinate is a lattice point inside the range invariant — hard, at snap, by construction.

Invariant: no edge shorter than minEdge, whichever writer made or moved it (insertion, boolean, buffer, offset, smoothing, warp) — hard, batch-local, on the commit record's new edges and moved edges (every edge incident to a vertex in moved, Steiner re-seats and slides included).
Invariant: clearance — every vertex ≥ minEdge from every edge outside its one-ring — hard, batch-local, new, placed and moved vertices and their incident edges against the index.
Invariant: one vertex per lattice point — hard, batch-local; by construction for insertions (coincidence is attraction); moved vertices against the index for a warp or smoothing step.
Invariant: faces simple except declared antennae; no two edges cross — hard, batch-local, touched faces.

Invariant: placement bound — every vertex a batch places, re-seats or slides onto a coarser edge lies within 0.71 cm of that edge's route at the edge's own level when placed; a later same-level change of the route (split, promotion, demotion, dissolution) moves no finer vertex, and the index items it rewrites box the finer vertices where they stand (K4-1) — hard, batch-local, the placed, re-seated and sliding vertices.
Invariant: held vertices — no vertex of a warp or smoothing step's held set moved — hard, batch-local, commit record's moved list against the held set.

Invariant: prepared contacts — a clear-region batch met finer geometry only at its KernelTx.prepared vertices, promoted exactly those, stripped their anchor contact names, and shared no finer edge — hard, batch-local, the promoted list against the resolved prepared set and new edges' birth levels.

Invariant: kept content — no finer face made by a stage before the batch's rederivesFrom (nor, in a clear-region batch, any finer face outside the region) was cleared, crossed, split or re-owned (moves keep nothing) — hard, batch-local, stage ranks and region test of the removed and changed finer faces.

Invariant: role consistency — every role the registry declares linear (way, wall, shore, tunnel …) forms, per entity, the connected simple chains or rings the entity declares; no structural role is lost by an absorption or merge — hard, batch-local, the commit record's role keys.

Invariant: every stored reference resolves — each FaceRef, ChainRef, EdgeSetRef, VertexRef of a live entity finds geometry; every indexed role (attach, anchor, weld, deck end, gate end, gate opening) finds exactly one vertex or edge set per ordinal; every ChainProfile's knots lie on its chain in ordinal order with at least one knot per ring; no geometry carries a dead entity — hard, at stage end and save, via the reverse indexes.
places: §3.3 M3a (roles unique per ordinal) (restated, per KERNEL-379)

facts.statement: Invariant: frozen base complete — at every pool freeze, after the freeze has rebuilt each static partition whose grid or tombstone set was not empty, every level's dynamic grid and every partition's tombstone set is empty (VK3-5) — hard, at the freeze at every pool size, two counts per level, O(levels).

Invariant: index levels and freshness — a batch wrote no index of a level coarser than its own except its promotions and demotions, and left no static item of what it deleted, re-levelled or changed unfiltered (each tombstoned in the partition its home entry named, successor in the grid of its current level; VK4-5) — hard, batch-local, index writes against level and promoted/demoted lists, each changed item with a static copy found in its partition's tombstone set (in a pool worker, the overlay's set).

Invariant: pool scope — no district overlay wrote outside its district's face set; no two overlays, and no concurrent eager write, touched one base record — hard, at the pool merge, overlays' copied-record lists against each other and the live arena's changes since the freeze.
Invariant: face corners ≥ minFaceAngle — soft for mandatory chains (W_ACUTE_CORNER), hard for optional chains; batch-local, touched corners.
Invariant: Euler characteristic per level (V − E + F = 1 + components) — hard, in CI (B-FUZZ, B-EDIT), whole arena.

The §3.10 rows are the kernel's part of the §5.3 suite. Batch-local checks read only the commit record's faces, its moved, promoted and demoted vertices, its changed and demoted edges and their one-ring, so a batch costs O(touched), never O(model) (SCL-1); whole-arena checks run at stage end, at save or in CI; the freeze check runs once per freeze and the pool check once per merge in O(overlay size).
Class floors (minimum width, area and angle per face class) are the stages' invariants and are always stated in width and area, never in minEdge (GEO-35).

Stage order: ground and water first, demand second, arterials between real places, side streets grown, districts typed before lanes are cut, wall traced from the stage it encloses, then blocks, plots, owners, buildings, fields, greenery, names; every stage can also run on part of an existing town.

Stage graph: S0 Blueprint → S1 Site → S2 Programme → S3 Siting/reservations/stage-1 boundary+trace → S4 Backbone → S5 stage k=1…K (S5a boundary+trace+gates, S5b main-road step, S5c secondary growth, S5d capacity check) → S6 districts/quarters/field pass 1 → S7 wall strips + fortification lines → S7b allocation + district claims → S12a hinterland siting → S8 infill per district → S9 corridors (L2) → S10a block allocation + field pass 2 → S10 step (0) shared-edge bands → per district in pool (hinterland unit on generation worker) S10 → S10b → S11 → S12b → S13a names + label candidates → S14 display list → S15 simulation (optional); S13b label placement is view data per zoom stop, never in the model.

Stage registration declares {inputs, outputs, streamKeys, invariants with their scopes, ladder, work-limit laws (operation counts over the batch scope population-derived counts), budgetMs per rung (reporting only), batch scope, lineageUnit, op form}.

Op form per stage: callback for S5c, S8, S10 (ops read faces earlier ops made); declared for S3, S4, S5a, S5b, S7, S9, S11 and an edit’s inserted feature; every other stage (S6, S7b, S12b, the hinterland unit’s stages) registers as callback.

The pipeline is the DAG induced by declared I/O, topologically sorted with stage id as deterministic tie-break; base registrations yield exactly the drawn order; a cycle is a registration error caught at load.
A later product may register a stage the base lacks (village density stage before its network, palisade before roads) without editing the pipeline.
Each growth stage k runs S5a–S5d in order; the same S5 runs incrementally for an epoch.

Order rationale — water before roads including every carved water body: harbour basins, canals, the castle and city moats and the hinterland decoration ponds are carved into L0 at S3 with the decks their crossings need; only an outer enceinte’s moat is carved later, by S5a through §4.11’s carve path, before that stage’s secondaries grow.
Programme before layout: buildings and people decided before geometry (demand side); geometry answers with capacity.

Large claims before streets: castle bailey, main plazas, market, church precincts and large institutions are reservations inserted as L1 barrier faces at S3 before S4 commits any way; district-level claims larger than one block are cut out at S7b before S8.

Walls before the streets they enclose: first enceinte is one construction at S3 (gate routes solved, boundary = travel-cost level set, gates where routes cross, castle weld and moat on the trace); each later stage’s boundary and trace fixed in S5a, gates first, before secondaries grow, so a secondary never crosses a wall except at a gate.

Further order constraints: districts and field pass 1 before infill (infill block band is the district class’s, J-2); S7 before S8 (no lane through a wall band or setback); S12a before S10b (outside sites exist for farms, mills, quarries); greenery after site plans.

Laziness contract (LC-2): a stage may run lazily for scope X only if its output for X is a pure function of eager upstream state and X’s own sub-streams, it reads no other scope’s lazy output, and it writes nothing outside X.
Eager, town-wide content: S2 roster, S3 reservations, S6 field bands, S7b and S10a allocations, S12a hinterland siting, S10 shared-edge step (0).

Per-district stages S10, S10b, S11, S12b (every district and the hinterland unit) may run lazily or in the pool, read only eager records and their own sub-stream, and write only inside their own faces; S12b plants avenue and street-tree rows only in its own half-corridor strips; an edge orchard is a hinterland allocation row built by the hinterland unit, never by a district.

S8 is eager: runs in the generation worker, district by district in lineage order; its only writes outside a district’s faces are lane-end vertices on a bounding spine, each recorded as a baseLane portal in the shared Seam record.
The F-CUT substitution rung reads the district’s allocation, never live roster state.

S13a draws a name only in four cases: (1) entity with no predecessor, town salt; (2) every unedited name under a town-wide rerollLayer(naming), new town salt; (3) entities an ids-scoped rerollLayer lists (§7.1), each with its per-entity salt; (4) an unedited generated name whose naming inputs changed, with the salt its record holds
View (S13b; never hashed; recomputed per zoom stop and cached, §9.2): which candidate each label uses, its size and glyph positions, the quarter cut, the halo roles.

One-click first paint is the complete city LOD: generate({seed}) runs S0–S13a eagerly for every district and the hinterland at city-band detail (every footprint with wings and heights, every quarter and district label candidate, hinterland fields, greenery faces); S14 with S13b builds the city band’s first frame.

Laziness is restricted to what the city band does not draw: yard sub-part detail at district LOD, entrance glyphs, roof constructions and hatching, way names and addresses, pins below the city band, tree instances and crowns, stage-2 close-up detail, stage-3 compositions.

Declared for the owner's veto: the first map is < 1 s for every TOWN and CITY request (band tops 246 and 589 ms) and METROPOLIS up to ≈ 14 200 buildings (≈ 48 000 people); the default METROPOLIS request lands at 0.86-1.05 s; above the knee it grows 62 µs per building to ≈ 2.3 s at the 35 000-building cap; chose to keep the one-click path complete at every size (every plot, site plan and building at city-band detail, no preview; J-R7, J-I2) over holding 1 s above the knee (linear model cost; only a partial picture — MFP-1 — or dropping plot detail, forbidden by the owner's plot-model ruling, would get under); reversal ≈ 1 person-week (city band district by district as the pool finishes, labels last); single-worker knee ≈ 11 400 buildings (≈ 39 000 people).

Eager model: everything the city LOD draws plus the town-level Allocation and FieldBands records; lazily derived content (close-ups, people, stage-3 compositions) is outside it until an edit materialises it

Determinism CI - derived-complete digest: every district's S10, S10b, S11 and S12b and the hinterland unit's (S12b named explicitly, NF-P3) derived for 50 METROPOLIS seeds in three random orders with pool sizes 0-3 give identical digests (laziness contract §4.1; §6.2)

facts.statement: Batch table S1: L0 — first the arena outer ring (frame + context margin, one closed chain with the structural margin role on the arena Terrain entity), then water faces, shores, banks (sea or river reaching the arena edge shares that ring), islets, and every crossing site’s two pinned deck_end bank vertices (Bridge state site).

Batch table S3: L0 — harbour basins, canals, castle moat, city moat, decoration ponds, deck bank vertices of every channel it carves; then L1 — the map border (frame rectangle, one closed chain with structural border role on the arena Terrain entity, laid across land and water, no L0 edge added) and land reservations as barrier faces (plazas, precinct, market, castle bailey) as independent ops of one declared batch.

Batch table S4: L0 only when F-ROUTE’s “one bridge at extra cost” rung fires on standing water (two deck_end vertices by two same-level shore splits, nothing cleared; inside S1’s water operator or a carve the rung only sites the deck); then L1 — arterial spines inserted once, each span laid through the deck ends its route uses (those bridges become built).

Batch table S5 per stage k: k=1 — S5a L1 S3’s trace with gate vertices; k≥2 — S5b L1 main roads, S5a L1 trace with every arterial crossing as a gate, then outer-moat carve batches (L1 crossings as straight edges between two deck bank vertices; L0 channel with those vertices as KernelTx.prepared); every k — S5c L1 growth, then L1 between-stage prune and trim; S5d top-up re-runs S5a’s arc and S5c on the rim, each L1.
Batch table S6: L1 settlement perimeter chain, then district owners and district_bound roles (one batch).
Batch table S7 per enceinte: L1 setback and glacis lines (wall strips), intervallum, gate-plaza claims, castle paths and inner-ward trace, quays, piers and moles.
Batch table S7b per district: L1 district claims (claimSubFace); S12a: no batch (siting decisions only); S10a, S10b: no batch (records; field pass 2 is a raster).
Batch table S8 per district: L1 lanes, rear lanes and through-alleys with their T-junction ends; S9 per district and hinterland: L2 corridorUnion.

Batch table S10: L3 step (0) eagerly on the generation worker after S10a and before the pool freeze — shared-edge bands on both sides at once: per enceinte the wall-strip blocks’ band, setback, glacis (or dry ditch), tower and gatehouse parts; the margin band (half-width 2 m, a table value ≥ residue class minimum width) along the settlement perimeter and any reservation boundary two districts share; ends by rebuilding the L3 static partitions it touched before the freeze; then per block in the pool: claims, plots, alleys-as-faces, residue; hinterland blocks: furlongs, outside lots, driveways, trails, woods, edge orchards.
Batch table S11 per block: L4 footprints and yard parts; a row’s party walls are one shared L4 edge.

Batch table S12b per district and hinterland: L3 park and grove layouts on its own reserved green faces and residue, then L4 yard-planting parts; avenue and street-tree rows write no plat edge; each batch whose commit changes a footprint face’s rings is followed by §2.6’s carry for that building before the next.

L0 writers: S1, S3, S4 (F-ROUTE extra bridge only) and S5a (outer moat carve); L1 writers: S3 (map border first), S4, S5, S6, S7, S7b, S8 in that order; no generation stage after S9 writes L1; S10 never writes L1.

J-P46: Chose the arena's outer ring (frame + context margin) as one L0 chain carrying `margin`, written first by S1, and the map border (the frame rectangle) as one L1 chain carrying `border`, written first by S3's L1 batch after S3's L0 batch, over both at L1 (every L0 face needs a boundary, and the sea and the rivers run out to the arena's edge) and over the border at L0 (L0 is land and water only, and it would split every water body the frame crosses) — because the border then meets no generation L0 batch, S3 stays the first L1 writer, and an outer moat's carve and an edit keep it closed across new water …

facts.statement: A rear or back lane is decided by S8’s deep-interior rule; a lane a user adds later is a drawWay edit through §7.3’s S5 operator, whose tree scoping re-derives every finer level under it.

Wall-clock time is read only by @plat/api's worker host, never by a model package; it may postpone or resume a lazy tier (F-BUDGET-TIME) and write telemetry but never changes what is computed; a tier computed late hashes exactly like one computed at once

Threads (4): the main thread runs the UI, compositing of transferred tiles, pointer hit-testing on hit-test slices, screen-space furniture (§9.5; placement scores and ruler snaps asked of the tile worker) and input; nothing model-sized ever reaches the main thread.

Derivation pool (primary configuration at every rung): up to 3 workers = min(3, hardwareConcurrency − 1) for S10, S10b, S11, S12b after S10a and S10 step (0); each district on its own copy-on-write overlay over a read-only frozen arena copy (typed arrays, lookup tables, static partitions of every non-empty level — L0–L3 at one-click, L4 too after edits — dynamic grids empty, dirty partitions rebuilt first; ≤ ≈ 15 MB at CITY); merge in district lineage order with slot remap and index partitions; any write outside a district’s face set is E_SCOPE; pool size 0 runs the same path in the generation worker.
Addresses and lineage keys derive from lineage, so no id ranges are reserved; there are no shared-edge writes in the pool (district boundary edges are L1/L2, committed before S10).

While a loaded document is verified (§2.9 step 3), every edit runs S10, S10b, S11, S12b in the generation worker by the pool-size-0 path, so the pool freezes no copy while a pool worker holds the verification replay’s model.

Which configuration is primary (NR3-1): at the same milestones the timing phase runs every sweep size (band bottom, target, top) with the pool (3 workers) and with a single worker (pool size 0) on the same generations (B-CITY-lite's 50 seeds × 4 water settings, paired), and the golden run generates 200 seeds at pool sizes 0-3; the pool is primary at a size when (a) it passes the sweep rule against the pooled law, (b) its p95 is below the single worker's on the same generations, and (c) model digests are identical for pool sizes 0-3 on the 200 seeds.

The single-worker column is the pre-decided fallback: on the low tier, in hosts that forbid extra workers, and at every size where the pool measures slower than a single worker or fails the digest check (NR3-1).

J-P10: Chose to specify the district pool and its merge protocol now (§4.1) over leaving pools behind a later measured need; reconciled with J-R18 and D-18 by the fix-all pass: the pool is the primary configuration at each size where M1 (TOWN, CITY) or M2b (METROPOLIS) measures it within its law + 10 %, faster than a single worker on the same generations and with identical digests for pool sizes 0–3, and the single worker is the pre-decided fallback elsewhere (§12.3; J-R44).

facts.statement: J-P27: Chose to run the hinterland unit (the hinterland's S10–S12b) on the otherwise idle generation worker as one more overlay of disjoint faces, over an eager L1 field partition before S8 (which would add ≈ 12 ms to CITY's critical path) — because fields are L3 content of the hinterland's own blocks and the generation worker waits for the pool anyway (§4.1, §4.9; NF-P8).

facts.statement: Blueprint = {version, seed, size {rung TOWN|CITY|METROPOLIS, population?|areaHa?|buildings?, tolerance, aspect 0.5–2 default 1 (frame width ÷ height)}, intent, site request (coast side/bearing with two arm rows, river with inflow bearing, islands and mouth, lake, hill…), toggles (walls; castle inside|on_enceinte|outside|auto|none; castles 0–2; plaza; temple; harbour; farms; forests; shanty; greens; waterfront open|quay_wall|sea_wall; wallPlacement; moat none|inner|all|auto — innermost enceinte by S3 or every enceinte, outer ones by S5a’s carve), circumstances (era, government, biome, economy, landscape toggles: fertile land, mines, quarries, fishing, logging), style, assignments, edits}.

Intent expansion is a pure function held in data: each intent field maps to internal parameters by { param, fn: 'const'/'linear'/'smoothstep'/'table', args } rows (tables interpolate linearly), evaluated in a fixed order

Size within a rung follows population: the requested population picks the rung whose band contains it (lower bound included, upper excluded): TOWN [1 500, 10 000), CITY [10 000, 30 000), METROPOLIS [30 000, 120 000]; roster, stage budgets, district count, frame and plots are computed from the population, never from the rung target.

Auto features: every toggle left on auto is resolved by a per-rung feature table (P(coast), P(river), P(castle), P(castle on the enceinte), P(temple), P(harbour|coast), P(shanty), P(greens) …) drawn once from concern blueprint.features before any other stage, never redrawn by a later rung; each auto-resolved value is recorded in the report with its reason.

What the base supports: several enceintes; 0–2 castles (a second is a citadel on the outer enceinte, by request or the METROPOLIS row); islands, confluences, distributaries; non-circular and polycentric settlements; routed non-radial arterials; generated institutions; multi-line labels; continuous zoom, save and load.

Heightfield: 5-octave fBm with low base frequency and a relief-character amplitude (flat/rolling/hilly/mountainous, metres by class) plus authored site primitives from the request (hill, spur, valley along the river bearing, terrace, cliff, ravine, hollow for a lake); heights in §2.3’s range and datum.

Heightfield evaluation: fBm on a 32 m grid over frame + margin; stored raster TOWN 5 m, CITY 8 m, METROPOLIS 10 m by bilinear refinement plus one fine octave inside the built extent; slope queries at 2.5 m via TerrainSampler on-demand interpolation.

Coast: from a sea bearing and an intent (bay/headland/straight/fjord/islands) one closed-outline routine draws the sea polygon; the base line is two arms from near the town toward two frame edges, each with a shape row (smooth/gentle/sharp: lateral amplitude and count of the arm’s 3–5 control points, then centripetal Catmull-Rom) and a detail row (none/bays/deep bays/rough/jagged: fBm amplitude, frequency, warp strength, bay count and depth); our own calibratable values.
The coast base line is displaced by domain-warped fBm with an amplitude envelope damping detail near the town → resample → Chaikin.

Coast simplicity (GEO-13): normal displacement at every sample clamped to 0.8 × local feature size (distance to the base shape’s medial axis from its straight skeleton; for an open arm, distance to the facing arm or the frame).

A self-touching resampled ring is repaired by non-zero union; the component containing the anchor keeps the outline id; other loops typed by rule — land loop in sea above minimum islet area → islet, water loop on land above minimum pond area → pond, smaller absorbed — and reported.

Stage property tests (outlines, plots, roster): 10 000 coast / island / fjord / sky outlines per intent → 0 self-intersections and 0 untyped loops; 0 overlapping or self-intersecting plots on concave, notched and curved blocks before any fallback; attached and party-wall shares on curved-street blocks inside the dense band; roster manifest(P₂) ⊇ manifest(P₁) for P₂ > P₁ on 1 000 seeds.

Contours and coast (GEO-14): the vector coast is authoritative; raster lowered below sea level on the sea side; land cells within two cells of the shore raised to ≥ sea level + 10 cm; sea cells ≤ sea level − 10 cm.

Relief tier (VN-029, VN-031; base should-have, optional, off by default): contour, hachure and grass marks are extracted per render tile from the terrain field by marching squares over the tile's cells plus a margin, then resampled evenly along each level line; hillshade runs on the same field; VG-specific looks (spotlight vignette, dramatic forest) stay in the reserved painterly family.

The same outline routine with a closed base curve makes lakes (from sinks), ponds, islands and, with elevationCm set, the floating-island outline of the LAYER hook (own arena, Terrain, datum, frame; may carry its own terrain from the same S1 with a request echoing the ground; ground footprint over water, fields or outskirts by default, over the built core only by assignment SkyIsland.placement; occlusion by LayerSpec.occlusion).
Standalone or sky outline base curve comes from an outline template row — disc, D-shape, lozenge, crescent, spindle — scaled to the requested area.

Rivers by descent: inlet on the arena’s upstream edge (requested bearing or highest edge) so the drawn margin shows the river arriving; course by steepest descent with a lateral meander term (Chaikin-smoothed control polyline, knots mostly on alternating sides); terrain carved to the course, then D8 recomputed on the carved corridor and accumulation once; the river always reaches sea, lake or frame.
River width w = w0 · acc^0.4 clamped to the class band (FTG ≈ 31 m mean river width at CITY is one calibration point); tributaries by the same rule from secondary inlets.

River bounds (GEO-36): knot offsets clamped to half the control spacing (river.controlSpacingM); S1 records the control knots in WaterBody.controls with ordinals in course order (the input moveCourseKnot addresses); a self-touching course is re-traced with offsets halved.
carveMaxCm: 400 cm at TOWN and CITY, 600 cm at METROPOLIS; a course needing more is re-routed by the F-RIVER rung (re-trace from last good knot, then move the inlet), never trenched.

Mouths: estuary = widening width profile; delta splits the course inside the delta zone (within the table distance of the sea where bed slope is below threshold) into 2–4 distributaries at splits spaced ≥ 3 channel widths, each with an accumulation share from water.delta (each ≥ 0.2), width w0·(share·acc)^0.4, traced by descent without rejoining; a distributary that would meet another merges; the land between becomes a river island.

River islands: river {islands: n} adds a branch leaving and rejoining after k cells; the enclosed land is an islet L0 face only if branch separation ≥ (w_main + w_branch)/2 + minimum islet width (20 m); else reported not built; mid-channel islets at reaches wider than a table threshold with a per-reach probability.
siteCrossings(reaches, bandM, existingDecks): S1 runs it over every reach; S1’s water operator over the re-traced reach only.
Crossing sites: narrowest/shallowest reaches within crossing.searchBandM (default 120 m) typed ford (width < table) or bridge_site, minimum spacing 40 m (table default).

Each crossing site is a pinned deck: bank-to-bank segment perpendicular to local flow (course tangent averaged over one channel width up- and downstream), endpoints inserted by S1’s L0 batch into the shores as the two deck_end vertices of a Bridge in state site, pinned against every later smoothing.

A site becomes a bridge only when a way uses it: the way routed through its two vertices lays the span, the way’s L1 edge carrying the structural deck role beside way; the Bridge becomes built with its way and S7 builds its furniture; no L0 edge crosses water and no deck splits a reach’s L0 face.
Harbour candidates: coast faces with depth ≥ threshold.

Bank classes: each shore segment classed bay/headland/straight (WaterBody.shoreClass) by signed curvature smoothed over 200 m (thresholds in a table); bank kind beach/rock/cliff/quay/marsh drawn from a per-class weight table conditioned on slope and exposure; class kept per segment for §8’s shore decoration.
Water faces enter L0 with shore/bank edges; land components by flood fill; every land component gets uses later.

shoreSetback per bank kind — plots: beach 6 m, marsh 10 m, rock 3 m, cliff 5 m, quay 0 m (quay plots front the quay way); fields 10 m; read by S10 and the hinterland unit; band typed shore greenery or commons.

SiteResources rasters on the terrain grid: stone (slope, rock class, cliffs), ore (relief × fBm propensity, hills only), timber (forest propensity from slope and soil, realised as woods by the hinterland unit), fish (water adjacency, reach width), clay (low damp river flats), fertile land (gentle, dry, non-rock); S0 landscape toggles clamp a kind to zero or raise its floor; read by S2’s resource gates and S12a. Drainage stays queryable.

F-RIVER (no course / no crossing; GEO-36) at S1, S3 and S1's water operator: detection: descent stalls in a sink, carve depth would exceed carveMaxCm, course leaves the frame before the core, no crossing site in the core band; ladder: carve the sink deeper up to carveMaxCm -> re-trace from the last good knot -> move the inlet along the frame edge (attempt) -> move the centre to the bank (S3) -> declare 'no crossing', route arterials to the bank road, report; a requested river island whose branch separation fails is reported 'not built'

S2 Programme: from population (or area/buildings via size tables): households by wealth band, institutions (market, temple, churches per capita, guild halls, inn, mill on water, tannery; seats forced by government per §10.2), building demand per class from our own dependency tables run as §10.2’s sequential prefix-stable roster, resource gates from SiteResources (no farmland → no farms, shops instead).
Outside classes (farmsteads, mills, quarries, lumber yards, fisheries, mines) are demanded by S2, sited by S12a and placed on outside plots the hinterland unit builds.

Stage demand in plot counts: n(c,b,k) = class demand × band shares × stage k’s quota share; residential band shares = roster household wealth shares (shifted by the character vector); workplace bands from the class row’s lifestyle band.
Stage land A_k = Σ_(c,b) n(c,b,k) · plotArea(c,b) / plotShare(regime_k); plotArea = plot area of the granularity table’s band centre (§4.7); footprints and coverage are not in the formula.
plotShare: dense core 0.62 (CONFIRMED from MFCG gross lot cover 0.60–0.65 at sizes 40–250), gapped rings 0.55, ribbon 0.45 (PLAUSIBLE).
J-P6: Chose plot counts per band with a measured plot share over one area per class with `1 − 0.38` — because 38 % is footprint over lot and plots span 11× in size across bands (§4.2 S2).

facts.statement: M-1 #5 measures FTG’s plot share; M1 measures B-CITY’s per regime; fallback: if S5d’s top-up fires on > 10 % of B-CITY seeds at a rung, plotShare rows refitted from B-CITY per regime by one scripted pass with a declared golden shift (§13.3).

Stage rows per rung: TOWN 2 stages (walled core 0.90, ribbon 0.10); CITY 3 (inner walled 0.55, outer walled 0.33, ribbon 0.12); METROPOLIS 4 (inner 0.30, middle 0.30, outer 0.28, ribbon 0.12); suburb regime only by era/form preset or shanty toggle; share inside the outermost wall ≈ 0.9 TOWN, ≈ 0.88 CITY and METROPOLIS (MFCG measured 0.87–0.92, CONFIRMED).
J-P5: Chose MFCG's walled share over 0.35–0.5 — because a mostly-extramural default reproduces MFCG's shanty case and a compact walled town with ribbons is the constrained medieval pattern (§4.2 S2).

facts.statement: S2 outputs: Roster (demand by class with area/frontage requirement classes, district affinities, wealth bands) and StageQuotas[] (plot counts per class × band, land area, regime per stage: dense core → gapped rings → ribbon, plus optional suburb).
S3 decides everything the first enceinte depends on in one construction and commits two batches — L0 (carved water with decks) then L1 (land reservations) — before S4 commits any way.

S3 (1) centres: candidates on a coarse lattice inside the frame’s middle third scored by a rule table (distance to a crossing site, to the harbour candidate, slope, elevation above flood line, wind exposure, distance from the frame, controlled random term); best = centre/market; the site is placed relative to the river, “no river through the core” checked and repaired by moving the centre, never by re-rolling.

Polycentric forms: twin-town and polycentric rows site k = 2–3 nuclei (candidates in the frame’s middle half), each with its own share A_1,i, main plaza and gates; market at the highest-scoring nucleus.

Nucleus separation floor sep_ij = τ(a₁)(R_i + R_j) + (outer setback + glacis)_i + (outer setback + glacis)_j + g, R = √(A_1/π); τ table 1.2 at a = 1.3, 1.4 at a = 1.8, τ = a otherwise; g = one ribbon plot depth (30 m); separation band floor to floor + 400 m (≈ 800–1 200 m for two 29 ha TOWN nuclei); ground between nuclei grown as an extramural regime in S5.

Main plaza per nucleus: area band TOWN 0.25–0.45 ha, CITY 0.35–0.6, METROPOLIS 0.45–0.8; compact 4–6-vertex polygon aligned to contours, compactness ≥ 0.8; its vertices are the attach points arterials end at.

S3 (2) also plans: temple/cathedral precinct adjacent to the main plaza by score, sized from its institution row; separate market square when the roster asks (CITY and above); harbour basin (template: rectangle, semi-octagon, semi-hexagon, L wide or narrow) scaled to port demand at the chosen candidate.

Canals along a least-cost line between two water bodies with decks at canalDeckSpacingM (150 m inside the predicted built extent, 600 m outside), each deck bank-to-bank, perpendicular, bank vertices pinned; planned polygons seen by the lattice as reservations and water (impassable except along decks), committed in (10) and (12).
S4’s candidate lattice and edge costs (§4.3) are built once at S3 (3) over the planned water and reservations.
Gate count N₁ per nucleus = the request or round(1 + 0.47 · √A_ha), A = stage-1 land (reproduces MFCG 5/8/12 gates at sizes 40/80/130 from walled 58/220/548 ha; 18 at size 200).

Gate picks: sequential nested picks from the gate.pick stream on the pick contour (level set of stage-1 land in the terrain-only field, a = 1, scoring only) scored by angular gap to earlier picks, nearness to a requested bearing, terrain (saddles and valley exits up, steep ground down) and jitter; a smaller N is a prefix of a larger; each pick’s bearing is the requested one or the least-cost outward direction to the frame; a polycentric nucleus’s first picks are forced at the bearings of adjacent nuclei.

Harbour pick (J-P45): with a harbour and N₁ ≥ 1, L* = path to the harbour destination node in the plaza-rooted Dijkstra tree (wall ignored) from the nearest nucleus’s plaza; if the node lies outside the pick contour, that nucleus’s first unforced pick is forced at L*’s first node beyond the contour (after polycentric forced picks; N unchanged); its bearing is the least-cost outward direction to the frame; its route’s inward part is L*’s prefix.

If the harbour’s nucleus has no unforced pick left (e.g. a < ≈ 10 ha nucleus between two neighbours with N₁ = 2, or a twin town with N₁ = 1) no pick is forced and the detour guard applies unconditionally (harbour route ≤ 1.5 × L*).

Harbour-pick measurement (M1): committed harbour route vs L* on every B-CITY walled coastal seed, p99 ratio ≤ 1.5, and ≤ 1.5 on every §13.2 walled coastal fixture; pre-decided fallback the detour guard of (7).

Water gates are added where the river crosses the boundary (not counted in N); N = 0 gives no main gate and no external arterial through the wall (a harbour outside the stage-1 region still gets the harbour gate); the sealed circuit is reported and extramural stages fold into the walled stage.

S3 (5) gate routes solved, not committed: plaza attach point → pick (plaza-rooted Dijkstra tree) → frame at the bearing (heap A*) on (3)’s lattice with S4’s cost; island town routes to landings; polycentric pair gate to gate; S4 commits exactly these and reuses the plaza-rooted tree; the harbour ↔ plaza route is not among them and never in T’s road set (solved in (11)).

S3 (6) stage-1 field: T computed by multi-source Dijkstra from the plaza(s) over the lattice with road multiplier 1/a₁ (walled core a₁ = 1.3) on the lattice edges of (5)’s routes; each node records its source nucleus; t_1,i chosen so nucleus i’s nodes with T ≤ t_1,i hold A_1,i (exact to one cell); boundary = that contour, Chaikin-smoothed and resampled.

Nuclei too close (regions nearer than setbacks, glacis and g): the later-scored nucleus is re-sited to its next candidate (≤ 3 attempts); failing that, merged — one enceinte around their union and a cross wall along T’s partition line (open chain anchored on the enceinte at both ends, gate where the inter-nucleus route crosses) — and reported.

S3 (7) each gate is the first point where its solved route, walked outward, reaches T = t_1; the gate keeps the pick’s identity, ordinal, bearing and route; two routes crossing the boundary at one point: the later pick is re-drawn (≤ 3 attempts), then dropped and reported (F-WALL).

Sealed town’s harbour gate: N = 0 and the harbour node outside {T ≤ t_1} → one harbour gate (kind water, not counted in N, carrying a way like a quay-access water gate, reported) where L* first reaches T = t_1.

Detour guard: the same harbour gate by the same rule is given to a town with gates whenever its best gate-bound harbour route (boundary impassable except at gates) is longer than 1.5 × L*, if M1’s harbour-pick measurement fails and, unconditionally, when the harbour’s nucleus had no unforced pick.

S3 (8) castle: bailey sited by defensibility (height + water on ≥ 1 side + control of the main route), restricted by the castle option to inside/on/outside the stage-1 boundary, hard filter that no (5) route crosses the claim or its planned castle-moat band; 5–7-vertex polygon on a jittered circle, area TOWN 1.0–3.0 ha, CITY 1.5–3.5, METROPOLIS 2.0–5.0, compactness ≥ 0.75.

on_enceinte castle: exactly two bailey vertices on the boundary (weld vertices); the outer arc between them becomes the shared stretch of town wall; the castle’s town-side gate is fixed at the midpoint of the bailey side with the least-cost path to the plaza (for on_enceinte, among the town-side arc’s sides).

S3 (9) stage-1 trace: the registered EnceinteStrategy traces by S5a’s rules (boundary pulled to defensible ground within the 40 m band, gates and weld vertices pinned, pinned-vertex smoothing, topology-preserving simplification); between weld vertices the trace is the bailey’s outer arc (one wall with both enceintes’ wall roles, Castle.cityWeld); pull and simplification never cross planned water or a planned ring castle moat; S5a commits it unchanged for k = 1; an unwalled town keeps the boundary.

Every gate and weld vertex lies on the committed trace exactly (lattice equality); the trace departs from the boundary by ≤ 40 m except along an on_enceinte castle’s shared stretch, which may bulge up to the bailey’s width.

The replaced two-construction mismatch (anisotropic contour 76 m beyond / 35 m inside the terrain-only contour at 58 ha, five roads, a = 1.3; 147 m / 82 m at a = 1.8) cannot occur because stage 1 has one boundary.

facts.statement: S3 (10) L0 carvings: harbour basin and canals with decks; castle moat when water is within reach — ring band around an inside/outside bailey outside its curtain’s outer half-band and a berm with one deck at the castle gate; for on_enceinte only the outer arc (city moat’s own stretch at the wider width row where there is one, else a channel clipped at each end by trace ⊕ (outer half-band + berm)); town-side arc takes the castle template’s townSide (dry ditch or nothing), no deck on that side.

City moat when moat is inner or all: channel of the era row’s width along the (9) trace, outside its outer half-band and a berm (table 2–5 m), one deck at every main gate and at a harbour gate where the route crosses, perpendicular.

Decoration ponds: the pond row of §4.9’s decoration table (count by rung and biome), sites scored on hollows, flow accumulation and damp ground, each ≥ pondClearM (150 m) beyond the predicted built extent {T ≤ t_K} and ≥ 30 m from every (5) route and planned canal.

No castle moat crosses the city trace (a ring surrounds a bailey the trace keeps off; an outer arc runs beside the trace), so §4.4’s rule that the trace crosses water only at a river’s water gate holds for every castle option.
When a moat is carved, T is recomputed once over the new water (≈ 4 ms at CITY) for stages k ≥ 2; stage 1’s boundary is never re-derived from it.

S3 (11) harbour route after the L0 batch: solved on the lattice with committed water impassable except along decks, reservations impassable and (walled) the trace impassable except at gates; a harbour inside {T ≤ t_1} or in an unwalled town by heap A* from its nucleus’s plaza; outside, one multi-source Dijkstra from every gate’s exit (far bank vertex of its moat deck, else the gate) finds the serving gate (least cost; ties by gate ordinal; a harbour gate competes; with N = 0 it is the only gate) and the branch; the route = serving gate’s inward street, passage, moat deck and branch; roads leaving = N plus a harbour gate where placed; data committed by S4, not in T’s road set; cost inside S3’s §12.4 row (PLAUSIBLE).

Walled coastal harbour fixtures of §4.2 S3 (11) (harbour outside the stage-1 region, with and without moat: 'inner'; sealed with N = 0; a polycentric coastal town whose nucleus nearest the harbour has no unforced pick left): each harbour served, 0 non-gate ways reaching the trace, every way–moat crossing on a deck, roads leaving = the N main gates plus a harbour gate of §4.2 S3 (7) where placed; harbour route ≤ 1.5 × the plaza ↔ harbour least-cost lattice path with the wall ignored, one main gate on the harbour side (§4.2 S3 (4)).

S3 (12) land reservations enter L1 as barrier faces with the reserved role (plazas, precinct, market square, castle bailey): no way crosses them (S4, S5), S8 does not cut them, the claimed entity is built inside.

Destinations (typed entities): plazas’ attach points; each gate with its bearing (external bearing per gate if walled; an unwalled town derives bearings by the same law on its own land); the town bridge (crossing site nearest the centre when a river passes through the stage-1 region, connecting in town; every other site becomes a bridge only when S4 or S5c uses it); the harbour (node = basin’s landward attach point); the castle’s town-side gate; the precinct.

Island towns: when the land component does not touch the frame, external destinations are shore points — the harbour, one landing per requested bearing (shore point nearest the bearing with the best deep-water score) and a ferry point; O4 (g) counts landings as external connections.

J-P26: Chose to solve the gate routes at S3 and take the stage-1 boundary, the gates, the castle weld, the wall trace and the moat from one travel-cost construction over a provisional boundary on straight corridors (which still differs from the routed arterials) or sliding the gates at S5a (which leaves a moat carved at S3 off the wall or forces water into L0 after the arterials) — because a moat must enter L0 before any L1 edge and can follow the real wall only if the wall is known then (§4.2 S3; NF-P1; `fixall_pipeline_r2_levelset.out`).

facts.statement: The routing lattice and its edge costs are built once at S3 (depending only on frame, terrain, water and reservations) and reused by S3’s pick contour, gate routes and field T, by S4’s routes and by every S5a boundary.

Candidate lattice: jittered hexagonal point set at ≈ 25 m spacing, six neighbours per point by construction, jitter bounded so no edge crosses another (no Poisson sampling, relaxation or triangulation).

Edge cost = length × (1 + k_slope · slope²) × waterCrossingPenalty (impassable except along a pinned crossing deck — site or built bridge) × reservationPenalty (impassable inside; plaza and castle reached only at attach points and gate) × wallCrossingPenalty (only at gates) × existingFabricCost (epoch > 0: crossing a built face costs by its class) × landValue.

At epoch 0 the plaza-rooted Dijkstra tree from S3 gives every plaza-anchored route; a tree path crossing a claim or water S3 added after the tree (bailey, moat) is re-solved by heap A*, as are routes without a plaza end and every route at epoch > 0 (with existingFabricCost).

S4 commits S3’s gate routes without re-solving, each split at its gate into the inward street (plaza attach point ↔ gate, primary) and the outward arterial (gate ↔ frame at its bearing, through); roads leaving the walled stage = N (plus a harbour gate where placed); each gate carries one road out and one street in.

Where S3 carved water across a solved route (the city moat outside each gate) S4 re-solves only that stretch, last lattice node before the channel to first beyond, through the gate’s deck; the deck continues the gate passage straight across, perpendicular.

S4’s remaining routes: town bridge ends → nearest arterial on each bank in town; a site outside the boundary used by a route is reached through the nearest gate (never a new wall crossing); other sites stay sites unless S5 growth uses them; castle town-side gate ↔ plaza (castle street, across the castle-moat deck when there is one); precinct frontage ↔ the plaza side it faces; canal decks inside the boundary ↔ nearest arterial; harbour ↔ plaza and island gate ↔ landing come solved from S3.

Polycentric: the gate-to-gate route between adjacent nuclei (solved at S3 between their forced gates) joins their plazas through both nuclei’s gates; for a merged pair it crosses the cross wall at its gate.

One graph, one smoothing (GEO-16): all routes solved first; arterial graph = union of lattice edges used, each with its multiplicity; split into chains at nodes of degree ≠ 2 and at pinned nodes (gates, attach points, deck endpoints, landings); junctions closer than 8 m merged on the graph; each chain simplified (Visvalingam) and smoothed (Chaikin × 2, then curvature-limited to the class minimum radius) once with end nodes pinned, and inserted into L1 once as a mandatory chain with the way role whose attraction folds residual near-duplicates within 26 cm into a shared stretch.

Way class and width from multiplicity and betweenness on the arterial graph (width table keyed by class, class by betweenness); where width varies along a way S4 places width_knot vertices at class-change junctions (insertChain opts.knots) so width is a knot profile on the spine.
Junction rules: minimum crossing angle 30° (else deflect); Y → T conversion where the acute arm can be bent within its class curvature limit.

F-ROUTE (no arterial path; GEO-17) at S4 and S4's local operator: detection E_NO_PATH, or an approach cannot meet a pinned bridge deck within the class's minimum radius; ladder: another crossing site on the reach within its search band (one S1 or S3 already emitted, a 'site' no way uses yet; river and canal decks; a moat deck is fixed at its gate; deck stays perpendicular to local flow) -> one bridge at extra cost (a new deck whose two deck_end vertices are placed by one L0 batch of two same-level shore splits, nothing cleared, before the way's L1 batch lays the span) -> relax the slope limit one class -> route to the nearest reachable junction and mark the destination 'unserved' in the report
Every deck a route uses (site or added) becomes a built bridge when S4’s spine lays its span through the two bank vertices.
On B-CITY no two spines run closer than their class separation for more than one step length; every deck’s way angle within ± 10° of the channel normal.
Through-roads continue to the context margin with their bearings; later growth stages add main roads via S5b, which runs the same router incrementally with every existing arterial fixed.

Operator row S4 (drawWay of an arterial, moved arterial vertex, moved destination, castle placed or resized, deck re-sited or removed by S1's water operator): re-route only arterials whose corridors meet the edit region or whose destination or deck moved, each between its nearest pinned nodes (junctions of degree >= 3 or destination nodes) on either side, over S3's lattice, every deck a fixed graph edge; pinned: their endpoints, every spine outside the region; beyond: Re-derive from S3 when a destination is added or removed (gate count)

Each growth stage k runs four sub-steps; stage 1 commits S3’s boundary, gates and trace; stage k ≥ 2 takes its boundary first, then main roads, then trace, so every gate lies on the boundary it was picked on.

S5a boundary: the stage boundary is a level set of network travel cost T(x) = least cost from the plaza(s) over the lattice, a lattice edge inside an arterial corridor costing ρ_road/m and any other ρ_off/m, both times the slope term; water impassable except along decks, reservations impassable.

Anisotropy ratio a = ρ_off/ρ_road per stage regime and form: walled core 1.3, walled rings 1.8, ribbon 4, suburb 3, linear-street form 8 (our values; FTG’s measured road/non-road r90 ratio 1.26–1.65 is the calibration target for extramural stages).

T is one field: computed at S3 (≈ 4 ms at CITY) with the road multiplier on the gate routes’ lattice edges, recomputed once after S3’s L0 batch only when a moat was carved; S4’s remaining routes and the harbour route are not in its road set; each S5b’s new main roads re-settle T incrementally at the nodes whose cost they lower; no stage computes a new field.

Stage 1’s boundary is S3’s contour and S5a commits S3’s trace unchanged; for k ≥ 2 the boundary is taken from T as it stands when stage k begins (before its S5b): t_k chosen so land of {T ≤ t_k} ∪ enclosure of stage k−1 equals the land of stages 1…k from S2 (nodes sorted by T, cell areas accumulated, exact to one cell); boundary = outer contour, Chaikin-smoothed and resampled; S5b’s re-settlement serves stage k+1 onward.
Outline anisotropy (FTG-5; P): land-sector r90 CV and road / non-road r90 ratio by the band rule against FTG 0.20–0.33 and 1.26–1.65 (target for organic presets); monotone in the anisotropy row.

S5a trace (GEO-18, FTG-8), fixed before the stage’s secondaries grow (stage 1 by S3, k ≥ 2 right after S5b) by one rule set (registered EnceinteStrategy): boundary → pulled to defensible ground within a 40 m search band (ridges, slope breaks, river banks; cost-surface path with a penalty for leaving high ground) with gates pinned where arterials cross (stage 1: S3’s gates; k ≥ 2: every crossing of an S4, earlier-S5b or this stage’s S5b arterial) and an on_enceinte castle welded through its two weld vertices → pinned-vertex Laplacian smoothing → topology-preserving Visvalingam (kernel simplify: minimum segment 20 m, no interior angle < 100°; a removal that self-touches, crosses water, enters a reservation or moves a pinned vertex is refused) → insertChain on L1 as a mandatory chain with the wall role, gate vertices carrying wall_gate; on a shore the trace is attracted onto the outline (one edge, both roles).

A second castle on an outer enceinte (the citadel) is sited by S3 (8)’s rules against its stage’s boundary and entered as an L1 barrier face in that stage’s trace batch, with its gate and any moat deck.
placement: aroundStage traces only the stage’s new ring as an open chain anchored on the previous enceinte; nothing grown later crosses the trace except at a gate; S6 treats it as a barrier.

F-WALL (bad trace / infeasible gate count; GEO-18, FTG-8, NF-P1) at S3, S5a, S7: detection: trace self-intersects or crosses the core; a closed trace does not close or an open trace end is not anchored on shore/bank/cliff; fewer arterial crossings than N; a non-gate way reaches the trace; ladder: two gate routes crossing the stage-1 boundary at one point -> re-draw the later gate pick (<= 3) -> drop it and report; trace fixed before growth with gates pinned: re-offset with a larger radius -> topology-preserving union-simplify -> anchor open ends by attraction onto nearest shore/bank/cliff (shared stretch carrying bank and wall) and add water gates where the waterfront policy requires a quay wall -> divert excess arterials to the nearest gate as lanes -> add posterns and report when N cannot be met (N = 0: declared sealed circuit, harbour gate still placed) -> last rung: cut a way reaching the wall at the setback band and prune the outer stub, reported

Outer moats: when moat is all, S5a carves stage k’s moat (k ≥ 2) right after committing its trace through §4.11’s carve path; its way rule meets only arterials (each just outside a gate), so every way is kept with a deck and nothing is cut: the L1 batch places each deck’s two pinned bank vertices on its arterial (deck_end rows of a fresh Bridge, built with that arterial) with the span carrying deck (re-routing the arterial between the gate and its next pinned node where it would meet the channel > 10° off its normal); the L0 batch inserts the channel (era row width, outside outer half-band and a berm) through those prepared vertices; each deck perpendicular, continuing its gate’s passage; S7 builds bridge furniture; nothing finer than L1 exists so the carve clears nothing; the innermost moat is S3’s.

S5b main-road step (k ≥ 2 and every epoch stage): N_k = the §4.2 S3 gate law on the land inside the stage’s enceinte (walled) or one primary per mainRoadSpacingM of boundary (unwalled; 450 m at CITY); with c existing crossings, when N_k > c spawn N_k − c radial destinations on the boundary by nested picks (largest angular gaps first, terrain-scored) and route each with the incremental S4 router from the nearest junction on an existing primary outside the previous enceinte (never through an inner wall) to the frame at its bearing; crossings become main gates, posterns only for an explicitly requested remainder.
An outer enceinte never gets fewer gates than arterials cross it; a request below that is raised and reported; a requested gate count applies to the innermost enceinte.
Primary length per km² and share of gates on primaries in band from TOWN to METROPOLIS; each epoch stage whose N_k exceeds its crossings adds ≥ 1 primary.

S5c growth: priority queue of proposals {origin junction, heading, curvature, goalHeading, class, remainingSegments, branchCounter, priority}, lowest priority first; step length by class (secondary 25–40 m, lane 15–25 m).

Division of labour (MFP-2): in walled regimes S5c grows only the arterial-connecting secondary network at district scale (seeded at arterial junctions and gate plazas, separation floor 120/160/200 m at TOWN/CITY/METROPOLIS, destination bias toward other arterials); every lane and finer intramural street comes from S8’s bent cut; extramural regimes (ribbon, suburb, unwalled rings, ground between polycentric nuclei) grow at block scale FTG-style.

MFCG street signature (MFP-2; P, walled districts, band rule): lot-orientation coherence R4 within 60 / 120 / 250 m (MFCG 0.84–0.97 / 0.58–0.88 / 0.32–0.68); lot alignment with the wall by distance band (within 40 m median deviation 3.5–4.5° and 84–92 % within 15°; 56–70 % at 40–100 m; 38–58 % at 100–200 m); T/Y share, intramural dead ends, blocks per ha, lots per block from the sweep ⟨M-1⟩.

J-P4: Chose the bent cut for the intramural fabric and FTG growth outside the walls over FTG growth everywhere — because MFCG's measured intramural signature comes from recursion on the district polygon (§4.4).

facts.statement: Heading model ou: κ ← ρκ + (1−ρ)κ_goal + s√(1−ρ²)ξ per step Δs, ρ = e^(−Δs/ℓ), κ_goal = (θ_goal − θ)/L_r, s from headingSigma in degrees per 100 m; organic defaults 20°/100 m, ℓ = 90 m, L_r = 250 m; planned 5°/100 m; radiusHold (ring proposals keep curvature 1/r, small s; ringed preset); gridLock (headings snap to the preset grid table; american); CI tests the drift distribution per preset.
Executed ou heading (4 000 streets per setting): at organic defaults a 600 m street’s net turn p50 21°, p90 50°, 0.1 % beyond 90°; per-30 m-step turn p95 11.4°, p99 14.9°, Gaussian tails.
Branching after n segments with a per-class probability, perpendicular ± jitter or tangential to the centre (ringed preset’s ring branch).

Destination bias (switchable per class and preset): a proposal that can reach an unserved destination or existing spine within ≈ 1.5 step lengths turns toward it; off for suburb offshoots and ring proposals.

Legality (GEO-37): minimum separation from parallel spines = regime separation; same clearance to shores, wall setback bands, reservations and the stage boundary — a proposal within max(minimum regime block depth, separation/2) + half its corridor of any, within 30° of parallel, is deflected or rejected; meeting a shore or reservation at ≥ 30° ends there; a proposal reaching the setback band stops (wall never crossed except at a gate); snap to a junction within 0.35 · step; slope ≤ class limit.

Crossing matrix per preset (proposal class × crossed class → T stop, materialised crossroads, or deflect): organic crosses only a lower-or-equal class collinear within 6°; ringed crosses radials with rings; american crosses on the grid.

Water: a proposal meeting a river or canal bank within 0.35 · step of a site’s bank vertex snaps to it and crosses that deck to the far bank vertex (building the bridge) when its class row allows a bridge (table: secondary and lane by default); any other proposal meeting water ends there.
Junction rules as §4.3 with T-preference in organic regimes; junction-degree band per preset: organic 4-way 0–15 %, ringed 20–45 %, american 40–80 %.

Between stages: prune dangling secondary chains shorter than one block width; trim only S5-grown provisional spines running beyond the boundary; S4 and S5b arterials are never trimmed; the boundary becomes the next stage’s start.

S5d capacity check: the stage’s new coarse faces priced — built land = face area − corridor reserve of its spines (declared half-widths) − reservations; each face’s band = driver-only prosperity field at its centroid (S6 pass-1 kernels) cut by provisional cut points computed as §4.5 computes recorded bands, over land grown so far (S6 records FieldBands once over all stages).

If land per band falls short of the stage’s demand Σ n(c,b,k)·plotArea(c,b)/plotShare by > 5 % in total, one top-up runs (level set grows to cover the shortfall, S5a re-traces only the affected arc between pinned gates, S5c grows the added rim); a moated arc is never re-traced, so a moated stage’s shortfall moves to the next stage’s quota (the last stage’s to the exact check), reported; a remaining shortfall goes to the exact check after S10 and the F-SITING reconcile (F-BUDGET-STAGE).
B-CITY sweeps wealthLevel ∈ {0, 0.5, 1} and asserts population ± 5 % and the walled share inside its rung band.

StageRegime table: dense core (stage 1) block-depth floor 30–45 m (S8), separation 120–200 m (district-scale secondaries), a 1.3, ou + bias, lanes from S8, T-preference; walled rings (stages ≥ 2) 45–70 m, 120–200 m, a 1.8, ou + bias, courts and rear lanes; ribbon (default extramural) plots directly on the arterial, depth 30–50 m starting beyond outer setback/glacis, density falloff by distance-to-gate kernel, a 4 (MFCG: 71–85 % of extramural buildings within 100 m of a gate road); suburb (preset/era/shanty only) 40–60 m, 80 m, a 3, offshoots, bias off; american/ringed on request (gridLock/radiusHold, preset crossing matrix and junction band).

Suburb regime: optional perimeter lane (previous enceinte’s outer boundary offset by setback and glacis, typed lane, broken at arterials) seeds offshoots at a 60–90 m spacing row; offshoots grow as cul_de_sac/lane proposals without destination-bias termination; no infill below the band; plots directly along offshoots with small lots, a per-plot density Bernoulli from the distance-to-gate kernel leaves gaps (calibration: FTG 83 cul-de-sacs, 30.00 m suburb streets, 14.70 m lot outlines).
Fixture: ringed on a flat site gives ≥ 3 closed rings with radius CV ≤ 10 % and ring × radial crossroads.

Fusion risk gate (O4 f): S4 + S5 + S8 infill ≤ 100 ms at CITY on reference hardware; infill block-area and junction-degree distributions inside NG-measured bands on the same district shapes and MFCG street-signature rows (orientation coherence at 60/120/250 m, wall and shore alignment by distance band, T/Y share, intramural dead ends, blocks per ha, lots per block) inside their bands; M0 measures first; repeated at M1 on B-CITY-lite river, coast and relief configurations.

Fusion gate fallbacks: failing on time → extramural growth also stops at secondary (lane infill-only everywhere) and re-run; failing on statistics → infill constants recalibrated against NG vertex captures and MFCG size-sweep exports (spike M0-b) before M1; neither changes the architecture.

Settlement perimeter: S6’s one L1 batch first inserts the last stage’s boundary offset outward by the ribbon regime’s block-depth band top (50 m), rounded, as a chain carrying district_bound, closed against arterials, shores and frame; every coarse face outside belongs to the hinterland pseudo-district, every face inside to a grown district, fixed before any district is typed; no later stage splits a district face to make hinterland.

District grower: seeds = sited features (market, harbour, gates, castle, temple precinct, river banks, parks) plus a density-guided remainder; claims adjacent L1 coarse faces with validateEdge = no arterial of class ≥ primary, no wall trace, no water, no reservation boundary (unless the seed kind allows) and validatePatch = area within district band, compactness ≥ 0.5, no hole; check4holes → split; faces below the floor merged into the neighbour with the longest shared edge.
District count and band (MFP-10): N_d = round(3.5 · √(A_ha/10)) over settlement land A; band [0.5, 1.5] × A/N_d (mean ≈ 7 ha at 60 ha, ≈ 13 ha at 250 ha, ≈ 21 ha at 600 ha).

Quarter merge tree (QuarterNode, §9.1) built once per model after typing: repeatedly merge the adjacent pair with smallest cost = combined area + 1 000 ha when kinds are of different families + 10 000 ha when a wall or water barrier separates them, until one root; ties by id.

Quarters = the tree’s cut at min(N_q, L) nodes (after L − min(N_q, L) merges, L = districts the grower produced; every district alone when N_q ≥ L; QuarterNode.cityCut), N_q = round(1.37 · B^0.267), B = roster building count (least-squares fit of MFCG 9/12/18/22/24 districts at 1 475/5 242/13 091/31 951/48 379 buildings) → N_q = 9–10 at TOWN (1 200–1 500 buildings), 13–14 at CITY (4 500–6 000), 17–18 at METROPOLIS (12 000–15 000).

Executed quarter cut at matched sizes 40/80/130: 8/13/17 vs MFCG’s 9/12/18 labels (± 1 at every rung); TOWN band 5 (1 500 inhabitants) to 11; old N_d − N_q merges was negative (N_q 10 vs N_d 8 at size 40; 7 vs 5 at size 24).

facts.statement: District typing (G-P5, MFP-7): data-driven scorer per district kind reads remaining roster demand per class, adjacency (docks at harbour, gate wards at gates, central → market/merchant, noxious crafts downstream and downwind, near castle → military/administration, waterfront → docks) and a random term; typed greedily from the largest with a mixed-use floor (no single-use district unless requested).

District kinds are feature-named; wealth is not a kind (“rich quarter” is a description the naming engine derives from the prosperity field); no district zoned residential or by class; a shanty/squalid type only after the first half of the stages and only outside the enceinte; MFCG’s one prominent feature per named type survives as namingFeature; fabric is bent-cut unless a template is requested (PART II).

Prosperity field P(x) = Σ w_i·kernel_i(x) + characterOffset(district) + ε(x), clamped once to [0, 1]; driver kernels from a table (distance decay to plaza/market, main streets, gates, water and harbour +; elevation above flood line and upwind +; low, damp, downwind, flood-prone −; walls −; attractors at reserved institutions); ε low-frequency fBm from the field’s own sub-stream with declared share (default 0.15); smoothed by a Gaussian of one block width (σ ≈ 60 m at CITY); stored per coarse face and as a raster.
Field mechanism the budget assumes: 32 m cells over frame + margin; each driver kernel splatted within its radius (or one distance transform per driver class); Gaussian as an O(N) three-box blur.

facts.statement: Fields computed in two declared eager passes: pass 1 at S6 from drivers existing after S5 (the kernels S5d uses); pass 2 at S10a adding kernels around noxious trades, prisons, middens and institutions placed by block allocation; S6 typing and S8 block bands read pass 1; S10 onward reads pass 2.

Field brushes (LC-27): a stroke is a relative delta over the driver field (FieldStroke); the field = driver field + stroke list composited in log order and clamped once at the end, so undo removes a stroke and re-composites exactly (a per-stroke clamp is not exact: +0.3 then -0.3 on 0.9 gives 0.7)
Over time: an epoch re-evaluates the drivers with new circumstances; surviving plots keep built state and change only through the explicit, rate-limited transformation events of §4.11.

Owner rule AM-6 clause map: continuous field P(x); predictable drivers = kernel table; controlled random = ε with declared share; banded only where a table needs a class = FieldBands; continuous rules interpolate (§4.7, §4.9); dynamic yet predictable = epochs move drivers, survivors transform by rule; editable = brush and setAttr on FieldBands.
Density field and greenery-propensity field follow the same construction with their own driver tables and FieldBands; a second S6 pass applies the district-type term after typing.
S7b runs after S7 and decides all content allocation once for the whole town before any lane is cut.

S7b (1) town → districts: roster demand per class × band allocated to districts and, for outside classes (farmsteads, mills, quarries, mines, lumber yards, fisheries), to the hinterland pseudo-district, by capacity (district built land per band from pass 1) and affinity (district-kind affinity rows, adjacency to features, resource sites), greedy in declared order (institutions, large workplaces, households; classes by priority then id; districts by score then id) from the town’s alloc.district stream derived from lineage on demand (no allocation record stores a stream key); bounded reconcile ≤ 3 rounds; persisted as one Allocation per district and one for the hinterland.
S7b (2) sub-districts: classes with a cluster tag whose allocation in a district exceeds a threshold share get a SubDistrict; S10a gives it a contiguous group of blocks sized to its allocation.

S7b (3) district claims: every item larger than one block (institutions exceeding the block band, the district’s park/green quota share, area-bearing assignments, a castle’s esplanade) sized from its requirement table and cut out of the district’s coarse faces other than wall_strip faces by claimSubFace (within = that face list) at the best siting score, entered as a Reservation; S8 cuts around it as a hole; S10 keeps only sub-block claims; S12b builds parks only on reserved faces or residue; a castle esplanade is claimed beyond the bailey’s outer strip.

No S7b claim takes wall-strip ground (as no S8 cut does); strip ground is the band, setback and glacis S10 (0) builds; hard invariant footprints ∩ (band ⊕ setback) = ∅; only S7’s gate plazas use a strip’s setback zone.

J-P41: Chose to exclude an enceinte's wall-strip faces from S7b's claim candidates (`claimSubFace` within the district's coarse faces other than its strips) over letting a claim take strip ground — because a reservation there would site an institution or park where nothing may stand — the strip's ground is band, setback and glacis, and "footprints ∩ (band ⊕ setback) …

facts.statement: 100 % of institutions and parks larger than one block placed at their requirement (O18 f); 0 S7b claims meeting a wall strip.

S7b (4) edge greens and orchards: for every district touching the settlement perimeter whose band row carries the rule, S7b draws (before (3)) from the district’s alloc.district stream with probability RungProfile.greenery.edgeGreenProb: a green becomes one of the district’s claims built by its own S12b; an orchard becomes a hinterland allocation row {cls: orchard, areaM2, near: district} built by the hinterland unit’s S10 in the first ring beside that district; no district stage writes a hinterland face.

S7b (5) sky pseudo-districts (owner-staged): with the island toggle on, S7b first creates each sky pseudo-district’s Allocation; a prosperity island’s plot land = its area (from IslandRule.areaHaBand on the island.place stream) × 0.62, filled from the richest band down with the richest demand until land is used or three districts’ worth of households; an institution island holds its one institution; the ground’s districts get the remainder so population stays whole; SkyStrategy, registered after S7b, sizes and places each island to hold its allocation.

S8 runs per district (one batch each, lineage order, generation worker) on every coarse face except reservations (holes) and wall strips (never cut), whose kerb(F) (face minus buffered spines, §3.7) is larger than the district class’s block band (granularity table at the pass-1 band), floored by the stage regime’s band.

S8 plans each cut on kerb(F) of current L1 faces, inserts each accepted lane at L1 in the district transaction extended to the crossed spine as a T-junction, recurses on children’s kerbs; S9’s corridorUnion commits exactly those kerbs (contract test S8 working block ≡ S9 committed block, Hausdorff 0); no insetRing by corridor half-widths needed.

The wall is a barrier: kerb(F) beside a wall stops at the strip boundary (inner setback line or intervallum kerb), so no cut is planned through band or setback; S8 never meets an L3 face. Test: on every walled B-CITY seed 0 lanes cross a wall strip and 0 L3 band faces are cleared or split by an L1 batch.

Sides (GEO-22): face boundary reduced to runs (kernel sideRuns: maximal chains with cumulative turning ≤ 10°, with chord direction); a fillet arc replaced by its virtual corner; “perpendicular to a side” measured against the run’s chord or, on a curved run, the tangent over a ± 5 m window at the contact point.
M0 (b) includes curved, round-joined, triangular, C-shaped and holed faces and re-measures the NG signature on them before calibration.

Bent cut step 1 stop test: F is a block if its OBB minor extent < the band’s upper bound; slope term: on a face with mean slope > 5 % the working major axis is rotated toward the contour direction by weight min(0.5, slope/0.3).

Step 2 position: f ~ N(0.5, σ) of the working major axis, σ = 0.066 plain, 0.098 holed/annular; with probability 0.03 f uniform over [0.15, 0.85]; no clamp; f outside [0.1, 0.9] redrawn once; stream cut.t.

Step 3 start: the minor-axis line at f meets F in one segment around the OBB centre’s projection (concave: the segment containing the nearest point); its two ends are candidate starts; coin cut.side p = 0.5 (table cut.sideLongerBias records NG’s unconfirmed 2:1 lean, default 0.5) picks start A; leave A exactly perpendicular to its run.
Step 4 far side: the side hit by the perpendicular ray from A (NG R1); cut.farSideAlt (default 0) = probability of taking the next reachable side.

M0 (b) compares block-area, cut-length and junction-angle distributions with NG’s on the same faces; fallback if KS fails with R1: cut.farSideAlt = 0.34 and re-run; if still failing, far side from the minor-axis line through A (NG R4) — each a table value.

Step 5 straight or bent: straight if it reaches the far side within 2° of perpendicular (along the mean of the two run normals); else one corner at half the perpendicular projection A–F and the second leg perpendicular to the far side’s run; never two bends.

Step 6 fillet: probability 0.53 (stream cut.arc) replace the corner by an equal-chord circular arc with tangent length r_t × shorter leg, r_t ~ N(0.73, 0.10) clipped to [0.54, 0.87]; radius follows from the legs; chord steps equal and ≥ lattice minimum edge.

Step 7 ends (GEO-21): each junction end extended along its arrival direction from the kerb to the crossed spine and inserted there as a T-junction (splitThrough); stroke caps are the renderer’s rule; an end meeting a dead end or hole follows §3.6 contact semantics (antenna → T-junction; hole → connectHole); an end at a wall strip setback line stays square to it; an end at the intervallum is a T-junction.

Seam portals (NF-P6): when the crossed spine bounds the district (arterial or boundary secondary), S8 records the T-junction vertex as a baseLane portal with its SeamAmendment in the shared Seam record of that boundary run; a planned end inside an existing portal’s gap — max(6 m, 2 × the wider lane’s width), a table row — slides along the spine toward the side keeping arrival within 85–95°, else the cut takes its next ladder rung; each portal vertex carries exactly one lane.

When a re-derivation removes a lane its end vertex loses its portal role (removeEdges on its VertexRef), is dissolved, and its portal and amendment leave the Seam record so the spine reads as before; the neighbour step’s reversal restores the neighbour’s kerb.

Seam exception (NF-P6): a district-scoped re-derivation's effective scope also includes its bounding ways' chains and Corridor records, the half-corridor strips on both sides, the junction wedges at vertices its batches insert or remove on those spines (on a neighbour's side only II.1 (3)'s neighbour step: one corridor_split edge and the one kerb vertex it lands on, promoted, or adds), the neighbouring cells, plots and footprints whose rings pass through those vertices, and the wing rings of buildings on them (§2.6), all changed only by them (a promoted vertex returns to its level when the lane goes, §2.2 rule 3), and the Seam records it is party to (§4.6, II.4)

J-P32: Chose a portal gap that slides a planned lane end away from an existing portal over letting two districts' lanes share a boundary vertex — because a shared vertex is the cross-boundary crossroads GEO-42 forbids and binds either district's reroll to the other's lane (§4.6; NF-P6).

facts.statement: Every district reports the share of built land left as court or green by substitution; soft bound ≤ 5 %.

Step 9 width: one scalar per lane w = a_district + b·(L + e·n_free), a drawn once per district, b a rung-table slope, L final course length, n_free free ends, e = 0.025 × district median cut length; alleys 2–3 m, lanes 3–5 m; a cut longer than the lane length band in a walled regime is typed secondary; never narrower than a lower class; template roads take fixed per-district widths drawn once from the district stream.

Step 10 continuation: a cut may continue across an existing lower-or-equal-class street when collinear within 6°, only inside its own district, never across a district-boundary edge (GEO-42); step 11 recurse on both children with their own sub-streams.
J-P11: Chose to forbid bent-cut continuation across district boundaries over two-district transactions (§4.6).
