facts.statement: Deep-interior rule (IMP-8): when recursion stops and a block’s local thickness exceeds 2 × its band’s plot depth, the district band row chooses the interior in S8 by target shares: court, back_lane, through_alley, rear_plots; lanes/alleys chosen here are inserted as L1 spines in S8’s own batch, so S10 never writes L1.

Deep-interior default shares (court / back lane / through-alley / rear plots): poor 0.35/0.25/0.30/0.10; modest 0.45/0.30/0.15/0.10; prosperous 0.65/0.15/0.05/0.15; rich 0.75/0.10/0/0.15 — calibrated at M-1 on NG hollow-block frequency and MFCG inner-lot removal; keep-test: court share of deep blocks within band per class (§13.5).

Holes: a cut that would cross a hole is routed to the hole’s boundary (a slit via connectHole), the annulus becomes simply connected and the same ladder applies (σ = 0.098); cuts are inserted as lane/alley/secondary spines; junction fillets at street corners are a style-time smoothing, not a model change.

PartitionRecipe rows built only from splitFace, radialSplit, ringBand and insetRing: fan (k radial cuts from the centroid with alley-width gaps), semiFan (from a boundary vertex), ring (inset band around a court split into segments by slit cuts, short sides first); used by park layouts and institution templates (cloister, quadrangle).
Fabric strategy slot: S8 calls FabricStrategy.partition(district); the base registers BentCutFabric; stage 2 registers RingFabric, SquareFabric, StreetFabric.

The main plaza is S3’s reservation typed as a square face; other squares come from S7b claims sized from population; gate plazas and forecourts from S7; streets exist as geometry from S9 on; negative-space streets is purely a style; §8’s figure-ground contract fills blocks in a ground tone.

S10a block allocation (eager, town-wide) from the district’s alloc.block stream (keyed from its lineage), blocks by score then id, in three steps: (i) field-driving classes (noxious trades, middens, prisons, institutions below a block) by prosperity-free scores (downstream, downwind, extramural, frontage class, adjacency); (ii) field pass 2 adds their kernels; (iii) all other classes by capacity per band under pass 2, sub-districts receiving contiguous block groups; persisted as one block-level Allocation per block.

After S10a every district’s and the hinterland unit’s S10, S10b, S11, S12b is a pure function of the allocation records and its own sub-stream, writing only inside its own faces, so content is independent of derivation order, viewer order and worker count.

S10 step (0): a block whose interior is wall_strip gets no plots; its L3 content is built eagerly on the generation worker after S10a and before the pool freeze, covering the strip blocks on both sides of each trace at once (no district overlay may write the shared trace); commits by bandUnion the enceinte’s half-band each side, the rest of each strip as typed unbuildable residue (setback, glacis; ditch in place of glacis on an on_enceinte bailey’s town side with a dry-ditch row), each side’s parts of every tower and gatehouse; lays the margin bands (half-width 2 m each side, residue with its side’s ground role) along the settlement perimeter and any shared reservation boundary; band, glacis and tower/gate footprints are unions of these parts.

S10 (0) shared-edge bands (eager, before the freeze; J-I9) 5 ms: bandUnion on both sides at once — per enceinte the band, setback, glacis (or dry ditch), tower and gatehouse parts; the margin band (half-width 2 m: 2 m on each side) along the settlement perimeter and shared reservation boundaries (§4.7, §3.3); then the rebuild of the L3 static partitions it touched so the frozen copy holds every item in a static partition (≈ 9 000 items at CITY; fixall_kernel_r3_bench.out A; VK2-1); wall traces and ≈ 6 km of perimeter at CITY.

S10 frontage-first plots per built block: (1) classify each kerb edge as a frontage by way class; (2) block context (district kind, prosperity value and recorded band, density, growth stage) → granularity table gives frontage-width and depth bands, join maximum and vacancy-run share, interpolated along prosperity and scaled by RungProfile.granularity (frontage × and depth × every band; rich band’s join max + joinMaxDelta); GranularityLaw.bands takes the rung.

Granularity table defaults (calibratable, J-T): poor/dense frontage 4–6 m (log-normal CV 0.25), depth 12–20 m, join max 1, vacancy 0.03; modest 6–9, 18–30, 2, 0.06; prosperous 9–14, 25–40, 3, 0.08; rich 14–25 (joined), 30–60, 5, 0.05; institution/assigned by requirement, whole block above a share threshold.

S10 reads the block’s interior chosen by S8; (3) claims first: institutions and assignments smaller than a block claimSubFace (may span faces) the contiguous area and frontage class their requirement demands before ordinary plots (larger ones are S7b reservations); claims-first applies to every assign event’s scope.

S10 (4) per-frontage regions (GEO-24): block minus claims and interior partitioned into one region per frontage run by its straight skeleton, region depth capped by skeleton height and band depth; if the skeleton is downgraded (F-SKELETON) a reflex pre-cut partition (from sideRuns and splitFace) is used; validated skeleton arcs enter via insertChain; plots laid as strips perpendicular to each region’s frontage, widths drawn from the band, depth = min(band depth, region depth), side lines bent perpendicular to the frontage to the region’s rear line.

S10 (5) corners and seams: the corner plot takes the higher-class frontage and the shorter frontage’s depth; a wedge between two regions becomes a corner plot when it meets minimum width and angle, else a declared wedge class (bounded < 0.5 %) or residue; (6) residue typed court (S8 interior), yard (assigned to the adjacent plot when area < 1.5 × the plot), green, vacant, shore (shore setback).

S10 (7) joins and splits, one law: strips cut to the band’s lower end, then a merge operator joins k adjacent plots (along a frontage or back to back keeping a frontage) up to the band’s upper end, keeping members; poor bands stay at the lower end; one code path reading the same context vector.

S10 (9) alleys: slivers narrower than the minimum plot width connecting two ways become alley L3 faces (S10 never inserts an L1 spine); (10) every plot gets its ContextVector, DerivationRecord and access edges (100 %); NG’s ≈ 42 % discard becomes 0 by construction.
Party walls are shared L3 edges carrying the party_wall role in row classes (one edge per wall).
Unbuildable bands: the shore setback, the wall strips (band, inner setback, outer setback and glacis) and reservations are never plotted; ribbon plots begin beyond the outer wall strip.
Exact capacity check: after a stage’s last block, plots per class × band compared with the stage quota; a shortfall goes to S10b’s reconcile and the report (F-BUDGET-STAGE).

S10b placement: each block’s allocated classes placed onto its plots by a rule-based score over the plot context (noxious trades downstream and extramural, mills on water, markets and inns at tier-1 junctions or gates, religious precincts and faction turf as attractors, frontage class, area fit), descending score with capacity accounting; households take residential plots of their band ± drift.

Live-in (MFP-7): craft and shop rows default to liveIn; a live-in household is sited first at its workplace and recorded as the building’s dwelling; block acceptance measures share of residential-only blocks, per-block use-mix entropy and share of trade households at their workplace (§13.5).
Outside classes and farm households are placed by the hinterland unit’s own S10b on the outside plots its S10 built at S12a’s sites.

Plan–fit–reconcile (≤ 3 rounds) adjusts inside the district’s allocation where a class finds no plot (one more JOIN; class demoted within its band; surplus capacity typed yards, greens or vacant) — placement never gives up (F-SITING) and never reaches into another district; moving demand between districts happens only in S7b’s reconcile.

S10b mechanism the budget assumes: context-vector distances from per-feature-class distance rasters (16 m) computed once per model; top-k over candidates pre-filtered by district affinity and requirement class with incremental capacity.

facts.statement: Both entry points exist, read from recipe.entryMode: content-first (default) and layout-first (thumbnails, then populate); people derived lazily from the household key; a person is pinned only by an explicit edit, never by being viewed.

S11 arrangement table: row (footprint = plot ∩ frontage band of row depth, stored as one quad wing with its four corners in BaseWing.corners, stepped quads on a slope; party wall = plot side line; frontage none, rear wall or fence; dense/poor, shops, workshops); set-back compound (hall behind a forecourt, 2–5 disjoint outbuildings by a greedy packer on the plot’s OBB grid; enclosure wall or fence with a gate on the access edge; manors, inns, temples, guildhalls, farmsteads); detached (one OBB footprint with side yards, fence/railing/hedge with gate; prosperous/semi-rural sparingly); hovel (small footprint, mostly bare yard; squalid/outskirts); tents (1–3 footprints 6–15 m², class tent, fire-pit pin, dirt; squalid and shanty districts after the first half of stages); institution (claim’s own template, cloister via ring recipe; wall with gatehouse gap, churchyard wall); vacant run (no footprint; wall or fence).

Row footprints are made by S11’s boolean and passed to BuildingGenerator.outline() as fixed quad wings it never re-fits; every other arrangement’s footprints come from outline() (rect wings with per-wing ridge axes, footprint templates, axis-locked composer for institutions) inside the slot’s SlotPlan.hint (never stored).

The first carry (NP3-1): S11 inserts each footprint’s rings through every wing vertex on the wings’ union boundary; after the block’s batch commits it carries every wing onto the committed face by §2.6’s wing-carrying rule (boundary runs re-read from committed rings; a rect whose sides gain vertices records its corners), so the union of a building’s wings equals its footprint face exactly.

Scale: footprint targets × district buildingScale (0.5–2, continuous); heights per wing from class tables (floors × storey height + roof rise by pitch; eave and ridge; tower heights) with ground datum baseCm by §2.6’s deriveBase; entrance on the access edge 3 ± 1 m from the corridor; roof kind by class per wing (style sheet chooses construction); materials from MaterialRow; description, opening hours and sub-locations from the class table and naming engine; yards partitioned into typed parts.

Furniture pins (pin.* streams): main plaza one centrepiece — statue 0.6, fountain 0.3, market cross 0.1 — offset toward the longest edge for statues and 30 % of fountains; each gate plaza a well, cross or trough with p = 0.5; each block one weighted decoration row from a deck on unused plots and vacancy runs; singletons (bandstand, statue, monument) once per district in an unused plot; campfires in squalid districts; market stalls along the market square edge band and ringing a market hall, one per ≈ 150 m² of square (≤ 40), drawn as small tents.

district band: district names; footprints with outlines and entrances; yards by role; boundary treatments; every way stroked; courts; greens; crowns; way names. neighbourhood band: the family's close-up (§8.2); every named way; addresses; pins; stage 2 composes here (§8.6). building band: wings and rooms (stage 3).

The trace is S3’s (stage 1) and S5a’s (later stages), fixed before that stage’s secondaries grow; S7 builds everything on the traced wall once per enceinte after S6, in one L1 batch per enceinte; its L3/L4 geometry is built inside the wall strips by S10 and S11 after S9.

Setback and glacis lines carry the structural setback role, run gate to gate, stop at each gate’s plaza claim or arterial corridor, close on the secondaries S5c stopped at the setback band; strip faces inherit their district and are typed wall_strip; S8 never cuts a strip; both strip faces are unbuildable, so footprints ∩ (band ⊕ setback) = ∅ on both faces; ribbon plots start beyond the outer strip.

J-P29: Chose to cut the wall strips off as L1 faces at S7 and build the band, towers and gatehouses inside them after S9 over subtracting band ⊕ setback inside `kerb(F)` while committing the band at L3 before S8 — because an L3 face committed before S8 and S9 must be cleared or split by their batches, while an L1 strip boundary makes the wall a barrier the way …

wallToWay(enceinte) = retypeEdges(ChainRef(wall, enceinte), add (way, new ring road), remove wall): the wall chain becomes the spine of a primary way with ring-road width on the same edges; strips’ setback and glacis lines removed so strips merge into neighbouring faces; band, tower and gatehouse faces cleared with their finer content; S9 re-derives the corridor; towers removed; gates become junctions with a square option.

carve fate kept with a pinned deck: every through and primary way and any other way that is the only connection of the streets on its far side to a gate or the plaza; its deck (S1 (5) form, perpendicular) and re-route solved in the dry run by §7.3’s S4 local operator between the way’s nearest pinned nodes either side of S on S3’s lattice with existingFabricCost, through the deck as a fixed edge; a way already within ± 10° of the channel normal keeps its line; the old stretch between the re-route’s ends is the replaced stretch; S7’s rules give the deck its Bridge (events altered on the way, built on the bridge).

carve fate cut: every other secondary, lane, alley, cul_de_sac, track and path loses its stretch inside channel ⊕ max(bank setback, 1 m) (every cut end ≥ 1 m from the channel); a remainder dangling shorter than one block depth is pruned; quay and pier ways cut the same way and, where they met the new water at ≥ 30°, extended from the cut end to the new bank as a quay or landing.
The run of every enceinte the new or old course crosses is re-traced as data between its nearest unaffected towers, with a water gate where the new course crosses and none at the old (S7's operator)

Carve footprint R = ⋃ C exactly, C = the L1 cells that (a) the channel ⊕ (attractCm + bank setback) meets; (b) border a removed stretch, a pruned remainder or a stretch the new strips’ cuts remove; (c) border a kept way’s replaced stretch or are crossed by its new route; (d) where the channel crosses a wall, border the old run or the strip-line stretches batch (1) removes, or meet the re-traced run ⊕ (half band + setback, + glacis or berm field-side); R is the carve’s one clear region for batches (1) and (2), step (4) re-derives exactly its cells, the fate report lists exactly the protected entities in it, and locality checks require byte identity outside it less the seam exception.

Canal crossing a walled CITY's wall between two towers: no E_KEPT and no E_LEVEL; every face outside §4.11's footprint (cells the buffer meets and the way rule touches, old run's strip-line stretches and new strips' ground included) byte-identical less the seam exception; every way the new strips meet cut at their boundary; the water gate's Gate.banks on its two gate_end vertices.

Carve batch (1) L1, clear region R: clearFiner on R’s cells; cut stretches, pruned remainders and replaced stretches removed via StretchRef (a way cut in two first hands its far part to a new way by retypeEdges rekey); each kept way’s new route inserted whole with its deck’s two bank vertices (deck_end, pinned) and the span carrying deck beside way; each crossed wall run replaced by its re-traced run with the water gate’s two bank vertices carrying (gate_end, gate, 0|1) under a fresh Gate, old strip-line stretches removed (ends by splitThrough at the feet); ways the new strips meet cut; every other non-way L1 edge the banks cross (perimeter or district-boundary stretch, setback/glacis line outside a re-traced run) split at its two bank points by splitThrough with an anchor contact name (smallest free ordinal, from 2 on an enceinte) and the stretch between removed; the map border split the same way but kept whole across the channel; deck_end, gate_end and contact-name vertices are the prepared vertices.

Carve batch (2) L0, clear region R, KernelTx.prepared = batch (1)’s prepared vertices: the channel ring is inserted, attracts onto and promotes them, stripping contact names; each deck span (the kept way’s own edge between its promoted bank vertices) now crosses as the Bridge’s deck; no L0 edge crosses the channel, the water stays one L0 face; any other contact with finer geometry is E_LEVEL or E_KEPT back to the dry run.

Carve batch (3) L1: each kept quay or pier extended from its cut end to the new bank (end a Steiner vertex on the L0 bank line); S7’s operator re-cuts setback, glacis and intervallum lines along each re-traced run from the feet, closing them on the new banks, and builds towers and the water gate’s Gate record naming its two gate_end vertices in banks.

facts.statement: RosterTables {classes: BuildingClassRow[] ({id, use, perCapita [lo,hi], perOther? {class, ratio}, min, max, firstAtPopulation, requires (water|coast|route|farmland|ore|stone|timber|fish|clay)[], outside, liveIn, cluster?, noxious, lifestyleBand, shopProb, priority, footprintM2 [p10,p50,p90], floors, heights, coverageByBand, siteplan, subLocations, openingHours, tags}); institutions; government (offices and seat classes per government kind); religions; households (size distributions by class); professions; farm: FarmTable; names: NamePack; provenance}.

Sequential roster (FTG-14, shape only): a virtual population advances on a fixed grid of Δ = 10 people up to the rung maximum; at each grid point each class’s target is a monotone step function (perCapita/perOther ratios, core vs shop pools, lifestyle-banded pools with rare outliers, hard min/max, size gates firstAtPopulation, resource gates from SiteResources); every class below target receives its next building in class-priority then class-id order; each draw keyed by the building ordinal roster/<class>/<ordinal>; the run records each building’s appearance population; manifest(P) = every (class, ordinal) appearing at or below P.

Prefix stability: manifest(P₂) ⊇ manifest(P₁) whenever P₂ > P₁ (property test on 1 000 seeds); an epoch’s delta demand is exactly the suffix; a population fall selects the suffix in reverse order; negative deltas only from declared circumstance events; §7.8’s population control monotone by construction.

rosterMode: minimiseUnemployment (default: at each grid point, when the unemployed share exceeds a table threshold, the workplace class with the largest weighted job deficit receives one extra building) or matchRatios (configured ratios only); both grid-sequential, both prefix-stable.

Roster output: demand per class with area/frontage requirement classes, district affinities, cluster tags, live-in flags, outside flags and wealth bands; the character vector (mercantile/ecclesiastic/military/agrarian/squalid …) shifts the ratios.

Government: the government circumstance selects a GovernmentRow whose offices force seats (crown seat → royal castle or palace; seigneurial lordship → lord’s castle or keep; ecclesiastical lordship → bishop’s palace beside the cathedral; chartered commune → town hall and guild halls; merchant oligarchy → merchants’ hall) plus a military share (guard posts per 1 000; barracks at CITY and above near castle or gates); castle toggle auto reads it.

Religion: ReligionRows with worshipper shares (shifted by the character vector), practice share and clergy per 1 000; temples per religion proportional to practising worshippers; each religion has a faction.

After the roster, S7b allocates, S10b places, and a bounded plan–fit–reconcile loop (≤ 3 rounds, inside each district’s allocation) trims the lowest-priority classes where capacity is short and types surplus capacity as yards, greens or vacant plots; population honoured within tolerance and reported.
Pinning is an explicit edit, never a view (LC-16): opening a person writes nothing to document, hash or undo stack; which people a viewer has seen is per-user view state.

A person-table edit applies to households created afterwards; existing people change only through a diffed “re-derive people” action; an epoch ages everyone through the birth epoch; births and deaths are epoch events of the owner-staged engine; superseded households’ pinned or edited people are re-homed to the household inheriting the address or reported as orphans.

People storage: aggregates plus explicitly pinned people (kilobytes for a 50 000-person metropolis) until the relation store is materialised; then ≈ 12 bytes per relation, ≈ 1.8 MB raw for 50 000 people at ≈ 3 relations each, reported per 10 k population as the O7 module metric.

AncestryRow {id, lifeStages {name, fromAge}[], maxAge, heightCmBand, nameGrammar, appearanceTemplates} and a partnering matrix are data; the base ships one human ancestry, further ancestries only through setting packs.

Person.status ∈ worker, unemployed, retired, student, dependent; a dependent has a carer whose schedule it follows; when a carer is removed the household (then family unit) supplies the next carer by rule, reported; a dangling carer is a reference-integrity violation.

Appearance text from the §10.4 engine: weighted option tables per ancestry, line templates with substitution, conditional lines (gender, age, value predicate), fallback lines, article agreement; our own templates.

@plat/sim relations: the first run materialises the relation store by one global pass on the content/relations stream in person-key order (family units, partnerships, parent/child, siblings, carer/caree, friends, rivals, business and religious ties, affairs), persisted with lifecycle and reference integrity.

@plat/sim work: professions ↔ workplaces by greedy matching with id tie-breaks, persisted as Posting records; after an edit only changed workplaces’ postings and the unemployed pool re-matched in person-key order; unfilled postings tracked and reported.

@plat/sim occupancy(dayType, hour) resolves the whole population in person-key order in two passes (primary behaviours from profession templates; then occupancy criteria filling SubLocation capacities with relax options), cached per (day type, hour), invalidated by edits touching the people or buildings; whereIs(person, day, hour) reads the cache; resource provides/uses edges are data.
Simulation module (§10.3; FTG-11): one hour of occupancy for 50 000 people ≤ 50 ms in the worker, with a cost-model test (§13.2); never on the one-click path.

Calendar: configurable (hours/day, days/week, rest days, weekday names); the time is the view key time — view.set {time} sets it and sim.advance {hours} advances it over the bridge; occupancy recomputed for the new hour; neither changes the model.

Factions: seats on plots, influence field over districts (used by prosperity drivers and the grammar), named roles with member criteria and counts, goals with methods and progress, a secret flag; role headcounts reconciled with the seat building’s working capacity (excess filled by members housed elsewhere, reported).

EventTemplate {id, preconditions (predicates over relations, factions, buildings), weight, effects: EditEvent[]} ranks candidate events per building; starting one applies its effects as logged undoable edit events; data dictionaries (ages, genders, ancestries) are append-only and id-referenced.

Schema stubs (D-32), in the base registry from M1, empty until @plat/sim materialises them: ItemRow {id, category, unit, basePrice (pack coin unit), providedBy?}; ServiceRow {id, providedBy, basePrice}; Stock {building, item, qty}; PriceTable {multiplier, overrides} (global price edits are editTable events); PersonTraits {traits, motivation, mannerism, hobbies, education} derived from the person key; StatBlockPack {id, attributes, base, professionModifiers} off by default (D-3).

Query = gazetteer {text?, kinds?, page?} | people {type?, race?, gender?, profession?, workplace?, ageRange?, household?, district?, page?} (COV-FTG-C13) | hit {view, x, y} | whereIs {person, day, hour} | relations {person, up, down} (family tree, COV-FTG-C11) | inView {view} (features-in-view list, COV-FTG-A24; non-visual route, J-S19) | fates {token, page} (full fate list, then renames; VD4-4).

Naming engine: an original English-fantasy grammar (D-6) in our own Tracery-class engine (rules with modifiers, feature guards, weighted decks, conditional lines, article agreement) plus syllable and Markov generators over our own corpora; folk-contraction as an EVO event (≤ 3 syllables a parameter).

The same engine writes descriptions (a district’s one-line summary of its mix and features; each building’s description) and people’s appearance lines; descriptions regenerate when their inputs change unless edited.

Per-culture generators and user lists: every AncestryRow and culture row names its own grammar and corpora; a user-uploaded list (plain text, one entry per line) becomes a user corpus (syllable and Markov model trained at load) stored as pack data in the packs block with author user; selecting it is an adjust entering user:<content hash> with shipped: false, so a town whose history selects it never emits a link; the pack holds the corpus and the keyed row operation setting the chosen culture/ancestry row’s corpus field.

When an added or removed pack changes a naming slice (a grammar row, or the corpus a culture or ancestry row field names), S13a re-draws exactly the unedited names whose naming records cite a changed slice (§6.3 case (4); VD3-2), renames listed for confirmation

SettingPack {id, version, author, date, licence, provides {grammars?, corpora? {id, kind personal|place|word, entries}[], ancestries?, religions?, appearance?, rosterPatch? {table: RosterTableId, baseVersion, ops: RowOp[]}[], tablePatch? {table: TableId (naming, culture, ancestry), baseVersion, ops}[], styleHints?: Partial<StyleSheet>}}.

A pack is data, never code: schema-validated (zod), every entry with author and date, loaded as one layer of the override chain between shipped defaults and preset, recorded in the recipe or the adding adjust by id, version and content hash; the content of every non-shipped pack in the pack set is copied into the document’s packs block and stays there while any event of the log names it; a link is emitted only when every pack of the pack set is shipped.

Overrides are row operations, never positional patches: an override records { op, rowKey, field, value, baseRowHash }; when a newer table version changes or removes that row, the override is reported as an orphan - kept, not applied - with old base row, new row and user value side by side
The base ships exactly one pack, the original English-fantasy set; further packs are the owner’s adopted “setting packs later” default (D-6); adding one is a file, not a code change.

Stage 2 summary: any district can be opened as a detailed neighbourhood; shared streets, walls and shores are drawn once by the base; each district has its own random stream so rerolling one never touches another; NG’s four templates (area, street, square, ring) become layout strategies selectable per district.
SeamAmendment {kind baseLane|tJunction, spine, vertex: VertexRef (junction, inserted at L1 by splitThrough or as a lane end), portal, by, cause generation|EditId}.

SeamContract (a district’s view assembled on demand from its Seam records, never stored): {district, seams (ring order), sharedGeometry: ownedByBase, plotLinesOnBoundary, alleysOnBoundary, interiorSamples {prosperity, density, greenery, terrain}}.

NeighbourhoodRequest {district, key: PlatKey, boundary: TypedBoundary, seam: SeamContract, context: DistrictContext (kind, venue mix, character, prosperity band, growth stage, water, walls, slope), laid {blocks, plots, alleys}, layer ground|sky (sky: no portals, no roads, own terrain optional), mode refine|replace, strategy: FabricStrategyId (bent-cut refine | ring | square | street replace), params, outlineTemplate? disc|d_shape|lozenge|crescent|spindle (standalone and sky only), lod: neighbourhood}; streams keyed from the district lineage on demand, nothing stored.

NeighbourhoodResult {blocks, ways, plots, buildings, greens, pins, labels: LabelEntity[], seams: SeamReport, report: StageReport}; SeamReport {portalsTotal, portalsConnected (= total), unconnected, addedPortals, sharedEdgeHausdorffCm (must be 0), fieldJumps {at, field, delta, hard}[] (a soft-seam jump outside its band is a soft-invariant failure), superseded {old, new}[]}; NeighbourhoodStrategy.generate(req, ctx, k) → KernelResult<NeighbourhoodResult>; Pin defined in §2.7.

Seam edge type = the first its role rows give: way → way; wall → wall; shore or bank → water (cliff where the bank kind is cliff); reserved → reserve; district_bound alone (perimeter) → field; border or margin → frame; sky arena outline → sky.

A reserve run is a reservation boundary two districts share with no way on it (plaza, precinct or market edge where validateEdge stopped); its shared geometry is the reserved chain and the two margin-band parts S10 (0) lays along it; no portals; a close-up ends its plot lines on its own part’s inner edge and writes neither part (a replace close-up’s scoped regeneration re-lays its own side’s part).
hard flag from the editable seam-type row: wall, water, cliff, frame, sky hard; way, field soft; reserve by reservation kind — castle and precinct hard; plaza, market, park, institution soft.
II.1 rule (1): the base generates every shared edge once and both districts read it.

II.1 rule (2): a close-up either refines (neighbourhood-LOD presentation detail — roof construction and hatching, surfaces, pins, trees, local street names — as a pure function of the committed base state, sub-seed, strategy and params, never changing L1–L4 geometry) or replaces the base plots with a ring/square/street template layout; templates are FabricStrategy registrations selected per district, laid by the base engine with seams by construction.

II.1 rule (3) seam amendment (GEO-30): a close-up may end a street on a shared boundary spine; each end is a T-junction inserted by splitThrough at L1 so the spine stays one chain, recorded as a SeamAmendment (tJunction) and a new portal in the shared Seam record.

The neighbour step (VK2-11) is the only write on the other side, for a close-up T-junction and for a lane a reroll adds or removes on a shared spine: one L2 batch whose only face is the neighbour’s half-corridor strip inserts one corridor_split edge from the junction vertex to the foot of its perpendicular on the neighbour’s kerb; the strip holds no L3 content so nothing is cleared or re-derived; the kerb end lands by attraction within attractCm on a kerb vertex (a plot-line end or footprint corner promoted to L2; coarser rings gain it, each equal to its prior ring with it removed) or otherwise splits the kerb at L2 (adding the vertex to rings through it and to a fronting building’s wing ring).

Removing the street reverses the neighbour step (undo, reroll or later edit): removeEdges takes out the corridor_split, the strip is one face again, a kerb vertex the step created dissolves and leaves the wing ring, a promoted vertex returns to its level by demotion (keeping its split flag unless a warp has since moved it or its neighbours), so the kerb’s L2 route, index, digest and every touched ring are as before, with later kerb changes kept.
II.1 (3)'s neighbour step at a plot-line end, then the street removed by a reroll (not an undo): the kerb's L2 route, index and digest equal to those before the step.
S1 (stage-2 feature) acceptance: portal connection 100 %, shared-edge Hausdorff 0.

II.1 rule (4): footprint hashes at city LOD and neighbourhood LOD identical for every entity a refine close-up covers; a refine close-up is derived and outside the base digest until a closeup event is logged before its first edit; a replace close-up re-derives its entities under the anchor rule and records §6.3’s successions in SeamReport.superseded.

II.1 rule (5): the standalone no-portal mode is the same call with a synthetic boundary from an outline template (disc, D-shape, lozenge, crescent, spindle) through §4.2’s closed-outline routine; the sky-island call is the same request with layer sky, an outline from that routine, optional own terrain echoing the ground, no roads in or out, and a reason; its shadow projected by §8.4.

II.1 rule (6): lanes the base’s S8 ends on a district-boundary spine are recorded in the same Seam record with kind baseLane and kept at least a portal gap from every other portal; a close-up reads them like any portal; a reroll changes only the seam records it is party to, the vertices it inserts or removes and their neighbour steps.

J-P33: Chose one `Seam` record per boundary run, read by both districts, over a contract copied into each district — because one record cannot disagree with itself and a re-derivation then changes the seams a district is party to rather than its neighbour's district record (II.1; NF-P6).

facts.statement: RingFabric: concentric secondary ring roads at a radius law (table) are the only seed geometry (no template radials); bands processed outside-in, one hole-aware bent-cut recursion per annulus (σ = 0.098); each band’s first cut is a slit opening the annulus; later cuts are its radials arriving at right angles; each band draws from its own sub-stream so radials are staggered band to band; outermost radials reaching the boundary use II.1 (3)’s seam amendment.

SquareFabric: mode carved places a rectangular or round plaza face at the centroid or a portal, sized from population, frontages typed square, then the bent cut on the remainder; mode void carves nothing (plots facing a chosen open area left unbuilt); both modes place a centrepiece pin (monument, statue or fountain) at the nexus; the square row’s default is void (also for every square pair of the D-5 panel); a non-default mode is recorded as fabricParams.squareMode = 1 (carved; 0/absent = void), set by setAttr.

J-S42: Chose `SquareFabric`'s `void` mode for NG's `square` pairs and as the default of II.2's `square` row over the `carved` plaza — because NG's own square is the void its unbuilt plots leave, the panel must compare like with like, and a panel should rate the default a user gets — …

facts.statement: StreetFabric: a main street between two portals with plots directly on it, bent cuts on the deeper faces; template road widths (ring roads and template streets) fixed per district, drawn once from the district stream; cut streets follow §4.6’s width law.

A template is its seed geometry plus the number of sub-areas it hands to the bisector, a data row plus a strategy class; the area template is the base’s default; templates chosen by context read the district context (quay district → quay-parallel street; intramural → ring near the wall; stepped street on a slope).

Block content dispatch: a stage-2 table maps (block area, spacing to nearest green, spacing to nearest landmark or manor block, district kind, prosperity band) → weighted choice among Normal/Manor/Empty/Green (with a green target per band from §4.9’s rules); a minimum landmark spacing row keeps landmark and manor blocks apart.

Neighbourhood-tier pins (wells, fountains, large trees, statues, monuments, bandstands) placed in yards and squares by a probability gate per kind and band as refine-mode presentation detail; the base’s own pins are model entities at every LOD; local street identities (names, surfaces, widths) from way records and the naming grammar; context features (quays, intervallum, stepped streets, bridge approaches) are constraints; a manor compound’s enclosure wall and gate are the base’s PlotBound treatments.

Preset table — hatched (NG family; stage-2 close-up): city = masses in lit roof tone, ground = paper, street stripe in road, wood fills; district = two-tone roofs by fakeGablePerWing; neighbourhood = tapered-triangle hatching from the ridge (≈ 17 per wing), one prism shadow pass, lobed crowns in two greens, depth-sorted trees, chimneys and wells; building = per-wing hatching. Ink-family variants parchment (texture role), bw-print (monochrome), night (lights role with glow instances); painterly reserved (VG family for the village product: colour ramps, water bands, relief on, spotlight vignette, selective outlining).

Persistence (LC-18): a refine close-up is derived data (pure function of committed base state, sub-seed, strategy, params; identical eager or lazy; outside the base hash; never stored); the first edit inside is preceded by a logged closeup event, from which point the close-up enters the digest under closeups and replays exactly; editing a close-up element records an instance-override event on the host entity and ordinal (persists, undoes, replays, re-matched by position; carried over on re-derivation, orphans reported).

Close-up lanes, plots and houses are base entities (renaming a lane or locking a house is an ordinary base edit); a replace close-up is a model edit: setAttr(district.fabric, template) plus a scoped regeneration — logged, hashed, same for every viewer, visible at city LOD.

Workflow: open any district at neighbourhood LOD from the city view; “Same kind, new seed” per district with locks (New random scoped to the district); per-district reroll isolation — every other district byte-identical except the seam exception (bounding ways’ chains and Corridor records; half-corridor strips both sides and junction wedges at vertices D inserts or removes — S8 baseLane ends and close-up T-junctions — which on the neighbour side are only the neighbour step; neighbouring cells, plots, footprints and wing rings through those vertices, each the same polygon with the vertices removed; the Seam records D is party to); export of one district as its own SVG/PNG/VTT scene.

What the base already carries for stage 2 (base requirements): typed boundary edges with hard flags and portals in shared Seam records (incl. S8 lane ends); shared geometry owned by the base with seam amendment and splitThrough; boundary plot lines and alleys; seam-continuous fields with hard/soft seams; per-district streams keyed from lineage; hole-aware bent cut; FabricStrategy slot with BentCutFabric from M1 and three template fabrics at M5; stored wings, boundary treatments, complete pin vocabulary; neighbourhood LOD band and hatched programs; world-aligned tile pyramid invalidated per district; per-district regeneration ≤ 30 ms; close-up persistence rule and instance-override event; sky context and outline templates.

Stage-2 readiness of the base (M1 exit): on every B-CITY city every district’s SeamContract resolves completely — every boundary run in exactly one Seam record, every seam edge one of II.1’s types (way-less shared reservation boundary as reserve with its two margin-band parts), every portal vertex resolves, every baseLane portal matches exactly one S8 lane end and vice versa — 100 %; a New random on each of 20 districts per city changes nothing outside its seam exception.

Stage 2 acceptance (M5 exit) from SeamReport: portals connected 100 % (added included); shared-edge Hausdorff 0; soft-seam field jumps within band; neighbourhood-LOD footprint hash = city-LOD hash for every refine-covered entity; opening a district ≤ NG’s recorded 10–96 ms at comparable counts; per-district regeneration ≤ 30 ms; reroll isolation outside the seam exception; model hash unchanged by opening/closing/reopening any number of districts.

Floating islands (AM-2): the toggle creates 1–3 islands; reason prosperity (by rule the roster’s richest demand for up to three districts’ worth of households is allocated by S7b to sky pseudo-districts, S7b creating their Allocations first; plot land = area from IslandRule.areaHaBand on island.place × dense-core plot share, richest band down) or institution (one unique institution from an IslandInstitution row or an assignment).

A floating island is a SkyIsland with an organic oval outline from §4.2’s routine (the disc or lozenge outline template), an elevation from a band row, optionally its own terrain from S1 with an echo request (relief echo or own; a conjured river with the ground river’s bearing and width law); its districts laid by the ordinary pipeline through a NeighbourhoodRequest with layer sky; placed over water, fields or outskirts by default, over the core only by assignment; occlusion mode a rendering choice; no relation to the underground; shadow via the shadow pass; exports as its own layer.

IslandRule {reason prosperity|institution, maxIslands 1|2|3, elevationCmBand, areaHaBand, placement (water|fields|outskirts)[], terrain none|echo|own}; SkyStrategy.place(doc, rules, allocations (S7b’s sky allocations), ctx, k) → KernelResult<SkyIsland[]>, a Stage registered after S7b by declared I/O (inputs: sky allocations and ground plan; outputs: islands sized to each allocation, their arenas and districts).

Sewers: SewerStrategy registers as a stage after S11 (inputs: ways with flowToward, drainage raster and outfalls of §2.3, plots and buildings with the class table’s drain column, the underground plat; output Tunnel records); rule families follow-streets | drainage-lines | mixed; presets historical (open gutters, a few culverted mains, cess pits by class) and navigable (large vaulted mains with chambers); renders by §8.4’s cut-away or overlay; exports as the underground layer; SewerStrategy.derive(doc, rules, ctx, k) → KernelResult<Tunnel[]>.
The village generator is a separate owner-staged product with its own ladder (thorp → hamlet → village); the base carries hooks and does not pay for it.

Village would reuse unchanged: kernel and plat; the site model (descent rivers with carved field, level-set ponds, coast routine) and, for VG’s order, a RiverStrategy laying a terrain-independent spline course (6–7 control points) first and asking S1 to carve to it; sequential roster and lazy people; frontage-first plots and site-plan tables (cottage, farmstead, detached-in-yard classes); hinterland presets incl. VG sector look; the palisade enceinte kind; display list, style sheets, relief tier and reserved painterly slot; document, edits, exports, API.
Village hook 1: a density stage before its network — a VillageStrategy registers a density StageDecl whose output the network stage declares as input (pipeline = topological order of declared I/O).

Village hook 2: a palisade before its roads — hull of the populated points of a 10 × 10 lattice over the density field, cleaned and smoothed (live VG build 19365073); registered as an EnceinteStrategy; its tracker-steered NetworkStrategy receives it through the enceintes input.

Village hooks 3–4: a tracker-steered network with one through-road and partial driveways, a “houses along ways” FabricStrategy with no block cutting; a village is one district of kind village (one quarter), blocks = large faces between ways, plots line the ways, so building ⊂ plot ⊂ block ⊂ district holds unchanged.

Village size ladder below TOWN: THORP ≈ 20–80, HAMLET ≈ 80–400, VILLAGE ≈ 400 up to (not including) 1 500 inhabitants (VG spans ≈ 130–1 700); a request ≥ 1 500 is a base TOWN; below 1 500 LadderRouter routes to the village product; village default not walled (walls a rule keyed on rung); VG’s tree stream a keyed sub-stream; spotlight vignette and grass tufts as painterly programs; relief marks already the base’s relief tier (built at M2b).

Not-precluded checks (44/44): the strategy registry admits every strategy above; the level model tolerates nearly empty L2/L3; model time near-linear in building count; every VG rendering row has a program or preset slot; terrain-and-water as one picture is the base model. The base does not pay for tracker steering, the palisade construction, spotlight/painterly look, palisade look, VG’s grammar and tag vocabulary.

The unit of failure is one kernel transaction (batch), never the map; the pipeline has no whole-map restart path and no silent seed swap (MFCG City.hx catch-all and VG seed swap are the removed behaviours)

Each step's failure response is a short fixed ordered list: check, repair locally, retry that piece with its next stream, simpler shape, substitute (uncuttable block to court or green), omit and report; nothing on the list touches anything outside the failing piece

Feasibility by construction before geometry (tier 0): S1 guarantees river descent, S2 derives stage budgets from demand, S3 sites the centre relative to the river and reserves castle, plaza and institution precincts, so hard constraints are met before fabric is cut
Every stochastic step has a declared, bounded, deterministic ladder; every rung taken writes a report line with a cause code and its tier; the ladder path is replayable from the printed stream key
Invariants police validity, not regularity: FTG's sheared minority of quads and NG's wedge class are kept

Every limit that can change output is a work (operation-count) limit, never a time limit (GEO-2), and scales with the size of its scope (NF-S10); each stage declares its work limits (counts of kernel calls, proposals, candidates, skeleton events, recursion depth) as laws over its batch scope's counts, not fixed numbers per rung

WorkUnit = 'plots' / 'buildings' / 'households' / 'landHa' / 'frameCells' / 'latticeNodes' / 'faces' / 'vertices'; WorkLimitLaw { counter: string; unit: WorkUnit; perUnit: number; floor: number; log2?: boolean }; WorkLimits = WorkLimitLaw[] carried as StageDecl.workLimits
Work-limit law: limit = floor + perUnit x count(unit, scope); with log2 set (recursion depths) limit = floor + perUnit x ceil(log2(count))

count(unit, scope) reads only model values committed before the batch runs (request population via S2 demand and stage quotas, Allocation records, scope land area, frame cells, lattice size), never a measurement; a district batch gets a limit proportional to its district and a scoped re-run (edit, regeneration, replay) gets exactly the limit its scope had in the full run
A kernel call that reaches its count returns E_WORK_LIMIT (§3.1) and the ladder treats it like any other failure (F-WORK), so identical inputs take identical rungs on every machine

Work-limit coefficients are set by rule: each = 99.9th percentile of measured work per unit on B-CITY-lite x 1.5, computed by the spike or milestone that builds the stage and recomputed whenever the stage's code changes (a declared shift if output moves)

Work-limit confirmation (M1, then every nightly cost-model run, §13.2): the F-WORK hit rate per stage is flat across each population band - at the top of every band it exceeds the bottom's rate by at most 1 per 1 000 batches

facts.statement: Pre-decided fallback for a failing counter: raise its perUnit to the measured 99.9th percentile per unit at the band's top x 1.5 and re-run the sweep; a coefficient change that moves output is a declared shift (§6.4)
The millisecond budgets of §12 are reporting targets and cost tests only, never output-changing limits

J-DET-3: Chose operation-count work limits for every output-affecting budget over wall-clock watchdogs — because a watchdog makes one seed give different towns on slow, throttled or busy machines; wall clock only postpones or resumes lazy work (§5.1).

facts.statement: Retries are not rerolls (LC-5): ladder retries (tier 3) draw from the 'attempt' key component, which restarts at 0 for every reroll of the scope entity with the same cap; New random advances the 'reroll' component (§6.1, §7.1), so every reroll has its full ladder
Content digest: the Merkle node of an entity's subtree computed with identity (address, lineage) and lifecycle left out - kinds, geometry and attributes only

New random is checked to change its scope (NF-D6): after re-derivation each scope entity's content digest is compared with its pre-event value; an unchanged entity advances its reroll once more and re-derives, up to reroll.maxAdvance times; if still unchanged it keeps its original reroll (nothing changes, not even lineage) and the report lists 'no alternative within the ladder'; advances run on the dry run's overlay so only the chosen result commits; the event stores the rerolls actually used so replay repeats neither comparison nor advances
reroll.maxAdvance is a table value, default 3

B-EDIT minimal scopes: New random on a block holding one plot, a plot with a one-building row site plan, a one-cell district, a ruined building, and a person whose every attribute path is locked either changes the scope's content or reports it - never a silent no-op, never an identity change without a content change

Requested features are counted by delivery tier: full (tier <= 3), degraded (tiers 4-5), omitted (tier 6); acceptance counts a tier-6 omission of a requested feature as a failure (§15.2); 'no restart path' is a design property, not an acceptance number

The seven tiers: 0 feasibility by construction; 1 constraint check (typed KernelResult / invariant, nothing committed); 2 local repair (attract, widen, merge, re-inset, re-claim, re-site); 3 bounded local regeneration (next ATTEMPT inside current REROLL); 4 simpler primitive (bent cut to straight cut on mean normal to perpendicular mid-run cut; skeleton to medial axis for labels / plain roof for roofs); 5 substitution (uncuttable block becomes court, green or landmark plot, NG's rule); 6 documented omission, never silent
Tier 3 cap: at most 3 attempts per reroll

Tiers 2-5 run inside the transaction on the overlay; tier 6 commits without the feature; no tier re-runs another stage and no tier rerolls anything outside the failing entity's scope, because every retry draws from (entity lineage, concern, reroll, attempt) and nothing else reads that stream (§6.1)
Rows marked with a dagger carry a ladder whose mechanism another area owns (named with its section); the row repeats that area's rungs so the table and §3-§4, §9 agree

F-NUM (precision failure of an optional chain; GEO-3): detection E_OUT_OF_RANGE, E_BELOW_MIN_EDGE, E_BELOW_MIN_ANGLE, E_SELF_INTERSECT on optional chains, warnings W_SNAP_PASSES, W_ACUTE_CORNER; ladder for optional chains only (growth proposals, optional lanes, decorative lines): re-propose from the next attempt stream, then reject the chain with a report line (an uninsertable proposal is simply not a street)
Every kernel primitive is fuzzed with two input families (random and constructive degeneracies) and held to 0 crashes, 0 hangs (hard timeout), 0 invalid outputs at the sizes of §13.8's tiers.

F-CUT (bent cut fails; GEO-23) at S8, S10: detection E_NOT_TWO_CROSSINGS or a child failing simple/min area/min width/min angle; ladder: reflex pre-cut (face with a reflex vertex deeper than the band's block depth split from it first, and at antenna roots) -> redraw cut position x2 -> straight cut on the mean normal -> always-succeeding cut perpendicular to the longest side run through its midpoint, clipped to the face's own component -> substitution (court / green / landmark / joined plot for the largest unplaced class of the district's allocation, never live roster state, §4.7)
F-CUT substitution is allowed only for faces <= 2 x the band's upper block area

F-CUT property test: on 10^5 random concave and holed faces the ladder terminates in <= 6 kernel calls and the face count never decreases; built-area share left as court or green residue reported per district (soft band <= 5 %); NG signature regression (§13.5); MFCG baseline 19 skipped cuts and 3 of 16 cities restarted for 'bad poly'
facts.values: 10^5 faces; <= 6 kernel calls; residue soft band <= 5 %; baseline 19 / 3 of 16

facts.statement: F-CORRIDOR (union makes slivers or a collapsed block; GEO-35, GEO-4) at S9: a face below its class minimum width or area after corridorUnion; ladder: absorbSliver (merge across a partition edge, else keep face as 'residue'; a structural edge is never deleted) -> downgrade the offending lane to alley width -> retype the lane 'invisible' and log
B-CITY: 0 faces below their class minimum width and area; 0 structural edges deleted

F-OUTLINE (closed outline not simple; GEO-13) at S1 (coasts, lakes, islands, sky-island outlines): displaced outline self-intersects or loops; ladder: clamp the displacement -> repair by non-zero union -> type each resulting loop (islet / pond / absorbed), reported

Inside an edit the F-RIVER re-trace is confined to the edited reach and the inlet and centre rungs are not offered (the edit is then declared Re-derive from S1, §7.3); a moved course knot (moveCourseKnot, §7.1) is never re-traced away from the user's position: a course through it whose carve would exceed carveMaxCm returns F-EDIT with the nearest position along the drag within the cap

facts.statement: 1 000 seeds x {river, coast+river} x rung (WaterSetting spelling, §13.3; VS2-5, VS4-5): 'river within the core when requested' = 100 % (MFCG baseline: 7 of 10 attempts fail at size 80)

F-CONTOUR (contour crosses a shore; GEO-14) at S1; ladder: the coast construction of §4.2 S1, then clip every contour to the land faces in vector space before emission (always succeeds), reported; never an abort path
Steep-coast, cliff and spit fixtures: contours crossing water 0; 0 S1 aborts

F-SITE (no valid centre) at S3: every candidate fails slope/land/flood tests, or polycentric nuclei closer than the separation floor (§4.2 S3 (6)); ladder: relax the slope threshold one step -> the largest land component's centroid band -> report; for nuclei: re-site the later nucleus (<= 3) -> merge the two under one enceinte with a cross wall, reported
F-SITE: corpus sweep over relief characters; twin-town fixtures: walls apart by the floor or one shared enceinte with a cross wall
Scripted requests on 100 seeds with pathological sites; O4 (a): 100 % of through-roads at a named destination or reported; road and deck agree on 100 % of crossings

F-BUDGET-STAGE (capacity below demand; FTG-2) at S5: detection S5d's area test (stage's grown area vs its plot demand at the bands' plot areas); ladder: one bounded top-up before the next stage (widen the stage boundary by the shortfall at the stage's measured plot density, grow only the added ring, recompute the trace) -> accept and report the shortfall; the exact plot check after S10 feeds F-SITING

B-CITY: gates on arterials 100 %; main gates = N exact; roads leaving each walled stage = its N main gates plus any §4.2 S3 (7) harbour gate (NP4-5); 0 non-gate crossings; 100 % of quays reachable without crossing a wall except at a gate on coastal and river seeds; MFCG baseline sealed cities at 0 main gates without fallback

F-CASTLE (compactness / overlap; MFP-3) at S3, S7: detection compactness < 0.75 or the claim overlaps water or the plaza; ladder at S3 (bailey sited, before the trace welds to it), inside the reservation: equalise the claim's angles (<= 20 passes) -> bloat in 5 % steps up to the band's top -> re-site (reported) -> keep without a bailey (reported)

F-PLOT (unusable plot; GEO-24) at S10: frontage < min, wedge angle < 12 deg, landlocked; ladder: per-frontage regions (when the block's skeleton downgrades, a reflex pre-cut partition instead) -> merge into the neighbour -> insert an alley to give access -> typed residue (court / vacant)

F-SITING (roster item unplaced; LC-2, FTG-1) at S10b: the eager allocation cannot place a class's demand in its affinity district; ladder: reconcile inside the district's allocation (JOIN at block granularity -> a whole block -> the district edge); cross-district moves only in the allocation's own reconcile (S7b) -> reduce the manifest and report 'unplaced'; decided eagerly, never by lazy-district placement order, never silently

F-SITEPLAN (footprint does not fit; FTG-13) at S11 and the terrain operator: setbacks leave no rectangle >= the class minimum, or after a terrain stroke a row footprint's fall exceeds skirtMaxCm; ladder: on slopes above skirtMaxCm stepped wings first -> lower coverage one step -> next arrangement (compound -> detached -> hovel -> 'tents' row where the class allows) -> vacant plot typed yard, reported

O17 plot model, site plans, heights (must; §2.5–§2.6, §4.7 S11, §8.4): (a) coverage within the table [C]; (b) multi-footprint plots > 0 for institutions, manors, inns and farms [C]; (c) party-wall share by band, attached ≥ 90 % in dense bands [P — NG 39–43 %, 95–99 %]; (d) streetwall continuity ≥ MFCG Lots mode, walled or fenced frontage counted [P]; (e) yards owned 100 % [C]; (f) footprints fit 100 % [C]; (g) heights on 100 %, shadow ∝ height r ≥ 0.99 [C]; (h) ≤ 5 µs per plot median for site plans (§12.4) [C]; (i) footprint hash identical across LOD [C].

F-SKELETON (GEO-8, GEO-2) at S11, S13a: output validator fails (non-planar skeleton, non-monotone faces, inconsistent heights) or the skeleton's work limit (events processed) is reached (E_WORK_LIMIT, never a timeout); ladder: labels use a sampled medial axis (§3.8, used by §9.3); roofs a plain roof (VIS-11): footprint drawn with no ridge or hip lines, roof kind 'plain', heights unchanged; near-rectangular footprints never reach this row (exact OBB roof is the primary construction)

Ladder coverage (G-R9): every rung of every ladder in §5.2 is reachable by a fixture; each downgrade (medial axis, plain-roof downgrade, straight cut, substitution) is exercised; no roof line lies outside its footprint; a skeleton failure is never a crash nor a visual surprise.

F-LABEL ladder, view side (every rung reached counted in the report): (1) preferred spine at size ∝ √area, never below the floor; (2) the short name form; (3) straight label on the OBB axis, one line or two lines broken at a space (two lines at a breakAt position); (4) the OBB arc; (5) the quarter tree; (6) a declared overflow: ≤ 20 % of glyph area outside the face, never over a protected obstacle or another label; (7) a legend entry: a numbered disc on the face and a row in the legend (§9.5).

Label acceptance (B-ZOOM; default view of every rung; bundled font): every node of the city cut (min(N_q, number of districts), §4.5) labelled at or above the floor, and at the matched sizes within ± 1 of the 9 / 12 / 18 district labels MFCG's plain sweep draws at sizes 40 / 80 / 130 (captures/mfcg/exports-sweep-2026-09-25/README.md); 0 protected overlaps; 0 collisions at settled views and during a scripted zoom sweep, pins included; every placed glyph's text/halo pair at or above the label floor from rendered pixels (§8.3); overflows, legend fallbacks, quarter substitutions and hidden pins reported; ≥ 99 % of all area-label glyph area inside its face (O13 a), capping the overflow rung at 5 % of on-map area labels; ≥ 90 % of named streets labelled at the neighbourhood band (O13 b).
places: §8.3 census 'label floors, counts, collisions → §9.4' (restated, per RENDERING-380)

facts.statement: F-WORK (operation count reached) at any stage, ladder or kernel call: E_WORK_LIMIT when a declared count (candidates, proposals, kernel calls, skeleton events, recursion depth) is reached, each count the stage's law over its batch scope's population-derived counts (§5.1 (5)); ladder: the stage's declared coarser rung entered by the count, never by time (fewer candidates, larger cells, shallower recursion) -> report 'work_cut' with the count; map valid and identical on every machine

Golden suite under a time-dilation shim (every clock read x 10 and x 0.1): per-stage digests byte-identical; work-cut rate per stage reported on B-CITY; hit rate flat across each rung's population band (§13.2)

F-BUDGET-TIME (stage over its time budget; reporting and scheduling only, GEO-2) in the @plat/api worker host outside model packages: wall-clock watchdog; action: postpone or resume a lazy tier (cancel-and-resume only), telemetry records 'time_over', never a model change
A tier postponed and resumed hashes identically to the eager tier; per-stage timing against §12 in CI telemetry on reference hardware

F-EDIT (constraint conflict) at S0 and edits: detection: a drawn way crosses a locked entity; a targeted assignment names a locked entity; an assignment cannot be honoured within its drift bounds; a warp would break an invariant or carry a locked or pinned point-anchored record out of its host face (§7.4); the effective scope holds protected entities whose fate is not 'kept'; an undo or redo whose target has dependent live events (§7.4); a water edit's new channel + bank setback meets a locked or pinned way, wall or finer entity, or a reservation (§7.3 (b) 3); a moved course knot beyond carveMaxCm (F-RIVER); a host provider's output that would pass the 2 MB cap on pack data and host content (§2.9)

F-EDIT resolution: the dry run returns the conflict as an action (nearest valid position, the blocking lock, the edit-fate list for confirmation, the dependent events to undo first, Re-derive from S3 for a reservation in a new channel's way, or the provider and size that passed the cap); precedence lock > assignment > drawn geometry > rules (§7.7); never silently resolved
B-EDIT sequences and conflict fixtures: 0 planarity violations, 0 lost faces, 0 silent re-binds

F-REDERIVE (coarse re-derivation invalidates finer content or crossings; LC-7) in §7.3's local operators (S1 water and terrain, S4, S5, S6, S7): detection: a plot, footprint or yard in new water, in a new corridor, across a moved wall band or outside its new cell; a way that new water + its bank setback will meet off a deck (found on the new water's data before insertion, §7.3 (b) 1-2); a deck span no longer crossing water; a crossing 'site' whose bank vertices no longer stand on a shore of its reach

F-REDERIVE plots and buildings: re-cut the plot along the new boundary (ids kept by the anchor rule, §6.3) -> re-fit its site plan (F-SITEPLAN) -> demolish what still conflicts, with a lifecycle event whose cause is the edit

F-REDERIVE way meeting new water off a deck: applied before the water is inserted, in the L1 batch of S1's water operator (§7.3 (b) 3) and of a carve (§4.11 (1)), so the L0 insertion meets no finer edge except at the vertices that batch prepared (§3.3); an arterial, the only connection of streets beyond it to a gate or the plaza (§4.11's rule), or a way that crossed the changed water on a deck is re-routed through the nearest deck within the detour bound, a deck being sited for it by F-ROUTE's extra-bridge rung when none does; every other way is cut at the bank setback (stretch inside new water + setback removed, each land part kept as a way: the part keeping the old anchor - end junction else larger overlap, §6.3 - keeps the address, the other is a fresh way) and a stub (land part shorter than the district's minimum block width ending at the setback) is removed, leaving a dead end at the bank
Detour bound for re-routing through a deck: re-routed length between the way's nearest pinned nodes on either side of the water <= 1.4 x the old length

A deck over land (reach moved away and §7.3's re-siting found no site in the band): the Bridge becomes a tombstone (demolish, cause the edit); its span stays in its way as an ordinary segment of the way's class (the higher class of the two joined ways where the span was a separate 'bridge' way) or leaves with the way if removed; its deck and deck_end rows are removed (removeEdges on ChainRef('deck', bridge) and on its two VertexRef('deck_end', bridge, i)); demotion then takes its bank vertices to the way's level and clears their kernel pins (§2.2 rule 3; VK4-1)

A site over land (reach moved away and no successor site matched it, §7.3 (b) 2): the site is removed - its deck_end rows by removeEdges on their VertexRefs, its record a tombstone (§2.7; §7.3 (b) 9; NP3-4, NP4-7)

Every re-cut, demolition, re-route, cut and pruned stub is listed in the edit-fate report with its lifecycle event; a locked or pinned entity is never demolished, re-routed or cut - its conflict returns to the dry run as F-EDIT

Oracle (v) cont.: a river move across a street grid commits (no E_LEVEL or E_KEPT) with its decks on the kept ways and cuts on the others, every face outside (b)'s footprint byte-identical; a pond drawn inside a block and a river bank widened into its riverside blocks between two bridges each commit with no E_LEVEL or E_KEPT and every face outside the footprint byte-identical (VK3-1)

Every invariant declares a scope: batch-local (evaluated on the batch's touched faces plus their one-ring and on records the batch created, changed or removed), stage-end (once when a stage or its scoped re-run completes), save / load (when a document is written or verified), CI-only (test harnesses); only batch-local invariants run per batch

For an edit whose operators chain several batches (§7.3 item 3), batch-local rows are evaluated once after the chain's last batch over the union of the chain's touched faces, their one-ring and the records the chain touched (a river move places deck bank vertices in an L1 batch before its L0 batch inserts water, so the crossing row holds only at chain end); the kernel's own invariants (§3.10, first row) still hold at every batch, so each chained batch keeps every way and enceinte one connected chain (§7.3 (b) 3)
Class floors: min width / area / angle per class, never minEdge as a face floor (GEO-35); batch-local on touched faces
No footprint overlap; batch-local, touched footprints against the spatial index
Every plot has >= 1 access edge and every building its entrance on one; batch-local on touched plots and buildings
No way centreline crosses a footprint; no way crosses a reservation (§4.2 S3); batch-local
Walls not crossed by ways except at gates; batch-local on touched ways and wall edges

A way crosses water only on a deck and a deck only over water (LC-7): every way-role edge with both sides in water (L0 parents of both side faces are water) belongs to a Bridge's deck span (edges between its two deck vertices, carrying the deck role; fords included) or to a harbour work (VD2-2); every deck span crosses a water face with both ends on its banks; a wall trace crosses water only at a water gate; batch-local, checked by index against L0 parents of both sides (§2.2 rule 2)

Harbour-work check: for a touched pier/quay edge with water both sides, one walk of its connected pier and quay edges counting distinct L0 land faces its vertices touch (a harbour-wall row's few hundred edges at most); covers S1 river decks, S3 moat and canal decks, S5a outer-moat decks, carve decks and S7 harbour furniture; §13.2's harbour fixtures include a two-arm mole and a detached breakwater

NF-P5: no lane crosses a wall strip, and no L3 band, setback, glacis, tower or gatehouse face is cleared or split by an L1 or L2 batch - in every generation batch and every edit batch, except for enceintes whose wall-strip parts the edit's chain declares it rebuilds (S10 step (0)) or removes (VP2-4, VD3-6); a lane still never crosses a strip

NF-P5 exemption declaration: the dry run of every chained edit computes the set of enceintes whose strips any of its batches changes, each marked 'rebuilt' or 'removed'; every batch of the chain carries it; the check reads the declaration, never a list of edit kinds

Edits that declare an NF-P5 exemption today: tree-scoped re-derivation of a scope holding wall-strip faces (§7.3 item 2); S7's operator (drawWall, moved trace vertex, re-traced run, gateToJunction); S1's water operator for every wall strip its L1 batch changes (re-traced run's strips; a setback or glacis line it anchors and cuts outside a re-traced run, §7.3 (b) 3, 7, 8); a carve for every strip its batches (1)-(3) change and its step 4 re-derives (§4.11); removals: wallToWay, contractWall (§4.11) and an enceinte's delete (§7.1 walls row)

NF-P5 checks: touched lanes vs setback and wall edges; commit record's removed/changed L3 faces of kind band/setback/glacis/tower/gatehouse vs the declared enceintes; a CI registry test fails when an edit operator or conversion that can write a wall strip's L1 lines or L3 parts has no declaration path; §13.2 fixtures commit a canal carved across a wall between two towers and a river move whose new bank cuts a glacis line without crossing the wall with 0 NF-P5 violations; a drawWay lane across a strip is refused
Footprints intersect (wall band + setback) = empty on both faces of every wall (MFP-9); batch-local
Water intersect footprints = empty; batch-local

Every built bridge lies within +/- 10 deg of the channel normal, measured on the deck and on the way (GEO-17); a 'site' has no span and is outside every deck row (§2.7; NP3-4); batch-local on touched crossings
Exclusive land uses never overlap; batch-local

Reference integrity: every reference out of a touched record (people and relations included; a dependent's carer resolves) names a live id; every reference into a record the batch removed is carried over (§6.3) or reported as an orphan; batch-local via the reverse-reference index
Identity: every fresh address differs from every live and tombstoned address, and no two live entities share a lineage key (§6.3); batch-local at mint, O(1) against the identity set

Stage-end (S7): every gate joined to the network and the plaza; roads leaving each walled stage = its gate count (N main gates plus any §4.2 S3 (7) harbour gate); an outer enceinte's gates >= its arterial crossings; a coastal town's harbour joined to its plaza through a gate and crossing a moat only on a deck (§4.2 S3 (11)); one graph search per enceinte
Stage-end (S7, S9): every quay reachable from the town without crossing a wall except at a gate (FTG-8); one graph search
Stage-end (S5): no branch re-joins its parent within k segments; per growth stage
Stage-end (S7): a sealed enclosure only when declared; per trace
Stage-end (S1): contours never cross a shore - a check of F-CONTOUR's clip construction, never an abort path
Stage-end (S13a): names unique within their kind's scope; a new entity never renames an existing one; an existing generated name changes only by one of §6.3's draw cases (§9)

Stage-end: every requested feature (river through the core, N gates, harbour when coastal, ...) is delivered, degraded or omitted and reported with its tier (§5.1 principle 7); checked on the report's 'requested' list; acceptance counts omissions (§15.2)
Stage-end: containment complete building in plot in block in district, 100 %, via per-batch containment counters summed (not a model walk)
Save: the canonical document validates against its schema (Recipe.salts keyed by rerollable concerns only, VD3-8); the recorded digests are the maintained model and records roots (§6.2; VD4-6)
CI-only digest-maintenance oracle: a full recomputation of the Merkle root from its leaves equals the incrementally maintained root, on every B-CITY generation and every B-EDIT sequence
CI-only: digests equal across platforms, under time dilation, under district permutation (derived-complete digest), and replay = session (§6.5, §7.3)
Label collisions are not a model invariant: placement is view data and '0 collisions' is tested by B-ZOOM (§5.2 F-LABEL, §9)
Hard invariants abort the batch, which rolls back to the previous arena version while its ladder continues; soft ones (statistics bands) go to the report
CI counts hard invariant violations per 1 000 cities and requires 0 (O3 b)

Validation cost rule: validating a batch costs O(touched faces x log n), never O(model); the per-edit validation time for a fixed scope is flat from TOWN to METROPOLIS within +/- 20 % (cost test §13.2: TOWN to CITY at M2a; TOWN to METROPOLIS at M2b, which generates from M1, §16)
Pre-decided fallback: an invariant whose batch-local check breaks the flat cost moves to stage-end scope - still hard, checked later in the same stage

J-DET-39: Chose to scope the NF-P5 invariant to generation batches and to every edit batch except for the enceintes whose wall-strip parts the edit's chain declares it rebuilds by step (0) or removes — a declaration each dry run computes and a registry test requires of every operator that can write a strip — over dropping the invariant for edits and over an enumerated list of exempt edit kinds — because the edits that rebuild or remove a wall's parts must be allowed to clear them while every other edit and every generation batch must still never split them, …

facts.statement: GenerationReport { outputVersion; stages[] { name: StageId; work: Record<string, number> (op counts vs declared limits); attempts; ladderUses[] { cause; rung; tier 0..6; entity: Id; key (stream key textual form, §6.1) }; invariants[] { name; scope 'batch'/'stage'/'save'/'ci'; pass; count } }; requested[] { feature; delivered 'full'/'degraded'/'omitted'; tier; entity?; cause? }; requestedVsBuilt: Diff[]; autoResolved[] { param; value; reason; layer: OverrideLayer }; unserved: Id[]; unplaced: Id[]; kernel { engine ('plat-arrangement@<version>', §3.7); warnings: Record<string, number>; downgrades; workLimitHits } }
Telemetry { stageMs: Record<StageId, number>; timeOver: StageId[]; verifyMs?: number } - session-only, never saved, never in any digest

The generation report is a derived cache: rebuilt by every derivation and by the verification replay on load, saved only in the document's 'derived' section (so the panel shows it before verification finishes), excluded from the canonical form and every digest (LC-24)
The same report object is the UI's compact dismissable panel (O16) and the API's report(doc); every ladder use is replayable from its printed key (MFCG's replayable attempts kept)

Plain-words promise: the same seed makes the same town on any computer; decisions counted in steps never seconds; non-integer maths via a bit-identical library; the digest is kept up to date incrementally; every part draws from its own stream named by where it came from, so adding a decoration kind or naming rule, re-rolling one block or growing a stage never reshuffles what exists; not promised: a release that changes an early step changes towns built on it and says so stage by stage; edited towns keep their edits through permanent addresses separate from random streams
Keys are mixed from structured components, never from strings (SCL-12, K-6 / R-1 kept); no string is built on the generation path
Seed key (128 bits) is derived once from the seed by four 32-bit-lane finalisers with distinct salts, all Math.imul
Entity key = mix of seed key, lineage hash, layer and island (§6.3), computed once at mint and cached in the arena beside the lineage hash

Town-level draws (S0 feature draws, terrain noise, per-document furniture: compass and emblem, §9.5) use the town root's entity key = seed key mixed with the fixed town lineage (ground arena, no parent, creation epoch 0, index 0), so they depend on the recipe alone, never on docId
Paint programs and furniture pass the reserved stage id STAGE_VIEW = 0xffff to the one mixer (§14 Rng.stream; NF-D12)

Stream key = one finaliser round over the entity key combined with packed components (stage id u16, concern id u16, reroll u16, attempt u8, epoch u16, salt u16); its four words seed the state directly; the all-zero state is replaced by a fixed nudge
A stream is created once per derivation and continued; a second request in the same derivation returns the same stream
Textual stream-key form for reports only, rendered from the same components: S11/siteplan@plot:7kq2m9x4c1b0a/arrangement[/r=1][/a=2][/e=0]

Stream-key derivation budget <= 0.1 us per key (string paths measured 0.73 us, SCL-12); measured by the M0 (d) determinism spike over a B-CITY city; pre-decided fallback: derive a batch's keys in one vectorised pass over a typed array (output-neutral, no golden moves)
Lineage component: the entity's stream identity - layer, island, derivation unit, stage, creation epoch, creation index; kept by a surviving entity so nothing that survives is re-rolled
Concern component: what the draw is for (registry); streams are never shared across concerns

Reroll component (LC-5): the scope entity's New random count, an absolute number stored in its identity and written into the regenerate event as an explicit per-entity map (rerolls actually used, §5.1 (6)); children draw with their derivation unit's reroll, so New random on a block changes that block's plots and nothing else
A user's reroll count is capped at 32 767; rerolls 32 768 and above are reserved for §13.2's faithfulness references (§7.3 item 7 (iv))

Attempt component: the ladder's retry number (§5.1), restarting at 0 inside each reroll; its cap is declared per concern in the registry: 3 for every geometric ladder (tier 3), 8 for the naming re-draw of §9.6 (a repeated name re-draws on its own stream before taking a distinguishing suffix)
Epoch component: e for draws made by epoch e; epoch 0 is the original town

Salt component (COV-VG-VN-008): a per-concern number in the recipe (default 0) that rerollLayer(concern) bumps (§7.1), only for rerollable concerns: naming, render.instances, style.jitter, style.crowns, style.compass, naming.emblem (read by the compass furniture program and the emblem generator, §9.5); geometry concerns take no salt (their reroll is the regenerate action), so rerolling trees or names moves nothing else
The recipe's initial salts are keyed by the same registry-generated type and its schema refuses any other key (§2.9; VD3-8), so no recipe, link delta or log can give a geometry stream a salt

A town-wide rerollLayer sets the concern's town salt; an ids-scoped rerollLayer of naming (VD2-10) re-draws only the names of the listed entities, each with the per-entity salt the event carries in place of the town salt

Every other draw of a name uses the town salt (entity with no predecessor) or, when the name's naming inputs changed, the salt its last draw used, held in the name's naming record (§6.3 cases (1) and (4), §2.8; VD3-2); a name's salt is never in the model digest: the setting event holds it and the naming record caches it

The registry marks a concern rerollable only when a StageDecl.streamKeys entry or a paint program names it; rerollLayer's concern type is generated from those entries; a CI test fails when a rerollable concern has no reader (N-18)

Label candidates are geometric (S13a, §9.3) and placement is a deterministic greedy over a total order (S13b, §9.2), so no labels stream is registered; 'reroll the labels' is not offered; re-placing a label is moveLabel
Ordinal-keyed draws (roster's prefix-stable roster/<class>/<ordinal>, §10.2, FTG-14) use the class's registry entry as derivation unit and the ordinal as creation index through the same mixer

Concern registry (G-P6): adding a concern is a reviewed change to a registry file; concern ids are u16, append-only, never renumbered, so adding one changes no other key; each entry declares its reader stages, whether it is rerollable and its attempt cap
