model = G(outputVersion, base, log): a pure function; the base is the canonical recipe or a rebased state; the log is folded in order (§7.4)

Host-supplied tables, presets and styles are not in the recipe: they arrive as logged editTable, editPreset and setStyle events whose content is copied into the log (§6.5 (8), §7.6); packs a later adjust adds are named by that event and belong to the document's pack set (§2.9)

Nothing else reaches the model (VD2-7): no wall clock (every output-affecting limit is an operation count, §5.1); no host text engine (label placement S13b is view data per zoom stop from names, LabelEntity records and bundled fonts' metrics, not in the digest); no viewing order (lazy only under §4.1's laziness contract, tested by random district permutations §6.5); no worker timing (results merge in lineage order); one boolean and offset engine per output version on every host (§6.5, D-14); no host code (host provider outputs read from hostContent on replay, §6.5, §2.9); no installed pack (packs resolved by content hash from the document's packs block then shipped packs; missing or mismatched opens read-only, §2.9); no machine preference read at run time (user-global preferences folded into the recipe at document creation, §7.6)
Two machines or browsers produce identical model digests (O2 a); two renders of one model are pixel-identical at a given backend, DPR and style version

The model digest is a Merkle digest over the eager model's content only (SCL-1, LC-25, LC-2); the eager model = everything the city LOD draws plus town-level Allocation and FieldBands records (§4.5, §4.7); lazily derived content (close-ups, people, stage-3 compositions) enters when an edit materialises it

Merkle formulas: leaf(record) = H128(kind, id, lineage, parent, existence, flags, attributes in schema order, digests of owned faces and chains); node(n) = H128(tag(n), children digests sorted by address id); root = node(model) per layer

Digest layers: site (terrain raster, fields, L0 water); network (ways, junctions, walls, gates, towers); districts (district, block, plot, buildings, yards, households, pins); hinterland; content (Allocation, FieldBands, institutions, factions, relations); names and LabelEntity records; closeups (edited close-ups only); identity (tombstone ids and supersededBy links, the lifecycle event block); plats (per arena and per level, the kernel's level digests)

Geometry is hashed once by the kernel per level (GEO-1): each arena keeps a digest per level over its level-n route (vertices, roles, face owners and kinds of level <= n, never arena slots), updated along each commit record's dirty set (§3.3); a finer level's Steiner vertices belong to the finer digest, so deriving L3 never changes the L2 digest

Per-level digests read each vertex's and edge's current birth level: a promotion (§2.2 rule 3) moves a vertex into the coarser digest from that commit on; a demotion moves it back out (the neighbour step's reversal restores the kerb's L2 digest exactly); kept finer content (§3.3) keeps its digest leaves through a coarser re-derivation (VK-18, VK-1)
An entity's leaf takes the digests of the faces and chains it owns (FaceRef, ChainRef resolved), so no coordinate is hashed twice

Digest input canonical order: a level-n ring starts from its lowest-then-leftmost vertex of level <= n, finer vertices skipped (§3.3's key; VK2-4); integers as 32-bit lanes, doubles as IEEE-754 bit patterns (-0 normalised to +0; NaN refused by schema), strings as UTF-8; no text serialisation on the digest path; no byte-order dependence

H128 = MurmurHash3 x86 128-bit variant (published public-domain algorithm in 32-bit ops; own implementation tested against published test vectors), seed 0, so the digest hash is specified exactly as H32 is (§13.6 (2); VS2-6)

Digest inclusion: names and LabelEntity records (text, candidates, pinned, hidden) are model data and hashed; excluded: provenance, derivation records and naming records (provenance digest §2.8; records digest below); style, view, derived, hostContent and telemetry (§2.9); label placement decisions (S13b view data); never-edited close-ups (a close-up is a pure function of its district's committed state, sub-seed, strategy and params, and enters under closeups with its first edit; LC-18, §7.4)
Digest maintenance: at every batch commit the kernel re-hashes the leaves of touched records and the nodes on their paths to the root, O(touched x depth), never by serialising the model (§3.3)

The maintained tree is built by the generation run in a session and, for a loaded document, by the load's one full recomputation from the decoded snapshot under the model packages of the document's own output version (§2.9 step 3; VD3-1, VD4-1); the snapshot stores only the root; every edit from the first after opening maintains a complete tree

M2a's memory measurement (the milestone that builds the log and load verification over M1's document format, §16; VS4-3) includes load verification of the reference 300-edit CITY document with a district regeneration and a Re-derive from S3 made during it; the load's digest trees (model tree ≈ 1 MB and records tree ≈ 0.25 MB at CITY, §6.2) sit in the entity-store line; a bridged client that took the replayed town keeps the doc.load bytes (≤ 3 MB at CITY) until the mismatch is settled (§2.9 step 4); lines stay PLAUSIBLE until M1 (TOWN, CITY), M2a (that case) and M2b (METROPOLIS) measure them, with the steps below as fallbacks.
Canonical text serialisation (sorted keys, integer coordinates, floats as shortest round-trip strings) is used only for golden files and exports

The records-digest leaf encoding belongs to the file schema, not an output version (records are stored inputs, not derived output): any version checks it, and a schema transform that changes a record column (§7.5) checks the old root and writes the new one

Records digest maintenance: exactly as the model tree - a batch that rewrites a record re-hashes its leaf and partition node; finalised when read; stored in the snapshot as recordsDigest; recomputed by every load with the model tree

facts.statement: Never reused; one collision rule: minting runs after succession matching; a fresh entity whose natural address equals a live address, a tombstone or an address its own batch retires takes suffix ~k with the smallest free k; a fresh lineage key equal to a live entity's outside the batch's re-derived set (a survivor) takes the smallest free dup component; entities the batch itself replaces are not collisions (lets faithful Regenerate re-mint and reproduce them); collisions resolved in the batch's canonical order (records sorted by lineage hash)

An address that an undo withdraws (§7.4) is free again, but only the same derivation (same unit, lineage and reroll - what a redo or repeated New random re-runs) can mint it, so nothing is re-bound to an unrelated entity
Carry-over applies whenever a scope is re-derived: regenerate, Adjust, re-derive from Sk, a §7.3 local operator, template replacement, migration, epoch

Survival: an entity not re-derived (outside the invalidation set, a fixed input - locked, pinned, edited or assigned, §7.2 - or merely re-parented) keeps its address and lineage (its draws do not change); only its parent field and a reparent lifecycle event change

Succession: a re-derived entity is matched by anchor; the fresh entity of the same kind and class family whose anchor lies nearest within the kind's hysteresis radius succeeds it - takes the old address and old generated name with its naming record (references re-bind; §7.3 decides which overrides move) and keeps its own fresh lineage (New random really re-rolls); a carry event records the lineage change; the same batch re-owns the successor's faces and roles under the address (setOwner, retypeEdges, §3.4)

An old entity with no successor becomes a tombstone in the archive (§2.8) whose supersededBy names the fresh entity covering its anchor point, if any; a fresh entity with no predecessor keeps its fresh address

Lifecycle events are written only for changes (existence, flags, a lineage change, supersession, re-parenting), so a re-derivation that reproduces its entities exactly leaves the model digest unchanged

J-DET-2: Chose to keep the lineage (and so the draws) only for entities that survive un-derived, and to hand only the address to an anchor-matched successor, over carrying the lineage in both cases — because New random must really re-roll its scope while names, locks and assignments must follow the building the user means (§6.3).

facts.statement: Names follow the address (VD2-10, VD3-2): a generated name (text and short form) is handed to a successor with the address together with its naming record (§2.8: naming slices its last draw consulted and the salt used), as a lock or assignment is; a re-sited bridge, a re-cut street and a regrouped district keep their names

Case (4) triggers whenever S13a runs over the name's entity: after an adjust of the pack list (pack added/removed, corpus selected/deselected, §7.6); after an editTable or editPreset changing a naming slice (§7.6 invalidation by slice); in an upgrade's mapping (§7.5); at the event ending the name's protection (unlock or unassign that frees it; undo, redo or revert removing the setAttr, lock or assign that held it; §2.8 dormant record; VD4-3); in any re-derivation whose scope reaches S13a; it compares every slice the record cites with the current effective tables, and a slice whose hash differs or no longer resolves re-draws the name

Each field of a culture or ancestry row is its own naming slice - the (row, field) pair, hashed over the field's value and, for a corpus field, the named corpus's content hash (§7.6; VD4-5); a name's record cites only the fields its draw read, so selecting another corpus for one field re-draws exactly the names drawn from it (a street list renames that culture's streets, never districts or quarters)
A carried name is kept exactly while its naming inputs are unchanged; a change of features a grammar guard reads (a district that lost its gate) is not a naming input and renames nothing (§9.6)
Every name draw uses the entity's naming stream (keyed from its entity key, §6.1, with its case's salt and the attempt) and writes the name's naming record anew

Case (3) salts: the dry run gives each listed entity the salt one above the largest its name has been drawn with (town salt and every earlier ids-scoped salt); a re-drawn name equal to the old one advances the salt once more, up to reroll.maxAdvance times (as §5.1 (6)); the event stores the salts actually used so replay repeats neither

Case (4) renames: the dry run lists every rename (old and new text) in the edit's fate report with its other unprotected consequences; the edit commits after the user confirms; confirmed renames are stored in the event (EditBase.renames, §7.1; VD4-4); a replay or receiving client re-draws them identically, and one that computes different renames reports a mismatch as for fates (§7.3 item 4)

When carrying or a re-draw brings two equal names into one uniqueness scope (§9.6; a district merge joining two same-named lanes), the entity whose address sorts later re-draws on its own stream, and the rename is listed in the edit's fate report

facts.statement: Anchors and hysteresis (GEO-34): matching by distance, never quantised cell; candidate (old, fresh) pairs within the radius and of the same class family sorted by (distance, old id, fresh id) and assigned one-to-one greedily in that order

Plot anchor: highest-class frontage (way address, start offset along the way); radius 0.5 m along the same way or its successor; class family = use family (residential, commercial, institutional, agricultural)
Building anchor: footprint centroid; radius 0.5 m; class family = building class family (a table row: small dwellings; halls and manors; religious; workshops and stores; towers and keeps; ...)
Block and cell anchor: centroid; radius 2 m (block), 5 m (cell); no class family
District anchor: its seed feature's address (same feature); class family district kind family
Way anchor: its end junctions' addresses, else overlap >= 50 % of its length; class family way class family

facts.statement: Junction, gate, tower, pin anchor: position; radius 1 m (junction, pin), 2 m (gate, tower); family = kind

Bridge anchor (LC-7): its deck's midpoint on the same river (water body address or successor); radius = the crossing-site search band of §4.2 S1 (5) (crossing.searchBandM, default 120 m); family kind (bridge, ford)
Enceinte, water body, greenery, land use anchor: overlap >= 50 % (IoU); family kind
Household anchor (plot address, ordinal); person (household address, ordinal); label: target address
Seam (NF-P6) anchor: its two districts' addresses and its first chain's address (same pair and chain)
Portal anchor: position, radius 1 m, family portal kind (baseLane, growth, edit)

Households and people (LC-16): a household's address survives a re-derivation of its plot by succession (anchor plot address and ordinal), so a person's key (household address, member ordinal, birth epoch; §10.3) is stable wherever the household is

Anchor stability measurement (M1, B-EDIT-lite): 1 cm perturbations of every vertex keep >= 99.9 % of addresses; pre-decided fallback: building and plot radii double to 1 m and an IoU >= 0.5 test joins the class-family check

Matching routine (NF-D7): one routine hands addresses on in every re-derivation (scoped regeneration, Adjust, Re-derive from Sk - from S1 the whole town -, a local operator, template replacement, epochs, migration, §7.5 upgrade mapping); point-anchored kinds (plots by frontage offset, buildings, blocks, cells, junctions, gates, towers, pins, bridges) via a uniform grid per (kind, class family) with cell = the kind's hysteresis radius so every candidate is in the 3 x 3 neighbourhood, pairs sorted by (distance, old id, fresh id) and assigned greedily; overlap-anchored kinds (ways without matched end junctions, enceintes, water bodies, greenery, land use) take candidates from the kernel's spatial index (§3.3) and compute overlap on those only
Matching budget: <= 2 us per re-derived point-anchored entity and <= 20 us per overlap-anchored one, median, included in §12.6's scope costs

Matching measured (Apple M1, Node 24; docs/validation/bench/fixall_det_r2_match.out) on synthetic anchor sets: 0.60 us/entity for a 450-building district regeneration; 0.59 us for a 30 000-entity CITY re-derivation (0.38 us when unrelated); 0.59 us for an 80 000-entity METROPOLIS mapping at 2 m radius; to be measured in-engine at M0 d then M1 on B-EDIT-lite and a Re-derive-from-S1 fixture

Matching pre-decided fallback: match per static-index partition (§3.3) - candidates first from the entity's own district partition, only unmatched ones across partitions; a declared shift (§6.4) because a boundary entity can take a farther in-district candidate

JOIN and SPLIT: a joined plot takes its address by the anchor rule from the member whose frontage anchor it keeps; other members become tombstones with supersededBy = the joined plot; members is history; a later SPLIT resurrects a member whose anchor matches (the one permitted reuse of a tombstoned id, recorded as a resurrect event; safe because JOIN member ids were never given to another entity)

Document identity (LC-28): docId (UUID) minted at document creation, kept on save, re-minted on clone and save-as; addresses are document-scoped (a clone keeps them); at the API and bridge boundary every id is rendered <docId>/<id>; exports carry addresses and a supersedes table (tombstone to successor)

facts.statement: Scope of stability (O2 b, e; LC-3): (1) independent concerns - adding or changing a concern changes no other concern's draws; a naming-input change re-draws only names whose records cite it; (2) scoped rerolls - New random changes nothing outside its effective scope (§7.3); (3) upstream changes - a change to stage k's code or tables changes stage k's outputs and what derives from them, a declared cascade shift (§6.4, §13.3), never silent; stages upstream of k and independent of it stay byte-identical; (4) edited documents - stability across such changes comes from carry-over by anchor and migration (§7.5), never from stream keys

Identity measurement (M0 d and M1): minting and matching within budget; B-EDIT fixtures: drawBoundary, district merge and split, outskirtToDistrict, regenerate around a lock, a course-knot move re-siting a bridge (keeps address and name), New random on a district (matched successors keep names; only entities without predecessor draw), a district merge joining two equal lane names (later address re-draws, reported), the recycling case (a superseded assigned building whose creation slot is reused)

Preview flag (LC-19): links and documents made before output version 1 (fixed at M4's exit, §16) carry preview: true (in a link &pv=1) and the app shows §13.3's preview notice; the flag disappears from output version 1 on
Table versions: each rule table separately, pinned in the recipe; a table change that changes output is part of an output-version bump; a user override carries its base row's hash (§7.6)

Pack versions: each setting pack by id, version and content hash in the recipe or in the adjust event that adds it (§2.9 pack set); shipped packs belong to the output version like its tables (each retained version's chunk carries its own); a non-shipped pack's content travels in the document (NF-D2); a pack a later version stops shipping is copied into the document by the upgrade to that version (§7.5; VD4-9); a selected user corpus is a non-shipped pack user:<content hash> (§2.9; VD2-8)

facts.statement: A link is emitted only when it can rebuild the same town and picture on any machine: every pack of the document's pack set (base recipe packs plus every pack an adjust in the log names, a selected-then-deselected corpus included; §2.9; VD3-3) is shipped with the link's output version; the base is the recipe (VD4-8: a rebased town is not seed-reproducible); hostContent is empty; the style sheet is shipped; the whole URL fits in 2 000 characters

On a refused link the app states which condition failed (pack not built in; your own name list, also when deselected; host program content; kept from a saved copy; too many edits) and offers the .plat file, or &doc=<ref> when the host configured a DocResolver with publish (§11.5); the document carries pack content and host outputs (§2.9), so the file reproduces the town
preset=<id> never appears in a link: an edited preset elsewhere cannot change the town

J-DET-50: Chose to emit a link only when the document's base is the recipe — refusing it for every rebased base, a kept saved town included, with the `.plat` file or `&doc=` offered, and letting the CLI's `--recipe-only` export refuse one too — and to fold an undone `rebase` with its `undo` as a no-op pair in a replay from the recipe, over an exception for a rebase whose state its recipe could regenerate — because a link replays the recipe and the log and has no way to name a starting state, so for a rebased town it would show the replayed town …

facts.statement: Link CI: link to recipe to link identity; model digest built from a link equals the session's; refusal cases - recipe naming a non-shipped pack; district names from a user corpus selected after creation (user:<hash> named only by an adjust; VD2-8, VD3-3); a town that selected then deselected such a corpus, saved and reloaded; a document with a host provider's output; a town rebased by keeping the saved town after a forced load mismatch (VD4-8) - in each the link is refused and the .plat file opened by a library lacking the pack, corpus or provider replays to the session's digest

Retention of old output versions (LC-14): the browser library ships the current output version's model packages plus N-1 and N-2 as lazily loaded, tree-shakable chunks (@plat/*-o<k>; an embed may leave them out); the Node CLI replays any published output version by installing that exact package version; a document or link inside the window replays exactly

Outside the retention window a document opens as a frozen view (§2.9 step 2), checked by chunk content hashes only and labelled 'made with o5; not verified by this version' (its root was computed by o5's packages; VD4-1); a link (no snapshot) opens under the current output version with a visible notice ('made with o5, shown with o8; differences are expected') and the CLI command that replays it exactly; nothing changes silently
The retention window also bounds what the browser can undo by replay (an upgrade, a rebase onto an older version, §7.4): outside it the undo is withdrawn with the CLI command shown

Retention measurement (M3a): each retained output version adds <= 150 KB gzipped to its lazy chunk; golden suite replays under N-1 and N-2; pre-decided fallback: browser window shrinks to N-1 (CLI keeps every version)

Stage-isolated goldens (LC-3; §13.3 builds the tooling from M1): the golden store keeps per seed and stage the previous output version's frozen upstream outputs; a release computes each stage's digest by running the new stage code on those frozen inputs, so only stages whose own code or tables changed can differ; each such stage needs a shift record (stage, cause, seeds and statistics that moved, expected direction)

Declared-shift protocol: a release either matches or declares a shift record for every stage whose isolated digest moved (stage, cause — rule-table change, fix, new concern — seeds and statistics that moved, expected direction, output version created) and a cascade record for every end-to-end golden it re-signs (each downstream stage that moved, shown from isolated goldens to have moved only through its inputs; a downstream stage whose isolated digest moved needs its own shift record).

Determinism lint is an allowlist (GEO-31): in model packages and every adapter or provider whose output reaches the model, the only Math members allowed are abs, floor, ceil, round, trunc, sign, min, max, sqrt, imul, clz32, fround, plus arithmetic operators

The allowlist also covers view code whose output reaches a bit-compared digest (VS2-4): @plat/labels, every ObstacleSource and RoleIndex implementation (§14), functions they call, the S14 builder code writing the display-list columns they read (bbox, geometry ranges and GeomTable, layer, z, symbol extents from the style sheet's sizes; a rotated symbol's extent uses dmath), and §8.10's instance function with everything it calls (stamp, grid and line layouts, per-instance look draws, density edge test) whose positions §13.3 compares byte for byte (NR4-3); CI finds this code as the TypeScript import closure of those implementations, column writers and the instance function, so a joining module is linted without being listed; the rest of @plat/render (paint programs, backends, compositing) stays outside (pixels compared by visual regression, §13.3, §13.4)

** is allowed only with a literal integer exponent 0-4 and the build rewrites it into explicit multiplications; every other power goes through dmath.pow (S1's river-width law w0 x acc^0.4 is dmath.pow(acc, 0.4))

Also forbidden in linted code: Math.random, Date, performance, timers, crypto.getRandomValues, DOM access, locale-dependent string ops (toLocaleString, localeCompare, Intl), Array.prototype.sort without a comparator, and any dependence on object-key or Map iteration order beyond insertion order

Vendored dependencies are scanned too: every third-party library a kernel adapter imports is vendored at a pinned version and passes the same allowlist scan at each version change; an audit record (library, version, scan result, each exception with its wrapper) is kept in @plat/kernel; a failing library (e.g. one calling Math.hypot) is patched or wrapped in its adapter before adoption
Every sort uses a total-order comparator with an id tie-break (the OS ObjectMap key-order hazard cannot occur)

Host providers (LC-31): a host-supplied table arrives as an editTable, editPreset or setStyle event whose content is copied into the log with provenance 'host' (§7.6); host code registered as a provider (ContentProvider, §14) passes a double-run check at registration (same request run twice in two fresh workers returns identical digests); its results are recorded in the document's hostContent block keyed by (provider id, version, input hash) and read from there on replay (§2.9, §11.4); setting packs follow the same rule through the packs block (§2.9; NF-D2)
Determinism CI - cross-host: identical digests on Node x86 / arm64, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, workers on and off
Determinism CI - time dilation: the golden suite under a shim scaling every clock read x 10 and x 0.1 gives byte-identical per-stage digests (GEO-2)
Determinism CI - headless = UI (O11 f)

Determinism CI - replay = session: replaying base and log equals the session's digest on every B-EDIT sequence (§7.3), including the naming-collision fixture of §7.3 (7) (N-1), undo/redo sequences from several sessions, edits during load verification under both choices of a forced mismatch (§2.9 step 4; NR-8), and edits made before a records mismatch, re-applied (§2.9 step 3; VD4-6)

Determinism CI - truncation identity: a B-EDIT sequence folded with its undone pairs kept and truncated gives the same model digest (§7.4), including a redo followed by a user-created entity (same address in both folds, VD2-3), a setAttr(name) + undo pair and a naming rerollLayer + undo pair each followed by a corpus selection (naming records restored, §2.8; VD4-3), and a corpus selection + undo truncated, saved, reloaded and redone with its pack still in packs (§2.9; VD4-7)
Determinism CI - links and documents without their inputs: §6.4's pack, user-corpus, provider and rebased-town cases (VD4-8)

Determinism CI - checks under the recording version: a keptSnapshot-rebased CITY document upgraded across a test output version whose field driver and digest leaf encoding differ from 'from' opens editable after a reload and replays to the session's digest; a frozen view of a fixture written by a test build labelled o(N-3) opens with no mismatch message, while one with a chunk's bytes altered reports damage and refuses the frozenImport rebase (§2.9 steps 2-3, §7.5; VD4-1)
Determinism CI also includes the double-run check of registered providers and the distinct-key test of §6.1

J-DET-28: Chose to require byte identity of the WebAssembly accelerator only, and to admit the Clipper2-WASM fallback as a declared golden shift checked by cross-host digest identity, over requiring byte identity of both — because the fallback engine computes different integers by construction and would otherwise be unshippable (§6.5 (10); VK-13).

facts.statement: Plain-words promise: every user change (pin, bend a street, draw river or island, brush prosperity, rename, assign, draw a house, regenerate a block, edit a table, grow an epoch) is recorded in order as a small event on the permanent address of the thing it changes; town = starting point plus events, applied the same on screen and on reopen; touched things are protected; a change reaching a town-wide dependency is announced before it runs with a list of kept / moved / orphaned edits; otherwise regeneration is local and everything outside stays byte-identical

EditBase { seq (from the document's nextSeq; never reset; survives rebase); author 'user'/'host'/'epoch'/'migration'; session (authoring session, per document and author, reused across reloads - its undo and redo stacks; never read by the fold; VD2-4); group? (one undo step); renames?: Rename[] (case-(4) renames the dry run listed and the user confirmed; VD4-4) }

EditBase.renames is carried on any event whose fold re-draws a name because naming inputs changed: a pack-list adjust, a naming editTable or editPreset, an upgrade, a re-derivation reaching S13a, and the unlock, unassign, undo, redo or revert that ends a name's protection (§2.8; VD4-3); a replay or receiving client computing different renames reports a mismatch, as for fates
Rename = { id: Id; from: string; to: string } (name text before and after as the user saw them)
EditScope = { ids: Id[] } or { ring: PolygonCm; key: PlatKey; level: Level }; resolved to the effective scope at dry run and stored resolved
EditFate = { id; fate 'kept'/'carried'/'orphaned'/'discarded'; to?: Id; reason }

FieldStroke = { path: PointCm[]; radiusCm: Cm; falloff 'linear'/'cosine'; amount (relative delta: field units, or cm for terrain); water? 'locked'/'follow' (terrain only; default 'locked', §7.2, §7.3) }

EditEvent = EditBase and one of 46 kinds: lock, unlock (ids, paths? attribute-level locks COV-FTG-C12), pin, unpin, moveVertex, moveCourseKnot, warp, drawWay, drawWater, drawWall, drawGreen, drawBoundary, drawFootprint, build, moveFootprint, swapUse, fill, setAttr, setAttrMany, paint, paintGround, instance, delete, merge, split, join, revert, regenerate, adjust, setField, assign, unassign, moveLabel, hideLabel, setLayer, editTable, editPreset, setStyle, rerollLayer, convert, closeup, epoch, rebase, upgrade, undo, redo
pin / unpin is only ever an explicit user action, never emitted by viewing
moveVertex { key: PlatKey; at: LatticePoint (position before the move); sig: VertexSig (role signature at the edit, §2.2 rule 5); to: LatticePoint }
moveCourseKnot { water: Id; ordinal (knot's ordinal in WaterBody.controls, §2.3); at: PointCm (before); to: PointCm } - a river's control knot is S1's recorded input, not an arena vertex (VK2-12)

Draw events: drawWay { points; class: WayClass; widthCm }; drawWater { kind: WaterKind; add: PolygonCm[]; subtract?; line?; widthCm? } (add rings unioned, subtract rings = land brush for islands); drawWall { points; kind: Enceinte['kind']; closed }; drawGreen { polygon; kind: Greenery['kind']; densityPerHa? }; drawBoundary { polygon; district? } (snaps to whole L1 cells); drawFootprint { polygon; cls?; use?; heights?: Partial<Heights> }
build { plot; cls; use?; footprint?; heights? }; moveFootprint { id; deltaCm: VecCm; rotateCdeg? }; swapUse { a; b }; fill { scope: EditScope; arrangement: SitePlan['arrangement']; cls? }

setAttr { id; path; value }; setAttrMany { ids (resolved at dry run); query? (what the user asked, for display); path; value }; paint { target 'roofKind'/'roofColour'/'wallColour'; ids (resolved under the brush); brush: BrushPath; value }
paintGround { region; cover; colour? } is a style region (FTG texture brush), outside the model digest

instance { entity; ordinal?; point?; op 'add'/'move'/'remove'/'restyle'; to?; style?: Partial<InstanceStyle> } (LC-20); for an ordinal-addressed event the dry run fills point with the instance's generated position
delete { id }; merge { ids }; split { id; cut: PointCm[] }; join { ids }

revert { id } = 'reset to generated' (COV-MFCG-L08): one undoable event that applies, in reverse log order, the inverses of every logged event whose target is this entity (its own edits only); ctrl / cmd+click (§14 keymap, MFCG's ctrl-click reset)
regenerate { scope: EditScope; mode 'keep'/'newRandom'; rerolls: Record<Id, number> (absolute, per scope entity, rerolls actually used; LC-5, §5.1 (6)); discardEdits?; fates: EditFate[] }
adjust { param; value; fromStage: StageId; fates: EditFate[] } - Adjust and Re-derive from stage k (LC-4)
setField { field 'prosperity'/'density'/'greenery'/'terrain'; stroke: FieldStroke } - a relative delta; the stroke list is composited once (§7.2)
assign { assignment: Assignment }; unassign { id }
moveLabel { id; placement: Placement }; hideLabel { id; hidden } - LabelEntity.pinned / hidden are model data (§9)
setLayer { layer: Layer; spec: Partial<LayerSpec> }

editTable { table: TableId; ops: RowOp[]; provenance? 'host'; fates? (confirmed fates of §7.6's fallback re-derivation from the table's first reader stage; VD4-4) }; editPreset { preset; ops; provenance?; fates? }; setStyle { ops; provenance? }

rerollLayer { concern: RerollableConcern (generated from the concern registry, §6.1); salt (town-wide: the concern's new salt; 0 with ids); ids? (naming only: re-draw these entities' names; VD2-10); salts?: Record<Id, number> (with ids: per-entity salts actually used, §6.3) } (COV-VG-VN-008)
closeup { district; strategy: FabricStrategyId; params } - logged before the first edit inside a close-up (LC-18, PART II)
epoch { epoch; inputs: EpochInputs } - an epoch is an event in the log (LC-11, §4.11)

rebase { reason: RebaseReason; stateDigest: Hash128; version (output version whose packages computed stateDigest - the document's output version from this event on; a frozenImport sets it to the library's current version, §2.9 steps 2-3; VD4-1); at (the log head its state materialises: the previous event's seq, or h0 when kept after edits during load verification, §2.9 step 4; any other value refused with E_REBASE_AT, nothing appended; §14; VS4-2) } (LC-13)

upgrade { from; to; mapping: MigrationMap (§7.5); baseDigest? (with a rebased base: base.state's model root computed under 'to', checked by later loads under 'to'; §2.9 step 3, §7.5; VD4-1) } (LC-14); undoable
undo { of: seq of the event undone, or of the first event of its group } and redo { of: seq of the undo it reverses } (NF-D1): applied at the head through the same fold (§7.4)
RowOp = { op 'set'/'insert'/'delete'; rowKey; field?; value?; baseRowHash?: Hash64 } - rows by stable key, never by position (LC-22)
WarpKernel = 'displace'/'liquify'/'relax'/'bloat'/'pinch'/'equalize'/'swirl'/'jitter'; WarpStroke = { kernel; centre: PointCm; radiusCm; innerRadiusCm?; strength; dragCm?: VecCm }

No event stores a VertexId, HalfEdgeId or FaceId (§2.2 rule 5, GEO-5): geometry is addressed by entity address, by lattice point with a role signature (bound by resolveVertexAt, never by distance alone), by a water body's address with a course-knot ordinal (moveCourseKnot, §2.3; bound as §7.4's row states), or by a ring
Undo and redo are events like the rest (§7.4): the log only grows, which lets a host store it (§11.3)
The named actions (G-R4; O16-core) are separate operations with distinct semantics, never one flag

Regenerate (keep settings) re-derives the scope with each entity's recorded inputs and unchanged rerolls (§7.3): faithful, byte-identical when nothing upstream changed; used after a lock or drawn constraint

New random advances the reroll of every scope entity by one, written into the event as an absolute map (replay exact; blocks at different rerolls each move on; LC-5); a scope entity whose content comes out unchanged advances again up to three times, and is otherwise reported (§5.1 (6)); the map records the rerolls used

Adjust re-solves with a changed parameter; locality promised only for parameters the control registry (§7.8) lists as consumed at S10 or later or that carry a spatial scope (a district's density, a block's granularity); a parameter consumed earlier (seed, rung, water setting and side, walls, castle option, gate count, planned/organic, wealth level, the recipe's pack list) is offered as Re-derive from stage k: everything from Sk down re-derives with carry-over (§6.3) after the user confirms the edit-fate report (LC-4)
Same kind, new seed = Enter's successor (new document with seed + 1 and same recipe, §6.1); per district (PART II) it is New random on the district
Surprise me = a new document whose intent is drawn from the intent.surprise stream of a fresh seed and written into its recipe (§7.7)

Warp is MFCG's staged edit (COV-MFCG-L03, COV-NG-CR02): strokes preview on the L1 overlay at interactive rate (vertex moves and a redraw of affected tiles, no invariants, §8.8); Apply commits one warp event holding the strokes in order (committed only on Apply); Discard drops them

On Apply and every replay each warp stroke is applied as its operation to the geometry current at that log position, never as stored displacements (LC-27): the operation computes a displacement field over the vertices under the brush and the kernel's warp(field, fromLevel, region) applies it

Point-standing records (pins, point decorations, positional instance overrides, pinned label placements) move with their host face; every footprint, trace and deck the warp moved is re-based on the ground it now stands on (§7.4 'Warp and what stands on the ground'; VK2-13)
A warp with fromLevel = 0 that moves water hands the moved shores to S1's water operator as its new water (§7.3 (b) 1)

Warp kernels vs MFCG tools: Displace = displace (drags vertices by dragCm, full weight inside innerRadiusCm, falling linearly to 0 at radiusCm); Liquify = liquify (as displace with smooth cosine falloff over the whole radius); Relax = relax (Laplacian relaxation toward equal edge lengths); Bloat = bloat (each L1 cell under the brush grows about its centroid by strength, neighbours yielding); Pinch = pinch (cell shrinks about centroid); Equalize = equalize (each cell moves vertices toward equal interior angles); swirl (own local rotation about brush centre, not MFCG); jitter (seeded random displacement from warp.jitter)

MFCG Rotate maps to the 'rotation' view key (§2.9): whole-map rotation about the frame centre as view state, never a vertex operation (would re-snap every vertex, §3.6); model north (+y) unchanged; the compass is decoupled - view key trueNorth (default: keeps pointing at model north) or free (own angle, MFCG's behaviour)

Measure tool (L10, L08): an @plat/app ruler — polyline length in metres and feet; area mode in m², ha and acres; snapping to way centrelines, face edges and vertices via the display-list index (8 px radius) — RoleIndex.snap in the tile worker via §8.9's snap query, answered within one frame, unsnapped point shown until then (NR-4); exact in world cm; a measurement is view data and can be saved as an annotation.

J-DET-15: Chose MFCG's whole-map Rotate as a view rotation with a compass that points at model north by default (and can be decoupled) over rotating model coordinates — because wind, sun, aspect and slope read model north and GeoJSON must stay in the model frame (§7.1).

home.anchor: J-DET-15 (index row stays in the main document's Judgment calls index; the row names §7.1)

facts.statement: Picture exports (SVG, PNG, VTT) use the view's rotation; GeoJSON keeps model coordinates and records the rotation

Drawing at the authoring boundary (GEO-33): pointer samples resampled along arc length to spacing >= minEdge, simplified with topology-preserving Visvalingam at minEdge, a self-crossing stroke split into simple runs before insertChain (§3.4)

drawWater takes add rings (unioned by the boolean engine) and subtract rings (a land brush), so an island is a subtract ring inside an add ring and overlapping sea shapes union (FTG's method); rivers and canals take a line and a width
drawBoundary selects the L1 cells whose area lies at least 50 % inside the drawn polygon; the district boundary becomes those cells' boundary; the dry run shows the snapped boundary before commit

J-DET-14: Chose to make `drawBoundary` snap to whole L1 cells over creating invisible `district_bound` edges through blocks — because every seam edge must be typed street, water, wall, reservation boundary (`reserve`), field, cliff or frame for stage 2's `SeamContract` (§7.1).

home.anchor: J-DET-14 (index row stays in the main document's Judgment calls index; the row names §7.1)

facts.statement: A drawWay of class bridge across a river face becomes a Bridge whose deck is §4.2 S1 (5)'s perpendicular deck at the point where the drawn line crosses the channel's centreline; the drawn way's ends are routed to the deck by S4's operator (§7.3)

drawFootprint (COV-FTG-M01) places a hand-drawn footprint (concave allowed, simple) on the plot containing it; spanning several plots proposes their JOIN in the dry run; on unplotted land (green, residue, field) creates a plot around it with access to the nearest way, or returns a conflict if none is reachable; the host plot's site plan is re-fitted around it as a fixed slot (buildings no longer fitting listed in the fate report)
build places a building of a class on a plot (site plan picks the footprint when none is given) - §4.11's build(...)

moveFootprint moves or turns a footprint; leaving its plot re-homes it to the plot it lands on with both site plans re-fitted; swapUse exchanges two buildings' uses, occupants and assignments atomically (footprints stay); fill forces an arrangement on the scope's plots and re-runs S11 there

paint (COV-FTG-M04) sets roof kind, roof colour or wall colour on every building whose footprint centroid lies under the brush path (ids resolved at dry run and stored); paintGround records a ground-cover region in the style (pixels only)

The tree brush is a batch of instance events on the entities under the brush (§8.10), one undo step; painting trees where no green entity exists first logs a drawGreen (a wood on open land, a yard_planting in a yard) to host them; instance events also carry close-up presentation edits (PART II II.4)
Field brushes are setField strokes (§7.2); the terrain brush's water mode chooses whether water stays (locked, default) or follows the new ground (follow, §7.3)

People (COV-FTG-C12, C13): a lock with paths fixes chosen attributes of a person (name, age, role ...); New random on a person re-derives it with a new reroll keeping locked paths; relations and schedules are not re-derived by a person reroll (town-wide, §10)
setAttrMany edits many entities at once (job, workplace, schedule, household relocation) from a query resolved to ids at dry run and stored, so replay never re-runs the query; one undo step

Edit targets (owner amendment 5), clause by clause: every generated element is editable; every rule table and preset is editable (§7.6) by users via the preference layer and by us via new table versions; edits are first-class events that persist (log, §2.9), undo (§7.4; undo and redo are log events so they work in shared documents), survive regeneration (§7.2-§7.3) and migrate between versions (§7.5); the generator repairs around them locally (§7.3 operators, F-REDERIVE); the preference and override layer sits above the defaults (§7.6)

Edit-target table (15 rows): terrain - setField(terrain) with water locked/follow, drawWater (hollows, lakes), setAttr on site features; water/coast/rivers - drawWater, moveVertex on shores and coasts, moveCourseKnot, setAttr (bank class), delete; ways/junctions/bridges - drawWay (class bridge for a new crossing), moveVertex, warp, split, merge, delete, setAttr (class, width, surface, name; bridge kind); districts - drawBoundary, merge, split, setAttr (kind, character, name), regenerate, adjust, setAttr(fabric)+regenerate = stage-2 template replacement; blocks/plots - split, join, merge, fill, setAttr (use, owner), regenerate, lock, assign; buildings - drawFootprint, build, moveFootprint, swapUse, paint, setAttr (class, heights, roof), delete, convert (demolish, abandon, decay, ruin, clear, rebuild), assign; walls/gates/towers - drawWall, moveVertex, setAttr, delete, convert (wallToWay, gateToJunction); greenery/trees - drawGreen, tree brush, instance, setAttr, delete; fields - setField (prosperity, density, greenery), setAttr on FieldBands (explicit re-banding); names/labels - setAttr (text), moveLabel, hideLabel, rerollLayer(naming) town-wide or ids; layers/style - setLayer, setStyle, paintGround; people/households - setAttr, setAttrMany, lock with paths, regenerate (person scope), pin; close-ups (stage 2) - every kind above after closeup, instance for presentation; rule tables/presets - editTable, editPreset; history - epoch, convert, rebase, upgrade, undo, redo

Dry-run validation (G-R10): every event is validated before commit on the scratch overlay - the schema, the batch-local and stage-end invariants of its scope (§5.3), the edit-fate report of its effective scope with the case-(4) renames (§7.3 item 4); for a chained operator the whole chain runs on the overlay so the report lists every re-sited bridge, re-routed or cut way and re-based building before commit; for undo or redo, the independence check of §7.4

Dry-run conflicts come back as actions (nearest valid position, blocking lock, fates to confirm, dependent events), never silently resolved; a warp that would break an invariant is halved and reported

Logging (LC-31): every model change over the bridge is a doc.apply of EditEvents logged one to one; no bridge command changes the model any other way; undo and redo are EditEvents (§7.4) travelling as doc.changed / doc.apply, the envelope's session is their EditBase.session, and a client never truncates a bridged log; a provider output refused at §2.9's cap returns the requesting edit as doc.rejected { reason 'invalid', conflicts } (VD2-8).

Protection kinds: a locked entity (or locked attribute paths) is a fixed input - regeneration never changes it and re-derives dependants around it; a pinned entity keeps existence and position, other attributes may re-derive; an edited attribute implicitly pins that attribute and the entity's existence against Regenerate and New random (O9 restored, LC-8) unless the user chooses 'discard edits in scope', only by confirming the fate list (§7.3), recorded in the event; an assigned attribute is held at its assignment within drift bounds (§7.7)
Every finer face under a locked or pinned entity is a fixed input too
Precedence when protections meet: lock > assignment > user-drawn geometry > rule tables > defaults (§7.7)
places: §5.2 F-EDIT 5139 (lock > assignment > drawn geometry > rules) (restated, per DETERMINISM-382)

facts.statement: Drawn constraints (G-P8; LC-10, GEO-11) - ways, water, walls, greens, district boundaries, footprints - enter the plat through insertChain as mandatory chains with their roles (§3.6) after §7.1's resampling; locked by default; applied at their log position: inserted into the current state and, for the coarsest faces the chain touches, the class's local operator (§7.3) re-derives the affected scope

Drawn-constraint operator mapping: drawn water via S1's water operator (re-sites crossings on moved reaches and re-routes ways that used them); drawn ways via S4's and S5's (arterials re-route to reuse them); drawn walls via S7's run re-trace; drawn boundaries via S6's regrouping; drawn greens via S12 on covered faces; drawn footprints via S11 on the host plot
Session and replay run the same code at the same log position in the same canonical insertion order, so they produce the same digest (§6.5)

'Rebuild around my drawings' (the surviving form of the old insert-before-stage rule): moves drawn constraints into the recipe as constraints of their stages, regenerates the town, shows the diff as a migration does (§7.5), and commits as a rebase (reason drawnConstraintsRebuilt)

J-DET-6: Chose one ordered replay fold — drawn constraints, epochs, rebases and upgrades applied at their log positions — over hoisting drawn constraints before their stage — because hoisting makes every reload regenerate a different town than the one on screen; hoisting survives only as the explicit "Rebuild around my drawings" rebase (§7.2, §7.4).

home.anchor: J-DET-6 (index row stays in the main document's Judgment calls index; the row names §7.2, §7.4)

facts.statement: The terrain brush (LC-7) edits the heightfield raster under S1's terrain operator (§7.3) with the same stroke list and single clamp (to the declared relief limit, §2.3)

Terrain brush water mode 'locked' (default): the stroke's delta is zero on every cell whose centre lies in a water face or within one cell of a shore or bank edge, and under the footprints, bands and decks of locked or pinned entities (lock > drawn geometry); water bodies, courses and widths do not change; the dry run shows the masked cells

Terrain brush water mode 'follow': the stroke may change bed and bank cells; every reach whose bed cells changed is re-traced by S1's water operator (§7.3), which re-sites its crossings and re-routes the ways that used them

In both terrain modes S1's terrain operator re-bases every building, wing, tower, gate, wall vertex, bridge and pier whose terrain samples changed (§7.3), re-runs drainage locally and re-evaluates the terrain-reading field drivers, so the town stands on the new ground exactly as a reload would compute it

facts.statement: Edit fates (LC-8): the dry run lists every protected entity in the effective scope - locked, pinned, edited or assigned; hosting a pin; target of a pinned label placement; housing a pinned or edited person; an edited close-up entity - with its fate: kept (fixed input); carried (to its anchor-matched successor, §6.3, after the class-family check: an override moves with the address only if the successor's class family accepts the attribute, never by id alone); orphaned (no successor: edit stays in the log, listed in the document's orphan table, re-attachable); discarded (only with 'discard edits in scope', recorded as supersede events)

A chained edit's report also lists unprotected consequences (bridges re-sited or removed, ways re-routed, cut or pruned, buildings re-based or demolished) with their lifecycle events

Kinds without a derivation record (ways, districts, walls) re-derive from their current upstream state, which only an explicit edit or an epoch changes; the provenance rebuilt by their last derivation or the verification replay holds what they read (§2.8); their names keep their naming records

The dependency graph is the audit: Provenance.deps (every entity records what it read) serves (a) as the audit of item 7 and (b) as an Adjust optimisation - invalidating exactly the closure of a changed parameter or table slice - only where the oracle has proven that stage's declarations complete; elsewhere tree scoping applies

Lifecycle lock/unlock/pin/unpin: created by UI or API on any address, optionally attribute paths; read as entity flags derived from the log; persisted in the log; regenerate: a fixed input, dependants re-derive around it; a lock on a name path keeps the naming record dormant and an unlock that frees it runs §6.3 case (4) in its dry run (rename listed, confirmed, stored; VD4-3); undo: inverse event (undo of a lock that frees a name runs case (4); an unlock that re-drew a name keeps an undo record with the former name and naming record); migrate: address mapped (§7.5); an orphaned lock re-imposes its last geometry as a drawn constraint unless the user drops it

Lifecycle setAttr/setAttrMany/paint: bulk query resolved to ids at dry run; read as entity attributes, flags.edited, editedPaths; log; regenerate: an input override at the stage computing the attribute (name: S13a keeps and never re-draws it while edited, naming record dormant; district kind: S6 reads as fixed; heights and roof: S11); implicitly pinned (§7.2); undo: inverse with old values in the undo record; undoing or reverting a setAttr on a generated name returns it to unedited and runs case (4), the rename listed and confirmed and the replaced text kept in that event's undo record (VD4-3); migrate: attribute names schema-versioned with a rename table; unmappable -> orphan, reported

Lifecycle moveVertex/warp: vertex handle stored as lattice point + role signature / staged warp session with Apply; persisted as the operation (arena key, strokes, fromLevel; moveVertex's at with VertexSig), per-vertex displacements only as a verification record; regenerate: whole-step validation (§3.6) - moved edges >= minEdge and against swept triangles, one vertex per lattice point, clearance, global deterministic halving; vertices on fixed coarser routes slide; locked/pinned entities' vertices held; kernel-pinned vertices move (pins constrain smoothing, simplification and cutting); point-anchored records and stored wing rings move with host faces and everything carried is re-based; a move of water goes to S1's water operator; undo record: moved vertices, re-derived faces, promoted/demoted vertices' and edges' former birth levels and flags, former points of displaced records, former wing rings and stored compositions, former bases; migrate: operation replays at its log position; moveVertex binds by resolveVertexAt - exact point, else signature match within the rebind radius, else orphaned and reported

facts.statement: Undo targets: each session has its own stacks; undo targets the session's latest live event (live unless an undo targets it and no later redo re-applies it); a group counts as one step and of names its first event; redo targets the session's latest undo whose target is still undone; a new event from the session clears its redo stack; an unshared document has one stored session so undo there is linear and continues across reloads
A session with the owner role (the app's role for an unshared document) may name any live event (undo(h, of), §11.2), which is how events of an earlier session are undone

Undo record: every committed event keeps the inverse event when one is exact, otherwise the faces, entity records, lifecycle events and tombstones its effective scope replaced, the former birth levels, split flags and stripped contact names of the vertices it promoted, the former levels and flags of vertices and edges it demoted or unflagged (§2.2 rule 3; CommitRecord.promoted, demoted, unflagged), and its touched set (addresses created, changed or removed); undo costs O(scope), never a model copy

undo restores the target's scope from its record and withdraws the addresses the target minted (§6.3); redo re-applies the target at the head from its stored already-resolved payload (scope, absolute rerolls, confirmed fates), reproducing the target's result exactly

Independence check: an undo is applied only if every live event after its target is independent - the later event's touched set and effective-scope faces are disjoint from the target's touched set and the target's effective-scope faces dilated by one ring of adjacent faces at the coarsest level either touches; otherwise the dry run returns an F-EDIT conflict listing dependent events and authors; the session may undo its own dependent events first and an owner may undo through a chain; a redo is checked the same way against live events after its undo

Every client folds the same events in the host's order on the same state, so the check has the same outcome everywhere; an undo or redo whose check fails at its log position (only possible in a hand-built log) is a reported no-op identically on every client and on replay; a whole-town event (upgrade, rebase, Re-derive from S1) is undoable only while it is the latest live event

A client holding no record for a target (joined after it, or record left the cap) rebuilds it by replaying from its nearest checkpoint before the target or from the base, and says it is slow; the replay keeps full records only for events later undo events target (found by a log pre-scan) and touched sets for all; deterministic, so every client reaches the same state

Truncation, in unshared documents only (VD2-3): when an unshared document's undo targets the immediately preceding event, the engine may drop both from the log and hold the target on the session's redo stack; a redo re-appends the target with its original seq and advances nextSeq by one (the seq the kept log's redo would have spent), so every later event and every user-created address is the same in both logs; canonical nextSeq (§2.9) never moves back; lifecycle block, archive and model digest of the truncated log equal those with the pair kept; the truncated target is held in the saved undo section (UndoRecord.redo, §2.9) so a redo after reload re-appends it; a document attached to a host bridge never truncates

B-EDIT truncation property test over random sequences (§6.5 (9)) folds each both ways (including a redo followed by a user-created entity, setAttr(name)+undo and naming rerollLayer+undo pairs each followed by a corpus selection, a corpus selection+undo truncated, saved, reloaded and redone; VD4-3, VD4-7) and requires equal model digests and equal addresses

Checkpoints: copy-on-write (arenas chunked per district, so a checkpoint costs only chunks changed since the previous one), taken whenever accumulated replay cost since the last passes 80 ms at the session's rung and before every epoch, rebase and upgrade, so any replay from a checkpoint stays <= 100 ms; a load taking §6.2 (iii)'s off-path recomputation also takes one at h0

Undo measurement (M2a): undo of a CITY district regeneration <= 30 ms; undo memory <= 25 % of the model's working set after 100 edits; (M3a) the host-and-three-clients convergence test of §11.3 with interleaved undo and redo from every client; pre-decided fallback: saved undo section shrinks to 16 events and checkpoints every 40 ms of replay cost

Expansion examples: wealthLevel in [0,1] -> field.characterOffset = lerp(-0.3, +0.3), granularity.joinMaxBonus = 2 x wealthLevel (fractional part = probability a candidate plot takes one more join, from the plot.join stream), greenery.parkPer1000 = lerp(0.1, 0.8); planned in [0,1] -> growth.headingSigma = lerp(20, 5) degrees per 100 m of street, growth.crossroadProb = lerp(0.02, 0.15), avenues.probability = smoothstep(0.3, 0.7, planned) per eligible tier-1 way
Every internal parameter is documented (unit, range, effect, provenance, consuming stage) and reachable in the advanced panel (O10 a); the registry test proves 100 %

Surprise me (LC-30) draws every intent field from its declared range and weights on the intent.surprise stream of a fresh seed and writes the drawn intent into the recipe, so the town's link reproduces it

Character and circumstances: a district character vector (wealth, density, age, function mix, planned/organic, greenery, fortification, building scale) supplied automatically per district and overridable; circumstances (era, economy, lordship, government, biome, season, threat, trade, population, terrain events, landscape toggles) as data presets on a timeline that schedules epoch events - an epoch happens only as an epoch event in the log (§7.1, hook 8)

Assignment { id; granularity 'building'/'neighbourhood'/'dispersed'; target? (one building/plot or one district); dispersed? { count; kind: BuildingClass or string; criteria: PlacementCriteria }; name?; function?; shapeClass?: BuildingClass; drift: DriftBounds (+/- area %, +/- floors, allowed layouts and roof kinds, class family); precedence 'overClassRules'; placed?: Id[] (solver placements, persisted with the event) }
PlacementCriteria { districts?; districtKinds?; prosperityBands?; minSpacingM?; nearM?: { to: 'water'/'gate'/'market'/'centre'/Id; maxM }[]; frontageClass?: WayClass[]; avoid?: Id[] }

PlacementSolver.solve(doc, a: Assignment, fixed: Id[] (mapped placements, kept), exclude: Id[] (locked entities), rng: Stream): KernelResult<Id[]> - greedy max-min-distance by score with a bounded swap pass; reports infeasibility with the nearest achievable count

Precedence at S10-S11: lock > assignment > user-drawn geometry > rule tables > defaults (LC-9); a targeted assignment on a locked entity (or locked attribute path) is an F-EDIT conflict returned as an action (unlock, choose another target, or keep the lock); the dispersed solver never places a member on a locked entity

facts.statement: Re-solving: when a dispersed member is superseded without a successor only that member is re-placed, every mapped placement fixed (minimum spacing measured from them), nothing still mapped moves; epochs keep placed members; members are added only by an event changing the count or criteria, then placed with existing members fixed

A whole-neighbourhood assignment sets the district's character and class mix while every building stays individually diversified by class rules within drift bounds; drift bounds are inputs to BuildingGenerator.compose; assignments are events (persist, undo, migrate) and take precedence over class rules (O10 e); stable addresses are §6.3's

Forms catalogue (should-have; schema is the must-have hook): a form is a row { id, constraints, growthProgramme, signature } - constraints (site request, wall rings, plaza position, planned flag, gate count band), growth programme (stage regimes and branch tables, §4.4), morphometric signature (radial share of arterials, orthogonality index, street-density profile, block-area CV, enclosed share); initial rows: organic, bastide-grid, linear-street (growth anisotropy a = 8 along the main road, §4.4), radial, hill-acropolis, bridge-town, port-quay-parallel, monastic-close, island-city (shore destinations, §4.2 S3), confluence, twin-town, polycentric (two or three nuclei, §4.2 S3); forms compose by growth stage; O10 (g)'s classifier runs on the signature vector

Control registry: declares for every control its output metric (e.g. density -> buildings per ha; wealthLevel -> median plot area and greenery share; greenery -> private green share), range, consuming stage (earliest stage reading it), locality class (local: consumed at S10 or later or spatially scoped; or re-derive from Sk, fate report first, §7.1; LC-4), continuity class (continuous or discrete with levels), and a documentation anchor linked as context help; the same fields generate @plat/docs' reference pages (COV-FTG-A25)

Monotone and continuous stated statistically (GEO-41): CI sweep runs each continuous control over 21 evenly spaced steps x 50 seeds at TOWN and CITY (METROPOLIS nightly): monotone - mean metric moves in the declared direction between adjacent steps, a reversal of at most 2 standard errors allowed; continuous - no adjacent step moves the mean by more than eps = max(3 SE, 3 x the median adjacent change of the mean); per seed - at most 10 % of seeds jump by more than 5 x the median per-seed step at any one step; formula fixed now, SEs and medians measured by the M1 sweep
facts.values: 21 steps x 50 seeds; 2 SE; eps = max(3 SE, 3 x median); 10 %; 5 x

facts.statement: Continuous controls are smooth maps with no thresholds inside (VG's '1 vs 0.999' is the failure); discrete controls (walls on/off, form) declare their effect in the report

Sweep-failure fallback (NF-D7): failing interval = smallest run of adjacent failing steps widened by one step each side; (1) the control's expansion row is replaced over that interval by a smoothstep between the row's values at the interval's ends (table change with provenance 'sweep fallback', a declared shift §6.4) and the sweep re-runs; (2) if it still fails it is declared discrete: continuity class discrete with levels where the metric's mean is stable (steps between failing intervals, each represented by its median step), shown as a stepped control in basic and advanced panels, listed in the report and release notes
The population control is continuous by construction (§10.2's prefix-stable roster) and checked the same way; its work-limit side is §5.1 (5)'s flat F-WORK rate

J-DET-27: Chose, for a control that fails its sweep, a smoothstep over the failing interval of its expansion row and then a declared discrete control, over widening ε until it passes — because a widened ε hides the jump the user sees while the discrete declaration tells the truth (§7.8; NF-D7).

facts.statement: Proxy thumbnails (G-R4; O16 e; LC-30, SCL-16): 'Surprise me' and the size / water controls preview six candidate towns as the towns' own S0-S4 runs (site, water, backbone at city LOD from those stages' display list) under the same deterministic work limits as a full generation (§5.1), so a proxy is bit-identical to the first stages of the town it previews; choosing one continues that recipe from its committed S4 state and asserts the S4 digest equals the proxy's
Proxy budgets on reference hardware (§12): all six within 1 s at TOWN (O16 (e)); at CITY and METROPOLIS progressive - the first within 300 ms, each within 250 ms at CITY and 500 ms at METROPOLIS
facts.values: 1 s TOWN; first 300 ms; 250 ms CITY; 500 ms METROPOLIS

facts.statement: Control surface is a budget (R15): the front door is one action; the basic panel holds <= 12 controls - seed (with the Surprise me dice as its button), size rung, water setting and side, walls, castle, gates, features (one checkbox strip: plaza, temple, shanty town, farms, greens - MFCG's first-level toggles, one control; MFP-12), planned/organic, wealth level, greenery, style preset, labels
Everything else sits behind an advanced panel; 100 % of parameters documented (registry test); new templates and presets are data, not code; release notes name known defects

D-9: "no restart path" is a design property; acceptance numbers are requested-feature delivery by ladder tier (tier-6 omission of a requested feature a failure, target 0; degraded ≤ 5 %) and p95 time per delivered town on MFCG's worst configurations (≤ 1.0 s vs MFCG 3.7–4.0 s). Rejected: "0 whole-map restarts" as the number; a p99-bounded restart tier. Cost: low.
places: §13.5 MFCG-worst and delivery rows (restated, per SCOPE-518)

facts.statement: D-14: booleans, buffers and bands on the kernel's own arrangement — one engine on every host; Clipper2 and polygon-clipping as CI oracles only; the straight skeleton built in-house under §3.8's contract and validator; the M0 bars and pre-decided fallbacks in §3.7–§3.8 (Clipper2-WASM as the single engine; the downgrades as the default paths). Rejected: CGAL (GPL); a JS skeleton port; a runtime pure-JS boolean fallback (second engine, different digests). Cost: low (adapters).

D-23: deterministic transcendentals through dmath (our TypeScript port of fdlibm 5.3 with Sun's notice) with an allowlist lint (exact Math members only; ** only with literal exponents 0–4, rewritten to multiplications; ratio() for computed divisors) that also scans vendored dependencies. Rejected: in-house polynomial approximations; trusting Math.*; the @stdlib packages (94-package closure). Cost: low.

Effective scope: the coarsest faces covering an edit's scope at its level (possibly larger than the drawn area), union over chained operators, plus the seam exception; shown to the user before commit; EditScope is stored resolved to it
Touched set: the list of addresses an event created, changed or removed, kept in its undo record; used by the independence check and by edits during load recomputation
Live event: an event is live unless an undo targets it and no later redo re-applies it
Render key: the low 64 bits of an entity's entity key (mixing seed key and lineage), used with the instance ordinal for decoration draws (§8.1 item 5; VD2-6)
h0: the log head at which a load's copy-on-write checkpoint of the decoded state is taken; the rebase at-value when the saved town is kept after edits made during load verification

Plain-words intro restates §8.1-§8.10: one display list feeds screen/SVG/PNG/print/3-D; style sheets are data; blocks get their own ground tone so streets and squares are the only paper-coloured gaps; walls/towers/gates at a table symbol size; too-small houses drawn as merged masses; a tile pyramid for zoom; trees keep places and are movable one by one; one Canvas 2D renderer draws every look; layers and heights carry sewer/island hooks (§8.4).
LodBand, Role and ZoomStop are declared in @plat/model so @plat/labels and @plat/render share them without importing each other's code (N-22).
LodBand = 'city' | 'district' | 'neighbourhood' | 'building'.
MarkKind has ten values: area, ribbon, outline, hatch, glyph, text, instances, shadow, field, shore.

MarkTable: one row per mark, every column a typed array so any slice is transferable (§8.9). Columns and bytes/mark: kind 1, semantic 2 (index into DisplayList.semantics), entity 4 (interned handle, session-local, never hashed), key 8 (2 words: render key), layer 1, z 4, lodMask 1 (one bit per LodBand), pass 1, group 4 (district handle), bbox 16 (world cm), geomStart+geomLen 8, revision 4; attrs = named 4 B/mark columns (heightCm, baseCm, prosperity, class, block, bankKind, waterKind, exposure, material, tintKey, …).
facts.values: fixed columns 54 B/mark; attrs 4 B/mark each

facts.statement: A mark's geometry never changes with the band; lodMask only says in which bands the mark exists.
pass values: 0 fills, 1 casings, 2 bodies, 3 linework and symbols, 4 overlay; the pass is the order within a slot.
group (the district handle) is the unit of delivery and invalidation, never a raster cache unit; rasters are cached per world-aligned tile (§8.8), never per district.
MarkTable.revision = low 32 bits of the entity's §6.2 leaf digest (content revision of its inputs); it is the cache key (LC-23).
GeomTable { rings: Uint32Array ring start offsets; coords: Int32Array x,y cm pairs }.
FieldRaster { id; originX, originY (cm); cellCm; cols; rows; values Float32Array|Int16Array; meaning 'heightCm'|'shoreDistanceCm'|'depthCm'|'custom' }.
StringTable { utf8: Uint8Array; offsets: Uint32Array } holds names and species kinds as one transferable UTF-8 blob.

LabelTable: one row per LabelEntity drawn at the band — everything S13b reads: mark, key (2 words, render key), kind, lodMask, priority, areaM2 (order's second key), text, shortText (StringTable rows, ~0 = none), spines (GeomTable range, in preference order), anchors, breakAt, parent (row of parent QuarterNode's label; ~0 at root), pinStop (−1 = not pinned), pinSizePx, pinAnchor (world cm), pinSpine, pinSeq (the pin's moveLabel seq = PinnedPlacement.seq; order of the pin pass, NR3-3), hidden, revision.
facts.values: ≤ 96 B per row plus geometry and text

facts.statement: InstanceTable: one row per instances mark: mark, layout (stamp|grid|line), offset (2 words, cm), rotationCdeg, spacingCm, species range, overrides range; speciesRows {kind (StringTable row), inner, outer, leafType}; overrideRows {ordinal (2 words), op, x, y, style (2 words, InstanceStyle fields), state byOrdinal|rematched|orphaned (§8.10)}.

DisplayList { marks, geom, rasters, semantics, strings, labels, instances, salts: Record<RerollableConcern, number> (§6.1's effective salt of every rerollable concern; type generated from the concern registry, VD2-5), layers: LayerSpec[], bounds, version }.
DisplayDelta { version; groups; removed (entity handles); marks; geom; strings; labels; instances; dirty: Box[] }.

DisplayListBuilder (S14, runs in the generation worker on the read-only model): build(model, band, groups?) = full build (generation, load) or one band for named districts (on-demand bands, §8.9); update(model, changed, band) → DisplayDelta for edits, scoped regeneration and override resolution (§8.10).

The display list is built by S14 from the model through the entity registry (each type → marks per band); backends never read the model. Footprint geometry is identical in every band (O12 a; O17 i); only emitted marks and programs change.
field marks carry a world-space raster (terrain height for hillshade and contours, distance to shore for water ramps and foam, depth) and cost nothing when no program reads them (VIS-12).
shore marks are chains, one per maximal run of equal attributes along a water face's boundary, with attributes bankKind (§2.3), waterKind, exposure and shoreClass (bay/headland/straight, §2.3).

exposure = sheltered when the segment bounds a harbour basin, moat, canal or pond, or when its fetch (longest straight run across water within ±30° of the outward normal) is below 300 m; river for river and tributary faces; else open (VIS-13).
text marks carry one LabelTable row each, so label placement (S13b, §9.2) needs nothing but the display list (N-4).
Draw order is slot-major across the whole scene: every mark of slot s (§8.2 layer-order table) draws before any mark of slot s+1 in every tile; within a slot by pass, then z, then key (N-7).

A mark's slot is resolved from (semantic, pass) by the style's OrderSlot entries when the sheet loads — exactly one slot per pair or the sheet is refused (§8.2, NR-3) — and cached per style version as a (semantic index, pass) → slot table.

S14 emits one mark per pass an entity draws in, as the registry declares per band; a cased ribbon is a pass-1 casing mark plus a pass-2 body mark over one geometry range (≈ 60 B for the second mark, never a second geometry copy; one extra mark per drawn way, a few thousand at CITY).
The raised under-copy (slot 11) and the projected-shadow union (slot 10) are not marks: they are per-tile operations over caster marks, placed by OrderSlot entries with `derived` (§8.2).

Way casings (slot 5) and way bodies (slot 6) are separate slots holding every way class; shipped sheets' entries {slot 5, 'way.*', passes [1]} and {slot 6, 'way.*', passes [2]}, so every way casing precedes every way body across the scene (GEO-28); masses, fields, woods and shadows keep their slots after the roads (K16, NG shadow order, MFCG wards after roads).

Every derived artefact (roof geometry, label spine, footprint mass, instance set, tile raster, glyph run) is keyed by (entity key or tile address, content revision, band, style version, roof construction where it applies), never by id alone (LC-23, NF-D10).

Every hash drawn at render time (multi-colour role index, weathering, stamp tile variant, grid jitter, crown index/colour/scale jitter, hatch phase, roof detail, ruin dash) is RH32(tag, key, salt[, ordinal or cell][, style id]); the style id enters only for looks (colours, crowns, hatch), never positions.

RH32 = the render hash, distinct from the string hash H32 of §13.6; the tag is an index into a fixed render-tag table; words folded through MurmurHash3's 32-bit finaliser; never reads the interned handle.

Because the entity key is a pure function of model data (seed and lineage), an unchanged model renders pixel-identically after a reload (§6.2) and golden PNGs hold (§13.3); where a render rule orders entities (tint colouring, §8.2) it uses address order (§6.3).

Display-list size: 54 B/mark fixed + 4 B/mark per attribute column + label/instance tables + geometry; CITY city band ≈ 60 000 marks ≈ 3.2 MB fixed, ≈ 2.4 MB attributes, ≈ 4 MB coordinates, ≤ 0.5 MB label/instance/string rows ≈ 10 MB (N-9 c).
The tile worker holds the only full display-list copy; after each transfer the generation worker keeps only the columns update() reads (entity, bbox, group).

An export that draws (SVG, PNG, print, .dd2vtt image) builds its own transient list in the generation worker: SVG writes from it there and releases it; a raster export transfers it to the tile worker with its request, which rasters from it and releases it (NR-5, NR3-6).

J-R1: Chose a columnar, transferable mark table over `Mark[]` objects — because a 60 000-object list costs the receiving thread ≈ 140 ms to deserialise while typed arrays transfer in constant time and slice cheaply into deltas (§8.1).

facts.statement: StyleSheet { id; version; family 'ink'|'lit'|'hatched'|'painterly'|'graphic'; palette Record<Role, Color|Color[]>; symbols Record<semantic, Partial<Record<LodBand, Symbolisation>>>; order Record<LodBand, OrderSlot[]>; programs Record<semantic, Partial<Record<LodBand, PaintProgram[]>>>; roofConstruction 'plain'|'skeletonHip'|'skeletonGable'|'fakeGablePerWing' (over stored wings §2.6); labels LabelStyle (§9.4); shadows {projected 'off'|'drop'|'prism'; penumbraPx; sun SunSpec; raised {on; offsetM [x,y]; minPx; maxPx}}; overrides ThematicRow[]; post PostOp[]; budgets Record<LodBand, DetailBudget>; referenceBackend 'canvas2d' }.
A style sheet maps (semantic, attribute predicates, band) to paint programs over a palette of roles and a symbolisation table.
Every shipped preset's referenceBackend is 'canvas2d' (§8.9).
Symbolisation { mode 'model'|'paper'; k? (drawn = k × model width); minPx?; maxPx?; px? (paper width at 1×) }.

OrderSlot { slot (row of the layer-order table; several entries may share a row); semantic (a semantic or a dotted prefix ending '.*'); passes? (absent = every pass, NR-3); derived? 'raised'|'shadow' (per-tile raised under-copy or projected-shadow union over the matched marks, §8.4); reason; recordedAs? (reference step matched, for order parity §8.3) }.

Roles (23): paper, road (way bodies, squares, bridges; = paper in the ink family so streets are negative space), ground (built-block ground, yards at city band, settled ground), court, garden, green, tree, field, verge, water, building, roof, wall, ink (every outline and text), label, shadow, ambience, light, sand, plank, grid, snow, lights.
A role never changes meaning across the bands or the presets of one family; the reference schemas (MFCG 13 keys, NG 26, VG 40) map onto the role set without loss.

Contrast matrix (replaces the luminance rule; O12 f), city band unless a row says otherwise, floors ΔE2000 / ΔL*: road/ground 6/5; ground/building 12/12; road/building 15/15; garden/building and green/building 10/—; tree/water 10/—; green/road and tree/green 8/—; water/road and water/ground 8/—; wall/water 20/—; field/road and field/ground 4/—; court/road 4/— and court/ground 3/— (district band and finer; courts drawn as ground at city band, §8.5); ink/road, ink/ground, ink/paper 40/50 (the label floor, §9.4); ink/building 30/40; ink/tree 25/30.

The contrast matrix is checked (1) on every palette when loaded (built-in, user-edited, random) and (2) on rendered city-band images in B-ZOOM using the mean CIELAB of pixels whose top mark has each role (read from the pick buffer), for every pair present in the view.
A failing user palette edit is shown with the failing pair and kept only with an explicit 'accept low contrast' flag recorded in the report.
MFCG's default palette has garden = building (ΔE2000 0.6) and tree = water (0.0); recorded as reference weaknesses not to copy (VIS-2).
Random style: each role's L* within ±12 of the family's shipped value, chroma in [0,18] in ink and [0,30] otherwise, any hue, keeping road = paper where the family ties them (N-26).

Bounded palette repair: take the first failing pair in matrix row order; raise its lighter role's L* by 1 (up to 97) or, if already 97, lower the darker role's L* by 1 (down to 3); re-check every pair; stop when all pass or after 100 steps; a repaired palette must still pass after sRGB conversion; a failed repair is redrawn on the next attempt; after three failed attempts the family's shipped palette is used and the report says so; ends by construction (≤ 300 steps).
facts.values: step 1 L*; bounds 97 / 3; 100 steps; 3 attempts; ≤ 300 steps

facts.statement: The old rule (raise the lighter role until every pair passes) could cycle or never end.

home.anchor: drop from the normative text; keep at most a one-line receipt pointer

facts.statement: Measured on 2 000 seeded draws per family (fixall_rendering_r2_palette.out): 4-18 % pass as drawn, 77-83 % after first repair (median 5-17 steps), 99.1-99.6 % within three attempts; shipped-palette fallback 0.4-0.9 %.
Confirmation at M3b (random styles ship with O12's extras): shipped-palette fallback ≤ 2 % of 10 000 draws per family; pre-decided fallback: the L* window narrows from ±12 to ±8 and the run repeats.

J-R30: Chose a bounded random-style repair — fixed row order, ≤ 100 steps, ≤ 3 draws, then the shipped palette — over the unbounded raise — because only a bounded procedure can promise that every presented style meets the floors (§8.2; N-26).
