facts.statement: Role values table (our own, calibratable rows), sRGB for ink / lit / hatched: paper #F6EDDE/#DED6CC/#D4CABF; road #F6EDDE (=paper)/#D8D0C8/#B6A99B; ground #DED0BB/#CBB9A2/#D4CABF (=paper); court #ECE0C6/#D1C5B2/#B7B898; building/roof lit side #A49689/#AD8A72/#9D7D68; ink/label #292522/#34281E/#2A231D; wall #292522 (=ink)/#857A6E/#685C51; water #AABBC5/#6D9CB9/#98AFBB; green #BCC8AB/#9AB37F/#B0B48C; garden #C7CCAF/#8EA96D/#A8AF83; tree #7E907A/#5B7A4F/#798C67; field #ECDFBF/#D8BE89/#E5D6B5; verge #D9DCC5/#ADBB95/#BBBEA1; shadow = ink at α 0.35/0.45/0.40.

facts.statement: Symbolisation (VIS-1): drawn width px = clamp(k × model width × px per metre, minPx, maxPx) in model mode, or a fixed paper width at 1× (times device pixel ratio) in paper mode; no length is written in any reference's private unit.
Exaggeration never enters the model, GeoJSON, VTT, glTF or CityJSON (they carry model widths); styled SVG and PNG carry drawn widths.

ink rows are calibrated on MFCG's metre-unit export at the matched view scale (MFCG size 40 at 0.816 px/m, 1.23 m/px): walls 7.6 m, towers 15.2 m across, road cores 8 m, piers 4.8 m; its SVG writes them in its 4 m internal unit (wall 1.9, road 2) (MN-1, MFP-8).

Symbolisation rows: wall.curtain (city, district) model k = 3 on band thickness (2.5 m → 7.5 m), minPx 2, maxPx 12 (≈ 6.1 px vs MFCG 6.2); wall.tower diameter = 2 × drawn wall width, never below model diameter (≈ 12.2 px vs 12.4); wall.gate = stroke gap max(model opening, 1.2 × drawn wall) flanked by two square blocks of side 2 × drawn wall (≈ 12 px); way.through/way.primary body (all) k = 1, minPx 1.5 (8 m core ≈ 6.5 px); way.secondary and lane symbol body (city) k = 1, minPx 1; way casing (all, paper) h = 0.5 px each side (casing = body + 2h); way.pier and bridge deck (city, district) k = 1, minPx 1 (4.8 m ≈ 3.9 px).

Symbolisation rows: building outline (city, paper) 0.5 px × clamp(s ÷ 8, ⅓, 1), s = median footprint side in px at the zoom stop (outlines thin, then hold at one third); building outline district and finer 0.5 px; raised under-copy offset (city, district, model) (+0.4 m, −1.0 m) east/north, drawn length clamped to [0.3 px, 2.5 px]; boundary treatment (fence, hedge, yard wall, railing; district and finer, paper) ≤ ½ building outline weight, never filled, gaps at gates; minimum feature (all) 2 px, met by masses and settlement dots (§8.5), never by enlarging one footprint.

Curtain walls draw after footprints; the wall symbol is clipped on its inner side to the band's inner edge minus the setback, so the exaggerated symbol overhangs only outward (berm, moat, glacis) and never covers a plot.

The dry ditch (VP2-10): the ditch residue on the town side of an on_enceinte bailey (§4.7 S10 (0), §4.8) draws with the glacis parts' role in a dry-ditch variant — fill 5 ΔL* darker than the glacis fill and, at district band and finer, a short inward hachure along its inner edge; at city band the glacis parts' plain fill; the overhang rule covers it.

Paint-program vocabulary: fill; stroke(width by symbolisation, join, cap); casing(w, h) (ink at w+2h in the casing pass, body at w in the body pass); bands(N, W, exponent, ramp); raised(offset); shadowPass(mode, colour, alpha, penumbraPx) (§8.4); hatch(angle|ridge, pitch, taper); roof(construction, dark = lit × lerp(ambience, shadow, α)); crown(library); halo(role rule) (§9.4); glyphAlongSpine; pattern(texture, tintRole, metresPerTile); faceLight(dir); ramp(field, stops); hillshade(sun, strength); contourMarks(levels, mode contour|hachure|grass); foam(widthM, alpha); feather(widthM); outlineMix(factor); tint(method, strength); weathering(amplitude); instances(library) (§8.10); vignette; ruin; symbol(glyph).

hillshade(sun, strength): Lambert on bilinear-interpolated cell normals of the terrain field, water faces masked, strength from the shadow role's alpha, multiply-composited after fills and way bodies and before buildings and trees (no blur).
foam(widthM, alpha) comes from the shore-distance field on open segments, half alpha on river, none on sheltered and quay.
feather(widthM) = three inset vector bands at α ⅔, ⅓, 0 toward open ground — no bitmap blur (COV-FTG-I05).
ruin program: outline dashed by an entity-keyed pattern, fill at 30 % alpha, rubble stipple — the hook for the owner-staged ruined state, with the none roof kind (§2.6).
Decline tone overrides (§2.8): existence = abandoned → roof tone lerped 30 % toward ground, no raised under-copy; existence = decayed → outline dashed, fill at 60 % alpha.
Lane ends: a lane's body and casing end square at the kerb of the way it meets; the junction wedge belongs to the higher-class way (renderer half of GEO-21).
Hairlines and casings are in paper px; ribbons and symbols follow the symbolisation table (MFCG's two coordinate spaces).

Multi-colour roles (XB17): an individual mark (building, roof, tree, stall) takes index RH32(role, key, salt[, instance ordinal], style id) mod n over its render key; aggregate fills (block ground, city-band masses, wood fills) take index 0; deterministic, so two renders are pixel-identical (§6.2).

tint (K12): per district a hue from a greedy colouring of the district adjacency graph in address order (§6.3): hue = base + 137.5° × colour index, stepped by 30° until every neighbour differs by ≥ 30°; method spectrum | brightness | overlay; strength 0-1; applied to roofs of built districts; outlines take lerp(ink, tint, 0.3); recomputed when the palette changes; off in ink by default.
weathering: each roof's RGB scaled by 1 + u·w, u ∈ [−1, 1] from RH32('weathering', key, salt, style id), w = 0.04 (ink), 0.06 (hatched), 0.08 (lit).

Materials, season, weather (COV-FTG-F20, K06): override rows may key roof and wall colours by roof.material and the enceinte's wall material; view state (§11.3) carries season ∈ {spring, summer, autumn, winter} and weather ∈ {clear, overcast, snow}; autumn/winter re-skin deciduous crowns (by leafType, deciduous when absent) via role variants (tree@autumn; winter = bare-crown symbol); snow lays the snow role over ground, fields and roofs while road keeps its value; overcast turns projected shadows off (raised under-copy stays); nothing in the model changes, model hash untouched.

Post operations (K07): applied once per tile after its marks: greyscale, sepia, tint(colour, strength), vignette (on the view), pixelate(cellPx), dotScreen(cellPx, angle), scanline(periodPx, alpha), crosshatchNoise(periodPx, alpha); Canvas2D on the tile's pixels in the tile worker; PNG export applies them per tile; SVG carries greyscale, sepia and tint as colour-matrix filters and omits pixel operations, which the export report lists; replaces the 'WebGL2 post hooks' pointer.
LiveLayerProvider { id; target 'base'|'overlay'; marks(view: ViewState, model: ModelView, region: Box): MarkTable } adds display-list groups that are view data, never in the model hash (K13, N-4).

Live-layer providers run in the generation worker (which holds the model); a provider is called when the view state it reads, the model, or the visible region (dilated by one tile) changes; marks are delivered as a DisplayDelta of group live.<id> (§8.9).

overlay-provider marks are drawn in the tile worker's composition step with the labels (§8.8), so a selection or moving person re-composes tiles without re-rastering; a base provider (thematic recolouring) is part of the tile key (§8.8).

Shipped live layers: live.selection (overlay); live.favourites (base: favourite buildings as a thematic override keyed by view state's favourites); live.people (overlay, registered by the simulation module: favourite persons' positions from occupancy at the view-state hour, one categorical colour per person).
Thematic layers: FTG D7's matchers are override rows keyed by entity attributes (prosperity, use, epoch, owner, material) — data, not code.

MFCG's recorded order (water → road casing → road body → river → landmarks → wards → piers → fields → walls → towers → grid → scale bar → compass → labels → title) is a subsequence of the layer-order table (order parity, §8.3); NG's recorded order (greens → roads → shadows → buildings → props → trees depth-sorted → title) is a subsequence of the hatched sheet's slots.

Layer-order table (ink; same list for city and district bands), 25 slots: 1 paper; 2 water; 3 ground.block; 4 relief (off by default); 5 way casings (way.*, pass 1); 6 way bodies (way.*, pass 2); 7 river casing and body; 8 shore marks; 9 greens, parks, yard parts by role; 10 projected shadows (off by default; derived 'shadow'); 11 raised under-copy (derived 'raised'); 12 landmark footprints (solid ink); 13 building masses/footprints/roof detail; 14 piers and bridges; 15 fields and hinterland land use; 16 trees: wood fills and crowns (woods may cover track casings, K16); 17 boundary treatments (district band); 18 curtain walls; 19 towers and gate blocks; 20 grid; 21 scale bar; 22 compass; 23 labels; 24 title, legend, emblem; 25 live layers, annotations, measure overlay — each with its reason/reference step.
A bridge or pier (slot 14) is cased along its sides only — its ends are open where it meets its way — so no later casing crosses an earlier body.

Slots 1-20 are the base raster; slot 23 and slot 25's world-space live marks and annotations are composed onto each tile by the tile worker (§8.8); slots 21, 22, 24 and the measure overlay are screen-space furniture drawn by the main thread over the composed tiles (§9.5).
The census checks that every tile's draw calls follow the layer-order table (§8.3).

Slot resolution (NR-3): at sheet load (built-in, user-edited, random, host-supplied), per band, every (semantic, pass) pair the registry says S14 emits at that band and that the sheet paints is resolved against the band's non-derived entries: candidates match the semantic (equal, or prefix x.* with the semantic under x.) and have passes including the pass or absent; winner = most specific (exact before prefix, longer prefix before shorter). Refused when a pair has no candidate, two candidates tie at highest specificity, or one derived kind is placed in two slots of a band; result cached per style version.

Shipped sheets place way.* pass 1 in slot 5 and pass 2 in slot 6; pier and bridge-deck semantics have exact entries in slot 14 that outrank the prefix; a river's casing and body share slot 7 through one entry with no passes.
A CI test loads every shipped sheet at every band (§8.3).

A refused user edit is shown in the style dialog with each unresolved or ambiguous pair and not applied; a setStyle event carrying a refused sheet fails its dry run with conflict action invalid (§7.1), so no document holds a sheet two loaders could read differently.

J-R39: Chose explicit passes on `OrderSlot` with most-specific-wins resolution and refusal of any unresolved or tied (semantic, pass), with `derived` entries for the raised under-copy and projected shadows, over one slot per semantic or an order fixed in code — because a way's casing and body must sit in different slots while sheets stay data (§8.2; NR-3).

facts.statement: Presets: each family defines all four bands with invariant roles (VIS-9); detail is added band by band, never re-coloured; added detail cross-fades over the band's hysteresis interval (α 0 → 1 across it).

facts.statement: lit on the reference backend (VIS-7): every lit program runs on Canvas2D; textures are pattern fills of greyscale seamless tiles tinted by the role colour (multiply); lighting is faceLight per face from stored geometry, one directional light from the sheet's sun.
In path sun mode lighting uses the sun's light step: its path position quantised to 15° of azimuth and 5° of altitude, shared by every tile of the view (§8.4; NR4-5).

Soft shadows are shadowPass polygons with penumbraPx: the shadow polygon plus two outward offset rings at ½ and 1 penumbra with α ⅔ and ⅓ — vector, no bitmap filter (avoids Fantasy Manor's ≈ 90 % bitmap-shadow cost).
Canopy shading is baked into crown sprites per (style, light step) — once per session with a fixed sun, once per light step with a path sun (§8.4, §8.10).
Water depth ramp and foam are ramp and foam over the shore-distance field, per tile.
The one thing lit does not draw is per-pixel normal-map relief on roofs and walls; lit uses per-face tones plus texture instead, and the style dialog says so.

Texture set (our own, procedural: generated by plat/tools/textures/ inside the product repository (§17.1 (3)) with fixed seeds; every file in plat/assets/textures/ names its script and seed (§17.1 (5)); no third-party texture; NF-S11): tilled soil, grain, pasture, meadow, orchard ground, marsh, sand, pebble, rock/cliff, paving stone, clay tile, thatch/shingle, wall stone, water ripple, parchment — 15 greyscale 256 × 256 px toroidal tiles; metres per tile per band in the sheet; crop and livestock variants chosen by LandUse.crop and LandUse.livestock when present (VS27), else by land-use kind; authored in M2b.

Layers draw in zOrder: underground marks (sewers) through a cut-away mask or a translucent overlay; sky marks above, with their shadows projected onto the ground layer.
opaque hides the ground beneath; ghost (default for sky) draws the layer at alpha 1 − g so the covered district stays readable; offset moves the whole layer clear of its footprint.

facts.statement: Shadow casters (WC5): buildings and wings (prism from baseCm to eave and ridge), towers and gatehouses (prism), curtain walls (prism of the band), bridges and piers (deck prism over water), trees (crown offset by crown height), sky layers (island outline projected by elevationCm); a wing's foundation skirt (§2.6) is part of its prism.

Every caster projects along the sun vector from its base elevation (baseCm, FTG-13) onto the ground; the ground under a footprint lies within FTG-13's plinth tolerance, so a flat projection from the base is exact to that tolerance.

Shadows are unioned per layer and composited once per layer per tile — into the base raster in fixed sun mode, and into a per-tile shadow layer of their own in path mode where the tier's canvas budget admits it (§8.8), so a moving sun re-rasters only shadows.
drop mode offsets each caster's footprint by height × cot(altitude) along the sun's azimuth; prism mode draws the swept prism; both from the same heights.
SunSpec = { azimuthCdeg; altitudeCdeg; colour; intensity; mode 'fixed'|'path'; latitudeDeg (path mode; default 50) } (K05).
Fixed sun by default: azimuth 315°, altitude 45° (light from the upper left).

In path mode azimuth and altitude come from sunPath(latitudeDeg, dayOfYear, hour) (solar declination and hour angle, evaluated with dmath), driven by the view-state time (§11.3; the simulation module's clock when it runs); the hemisphere follows the latitude's sign.

The shadow pass reads the path-mode sun quantised to 1° in azimuth and altitude (§8.8, N-8); every other program that reads the sun — faceLight, the two-tone roof, hillshade and the lit crown bake — reads its light step: the path-mode sun quantised to 15° azimuth and 5° altitude (NR4-5).

Below −6° sun altitude the sheet switches to its night variant (night roles; lights glow instances from the module); shadow length is capped at 8 × height near sunrise and sunset; shadows are vector so there is no shadow-resolution setting.
The projected shadow pass costs ≤ 20 % of a tile's raster time (vector offsets and one union per layer) (AM-3); penumbraPx is two vector rings, not a blur.
Measurement: M2b times the projected pass on METROPOLIS tiles with prism shadows on; pre-decided fallback: a rung that misses the budget draws drop mode instead of prism, and the report says so.

Moving sun (N-8): in path mode one 1° step re-rasters the visible tiles' shadow layers and re-composes them — ≤ 20 % of the view's settle raster plus ≈ 0.2 ms per tile, inside §12.5's settle budget; a newer step cancels an older step's pending tiles (latest wins); on a tier with no room for shadow layers the step re-rasters base tiles within the same settle budget.

Measurement: M2b times sun steps on METROPOLIS views, one step per frame, on reference and low-end devices; pre-decided fallback: a tier whose step misses the settle budget quantises the path sun to 3° instead of 1°, and the report says so.

Light pass (NR4-5): when the path sun enters a new light step, a light pass first bakes the lit crown sprites for it (§8.10), then re-rasters the visible tiles' under and over layers (or base layers on a tier without shadow layers) at that step, centre-out like a settle, each tile swapped in when ready.

A light pass is never cancelled by a newer light step: the newest waits and starts its own pass when the running one completes, skipping steps between, so the view reaches one light step within two settles; 1° shadow steps go on beside it (latest wins).

Drawn light step = the running light pass's step, or the last completed pass's; every raster of the view uses it, so a tile newly exposed during a pass is rastered at the pass's step; once a pass completes no tile keeps another light step, and tiers with and without shadow layers draw the same roof and crown tones (§8.3 light-step row).

Measurement (M2b, moving-sun runs): every light pass within the settle bound and the crown bake ≤ 20 ms per light step (§12.7); pre-decided fallback: in path mode faceLight, two-tone roofs, hillshade and crowns hold the sheet's fixed sun (only shadows follow the path), reported.
facts.values: crown bake ≤ 20 ms per light step

facts.statement: J-R54: Chose a light step — the path sun quantised to 15° of azimuth and 5° of altitude — for `faceLight`, the two-tone roofs, `hillshade` and the `lit` crown bake, keying the `under` and `over` layers (or `base`) by it and re-rastering them in a light pass that runs to completion, over lighting them by the 1° sun (a full re-raster per 1° step) and over keying only the shadows by the sun (roofs and crowns of several suns side by side, differing by tier); the fallback holds the fixed sun for all but the shadows (§8.4, §8.8, §8.10, §12.7; NR4-5).

Continuous zoom selects the band with hysteresis (a band is entered at its threshold stop and left one stop past it); added detail cross-fades across that interval; per-band detail budgets by hardware tier; no feature pops more than once across a zoom sweep (B-ZOOM).

Figure-ground contract (MFP-1) (1): every L2 built block is filled with ground at every band; at the city band yards are not subdivided (parks and greens ≥ 0.3 ha show in green; enclosed courts stay ground at city band and take court from the district band — keeps ink's eight city-band tones, §8.2, N-25), so inside the built area streets and squares are the only road-role voids.

Figure-ground (2): at the city band footprints are drawn as masses: per block, closed across gaps narrower than 1.5 px at the current stop (offset +r then −r, r = 0.75 px × metres per px, in the kernel's integer offset, computed and cached per (block, stop, revision) in the tile worker from footprint marks carrying their block in the block attribute column), never across the corridor of a way drawn at the band (closing clipped by those corridors), filled with building and outlined at the band's outline width; party lines between a mass's footprints at one third of that width only where the footprint's short side ≥ 4 px.

facts.statement: The neighbourhood band of every family (§8.2) is the stage-2 render tier (IMPROVEMENTS S5): hatched is NG's family; the stage-2 side-by-side against NG shows hatched with the ink close-up alongside, so a default-ink user opening a district sees the same palette with more detail (VIS-9).

Close-up content (PART II) is derived on demand for visible tiles from the district's committed state and sub-seed — in the derivation pool, or in the generation worker when the pool is off (needs kernel and model) — and reaches the tile worker as DisplayDelta slices answering the tile's band request (§8.9), into the same mark tables and tile pyramid.

Stage 3 plugs in at the building band: marks from BuildingGenerator.compose(…, 'wings'|'rooms') (takes a Kernel and a BuildingInput with a TerrainSampler, §2.6), computed on demand for visible buildings in the same place and cached by (entity key, revision, lod); the tile draws the outline until compositions arrive; every other band draws the outline, which equals the union of the composed wings by contract (SCL-13), so the footprint hash is the same at every band.
The tile worker never runs compose() or close-up derivation: it holds no model and no terrain (N-4, §12.8).

facts.statement: Roof construction (§8.2) runs per stored wing (VIS-10) by BaseWing.kind (§2.6): rect → exact OBB ridges with hips from its four corners (BaseWing.corners when sides carry other vertices); a warp-de-rectangled rect is a quad by §2.6's carry rule; quad → exact OBB path if it passes the near-rectangle test, else the validated skeleton, gable constructions draw its stored ridge (arc-length midpoints of the two side chains ridgeAxis names; VP2-5); polygon → pyramid, cone or dome; the plain roof (no ridge or hip lines) is the downgrade (§3.8); two-tone lit/shadow faces per roof face by its normal against the light (faceLight).
The derived-roof cache is keyed by (entity, revision, construction), so switching ink's hipped roofs to hatched's per-wing gables needs no regeneration.
SVG is resolution-free and layered, written at a declared band (city band by default; §11.1).

PNG and print render by the band-streamed tile assembly of §8.8 at any DPI, with labels placed for the export's own scale (a zoom stop computed at that scale, §9.2); paper-unit rules keep hairlines at their paper width at every scale; symbol widths from the symbolisation table at the export scale.
VTT export declares a grid scale (default 1 square = 5 ft = 1.5 m at 100 px), produces exact pixel-per-cell output (grid alignment error 0 px per cell, O11 g) and carries model widths only.
facts.values: 5 ft = 1.5 m at 100 px; 0 px per cell

facts.statement: A 100 m scale bar is accurate to 0.5 % at every zoom (O6 c).
Zoom stops (ZoomStop, declared in @plat/model, §14) at 2^¼ steps of scale (four per doubling) cover B-ZOOM's 1:50 000 → 1:500 in 27 stops; stop k has scale m_k metres per CSS pixel (N-9 a).

Tiles are 512 × 512 device px at the view's tile DPR d (device pixel ratio after the tier's cap) and world-aligned per (stop, d): tile (i, j) covers the world square of side 512 × m_k ÷ d whose corner is (i, j) × 512 × m_k ÷ d from the world origin — stable under panning and shared between views and exports at that stop and DPR.

A tile draws every mark whose bbox meets the tile dilated by margin m = the largest of casing half-width, drawn wall half-width, projected-shadow length, largest crown radius and halo width at the stop, in §8.1 item 3's slot-major order, identical in every tile; each tile clips to its own square, so no seams and no casing bar across a junction on a district boundary (GEO-28, N-7).

Fills of one semantic within a tile are one Path2D with the non-zero rule (a union: no AA seam between same-role neighbours); semantics declared seamClose (ground, masses, yard parts, shadow union) also get a ½-px same-colour stroke underneath (NG's seam dilation).
Render tests: 0 casing pixels inside junction mouths on district boundaries; the census draw-order check (§8.3).

Tile layers and composition (N-5): the tile worker rasters a base layer per tile (slots 1-20 of §8.2) and keeps it; it composes the base, the glyphs of labels placed at that stop (§9.2) and overlay live marks into one bitmap transferred to the main thread, one bitmap per tile position; a label edit, label toggle, selection or moving person re-composes touched tiles and never re-rasters a base.

In path sun mode, on a tier whose budget admits it, the base is rastered as under (slots 1-9) and over (slots 11-20) with projected shadows (slot 10) in a layer of their own at half resolution (256² per tile; bilinear-scaled when composed), so a 1° sun step re-rasters only shadow layers and only a new light step (15°/5°) re-rasters under and over through §8.4's light pass.

J-R21: Chose composing base and labels into one bitmap per tile in the tile worker over two tile layers committed to the main thread — because it halves first-paint commits and per-frame draws at the same memory while a label change still never re-rasters the map (§8.8; N-5).

facts.statement: Tile key = (stop, i, j, tile DPR d, tile layer — base, or in path mode under/shadow/over —, style version, the view-state switches that change that layer's pixels: season, weather, shadows on/off and mode, model-layer toggles, base live layers; for the shadow layer (or, while projected shadows are on, base on a tier without shadow layers) the path-mode sun quantised to the tier's sun step (1°, or 3° after §8.4's fallback); for under and over (or base without shadow layers) of a sheet whose band programs read the light (faceLight, two-tone roof, hillshade, lit crowns) the light step; in fixed mode the sheet's sun belongs to the style version) (LC-23, N-8).
Content version = combination of the revisions of the marks drawn; a composed bitmap is keyed by its base key plus the label placement's revision at that stop and the overlay providers' versions.

A DisplayDelta's dirty boxes invalidate every cached tile they meet, at every stop and DPR; in path mode a new 1° step invalidates only the layers keyed by it and a newer 1° step cancels an older one's pending re-rasters (latest wins); a new light step invalidates the layers keyed by the light step, which §8.4's light pass re-rasters to completion.

Canvas budget per hardware tier (N-9 b): per visible tile position the worker's base (1 MB at 512²) and the main thread's composed bitmap (1 MB); next coarser stop's composed bitmaps kept for gestures (≤ 1 MB per visible position); fixed scratch: shadow and post-operation buffers (2 MB), crown library sprites (with a path sun in lit, one set per cached light step: the drawn step's set always, earlier sets while they fit, §8.10) and glyph atlases (≤ 5 MB).
facts.values: 1 MB + 1 MB + ≤ 1 MB per position; 2 MB; ≤ 5 MB

facts.statement: P = (⌈W·d ÷ 512⌉ + 1) × (⌈H·d ÷ 512⌉ + 1) worst-case tile positions for a W × H CSS-px view at tile DPR d; need = 3P + 7 MB, and 4.25P + 7 MB with path-mode shadow layers (under and over replace the base; the shadow layer adds ¼ MB).

Tier ceilings: low 72 MB, mid 128 MB, high 192 MB; tile-DPR caps: low 1, mid 2, high 3; the tile DPR is the device's pixel ratio capped by the tier, then stepped down (3 → 2 → 1.5 → 1) until 3P + 7 MB fits; path-mode shadow layers used only where 4.25P + 7 MB also fits, otherwise a sun step re-rasters the base.

Worked cases (fixall_rendering_r2_budgets.out): reference view 1 440 × 900 CSS px at DPR 2 → P = 35, 112 MB (156 MB with shadow layers) — mid or high tier; low-end 1 366 × 768 or 1 920 × 1 080 at DPR 1 → 43 or 67 MB, inside low tier's 72 MB.
Cached tiles beyond the visible and fallback sets are evicted least-recently-used by bytes.

The hardware tier is chosen at app start from the Canvas2D part of bench/calibrate (8 fixed tiles, ≈ 40 ms) and the host's reported device memory; can be overridden in the advanced panel; shown with the tile DPR in the view status.

J-R22: Chose a canvas budget derived from the viewport (3P + 7 MB) with tier ceilings and a tile-DPR step-down over fixed per-tier numbers — because the fixed low and mid budgets could not hold their own worst-case views (§8.8; N-9).

facts.statement: Gestures (SCL-7, VIS-6): during pinch or wheel zoom the compositor shows the nearest cached stop's composed tiles scaled (labels scale with them); 120 ms after input stops the view animates (≤ 150 ms) to the nearest stop and the tile worker re-rasters visible tiles centre-out, swapping each in when ready; panning composites cached tiles and shows newly exposed ones from the next coarser cached stop until rastered.
While a gesture runs at most 4 new bitmaps are committed per animation frame; at first paint and at settle every ready tile is committed in the frame it arrives (§12.5).

facts.statement: Print and large PNG (O12 e): horizontal bands of tiles (512 device px high) are rastered and composed at the export scale; each band's scanlines are streamed into the PNG encoder, each row filtered by the per-row rule (of PNG's five filter types, the one whose filtered bytes have the smallest sum of absolute values, bytes read as signed; NR4-4), then one zlib stream (CompressionStream in browsers, zlib level 6 in Node), written as IDAT chunks band by band; §12.7 holds encoding time and fallback.

Peak canvas memory in print is one band (A2 at 300 dpi: 7 016 px × 512 px × 4 B ≈ 14 MB); no canvas is larger than a tile band; per-layer transparent PNGs use the same path with the layer set restricted.

Warp preview (SCL-9): while a warp brush is held the moved L1 vertices are applied to a transient copy of affected ways' and blocks' marks and only tiles meeting the brush's dirty box re-raster; Apply commits the warp event (§7.1), whose invariants and re-derivation run then; Discard drops the copy (MFCG's staged warp).
facts.values: ≥ 30 fps for brush radius ≤ 150 m at district band

facts.statement: Canvas2D is the reference backend of every shipped preset (ink, lit, hatched and variants), running on an OffscreenCanvas in the tile worker through resumable raster jobs (NR3-2); programs render typed-array paths, one Path2D per (program, semantic, variant) per tile, sprites by drawImage.

facts.statement: SVG is written from the same display list (§11.1).

WebGL2 draws no marks: it exists only as a pre-decided fallback compositor that uploads composed Canvas2D tiles as textures, composites them with the view transform and runs post operations as one fragment pass — no stroke tessellation, no SDF text, no look that differs by backend (VIS-7).

Measurement at M2b: pan and zoom frame rates of the Canvas2D compositor on reference and low-end devices at METROPOLIS scale (§12.5); the WebGL2 compositor is enabled for a hardware tier only if the Canvas2D compositor misses ≥ 60 fps (reference) or ≥ 30 fps (low end) there.

Text (DEF-6): all text is drawn by Canvas2D in the tile worker's composition step (§8.8), glyph by glyph at positions from the bundled font's own metrics (§9.2), through a glyph atlas per (face, size, stop): each glyph drawn once into the atlas and copied per placement; SVG writes the same per-glyph positions — as the face's own glyph outlines by default, or as text in the embedded face on request (§11.1, N-13).
J-R9: Chose Canvas2D glyphs composed onto the tiles over SDF text — because once tiles are composited text never needs the GPU, and one text path keeps text identical on every output (§8.9).

facts.statement: Measurement at M1: a tile's label composition ≤ 3 ms at ≤ 150 glyph runs; pre-decided fallback: whole words cached as bitmaps per (text, size, stop) in the atlas.

Threads (N-4) (1): the generation worker holds the document and model and runs S0-S14; also resolves instance overrides (§8.10), runs live-layer providers (§8.2), builds on-demand bands (district, neighbourhood, building bands of districts a band request names, via DisplayListBuilder.build(model, band, groups)), writes every export (§11.1: SVG from a transient list it builds and releases; raster formats from a transient list it transfers to the tile worker with the request; NR-5, NR3-6), answers the API's hit and inView queries (§11.2) from the model and its 24-B index (entity, bbox, group), and hands stage-3 compose() and close-up derivation (§8.6) to the derivation pool.

Threads (2): the derivation pool — up to three workers — runs the per-district stages at every rung (§12.3; merge protocol §4.1) and, on request, compose() and close-up derivation from the committed state of the district it is handed; with the pool off the generation worker runs them itself.

Threads (3): the tile worker holds no model: it holds the display list with its label, instance and string tables (the only full copy, §8.1 item 6) and rasters base layers, runs S13b (§9.2) and decoration instancing (§8.10), composes labels and overlay live marks (§8.8), runs post operations, answers the main thread's furniture and snap queries and rasters raster exports from each request's transient list (§11.1; NR3-6), all through the queue.

What crosses (SCL-6, N-4) — generation → tile worker: display-list deltas (mark columns with key, geometry, field rasters, changed label/instance/string rows), transferred as fresh-buffer copies, the generation worker keeping only the 24-B index columns; bound O(changed marks), ≤ 96 B/label row, ≤ 40 B/instance row, ≤ 16 B/species row, ≤ 32 B/override row, plus geometry and UTF-8 text.
What crosses — generation ↔ tile worker on cross-origin-isolated hosts: the mark table as SharedArrayBuffer columns, no copy — optional, never required (needs COOP/COEP from the embedding host).

What crosses — tile worker → generation: band requests (districts and band that entering tiles need and the tile worker lacks; buildings needing compose() at the building band), copied, ≤ 4 KB per request; generation or pool → tile worker: answers (on-demand band marks, compose() wings and rooms, close-up marks) as DisplayDelta slices naming the request, transferred, ≤ 1 MB per answer; generation → tile worker: live-layer marks (live.<id> groups), transferred, ≤ 256 KB per delivery.

facts.statement: What crosses — tile worker → main: composed tile ImageBitmaps and per-tile hit-test slices (mark bboxes + entity handles), transferred zero-copy, ≤ 1 MB bitmap + ≤ 64 KB slice per tile; main → tile worker: furniture-placement queries (view, stop, ≤ 16 candidate boxes: compass's eight, title's and legend's four corners) and snap queries (pointer in world cm, radius in px, stop), each with a request id (NR-4), copied, ≤ 4 KB per query; tile worker → main: per candidate box its ObstacleSource.coverage record, the snapped point from RoleIndex.snap or none, copied, ≤ 4 KB per answer within one 16.7 ms frame.

What crosses — generation → tile worker: raster-export requests (PNG, print, .dd2vtt scene image): frame, scale, band, layers, post operations and the export's zoom stop (§8.7; NR-5), each carrying the export's transient list (mark, geometry, label, instance and string tables for the export's band and frame; §11.1; NR3-6); request copied, list columns transferred; ≤ 4 KB plus the list (≈ 1.9 KB per building at the city band, §12.8).

What crosses — tile worker → generation: the encoded raster (PNG bytes streamed band by band, §8.8) and a progress message per band (bands done, bands total) for the export dialog (NR3-6); bytes transferred, progress copied; the file's size; < 64 B per progress message. main → workers: view changes, input, API calls (§11.2), copied, small.
Main-thread receive work ≤ 4 ms per delivery (bitmaps and slices only), measured in B-CITY's browser runs.
Resumable rasters (NR3-2): a worker serves its message queue only between two calls it makes, so a tile is rastered by a job the tile worker can stop and resume.
TileAddress = { stop; i; j; dpr } (§8.8's address; an export's tiles are addressed at the export's stop and DPR).

TileRasterOpts { layers: Layer[]; tileLayer 'base'|'under'|'shadow'|'over'; shadows 'off'|'drop'|'prism' (§8.2's StyleSheet.shadows.projected); sun?: { azimuthCdeg; altitudeCdeg }; tier 'low'|'mid'|'high'; dpr }.

TileBackend { begin(tile, list: DisplayList, style: StyleSheet, opts: TileRasterOpts): RasterJob } — fixes the tile's draw sequence and draws nothing; RasterJob { step(deadlineMs): boolean (runs on from where it stopped, returns after the first draw call ending ≥ deadlineMs after this call began; true when complete); finish(): ImageBitmap (canvas transferred); cancel() (tile left the view, newer sun step, dirtying delta); readonly spentMs }.

begin finds every mark whose bbox meets the dilated tile (§8.8) and fixes the draw sequence: native calls in §8.1 item 3's (slot, pass, z, key) order, each a fill or stroke of one batched Path2D, a run of ≤ 64 sprite draws (crowns, glyph copies), or a derived per-tile operation (projected-shadow union, raised under-copy, post operation).
facts.values: ≤ 80 Path2D per tile (§12.5); ≤ 64 sprites per run

facts.statement: The JavaScript that prepares a call reads the clock after every mark and every 64 instances and can stop there; a native call is never split (a split batched fill would draw AA seams); a derived operation (using shared shadow and post buffers) runs whole inside one step; overrun past the deadline is at most one native call or one derived operation.

Each job owns its canvas and context state; deltas are applied between steps; a removed mark becomes a dead row and an added mark a new row; the tile worker compacts its list only while no job is live; a job whose tile a delta's dirty boxes meet is cancelled and queued again. Slicing changes when calls run, never which or in what order: a tile rastered whole and in 1-ms slices is pixel-identical (§8.3 census row).
The queue calls step(8) — step(4) after the pre-decided fallback.

Tile worker's queue (NR-4, NR3-6): between two steps it serves its message queue, then runs one step of the highest class with ready work: class 1 furniture and snap queries (answer due within one frame); class 2 incoming deltas (edit deltas, band answers, live-layer deliveries) in arrival order, each O(changed marks), ≤ 1 MB per answer; class 3 the visible view: S13b at the view's stop (resumable, one unit at a time, §9.2; NR4-2), with a path sun after a new light step the lit crown bake (one sprite per unit) and §8.4's light pass, visible tiles' raster jobs centre-out, compositions and commits, re-compositions for label and overlay changes; class 4 exports: first S13b at the export's stop over its transient list (memo held by the job), then band by band the raster jobs, composition, read-back (64 rows per step) and encoding.

A class runs only while every higher class is empty, one step at a time; within a class the job in progress runs to completion before the next begins (at most one raster job per class live); a query waits at most one step; a pan or zoom during an export pre-empts it within one step.

No starvation: an export that has waited 100 ms since its last step runs its next step ahead of class 3 (never ahead of classes 1 and 2) — at most one step in any 100 ms, ≤ 8 % of the worker — so an animated view slows an export but cannot stop it.
A settle contains at most two export steps at CITY (≤ 150 ms) and three at METROPOLIS (≤ 250 ms): ≤ 16 and ≤ 24 ms beside the ≈ 42-83 ms settle rasters of §12.5.

A newer sun step or a tile leaving the view cancels its job (latest wins; §8.4, §8.8); the export dialog shows the tile worker's progress messages (bands done of total) and, while class 3 holds the worker, that the export is waiting for the view.

Placement is stepped like a raster (NR4-2): S13b (view's in class 3, export's in class 4) is a PlacementJob (§9.2) called with step(8) (step(4) after the fallback); unit = one decision (a label's rung-(5) test, one pin of the pin pass, one push or one local-evaluation decision, or glyph layout of one placed label); reads the clock after every unit, so overrun ≤ one unit (≈ 1 µs on average, tens of µs for the longest name).

A print's placement over its whole frame (≈ 1 µs per candidate, ≤ 20 ms for 20 000 candidates, §12.7) runs as a few class-4 steps; every query/settle bound holds while an export places its labels; a crown bake after a new light step (§8.4, §8.10) is stepped the same way, one sprite per unit.

Queries to the tile worker (NR-4): compass, title and legend placement (§9.5) and the ruler's snapping read the display list, which only the tile worker holds; the main thread asks through the query rows and the tile worker answers with ObstacleSource.coverage and RoleIndex.snap over its list — the implementations S13b uses (§14).

A query is class 1: waits ≤ 8 ms plus one native call or derived operation, runs in ≤ 4 ms of tile-worker time; answer within one 16.7 ms frame; most tiles are one step (a city-band tile of a whole-CITY view rasters in ≈ 1.2 ms, §12.5).

The ruler keeps one snap query in flight (a newer pointer position replaces a queued one) and shows the unsnapped point until the answer arrives; furniture placement is asked when the view settles, and the furniture keeps its previous place until its answer arrives.

Measurement with the first map (M1 at TOWN and CITY, M2b at METROPOLIS) in B-CITY's browser runs: query round trip p95 ≤ 16 ms during a settle raster and ≤ 4 ms tile-worker time per query (each tile's longest native call and derived operation logged); scripted pan and zoom during an A2 300-dpi CITY export (§12.7): every settle within §12.5's bound, the export completes, and its PNG is byte-identical to the export made with the view idle and one during which an edit is made (transient list, §11.1).
Pre-decided fallback: the step limit falls from 8 ms to 4 ms (step(4)), halving a query's wait and an export step's share of a settle.

facts.statement: InstanceStyle { species? (a species kind of the entity's mix); crown? (crown-library index); scale? (0.5-1.5); tone? (colour jitter −1…1); leafType? 'deciduous'|'evergreen' } — what a restyle or add override sets (§7.1).

One instance set per entity, independent of the band: every instances mark (wood, garden, park, copse, orchard, avenue, hedgerow, yard planting, scatter class) has one set of positions in one of three layouts: stamp of a per-class blue-noise tile for areas; jittered grid for orchards (6-8 m); jittered line for avenues and street trees (along the row §4.9 derives in the planting district's own half-corridor strip at Greenery.along's offsetCm from the kerb, no plat edge) and for hedgerows along their L3 field-boundary chains (8-12 m along the line).

S14 draws each layout's parameters — offset, rotation, spacing in whole cm inside its class's range (§4.9; 300-500 cm woods, 400-600 cm gardens) — from the entity's render.instances stream (§6.1) in the generation worker and carries them in the mark's InstanceTable row (§8.1).

facts.statement: Stamp tiles (NR3-7, NR4-1): per stamped class four toroidal blue-noise tiles of 6 400 × 6 400 cm at reference spacing r₀ = 400 cm (≈ 162 points each, fixall_rendering_r5_seamstrip.out), each point carrying a progressive rank (void-and-cluster order: every prefix is evenly spread; the lowest-rank quarter keeps ≈ 1.5-1.8 × r₀ between any two points).
Seam-compatible tiles: the four tiles share one border band — every point with edge distance e = min(x, 6 400 − x, y, 6 400 − y) below r₀ ÷ 2 — and differ only inside it.
An entity whose spacing is r stamps the tiles scaled by s = r ÷ r₀, so one tile set serves every spacing of the class (a wood at 3 m stamps 48-m tiles, a garden at 6 m 96-m tiles).

No two instances of one stamp lie closer than the entity's spacing (less ≤ 1.5 cm of centimetre rounding): inside a cell because each tile is spaced at r₀ toroidally; across every seam because outside-band points are ≥ r₀/2 from cell edges and a band point is present at the same position in the other point's tile and was spaced against it there; every band draws a subset (ranks below s_b), so it holds at every band.

Measured on five seed sets (fixall_rendering_r5_seamstrip.out): 0 pairs closer than r₀ across cells in all 256 arrangements of 2 × 2 cells, for all ranks and for rank < 0.6 and < 0.25 subsets; four independent tiles have 3.5-5 such pairs per 64-m seam (NR4-1).
The tile variant used by a stamp cell is RH32('stamp.variant', key, salt, u, v) mod 4 (§8.1 item 5), breaking visible repetition: only the band, ≈ 11-14 % of a tile's points, repeats in every cell.

Sampling: Bridson with k = 50 candidates, all evaluated; every accepted point rounded at once to integer cm inside the 6 400-cm tile so the spacing test is an exact integer comparison of squared toroidal distances with r₀²; first point (int(0, 6 399), int(0, 6 399)); active point int(0, n − 1) over the active list in insertion order, a retired point replaced by the list's last; each candidate at radius r₀ × (1 + float01) along angle 2π × float01 (cos/sin from dmath, §6.5); candidates tried in draw order.

The band (creation index 4): a full toroidal tile sampled as above and cut to its points with e < 200 cm, in index order. Each tile (creation index 0-3): the band's points pre-placed in that order (spacing grid and initial active list), sampling continues over e ≥ 200 cm (no first point drawn; a candidate with e < 200 cm rejected); the tile is the band's points followed by its own in acceptance order.

Ranking per tile: every point's energy = sum over other points in point-index order of exp(−d² ÷ (2σ²)), d toroidal distance in cm, σ = r₀, exponential dmath.exp; the highest-energy point (tie: lower index) is removed and takes the highest free rank (n − 1 first); every remaining point has the removed point's term subtracted in point-index order (removal update), costing ≈ 1.5 n² exponentials (O(n²)), never a re-sum (O(n³): ≈ 53 ms vs ≈ 1.8 ms per tile at 161 points); a needed square root is Math.sqrt, exact by specification (§6.5 (2)).

facts.statement: Stamp (NR4-3): from the row, offset o ∈ [0, 6 400)² in whole reference cm, rotationCdeg ∈ [0, 36 000) (S14 draws int(0, 35 999)), scale s = spacing ÷ 400 cm; R_θ's cos and sin = dmath.cos/dmath.sin of rotationCdeg × (π ÷ 18 000) (a double literal); tile point t of cell (u, v) lies at R_θ · (s · (6 400 · (u, v) + t + o)), each coordinate rounded to whole cm (Math.round) = the instance's world position, the one position the face test, density test, drawing, override resolution and every export read.

Stamp cells are those of the rotated, scaled lattice covering the entity's face (bbox taken into lattice coordinates by the same cos/sin, widened by one cell); a point survives if its world position is inside the face (exact point-in-polygon with holes on integer cm, §3.2) and, for woods, passes the edge test of a domain-warped density evaluated once per point at its world position in metres.
Rounding moves a point by ≤ 0.71 cm, so two instances keep the entity's spacing less ≤ 1.5 cm.

One result on every engine: the stamp, grid and line layouts, the per-instance look draws and the density test, with everything they call, are held to §6.5 (3)'s allowlist lint, so they compute the same integer positions and draws on every engine, and a GeoJSON, glTF or CityJSON file with trees is byte-identical on every host (§11.1; the five-engine golden run compares one, §13.3).

facts.statement: Grid: one point per cell (u, v) of the rotated lattice at the row's spacing, jittered ± 15 % of spacing in x and y from two RH32 draws over (key, salt, u, v) (tags grid.jitter.x, grid.jitter.y), rounded to whole cm and kept if inside the face; ordinal = (u, v).

Line: point i at arc length (i + ½) × spacing from the line's start end (the end whose junction address sorts first; for an along row, the end at its way's first junction), jittered along and across the same way and rounded to whole cm; ordinal = i. Park paths are L3 path faces drawn by the path program, not instances.

Rank and band thinning (N-10): every instance has a normalised rank r ∈ [0, 1): stamp = progressive rank ÷ tile point count; grid = 32-bit bit-reversal of the Morton interleave of (u, v) ÷ 2³² (2-D van der Corput); line = bit-reversal of i ÷ 2³². Band b draws instances with r < s_b (city: none — the wood, orchard or green fill; district 0.6; neighbourhood and finer 1), so every coarser band is a subset of the finer: an instance keeps its position once visible and appears at most once in a zoom sweep (LC-20, VIS-5); census covers all three layouts (§8.3).

Per-instance look keyed by (key, ordinal): species drawn by its share from Greenery.species (inner or outer share by distance from the edge) picks the crown class; crown index into the style's crown library; colour jitter; scale jitter ± 15 %; leafType (from the species when present, deciduous otherwise) — all RH32 draws over (render key, ordinal, concern salt); hatch phase and roof detail keyed by the entity's key; nothing keyed by band or interned handle.

Crown library: 20 crowns per class per style, built once per session from rng.stream keyed by the sheet's key (hash of id@version), STAGE_VIEW, the concern style.crowns with its salt, and class and index i as creation index (§6.1's structured components; the path form is a report rendering, §14), drawn as sprites.

A lit sheet bakes its crown sprites per (style, light step): once with a fixed sun, and with a path sun again at each light step, in the tile worker as one-sprite units of §8.9's queue; the drawn step's set is always kept and earlier sets while they fit §8.8's crown-and-atlas scratch (§8.4; NR4-5).

Override resolution runs in the generation worker whenever a commit touches an entity carrying overrides (re-runs this function for that entity only): applies by ordinal when the entity's lineage is unchanged since the event (no carry lifecycle event and no supersession after the event's seq, §6.3) and that ordinal's generated position lies within 0.5 × spacing of the recorded point; otherwise (carried successor, superseded entity — overrides move to the supersededBy successor —, or a moved ordinal) re-matches by position to the nearest unclaimed generated instance within 0.5 × spacing (candidates in (distance, ordinal) order, overrides in log order); else kept orphaned and reported.

Resolution reads each positional override's current position from its entity's overrides table (§2.7) — a move's to, an add's point, and for a line layout the recorded generated point — which the event writes when it applies and a warp or vertex move displaces with the host face (§7.4; VK2-13); for stamp and grid layouts the recorded generated point stays world-anchored.

An add override stays while its point lies in the entity's face (or within 0.5 × spacing of its line) and is orphaned otherwise; resolved overrides (ordinal, op, position, style, state byOrdinal/rematched/orphaned) cross to the tile worker as the InstanceTable's override rows (§8.1, §8.9); a tree brush is a batch of instance events (COV-FTG-M04).

facts.statement: Plain-words intro restates §9.1-§9.5: district names curve along the district middle, never cross an inner river nor cover gate, bridge or keep; too-small districts labelled as named quarters; street names appear on zoom; labels never collide; identical placement everywhere via shipped font metrics; names are model data, placement is view data; scale bar, compass, grid, title, legend, emblem and ruler are drawn on top and each is movable, restylable and switchable.

LabelEntity { id; target; kind 'district'|'quarter'|'way'|'landmark'|'water'|'wood'|'gate'|'title'|'annotation'|'address'; text: NameRef; shortText?: NameRef; priority; lod: LodBand[]; candidates { spines: Polyline[] (area and path labels, world cm, preference order); anchors { p; dirCdeg? }[] (point labels); breakAt? (allowed two-line breaks) }; pinned?: PinnedPlacement (user placement, model data); hidden? }.

Placement { stop (zoom stop where the user placed it); sizePx (cap height in display px at 1×, never below the kind's floor, §9.4); anchor: PointCm (point labels: text origin; area/path: spine midpoint); spine?: PolylineCm; dirCdeg?; lines? 1|2 (two lines broken at the entity's first breakAt) } — a user placement set by moveLabel (§7.1), model data (N-28).

PinnedPlacement extends Placement { seq } — the seq of the moveLabel event that set it (§7.1); applying the event writes pinned = { ...placement, seq }; a warp or vertex move carrying the pin keeps it; it orders §9.2's pin pass (NR3-3).

Pinned placements are honoured by §9.2's pin pass: fixed at their own stop and finer stops unless a pin set earlier is already fixed where they would stand (then hidden at that stop and reported); candidates that yield or hide at coarser stops.
The model hash does not depend on fonts, viewport or device pixel ratio, so O2 (a) and O11 (f) hold (GEO-29).

facts.statement: Metrics: @plat/labels parses the bundled OFL font files itself (default label face IM FELL Great Primer, §17.2): cmap, hmtx, kern and GPOS pair adjustments (formats 1 and 2), GSUB single substitutions for smcp and onum, and loca/glyf for SVG's outline text (§11.1); advance widths and kerning in font units become world metres at a zoom stop; no contextual shaping (Latin faces, ligatures off); glyphs placed and drawn one by one (§8.9), so drawn equals measured on every backend and in SVG.

Font features (N-12): from M1 a PR-tier CI test asserts for each bundled label face that it carries cmap, hmtx and TrueType glyf outlines and reports whether its GSUB has smcp and onum single-substitution lookups for Latin.

Pre-decided path per face, chosen by that test, never by hand: with smcp, small caps from the face; without it, the family's OFL small-caps cut (for IM FELL Great Primer its SC face, bundled unmodified) measured by the same reader; with no such cut (a user face), small caps synthesised as capitals scaled to 0.75 × cap height with letter-spacing kept; without onum the scale bar uses default figures; the style report names each face's path; census floors (§9.4) run on the active path.

Placement is computed per zoom stop (§8.8): at stop k each glyph box in world units = pixel box × the stop's metres per pixel; protected obstacles (gates, castle, plaza, bridges, walls — MFCG's measured defect) are their drawn symbol extents at that stop.

S13b reads the display list through ObstacleSource and RoleIndex (§14); both implementations, what they call and the S14 writers of the columns they read are under §6.5 (3)'s allowlist lint, so S13b's inputs are bit-identical on every engine and §13.3's placement digests compare across five engines (VS2-4); a symbol's rotated extent uses dmath, never Math.cos or Math.hypot.

Between stops the view uses the placement of the stop at or coarser than the current scale: zooming in only shrinks every label's world box, so no collision appears; crossing below a stop switches to that coarser stop's placement; zero collisions hold at every zoom, not only at stops.

The candidate set of a stop is fixed before the greedy: every LabelTable row drawn at the band, minus labels §9.4's rung (5) hands to a quarter at this stop, plus one candidate per QuarterNode rung (5) activates (created once however many members yield, not again when the stop's cut already labels that node) with the highest priority among its yielding members, the node's area and the node's own label id (N-11); rung (5) is decided from geometry alone (whether a label fits its own face at the floor).

The greedy: candidates at a stop are totally ordered by priority (title > quarter/district > water > landmark > gate > way > address), then larger target area, then id; a candidate takes its first alternate (spines in order, then §9.4's ladder) meeting no placed higher candidate, no obstacle and no fixed pin; otherwise it yields.

The whole-map greedy is evaluated locally: deciding c first decides (memoised) every higher candidate whose alternate boxes meet c's; the dependency graph is acyclic because the order is strict, so the result is independent of tile order and viewport.

LabelPlacer (@plat/labels; §14 declares the same) { begin(stop: ZoomStop, labels: LabelEntity[], obstacles: ObstacleSource, roles: RoleIndex, fonts: FontMetrics, memo: PlacementMemo): PlacementJob; place(same args): PlacementSet — begin then step(Infinity), for SVG exports and tests }.

PlacementJob { step(deadlineMs): boolean (runs units on; returns after the first unit ending ≥ deadlineMs after the call began; true when the stop's placement is complete); result(): PlacementSet; cancel() (memo entries it wrote stay valid, keyed by stop, candidate id and revision); readonly spentMs } (NR4-2).

A placement unit is one of: the rung-(5) test of one LabelTable row; one pin of the pin pass; one step of the local evaluation on an explicit stack (push the highest undecided candidate whose alternate boxes meet the top's, or when all such are decided decide the top, write the memo, pop); or the glyph layout of one placed label. The job takes the scope's candidates as roots in strict order, pins first.

The stack and memo persist between steps; every decision reads only already-decided candidates, so step placement never changes the result: a stop placed whole and one unit per step give identical placement digests (§8.3, §13.3); a unit costs ≈ 1 µs on average and tens of µs at most, so a step overruns by one unit.

The view's job reads the tile worker's list, which deltas change between steps: a delta applied between two steps drops the memo entries its dirty boxes invalidate and, when it changes a label row or an obstacle of the job's stop, the job is begun again keeping every memo entry left valid; an export's job reads its own transient list, which nothing changes (§11.1).

Pinned labels (N-28, NR3-3): a pinned label is shown only in its bands; at its own stop and every finer stop it is placed exactly as the user left it, before any other candidate, by the pin pass: pins eligible at the stop (in their bands, own stop at or coarser than this stop) taken in moveLabel seq order then label id (LabelTable.pinSeq, §8.1); each whose box meets no already-fixed pin becomes a fixed pin (an obstacle every candidate avoids); one whose box meets a fixed pin is hidden at that stop and reported ('pinned label hidden: overlaps pin P at stop k').

The pin pass is a greedy in strict order evaluated locally (deciding a pin decides, memoised, every earlier pin whose box meets it), so it is tile-order independent; a pin's box is sized in pixels, so a pin fixed at stop k meets nothing new at finer stops and a pin hidden at k is fixed again where the boxes part.

moveLabel's dry run (§7.1) refuses a placement whose box at its stop meets another pinned label's box there, returning the nearest free position as the conflict's action (interactive guard); the pin pass is the guarantee because pins also come together without moveLabel: a warp or vertex move (§9.1, §7.4), a setAttr rename or ids-scoped rerollLayer(naming) lengthening a pin's text (§9.6), a setStyle changing face widths.

At a coarser stop a pin's world box grows, so it is not fixed: it keeps its anchor and spine and enters the greedy at its entity's priority with that placement as its only alternate — drawn when it meets no higher candidate, obstacle or fixed pin, otherwise hidden at that stop and reported ('pinned label hidden at stops coarser than k'); zero collisions hold at every zoom with pins included.

Test (B-ZOOM, §13.4): two pins 20 px apart brought together by a warp, and two by a rename lengthening the earlier pin's text — at every stop 0 collisions, the later pin reported hidden where boxes meet, per-stop placement digests (§13.3) identical after a log replay.

Scope: area and way labels for all candidates of the band; addresses and repeated street names only for candidates in visible tiles and their dependency closure; memo keyed by (stop, candidate id, candidate revision).
Incremental (SCL-9): after an edit, memo entries of candidates whose boxes meet the dirty boxes are dropped and re-decided; change propagates only through candidates whose outcome changes.

Placement ≤ 2 ms per stop for ≤ 2 000 visible candidates, in the tile worker (§12.7), from the LabelTable alone (§8.1, §8.9); an export's placement ≈ 1 µs per candidate in its frame, in class-4 steps (§8.9, §12.7; NR4-2) (SCL-10).

J-R26: Chose pins fixed at their own and finer stops and yielding at coarser ones over pins fixed at every stop — because a pixel-sized pin grows in world units as the view zooms out and would collide there (§9.2; N-28).

facts.statement: Area labels (districts, quarters, water bodies, woods; GEO-39): simplify the face with the kernel's topology-preserving Visvalingam (simplify, §3.4; a removal is refused when the new edge would cross another edge of the face or its holes) to half the label's cap height at the band's coarsest stop; hole-aware straight skeleton (skeleton(rings, 'spine'), §3.8, gated by its validator: connected, one independent cycle per hole); each skeleton edge's clearance = smaller event time of its ends; maximum-clearance spanning tree (Kruskal by clearance descending, ties by edge index) drops each cycle's lowest-clearance edge; spine = longest path of that tree by length (two linear passes), smoothed (Visvalingam → centripetal Catmull-Rom).
O13 (a) label curvature: a label's spine turns ≤ 45° over any window of the label's length (§9.3); M1; fallback: the spine's smoothing step doubles; a label still over takes §9.4's next ladder rung.

When the skeleton fails (F-SKELETON), the medial axis of boundary samples is processed the same way; candidates per area in order: the spine; the spine trimmed to its central 80 %; the OBB-axis straight line; the OBB arc.

Path labels (streets — new to all four references —, rivers, walls): along the centreline at the district and neighbourhood bands, repeated per segment above 12 em of length, kept upright (flipped when the tangent points left).
Point labels (gates, bridges, landmarks): eight anchor offsets; a leader line when the footprint is under 12 px.
Addresses: the numbering is model data (S13a: monotone along each way, per side); the numbers are placed as view data at the neighbourhood band.

Legibility floors (display px at 1×): area labels cap height ≥ 7 px (and ≤ 14 px, ∝ √area within the band); way labels cap ≥ 6 px; point labels ≥ 6 px; addresses ≥ 5 px; area labels are letter-spaced small caps (0.15 em).

Rung (5) (N-11): decided per stop before the greedy from geometry alone: when none of rungs (1)-(4) fits the label's own face at the floor at this stop, the label yields to the smallest ancestor QuarterNode (following LabelTable.parent, §8.1) whose spine fits that node's own name at the floor; the yielding label is suppressed at that stop and reported ('named by quarter Q at stops k…k′'); the ancestor's LabelEntity becomes a candidate once (not again when the stop's cut already labels that node) with the highest yielding priority, the node's area and label id; it takes its own alternates (spines, rungs (3), (4), (6), (7)); members whose own rungs fit keep their labels and are obstacles to it.
S13a gives each internal quarter node a name from the grammar, conditioned on its dominant kind and on the naming feature of its largest member (§10.4), and a spine from its union (§9.3).

Halo (VIS-15, N-3): each glyph's halo, 1.5 px wide, takes the role of the area mark under the glyph's centre (looked up in the display-list index at the label's band) when the text colour against that role passes the label floor (ink/ground row: ΔE2000 ≥ 40, ΔL* ≥ 50, §8.2); otherwise it takes ground, which passes by that row in every accepted palette; over masses and woods the halo is the block's ground tone.

With the shipped palettes the local halo role is kept over paper, road, ground, court, field, verge and green in every family and over garden and water in ink and hatched; ground replaces building and tree in every family and garden and water in lit (fixall_rendering_r2_palette.out).

SVG writes the halo as a paint-order stroke per glyph in the halo's colour; a user palette accepted with 'accept low contrast' (§8.2) may fail the floor, and the report lists the failing text/halo pairs.
Pre-decided fallback if a rung labels fewer than its city cut at M1: the default framing percentile (§9.5) tightens from 95 % to 85 %, enlarging every district on screen, and the check re-runs.

The old bar ≥ min(12, number of districts) failed by construction where the cut is smaller than 12 (at 7 500 and 10 000 inhabitants, fixall_pipeline_r2_quarters.out), and its 'MFCG size 80 draws 17' was not the plain sweep's 12.

facts.statement: Scale bar: metres ↔ feet, major and minor ticks, old-style figures (onum); accurate to 0.5 % at every zoom (O6 c).

Compass (XB08): procedural 8-ray design with ink and paper halves, rerollable per town; its stream is keyed from the town root's entity key (§6.1, §14 TOWN_ROOT — the seed key alone) with the concern style.compass and its salt, so a reroll is a logged rerollLayer('style.compass') event and a link or copy draws the same compass (NF-D12).

Compass auto-placement: candidates = four corners and four edge midpoints, inset 24 px; score = sum over display-list marks the compass would cover (labels × 3, protected features × 3, buildings × 1, ways × 1, water × 0.2, paper 0) + 0.5 × (1 − distance from view centre ÷ half-diagonal); lowest wins, ties NE, NW, SE, SW, N, E, S, W; re-evaluated when the view settles; covers computed in the tile worker by ObstacleSource.coverage per candidate box, reaching the main thread through §8.9's furniture query (NR-4).

Dragging places the compass and the wheel rotates it; both are view state (§11.3) and pin it; view key compass = trueNorth (default: needle at model north whatever the view rotation) or free; the map's own rotation is the rotation view key about the frame centre (§2.9, §7.1: MFCG's Rotate as a view rotation, never a model change).

Grid (XB15): kind none | square | hex (pointy or flat) | mesh (triangular); cell size in metres or feet (default: a round ground distance ≈ 1/10 of the view's short side on a 1-2-5 sequence; for VTT 1.5 m / 5 ft); colour role grid; fades out below its legibility zoom (cell < 12 px); skip water clips grid strokes out of water faces (on by default for overview grids, off for VTT grids).
facts.values: ≈ 1/10 short side; 1-2-5; VTT 1.5 m/5 ft; < 12 px

facts.statement: Title: in the emptiest corner (NG's rule: the corner whose box covers the least mark area, the sum of its coverage record from the same furniture query); movable.

GeoJSON projection: each model vertex (x, y) in metres, rotated by the bearing, is a transverse Mercator easting/northing (scale 1 on the central meridian through the anchor, false origin at the anchor) inverted to WGS84 with Krüger's series to fourth order in the third flattening, evaluated with dmath (byte-identical on every host); coordinates written with 7 decimals (≈ 1 cm); exterior rings CCW, holes CW (RFC 7946 §3.1.6).

GIS ellipsoid distances match model distances within a factor 1 + (d ÷ R)² ÷ 2 — at most 3.1 × 10⁻⁶, ≤ 5 cm, at the farthest corner of the largest frame (≈ 15.7 km from the centre at aspect 2, §12.2).
GeoJSON foreign member plat records the anchor, whether it is the default, the document id and the output version.

Metric GeoJSON (by prior arrangement, RFC 7946 §4): x east and y north in metres from the settlement centre with 2 decimals (the cm lattice exactly), no crs, in <name>.metric.geojson, beside a sidecar <name>.metric.json giving origin, unit, axes, document id and anchor if set.

facts.statement: DocHandle = { readonly id } — the document lives in the generation worker.

PlatApi: generate(bp, {onProgress?}) → DocHandle; open(bytes, {readOnly?, session? (host-assigned §11.3, else the document's stored session minted on first edit, §7.4; VD2-4)}) (.plat or CBOR twin; bytes transferred in); edit(h, e | e[]) → ApplyResult (an event may arrive with fates filled); regenerate(h, scope, 'keep'|'newRandom', {discardEdits?}) (§7.1's Regenerate and New random); adjust(h, param, value) (§7.1's Adjust, or Re-derive from Sk for an early parameter); confirm(h, token, fates, renames?) (NF-D14); cancel(h, token); undo(h, of?) (appends an undo event for the handle's session, §7.4; of only for the owner role; a conflict lists dependent events); redo(h); query(h, q) (≤ 64 KB per page, paginated); view(h, target canvas, opts?) → ViewHandle (tiles from the tile worker); setView(v, patch); export(h, fmt, opts?) → ArrayBuffer (transferred out); report(h); subscribe(h, handler) → Unsubscribe; close(h).

ApplyResult = ok { logHead (§2.9); changed (addresses whose records changed) } | conflict { actions: ConflictAction[] } (§7.1 dry run) | confirm { token; fates (first 1 000; rest by query 'fates'); renames (case-(4) renames, §6.3, §7.3 item 4; rest by query 'fates'); counts per fate; scope: EditScope (resolved) } — nothing committed until confirmed.
ConflictAction = { kind 'moveTo'|'unlock'|'unassign'|'reroute'|'stale'|'invalid'; target?; at?: PointCm; message }.
@plat/api/node: the same API over worker_threads plus by-value helpers generateDocument(bp): Document and exportDocument(doc, fmt, opts?): Uint8Array for scripts and tests.

confirm(h, token, fates, renames) commits the event with those fates and renames when the token is current (logHead unmoved) and the fates and renames equal the dry run's; otherwise re-runs the dry run and returns a fresh confirm; a changed list is never committed silently; resubmitting through edit with fates and renames filled is the same operation (how a host bridge carries a confirmed action, §11.3); 'discard edits in scope' is a new request (regenerate with discardEdits: true) with its own confirmation; cancel drops the token.

J-R33: Chose fate confirmation by token and fate equality (or resubmission with fates filled) over a force flag — because the committed event must carry exactly the fates and renames the user saw (§11.2; NF-D14, VD4-4).

facts.statement: The headless path runs the same worker code, and its model hash equals the browser's (text is not in the model, §9.1); ids cross this boundary as <docId>/<id> (§6.3).

Engine (§3.7, SCL-22): the product bundle has no WebAssembly dependency; if M0 triggers the kernel's pre-decided fallback (Clipper2-WASM as the single engine), WebAssembly becomes an embed requirement and a host without it receives E_ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE from generate and open.

BridgeTransport { send(msg: BridgeMessage); onMessage(handler) }; shipped WindowPostMessageTransport (iframe hosts; a fixed target origin; incoming origins checked against the embed's allowlist) and MessagePortTransport (any relay: browser-extension content script, SharedWorker, chat-bus relay; COV-FTG-N06); envelope { plat: 1, type, session, seq, logHead?, body }.

Bridge vocabulary (our own terms, FTG-22): host → PLAT doc.load { bytes|ref, role, session }, doc.apply { baseLogHead, events }, view.set { patch }, export.request { fmt, opts }, query { q }; PLAT → host ready { outputVersions, schemaVersion }, doc.changed { baseLogHead, events } (a local user's proposed events), doc.applied { logHead }, doc.rejected { reason 'stale'|'invalid'|'role'|'version', currentLogHead, conflicts? }, view.changed { patch }, entity.selected { id, kind }, export.ready { bytes }, query.result.

Convergence: the host holds the canonical document and log; a client sends its user's edit as doc.changed against its baseLogHead; the host accepts only when that base is the current logHead (appends, advances logHead, fans doc.apply to every client incl. sender), otherwise answers doc.rejected { stale }; the client applies pending doc.apply, re-runs its events through the dry run (§7.1) and resends, or shows its user the conflicts.

An action needing fate confirmation (§7.3 item 4, §11.2) is sent only after the local user confirmed, as an event carrying its fates and renames; if the state moved, the client's re-run returns a fresh confirmation instead of resending; every other client replays the event with those fates, reporting a mismatch if it computes different ones; every client applies the same events in the host's order on the same output version, so every client's model hash is the same (§6.2) — after a load mismatch, once the owner has chosen (§2.9 step 4).

Test (M3a): a host and three headless clients applying 1 000 interleaved random events — undo and redo from every client and one owner undo through a chain — converge to one model hash with 0 lost accepted events; one forced load mismatch settled by an owner's keep while two editors edit on the replayed town: all four converge to one model hash, editors' events re-applied on the saved town (VD3-4).

Version handshake: on doc.load the client compares the document's outputVersion (§6.4), not the generator version, with the output versions it can replay (announced in ready); when it cannot, it opens the snapshot read-only (role drops to viewer, says so) as §2.9 step 2's frozen view does — checked by its chunks' content hashes only, labelled 'made with o<k>; not verified by this version', never reported as a mismatch (VD4-1); never replays under another version silently.

Style is canonical; the viewer's preset is not (N-15): the document's style (§2.9 style: sheet and version, row operations, ground-cover regions) changes only through logged setStyle events, carried in doc.changed / doc.apply and sent only by owner and editor roles; view key stylePreset is a per-viewer preset choice that never writes setStyle — it replaces the document's sheet for that viewer only, with the document's own rows (thematic overrides, ground-cover regions) applied where the preset has the roles they name, the rest listed in that viewer's style dialog.

J-R34: Chose a per-viewer `stylePreset` view key over treating the canonical style as a last-writer-wins view key — because a viewer's look must neither rewrite the shared style nor silently diverge from it (§11.3; N-15).

facts.statement: Roles owner | editor | viewer given by doc.load; a viewer's client never emits doc.changed (edits disabled in the UI and dropped by the bridge) and emits only the view changes the host allows; the host enforces roles too; the host assigns one session per user and document and passes it on every load; a bridged client never mints a session or writes the session view key (§7.4; VD2-4).

Host inputs (DEF-11) only through these doors: (1) blueprint fields (seed, rung, population, intent, character, circumstances, assignments) to generate; (2) edit events via the API or doc.apply, logged; (3) tables, presets and styles as editTable, editPreset or setStyle events whose content is copied into the document with provenance host (source, date, version), so the document replays without the host; (4) a registered ContentProvider (§14) accepted only after a double-run check (at registration it runs twice on the same input and stream; outputs must be byte-identical, else refused), every output recorded in the document's hostContent block keyed by (provider id, version, input hash) and read from there on replay.
SettlementForge inputs (after the generators are mastered): the host-input contract and the host bridge — §11.4, §11.3.

Decision: the product contains no hosted service; for multi-client use a host (a VTT module, a web page, or SettlementForge in its owner-staged phase) is the store (§11.3) and owns accounts and access (DEF-12, COV-FTG-N07).

DocResolver { resolve(ref): Promise<ArrayBuffer>; publish?(bytes, access 'private'|'link'|'public'): Promise<string> }, configured by the embedding app; &doc=<ref> links produced only when a resolver with publish is configured, otherwise the app offers the .plat file and, for a small edit log, §6.4's inline compressed log; access levels are the resolver's; the reference app ships a file resolver (local files and inline logs) and no network resolver.

J-R15: Chose host-as-store over a sync service of our own — because the product is a standalone, backend-free library, a host already owns accounts and storage, and §11.3's protocol makes any host a correct store (§11.5).

Crown library (NR4-5): its build (20 crowns per class per style, once per session) and, in lit with a path sun, each light step's bake run in the tile worker as one-sprite class-3 units (§8.9), ≤ 20 ms of tile-worker time per (style, light step) for eight crown classes (PLAUSIBLE: ≈ 20-60 µs per sprite on Canvas2D, ≈ 3-10 ms for 160 sprites), started when the style loads so the first district-band raster finds it ready; a light step's bake runs at the head of §8.4's light pass inside its settle bound.

Crown library measured with M2b's moving-sun runs (§8.4), where lit ships; pre-decided fallback: §8.4's (with a path sun the lit programs and crowns hold the sheet's fixed sun, so the library is baked once), reported.

SVG at METROPOLIS, city band: ≤ 650 B per building plus text (outlines ≤ 64 B per placed glyph and ≤ 0.5 KB per distinct glyph, or each embedded face's base64 once, ≤ 0.5 MB per face) (§11.1, N-13) and ≤ 60 000 elements, written in ≤ 2 s in the generation worker — transient list build (≈ 4 µs per building, ≈ 54 ms at the METROPOLIS target), S13b at the export stop (≤ 2 ms per 2 000 candidates) and writing, list released after (§11.1; NR-5); Inkscape opens it within 120 s (§11.1).

PNG: A2 at 300 dpi of a CITY in ≤ 20 s on the reference machine with the view idle, peak canvas one tile band; inside it the transient list's build (≈ 4 µs per building at the city band — ≈ 21 ms at CITY — more at the finer band a large print's scale selects; §8.7, §11.1), the export's placement in the tile worker (≈ 1 µs per candidate — ≤ 20 ms for 20 000 candidates, more than a whole CITY's label rows at any band: ≈ 3 500 names, §12.4, one address per building and repeats of long street names — in class-4 steps, §8.9; NR4-2), and the encoding (§8.8's per-row filter rule, then deflate).

Encoding measured on a synthetic A2 map in Node 24 (fixall_rendering_r5_png.out): 3.5 s for flat ink-like colours, 5.4 s under smooth relief shading, 10.5 s for a textured lit-like look; the filter pass takes 2.7-3.4 s and deflate the rest (PLAUSIBLE for browsers: same JS filter pass; native deflate behind CompressionStream).

View work pre-empts the export's steps (§8.9), so a pan or zoom during an export lengthens it by that work (shown by the export dialog's progress), and an animated view still leaves it one step in every 100 ms (NR3-6).

Confirmation of export budgets (N-27 c): SVG and PNG measured at M1 on B-CITY-lite's TOWN and CITY seeds and at M2b on METROPOLIS; pre-decided fallbacks, taken once and reported: an SVG size or element miss at the city band writes path coordinates with one decimal of the export's unit instead of two and merges compound paths per (semantic, quarter of the city cut) instead of per (semantic, district), re-keying the <metadata> map; a district-band SVG missing its estimate draws woods and orchards as outlines instead of crowns.

PNG time-miss fallback, per host (NR4-4), same pixels in a larger file each time: on every host the row filter is fixed to type None for every row instead of §8.8's per-row rule (on the synthetic A2 encoding falls from 3.5/5.4/10.5 s to 0.6/1.3/4.4 s for flat/relief/textured, the file 4 % smaller to 10 % larger); in Node a remaining miss deflates at level 3 instead of 6 (a further 0.35-2.5 s; file 8-51 % larger); in browsers (CompressionStream takes no options — Node 24's implementation ignores { level }: 5.3 MiB with none, level 1 and 9 alike) a remaining miss re-declares the PNG budget at the measured p95 as a D-18 amendment.

Chose type None over the fixed Sub filter as fallback (None faster and no larger; Sub ≈ 0.2 s filtering, deflates as slowly as the default, files 7-30 % larger than the default's); chose §8.8's per-row rule as the default over None because it gives the smallest file where rows carry gradients or texture ('7-10 % smaller on the relief and textured looks') and the budget has room for its filter pass.
