During a raster export (NR3-6) its ≈ 15 MB of canvases count on top of the view's need: the reference view on the mid tier (112 + 15 ≤ 128 MB) and the low-end 1 366 × 768 view (43 + 15 ≤ 72 MB) hold both; where the sum passes the tier's ceiling (low tier at 1 920 × 1 080: 67 + 15 > 72 MB) the coarser-stop fallback set is dropped for the export's duration (need falls to 2P + 7 MB: 47 + 15 = 62 MB), and the export dialog refuses a width whose band does not fit beside the reduced need, naming the widest that does.

One-click default: generate({seed}) → a TOWN of 5 000 people whose complete city band (every block ground tone, every footprint mass, street, wall, gate and quarter label) is on screen within 150 ms of the click on the reference machine (124–145 ms across §12.2's building range); CITY and METROPOLIS default requests take ≈ 0.33–0.42 s and ≈ 0.86–1.05 s; every size follows §12.5's laws.

Every improvement ships behind the defaults (R8): the fast path never pays for the simulation module, projected shadows, relief, thumbnails or the advanced panel.

Thesis: the references' admitted weaknesses are geometry weaknesses on plain vertex arrays (MFCG 87882877 collapsed edges; FTG 133016301/153121107 hourglass footprints and coincident intersections; 2017 cut() returning its input on ≠ 2 crossings; NG's retries and 42 % silently discarded lot leaves; VG boolean "thorns"); the remedy is one robust planar subdivision — snapped, integer-lattice, exactly predicated, indexed half-edge, typed faces, refined in five nested levels — with every stage a transaction that commits a valid subdivision or is rejected with a typed reason, and everything else derived from it.

Fusion allocation: FTG's staged destination-driven growth for streets; MFCG/NG's bent-cut infill for lanes; MFCG's grower for districts; FTG's roster for content; MFCG's one-click ink look for the picture; our own site model, plot model, prosperity field, greenery rules, display list, document and stream design where neither reference answers.

Tiebreaker at every genuine conflict: the owner's DESIGN TIEBREAKER — the approach more faithful to how real settlements are constrained (terrain, water, defence, land use, access, growth) with precise real-unit geometry and measurable statistics, legibility and one-click use as a floor; rows marked TB are where it decided; each criterion carries its §15.2 class C (conformance), P (parity with a measured reference number) or O (outcome the references do not reach).

facts.statement: Repository: the product lives in its own repository plat/ at the root of this folder, outside research/, captures/ and reference/; a CI path rule fails any import, fixture or script path that resolves outside plat/ (§17; D-29).

Dependencies: permissive licences only, checked over the transitive production closure, pinned exactly and credited in a generated notices file (§17); every third-party routine behind our own adapter (D-22).

Five test benches run in CI in three tiers — quick on every change (minutes), full nightly (hours), largest at every milestone; reference comparisons are read from one numbers-only file, never from the captures; every acceptance number states its evidence kind; the owner judges side-by-sides by a written blind protocol; every threshold has a number and a stated way to confirm it.
Random inputs (fast-check): concave, holed, thin, near-collinear, snapped, duplicated-vertex, ≥ 300-vertex and zero-area polygons and chains.

Constructive degeneracies (GEO-12) are built on purpose from random parameters because random sampling almost never hits one: a line across a 2²⁴ frame holds at most 2²⁴ of its 2⁴⁸ lattice points, so a random third point is collinear with probability ≤ 2⁻²⁴.

Degeneracy fixtures (geometry classes): lattice points exactly on a segment by gcd stepping (p₀ + k·d/gcd(dx, dy)); collinear triples and collinear overlapping edges (shared runs 1 cm to whole edge, same and opposite direction); cuts through a vertex and grazing a reflex vertex (offset 0 and ± 1 lattice unit); antennae and chains touching a boundary at one point; coincident typed chains (wall on bank, quay on shore, street on district boundary, track on field boundary); rectangles, squares and regular n-gons (n = 3 … 12) rotated and snapped; holes touching the outer ring at a vertex or along an edge and touching each other; simultaneous skeleton events (regular polygons, equal-sided rectangles, symmetric notches).
Quantisation fixtures: half-centimetre ties before snapping and ± (2²³ − 1) must be handled; snap must refuse ± 2²³, NaN and ± ∞.
A carve chain touching a finer edge away from its prepared vertices returns E_LEVEL inside the clear region and E_KEPT outside (§3.3 clear regions).
A lane removed from a spine it ended on: the spine's chain restored exactly, its own shape vertices untouched (the split flag, §2.2 rule 3).

II.1 (3) neighbour step beside finished plots: a plot-line end within attractCm of the foot is promoted (every plot ring unchanged); one farther makes a kerb split (each ring equals its prior ring with the vertex removed); the street removed again, by undo and by reroll, at a promoted plot-line end and at a promoted footprint corner — kerb L2 route and digest, block and plot rings and wing rings equal to those before the step.
An S8 T-junction on a spine with a width profile leaves every sampled half-width unchanged.
A pool overlay writing outside its district is refused with E_SCOPE.
A logged moveVertex replayed after an upgrade that puts an unrelated vertex 20 cm from its position binds to the signature-matching vertex or is orphaned, never to the unrelated vertex.
A slot freed and reused inside a stage: the query returns the new item.

A pooled district beside the settlement perimeter commits plot lines ending on the backland part's inner edge with 0 unresolved crossings at pool sizes 0 and 3; every freeze finds every dynamic grid and tombstone set empty after its rebuild (§3.3 pool step 1).
An L3 query in a block before and after S11 derives L4 there (two plots sharing their lowest-leftmost vertex with an L4 vertex on their shared edge) returns results in the same order.

A warp over a spine carrying a same-level T-junction, then its lane removed: the junction stays a shape vertex of the warped spine; a warp re-seating a Steiner vertex, then clearFiner: the vertex dissolves and the coarser edge is restored exactly.

facts.statement: A warp moving a kerb beside a vertex 25.3 cm from it — kerb (0, 0)–(1 000, 9) past (517, 30) — commits, the re-seated vertex placed by the placement rule.

A warp over a locked plot and over a pinned building holds every corner (a neighbour's footprint corner on the locked plot's line slides); a warp with fromLevel = 1 over finished fabric gives 0 E_KEPT.
A way split between two width knots keeps every sampled half-width within 10⁻⁹ cm of its prior value; re-joined, the original profile returns bit for bit.
The frozen copy sent to a pool worker holds typed arrays only — no Map or Set reachable from the message.

A canal across an open enceinte's glacis line and a river moved through a walled town: every indexed role unique per ordinal (§3.10), the water gate's Gate.banks resolving to its two gate_end vertices, and no anchor contact name left after the edit.

A river moved away from a quay-lined and a walled bank: quay and wall edges back at L1, the L0 view land and water only, a deck left over land at the way's level after F-REDERIVE (before it, at the level of its deck_end rows, with no L0 edge at it), its bank vertices unpinned.

A warp re-seating two Steiner vertices whose projections lie within minEdge + 1 cm of each other gives identical output after a slot renumbering (the two placement orders differ in 6.8 % of such pairs).
A promotion leaving another finer vertex 1.2 cm from its new route edge commits with no E_INVARIANT, and every index query whose box meets that vertex returns it.
Two neighbour steps on one kerb edge, the first street removed by a reroll: its plot-line end back at L3 and the kerb's L2 route equal to the route with only the second step.
A warp that moves a spine's vertices around an unmoved same-level T-junction, then its lane removed: the junction stays a shape vertex of the warped spine.
A warp with fromLevel = 1 over a generated and over an edited water gate: neither gate's bank vertices move.

After a neighbour step and its removal by a reroll with no partition rebuilt in between, level-2 and level-3 queries over the kerb return exactly what they return after a rebuild; a slot freed in one district and reused in another (second district's partition rebuilt first) is returned as its new item, never its old one.
A declared preparation batch placing two contact names on one entity, its ops permuted, gives identical ordinals.
New water across a corner of the frame: the border's stretch between its two contact points, the corner included, unchanged and closed.

Properties checked after every operation (topology): output simple; nesting by index (every face inside its parent); no edge shorter than minEdge from any writer after every insertion and warp step, clearance ≥ minEdge; Euler characteristic after every insertion; remove(insert(x)) ≡ id on topology; splitFace children tile the parent exactly at the child level (integer area2 equality); mergeFaces ∘ splitFace restores ring and id.

Properties (constructions): corridorUnion faces disjoint and covering; offset(−d) ∘ offset(+d) ⊆ original and insetFace empties monotonically; every straight-skeleton output passes the §3.8 validator (connected graph inside the face whose independent cycle count equals the hole count) or is a reported downgrade; OBB contains the hull and collinear input returns E_DEGENERATE; LIR inside the face; snap rounding idempotent and terminating within its bound; orient2d sign equal to a BigInt reference on adversarial triples; Poisson minimum distance ≥ r.

Properties (index and levels): every index query's answer identical before and after a rebuild of the partitions it reads (§3.3); after every removal each edge's level is the lowest among its rows and no vertex is coarser than every edge and role at it (§3.10 level-consistency row); save → load → save byte-identical (§3.9).

Invariants: the §5.3 suite runs by scope (batch-local per batch, stage-end per stage, save/load per document, CI-only in the harness) on B-CITY — 1 000 seeds × 4 WaterSettings (§13.3) × 3 rungs nightly; 50 seeds per rung in the PR tier; all three rungs from M1. Each invariant has an id, a severity, a report count and a CI threshold: hard = 0 per 1 000 cities; soft within its band.

Statistics core record (SCL-21): O(n), emitted by every generation within 4 ms at CITY (§12.4): counts per entity kind and class; areas per class and band; fixed-bin histograms per district and band of plot area, frontage, depth, footprint area and storeys; way length per class; junction-degree histogram; turning per 100 m on ways resampled at 10 m; walled share and built extent; ladder uses per cause and rung; every requested feature's delivery tier (§5.1 principle 7); stage timings.
facts.values: ≤ 4 ms at CITY; 100 m / 10 m resampling

facts.statement: Bench metrics (detour index over sampled destination pairs, Moran's I, KS distances, junction-to-junction runs, orientation coherence and wall alignment, figure-ground metrics on renders (§8.5), tree nearest-neighbour and pair-correlation statistics from §8.10's stamped scatter) run through stats(doc, { level: 'bench' }) on demand or in the bench, never on the one-click path.

Cost-model tests (SCL-19; NF-S10): each stage timed on nine sizes — the band bottom, target and top per rung: 1 500 / 5 000 / 9 900 (TOWN), 10 000 / 20 000 / 29 900 (CITY), 30 000 / 50 000 / 120 000 (METROPOLIS) inhabitants, five seeds each, nightly; METROPOLIS sizes reported from M1 and gating from M2b.

Each stage's log-log slope of time against its declared work measure (Stage work-limit laws, §5.1 (5), §14) must not exceed 1.15 for a stage declared linear and 1.25 for one declared n log n; §12.3's per-rung cost laws are fitted on the same runs.

Work limits follow population: each run reports per stage the F-WORK hit rate (work cuts per 1 000 batches); CI fails when the rate at a band's top exceeds its bottom by more than 1 per 1 000, after which §5.1 (5)'s pre-decided coefficient fallback applies and the sweep re-runs.
Document-size test per rung: ≤ 320 B per building at CITY (§2.9).
The per-stop placement digests of §13.3 are the contract test of S13b; a stop placed whole and placed one unit per step gives identical placement digests (§8.3, §9.2).
Stamp-tile seam check: 0 point pairs closer than r₀ across cells in all 256 2 × 2 arrangements of each class's four tiles, for every band's rank subset (§8.3, §8.10).

Wall trace fixtures: every gate and weld vertex on its trace; stage 1's trace within 40 m of its boundary except along an on_enceinte castle's shared stretch; 0 lanes crossing a wall strip and 0 L3 band faces split or cleared (NF-P5); 0 S7b claims meeting a wall strip.
The seam exception on New random of 20 districts per B-CITY-lite city (NF-P6).
Decks on 100 % of way–water crossings, moats and canals included (NF-P4).
Harbour fixtures: a two-arm mole and a detached breakwater pass the crossing invariant as harbour works; a quay way drawn across a river without a deck fails it (§5.3).

Crossing-site fixtures: a river town whose growth leaves crossing sites unused — 0 site furniture and 0 site marks in the display list, every built bridge's span the way's own L1 edge; an epoch whose growth builds a site; a drawn bridge 15 m from a site builds that site and one 30 m from every site adds a deck by one L0 shore-split batch; §5.3's crossing invariant throughout (§4.2 S1 (5)).

castle: 'on_enceinte' with water in reach, with and without a city moat: 0 trace–water crossings off a river's water gate, the outer-arc channel beside the shared stretch, the town side dry-ditched or plain by its row.
Every seam edge typed; a way-less shared reservation boundary typed reserve (II.5).

B-EDIT locality oracle: §7.3 item 7 (i)–(iii) and (v), and (iv)'s byte identity of Regenerate (keep settings), run once per sequence — at its end and at one seeded random position — never per edit (SCL-18).

B-EDIT fixtures (structure): the re-parenting set (drawBoundary, district merge and split, outskirtToDistrict, regenerate around a lock, id-recycling); terrain-brush sequences in both water modes; course-knot, drawn-water and drawn-bridge sequences with §7.3 (7)(v)'s assertions (0 decks over land, 0 off-deck crossings, 0 wings off §2.6's datum rule, 0 footprints in water); table weight edits and row insertions; drawn features mixed with later attribute edits; epochs and rebases.

An epoch after 20 edits and a Re-derive from S10 after 20 edits, each at pool sizes 0 and 3 with identical digests, every freeze finding every dynamic grid and tombstone set empty after its rebuild (§3.3 pool step 1).

Undo and redo from several sessions with the truncation-identity property (§7.4, §6.5 (9)); New random on minimal scopes (§5.1 (6)); the naming-collision replay fixture (§7.3 (7)(i)); B-EDIT-lite identity fixtures (≥ 99.9 % of addresses kept under 1 cm perturbation, §6.3).

Naming-record fixtures: a snapshot with one altered naming record is a corrupt cache when its recordsDigest is left as written, and a records mismatch rebuilt from the replay, re-applied, then verified when it is rewritten to match.
A canal carved across a wall and a river move whose bank cuts a glacis line each commit with 0 NF-P5 violations; a lane drawn across a wall strip is refused (§5.3).

Campaign statistic: for each of four statistics (median plot area, median frontage width, density, attached share) the rank r = references below plus a uniform draw 0 … t over t ties (from the campaign's own stream), exactly uniform on 0 … K for a perfect regenerator; ranks binned into 10 bins ⌊r·10/(K + 1)⌋ with expected counts proportional to rank values per bin; χ² per statistic → four p-values; the campaign fails when Holm's procedure rejects at family-wise 0.01 (smallest p below 0.0025).
Campaign cost ≈ 40 800 scope generations (800 × 51), ≈ 12.5 CPU-min at §12.6's block and district costs (20 400 × ≈ 6.6 ms + 20 400 × ≤ 30 ms), inside the nightly tier budget (§13.8).

Why 800 scopes: with statistics correlated at ρ = 0.8, 400 scopes catch a +0.25 sd bias in only 92.2 % of nights and a 0.8 × too-snug regenerator in 95.2 % (verifier 92.0 % / 95.0 %), first-night detection 0.85–0.91. Executed at n = 800 (docs/validation/bench/fixall_scope_r3_o9c_n800.py → .out): perfect regenerator fails 1.0 % on continuous statistics (31/3 000 at ρ = 0.8, 15/1 500 at ρ = 0) and 1.4 % (14/1 000) on tied discrete ones; +0.25 sd bias and 0.8 × snug caught in 2 000/2 000 at ρ = 0 and 0.8 (95 % lower bound 99.8 %); 0.6 × snug and 1.5 × loose in 500/500; at ρ = 1 bias 99.3 %, snugness 99.7 %; without the randomised tie-break a perfect regenerator fails every campaign on a tied statistic (fixall_verify_scope_o9c_rank.out).
places: J-S (rationale for n = 800, check) (restated, per SCOPE-215)

facts.statement: A failing statistic's histogram names the fault: a hump is too snug, a U too loose, a slope a bias.

A failed campaign is re-run once with the next campaign seed (a perfect regenerator fails twice with probability ≈ 1–2 × 10⁻⁴; a fault of the sizes above is declared on its first night with probability ≥ 0.996 at ρ ≤ 0.8, ≥ 0.985 at ρ = 1); a second failure is a regeneration defect entered in known-defects.json, and M3a does not exit until it is fixed (§16), because no threshold can be relaxed without passing a wrong regenerator.

Control sweeps: §7.8's statistical monotonicity and continuity at 21 steps × 50 seeds at TOWN and CITY (nightly), METROPOLIS in the milestone tier; the population control's sweep also reports the F-WORK hit rate per stage, which must stay flat across each band.
Option-interaction matrix: every pair of toggles rendered and diffed; no option silently disables another (O12 c).

Documentation coverage (COV-FTG-A25): 100 % of controls and entity kinds have a guide anchor (§14 @plat/docs); every in-app help link resolves (CI link check); the release notes list every open entry of known-defects.json.

Golden suite: 12 seeds × {TOWN, CITY, METROPOLIS} × the four WaterSettings {none, coast, river, coast+river} stores per stage its stage-isolated digest (the stage's new code run on the previous output version's frozen upstream outputs, §6.4), entity counts, the core statistics record and one PNG per LOD and preset; and per shipped preset's label style a per-stop placement digest.

An undeclared move fails CI; a declared statistic moving against its declared direction fails CI until the record states why; only declared stages are re-signed; stages untouched by a release stay byte-identical (O2 e); a same-seed output change never rides silently (owner non-negotiable 10).
The records are product files (NF-S1): everything the golden gate and the release-notes generator read lives inside plat/, so §17.1 (3)'s path rule and the gate never collide.

WaterSetting = none | coast | river | coast+river — the one spelling of a water setting for B-CITY, the golden store and every record; a seed in a record is a Seed (u32, §2.9) written as its decimal string; permalinks write it in base 36 (§6.4).
facts.values: 4 values; u32 decimal; base 36 in links

facts.statement: ShiftRecord: id; release (generator version); outputVersion (the o<k> it creates, null for a view shift); stage: StageId | S13b | render.stampTiles; cause {kind: table | fix | concern | engine | feature | calibration | baselineShift; ref; note}; seeds[] {seed, rung, water, before, after: Hash128}; statistics[] {metric, rung, before, after, expected: up | down | none | any}; tiles?[] {tile, before, after} (render.stampTiles only, empty seeds list); d5SeedsChanged[]; milestone; date; author.
CascadeRecord: id; outputVersion; upstream (ShiftRecord ids); downstream[] {stage, before, after (end-to-end digests), isolatedUnchanged: true}; seeds[]; date.

MilestoneRecord: milestone; date; outputVersions[] (created during the milestone); shifts[]; cascades[]; parity (path plat/goldens/parity/<milestone>.json — the ParityReport the exit is judged on, §13.5); d5 {status: D5Status; record: plat/goldens/d5/<milestone>/record.json (§13.6)} | null; knownDefects {opened[], closed[]}; exitCriteria[] {id, result: pass | fail | fallback-applied, evidence}.

Golden store layout: plat/goldens/store/o<k>/ holds per seed and stage the frozen upstream outputs, digests, counts, statistics and placement digests; PNGs content-addressed in plat/goldens/png/ (large-file storage) referenced by hash; plat/goldens/shifts/o<k>.json holds the shift and cascade records creating o<k>; plat/goldens/shifts/view/<release>.json holds a release's view shifts; plat/goldens/milestones/<milestone>.json is each milestone's exit record.
The golden CLI refuses a record with a missing field; the @plat/docs release-notes generator reads only these files and plat/docs/known-defects.json.

docs/validation/shifts/<milestone>.md and docs/validation/d5/<milestone>.md are research-side copies generated by research/baselines/mirror_records.py (research may read the product; the product never reads research); no CI job reads them; a hand edit there changes nothing.

Placement digests (N-24; §9.1's cross-engine promise): for every golden town, every shipped preset's label style and each of B-ZOOM's 27 zoom stops, S13b places the band's area and way labels for all candidates and the addresses and repeated street names of the default view's visible tiles (§9.2's scope); the digest hashes per candidate in id order the label id, chosen alternate (or yielded), ladder rung, size and every glyph position and angle as exact IEEE doubles.

The PR tier compares placement digests on Node x86 against the store; the nightly tier compares them on all five engines with workers on and off; a digest that differs between engines is a determinism defect and fails the nightly run.

View shift: a placement digest that moves while every model digest holds needs a ShiftRecord with stage S13b and outputVersion null, bumps no output version (placement is view data, §9.1) and bumps the style version of every shipped sheet whose placements moved (the style version carries pixel identity, §6.4).

From M1 (LC-19): the output-version stamp, the shift, cascade and milestone records and the stage-isolated golden tooling are built at M1, not at hardening; every milestone from M1 writes its MilestoneRecord (output versions created, shift records, D-5 panel seeds changed) and cannot exit with an undeclared shift.
Retention of output versions N−1 and N−2 (§6.4) is built and its replay test passes at M3a; from then a link inside the window replays exactly and one outside opens with §6.4's notice.

Visual regression: Playwright renders the golden suite per preset, LOD and backend; SSIM / pixelmatch against the stored PNG with a per-preset threshold; the draw-style census of §8.3 per preset; a "no fills" and a "no outlines" render must remain legible (R13).

B-ZOOM (1:50 000 → 1:500, the default view of every rung): legibility floors; no feature pops more than once (footprint hash identical across bands); §8.3's checks — hairline fidelity, decoration stability, role continuity across band switches, no tree mark over a tier-1/2 casing, no casing pixels in junction mouths, the contrast matrix on the rendered city band.

App harness scripted tasks (O16 c; IMP-11) on the reference machine of §12.1: share a view link, export a layered SVG, change the coast side, see five variants of one kind, recover from a mistaken regenerate, measure a street with the ruler, find a named building through the gazetteer — each passes when completed in the stated number of UI actions (one where a reference needs a detour; recovery = one undo) with every app response ≤ 1 s; run on every PR.

Accessibility (COV-FTG-A24): axe-core on every screen and panel of @plat/app reports 0 serious or critical violations; every control reachable and operable by keyboard alone with visible focus; every scripted task also passes keyboard-only; the gazetteer list and search and the "features in view" list reach every building, plot, district and pinned person without the canvas.

Input scheme: every binding of the default keymap.json (§14) fires its action while the map has focus and none fires while a text field has focus; a user-edited keymap round-trips through save and load.

The parity CLI in @plat/testkit reads only baselines.json (our own numbers-only measurements of the references, generated research-side by scripts under research/baselines/ from the captures and committed into plat/packages/testkit/baselines/) and our B-CITY outputs, reports every metric against its band, and never opens captures/, research/ or reference/.

Baseline: id; metric; unit; reference: MFCG | FTG | NG | VG | corpus:<name> (corpus rows via §13.9); referenceBuild (itch build, FTG server date + create-request hash, NG/VG build — required); capture; script; date; matched? {rung, mfcgSize?, ftgSize?: BIG_TOWN | BIG_CITY | CITY | METROPOLIS, population?}; role: target | weakness | descriptive; values: {p10?, p50?, p90?, n, seeds} | {bins[], histogram[], n, seeds}.

ParityReport (written per run by the parity CLI; read by milestone exits, §13.9's CalibrationRun and the release notes): runId; date; outputVersion; generatorVersion; baselines (Hash128 of the baselines.json read); rows[] {metric, baselineIds[], role, rung, preset?, band {lo?, hi?, ksMax?, direction?: above | below, margin?}, ours {p10?, p50?, p90?, ks?, n, seeds}, verdict: pass | fail | reported (descriptive rows always reported), note?}; summary {pass, fail, reported}.
Each milestone's parity report is stored as plat/goldens/parity/<milestone>.json and named in its MilestoneRecord (§13.3).

The CLI refuses a baseline row without referenceBuild, capture, script or date; a new reference build never overwrites a row — it adds one (id gains the build) and is a declared baseline shift in the milestone's shift record (motivated by VG changing geometry for the same seed between builds 19251041 and 19365073); rows hold numbers, units and provenance only — no names, colours, grammars or code.

⟨M-1⟩ rule (NF-S5): a reference number marked ⟨M-1⟩ is measured by M-1 (§16 lists them); if M-1 cannot measure it (capture lacks the feature, or not reproducible across seeds) the cell becomes descriptive, gates nothing and enters known-defects.json with the reason; the parity CLI reports an ⟨M-1⟩ cell without its baseline row as fail, never pass.

Band rule (DEF-1; IMP-6): target rows pass when ours lies in [p10 × 0.9, p90 × 1.1] of the reference's seed spread (single-value baseline ± 15 %); distributions pass when our KS distance to the reference ≤ 1.25 × the reference's own seed-to-seed KS distance at p90; weakness rows are one-sided (beat the reference in the declared direction by the stated margin); descriptive rows are reported and gate nothing; thresholds no reference can set are §13.7's.

When M-1 re-measures a baseline (five seeds per matched MFCG size, FTG's new captures) the band is recomputed by the same rule with provenance "M-1 ⟨date⟩"; a recomputation turning a passing gate into a failing one is declared in the shift record.

Matched sizes (MN-2): TOWN ↔ MFCG size 40 and FTG BIG_TOWN; CITY ↔ MFCG size 80 and FTG BIG_CITY; METROPOLIS ↔ MFCG size 130 (FTG per D-31); MFCG numbers from its plain-option size sweep (walls, citadel, plaza, temple on; shanty town, parks, river, coast off; JSON in metres, internal unit 4.00 m).
Curves (FTG-15) are measured after both sides are resampled at a 10 m arc-length step, so neither FTG's 25–40 m placement steps nor PLAT's smoothed vertex spacing enters a number.

facts.statement: Street turning (P): weakness vs FTG (zero mass above 15° per step, flat heading spectrum): no cliff (no empty bin above 15° while the bin below holds > 1 %) and heading entropy ≥ FTG's; target for organic presets: median turning per 100 m within 0.5–1.5 × FTG's ⟨M-1⟩ (a declared exception to the band rule, FTG's ≤ 8 payloads being too narrow); fallback: headingSigma (table value, §4.4) set so the organic median equals FTG's and the growth-drift row re-runs; if drift then fails, headingSigma returns to default, the target clause enters known-defects.json as not met and the row gates on its weakness clauses.
Growth drift (C): net turn of grown streets over 600 m in organic regimes: p50 15–30°, > 90° on ≤ 1 %.

Junction arm angles and degrees (P), every L1 junction: median 85–95°; p5 ≥ 30°; 4-way share organic 0–15 %, ringed 20–45 %, american 40–80 % (NG 361/361 T target for organic; FTG median 90.02°, 58 % in 80–100°, 36.4 % 4-way — weakness for organic, target for ringed and american).

facts.statement: Street runs by class (P): junction-to-junction run lengths per class (never edge lengths) against FTG (main L + 0.5, district (L + 0.5)/2, suburb 30.00 m, lot outlines 14.70 m) — target for extramural ribbon and suburb regimes, descriptive inside walls; class medians by the band rule.

Blocks (P): L2 built-block areas per district — KS by the band rule against NG block counts per template at medium ⟨M-1⟩ on the same face shapes (O4 f); FTG block-lot median 441 m² in every class is a weakness (no gradient).
Deep block interiors (IMP-8; P): court share of deep blocks per band by the band rule per class (§4.6) against NG hollow-block frequency ⟨M-1⟩ and MFCG inner-lot removal ⟨M-1⟩.

Bent-cut signature (P) against NG (start at N(0.5, σ) of OBB major axis, σ 0.066 plain and 0.098 ring faces; one bend at mid-course in 380/519; ≥ 85° arrival in 96 %; 53 % filleted): σ within ± 0.02; corner within 0.10 of mid-course ≥ 80 %; arrivals ≥ 85° ≥ 95 %.

Plots and footprints (P): ordinary houses median footprint 60–160 m², p95 < 400 m², a sheared minority kept (FTG median 103 m², p95 154 m², quad side 10.3 m, worst-corner p95 22.9° as target; MFCG footprints 225–289 m² are lots drawn as buildings — descriptive, never a house-size anchor).
Entrance rule (P, L4): 100 % on the access edge, 2–4 m (FTG: on the outline, 2.99 m from the road; 53 % of buildings with a vertex ≤ 2 m from a road).

facts.statement: Party walls and attachment (P, row classes): attached ≥ 90 % in dense/poor; party-wall share by the band rule per class (NG 39–43 % of perimeter, 95–99 % attached — target; FTG residences 0–5 %, industry 96–98 % — descriptive).

Plot-area gradient (C / O): Spearman(prosperity, plot area) ≥ 0.8; Moran's I > 0 (both follow from the rules: C); within-district plot-area CV ≥ 0.25 (§13.7: O) (FTG 441 m² in every class; NG Moran's I −0.04 … +0.03 — weakness).
Alleys (C): alley length per ha by prosperity, Spearman ≤ −0.7 (FTG 0 alley length at every decile — weakness).
Vacancy runs (COV-VG-VN-170; C): share of frontage length in vacancy runs per band within ± 0.02 of the granularity table's share per band.
Quays and substitution (C): quays reachable from the network 100 %; blocks left as substitution residue (F-CUT tier 5) ≤ 5 % of blocks.
Walled share and ribbons (MFP-6; P, band rule): buildings inside the outermost wall and extramural buildings within 100 m of an arterial against MFCG 0.87–0.92 at sizes 40–250 and 71–85 % (sweep).

MFCG anchors (MFP-8; P, band rule; castle in band on ≥ 99 % of seeds): district areas (MFCG 2.4–17.6 ha at size 40, median 29 ha at size 80); wall vertex spacing p50 88 m at size 40; castle 0.5–3.2 ha (8.7 at size 130); plaza 0.32–0.58 ha; 9 / 12 / 18 districts at sizes 40 / 80 / 130.
Block-level use mix (MFP-7; O): residential-only block share, per-block use-mix entropy and trade households at their workplace in §13.7's bands (MFCG's venue mix descriptive).

Towers and gates (P, S7): tower spacing by the band rule (FTG 39 m median, 17/17 towers on ring vertices — target); ungated crossings 0 (FTG 6 and 2 — weakness); main gates = N exact (MFCG 5 / 8 / 12 gates at sizes 40 / 80 / 130); roads leaving each walled stage = its N main gates plus a harbour gate of §4.2 S3 (7) where placed.
Water (P, L0): outline step ≤ 25 m; width band by class (FTG 50 m resampling, rivers ≈ 31 m mean at CITY — target; MFCG riverWidth 142 m at size 200 — descriptive).

Tree scatter (O): NN p1 ≥ §13.7's canopy threshold; pair-correlation per class reported (FTG NN median 9.7 m, minimum 0.14 m, not Poisson — weakness; MFCG/NG Bridson k = 50 with a 140-point tile — target for the sampler).
Population and buildings (C): requested population within ± 5 % on ≥ 95 % of seeds; the persons-per-building ratio reported (MFCG ≈ 6.12 — weakness; FTG 3.4 — descriptive).

Generation time (MN-2, MFP-5; P): §12.3/§12.5 budgets; model ≤ 2.5 × MFCG at TOWN and CITY and ≤ 5.5 × at METROPOLIS (MFCG app 57 / 131 / 156 ms at sizes 40 / 80 / 130, descriptive with §12.9's declared trade); first map ≥ 10 × sooner than FTG at FTG's timed CITY preset (9 500 people, 2 798 buildings: PLAT TOWN law ≈ 0.24 s vs 6.4–7.0 s) and at BIG_TOWN and BIG_CITY from M-1's captures; NG hood 10–96 ms is the target for opening a district.

facts.statement: MFCG-worst configurations (IMP-5; O): wall-clock p95 per delivered town, ladder costs included, for METROPOLIS with river, coast, walls and castle ≤ 1.0 s (MFCG size 80 with river and coast: 10 attempts for 3 cities, 3.7–4.0 s; 24 restarts in 58 attempts — weakness).
Requested-feature delivery (IMP-5; O): tier-6 omissions of requested features 0; degraded (tiers 4–5) ≤ 5 % (§13.7) (MFCG requested river fails 7 of 10 at size 80; VG discards 4 of 13 highway maps).
places: §1.4 site and failure rows (restated, per SCOPE-285)

facts.statement: Ladder use (C): tier ≥ 2 on ≤ 2 % of transactions per stage; p99 ≤ 3 attempts.

Draw style (IMP-15, VIS-16; P): ink — casing law on 100 % of ribbons, round joins ≥ 99.9 %, order parity as §8.3 defines, widths ± 15 %, outline share ≤ 25 % (MFCG casing = core + 2h on 7/7 maps, round joins 4 062/4 063, 17-step order, wall/tower/road-core 6.2/12.4/6.5 px at size 40); hatched — 15–20 triangles per wing, no ridge stroke, outline = footprint (NG ≈ 17.4 triangles, 2.33 shadow quads per wing); our roof law within ± 0.02 and our water bands W · (i / N)^1.5 within 1e-4 (NG roof ratios 0.787/0.802/0.834 and VG water bands 5.196 : 2.828 : 1 descriptive).

Labels (O): protected overlaps 0; inside-area share ≥ 99 %; curvature within §13.7's limit; 0 labels crossing holes; count per the anchors row (MFCG covers gates and the keep and straddles walls — weakness).

Between-seed variety (IMP-12; O): dispersion of the §7.7 signature vector (radial share of arterials, orthogonality index, street-density profile, block-area CV, enclosed share, outline anisotropy) over 100 seeds per rung and water setting — mean pairwise distance of rung-standardised vectors — ≥ the larger of MFCG's and FTG's dispersion at the matched rung ⟨M-1⟩.

"Mastered" = the owner's eye on side-by-sides against MFCG and FTG at town, city and metropolis plus the measured parity numbers (D-5); the protocol makes the eye a recorded, repeatable judgement that cannot be steered by seed choice and never lets a milestone claim the eye's verdict without the eye.

When: M1 (diagnostic — recorded, not gating; covers all three rungs), M2b (gates "the base at parity"), M4 (gates "mastered"), M5 against NG (gates stage 2, replacing S2's blind preference test with n ≥ 20 raters, for which the program has no pool; IMP-11).
Seeds fixed before rendering: every pair's seeds come from a formula and are committed before any render; no seed is replaced after rendering; every list is reproducible from its formula.

H32(s) = the first 32-bit output word (h1) of MurmurHash3 x86 128-bit (the algorithm §6.2's H128 implements) over the UTF-8 bytes of s with seed 0; it passes the published verification value (SMHasher procedure 0xB3ECE62A); the result is a u32 Seed (§2.9) written in records as its decimal string.

plat d5 seeds ⟨milestone⟩ (product CLI) writes the milestone's pair list (one D5Pair per pair) to plat/goldens/d5/⟨milestone⟩/seeds.json before any render; besides the formulas it reads only the two numbers-only files the research-side panel script commits beside it — ftg-captures.json (M1, M2b, M4) and ng-counts.json (M5) — never captures/ (§17.1 (3), (4)); ⟨milestone⟩ ∈ M1, M2b, M4, M5; ⟨rung⟩ a Rung; ⟨water⟩ a WaterSetting; ⟨i⟩, ⟨k⟩ decimal.

Against MFCG (M1, M2b, M4): five pairs per rung and per water setting (none; coast+river), ten per rung; PLAT seed H32("d5/⟨milestone⟩/⟨rung⟩/⟨water⟩/⟨i⟩"), i = 0 … 4 (check vectors: "d5/M1/TOWN/none/0" = 1221236157; "d5/M1/TOWN/coast+river/4" = 3998735106); MFCG seed from the same formula with prefix d5-mfcg/, reduced as 1 + (H32 mod 2 147 483 646) into 1 … 2³¹ − 2 (MFCG's Park–Miller state range; check vector d5-mfcg/M1/TOWN/none/0 → 1965791931) by the research-side panel script; MFCG draws none with plain options and coast+river with river and coast on.

Against FTG (M1, M2b, M4; TOWN and CITY, METROPOLIS per D-31): FTG cannot be seeded, so one pair per FTG capture at the matched size (BIG_TOWN for TOWN, BIG_CITY for CITY), each used once in capture order — three pairs per rung; M-1 takes per size three captures with water options nearest none (one) and coast+river (two), recording each capture's id (folder under captures/ftg/), WaterSetting and recorded population (residents in its decoded payload) in the capture README (§16).

At each FTG milestone the research-side panel script writes plat/goldens/d5/⟨milestone⟩/ftg-captures.json (one FtgCapture per capture, capture order, ids and numbers only) and commits it like baselines.json (§17.1 (4)) before plat d5 seeds runs; PLAT's side is generated at the capture's recorded population and WaterSetting from that file with seed H32("d5-ftg/⟨milestone⟩/⟨rung⟩/⟨capture id⟩"), so every milestone pairs the same captures at the same populations with its own PLAT seeds.

FTG capture fallback: a capture whose payload yields no resident count takes its size's nominal target (BIG_TOWN 5 600, BIG_CITY 24 500), marked populationSource: nominal and reported; a population outside the rung's band (§1.1) is clamped into the band and the clamp reported; the capture file and seed list are committed before any PLAT render.

Against NG (M5): NG is seedable (MINSTD), so five pairs per NG template for the four templates PLAT registers as fabrics — area, street, square, ring (II.2) — twenty pairs; NG seed H32("d5-ng/M5/⟨template⟩/⟨i⟩"), i = 0 … 4, reduced as 1 + (H32 mod 2 147 483 646) into 1 … 2³¹ − 2 (check vectors d5-ng/M5/area/0 → 1819777585; d5-ng/M5/ring/4 → 951122398), generated at NG's medium size by the research-side panel script, which counts each hood's buildings; counts reach the product as numbers only in plat/goldens/d5/M5/ng-counts.json, committed like baselines.json (§17.1 (4)).

NG pair PLAT side: one district of a PLAT town opened with the same template at neighbourhood LOD (setAttr(district.fabric, template), II.4) in the template's default form (square: SquareFabric void mode); found by a committed search — town k = 0 … 31 generated with seed H32("d5/M5/⟨template⟩/⟨i⟩/⟨k⟩") (check "d5/M5/area/0/0" = 3881605733), water none, population ⌊min(50 000 × 1.25^⌊k/4⌋, 120 000)⌋ (four towns each at 50 000, 62 500, 78 125, 97 656, the rest at the cap); in each town the district whose city-LOD building count is nearest the NG hood's (ties to the smaller address id) is opened, and the first whose opened count lies within ± 20 % of the hood's is the pair's; k, the district address and both counts are committed with the seeds.

NG search fallback: a pair with no district within ± 20 % after k = 31 takes the nearest-count of the 32 opened districts, marked sizeMismatch; the ratio is printed on the sealed key and reported beside the verdict; the pair is rated like any other; the search's k and each pair's count ratio are reported with the panel (measurement at M5).

Matched pairs: each MFCG/FTG pair shows PLAT and one reference at the same rung, ground scale (metres per pixel) and frame; against MFCG PLAT's population is set so its building count matches MFCG's at sizes 40 / 80 / 130 (§12.2's rate); against FTG PLAT uses the capture's recorded population (near BIG_TOWN 5 600 and BIG_CITY 24 500) and water from ftg-captures.json; against NG each side fills the same frame (NG rescales its hood), so size is matched by building count, not metres per pixel.

Looks per reference: PLAT draws ink against MFCG's default style, lit against FTG's default from M2b (ink at M1), hatched against NG's (M5); against FTG the pair of each rung's first capture shows the extramural suburb at FTG's overview framing (both sides alike, VIS-3); the other two use the matched frame.

Blind order: generator-identifying furniture (titles, legends, compasses, interface chrome) removed from both sides; blind pairs rendered without labels, labels judged in a separate non-blind pass; left/right a seeded coin per pair, pair order shuffled; the key sealed (only its hash committed) and opened after the answers.

Rubric: three questions per pair, each answered left, right or same with an optional one-line note — (1) Legibility (which lets you read streets, walls and quarters more easily at this size), (2) Realism (more like a real medieval town), (3) Charm (rather use for a game or story).

Pass rule: per reference and question PLAT judged better or same on ≥ ⌈2n/3⌉ of that reference's pairs, counted per group — MFCG over the milestone's MFCG pairs (20 of 30 with all rungs rated), FTG per rung (2 of 3 per rung and question), NG over its twenty (14 of 20) — and in no rung (MFCG) or template (NG) is PLAT judged worse on every pair; a gating milestone whose rated run fails a question does not exit until a re-run passes or the owner accepts the failure in the record; the failing question and owner notes enter known-defects.json.

Rater and unrated panel (NF-S2): the owner is the declared rater, no seat rates on the owner's behalf; if unrated within seven days of the panel being ready, the build continues on measured numbers and the D-5 status is recorded provisional — not rated in its D5Record and MilestoneRecord; a provisional status never claims what the panel gates (M2b "the base at parity", M4 "mastered", M5 stage-2 gate), which only a rated pass or an owner acceptance recorded in the D5Record can claim.

facts.statement: The same panel (same seeds, re-rendered under the current output version) is offered again at every later milestone and, after M5, with every release, until rated; a later rated pass sets passed with its date; a later rated failure follows (6); the release notes state every provisional status (§14 @plat/docs); §16 states the same rule at each gating exit.

Threshold panel: at the same sitting the owner sees §13.7's strips (one seed at a threshold's number and one step either side) and picks one or answers same; the pick becomes the threshold with provenance "owner-eye ⟨milestone⟩".

house pick: from M4 the sitting also shows the three candidate house sheets drafted at M3b (D-1) on the milestone's seeds; if no house pick is recorded by M4's exit, candidate 1 (first in M3b draft order) ships as house, selectable and never the default; ink stays the default; the pick is offered again at every later sitting and a later pick replaces house's sheet as a style-version change (pixels only; no model digest moves).

Record and clean room (NF-S1): the panel is assembled research-side (research/d5/) from PNG exports the product CLI writes and from reference images in captures/; the product never reads the captures (§17); the machine-readable record lives in the product, committed by the seat that ran the sitting like baselines.json (§17.1 (4)) — numbers, hashes and answers only, no reference image or data.
D5Status = diagnostic (M1) | passed | failed | accepted (failure or unrated panel accepted by the owner in writing) | provisional-not-rated.

D5Pair (one per pair in seeds.json and the record, in (2)'s order): MFCG {rung, water: none | coast+river, i, platSeed, refSeed (1 … 2³¹ − 2)}; FTG {rung: TOWN | CITY, capture (folder name), water, population (from its FtgCapture), populationSource: recorded | nominal, platSeed, suburbFrame}; NG {template: area | street | square | ring, i, refSeed, k, platSeed, population, district (address id), buildings {ref, plat}, sizeMismatch}.

FtgCapture = {capture, rung: TOWN | CITY, water, population (decoded residents or nominal target), populationSource: recorded | nominal}; the file plat/goldens/d5/<milestone>/ftg-captures.json is FtgCapture[] in capture order, research-side, numbers and ids only.

D5Record (plat/goldens/d5/<milestone>/record.json): milestone; status; date; offeredAgainAt[]; pairs: D5Pair[] (seeds as decimal strings); platImages: Hash128[] (PNG hashes of PLAT's side in pair order); key {commitment: Hash128, revealed?}; answers[] {pair, question: legibility | realism | charm, answer: left | right | same, note?}; verdicts[] {reference, question, group: all | Rung, betterOrSame, pairs, needed (⌈2n/3⌉), worseOnEveryPairInARungOrTemplate, pass}; thresholdPicks[] {letter, picked: number | same}; houseSheet?; acceptance? {by: owner, text, date}.
The research-side docs/validation/d5/⟨milestone⟩.md (human-readable, with reference image hashes) is generated from record.json (§13.3); no CI job reads it.

Every threshold is in exactly one of two classes: reference-settable bands (§13.5, set by its band rule from baselines.json) or thresholds no reference can set (listed in §13.7) — each of the latter has a number now (provenance "architecture 2026-09-25"), is confirmed at the first milestone at which its mechanism runs, and has a pre-decided fallback; the corpus phase may later re-sign any as a declared shift (§13.9).

J-T, the calibration rule every table row and threshold cites (NF-S4): every value has a number now and a provenance (§17.1 (6)); a reference-settable value is set from baselines.json by §13.5's band rule; any value may later be re-signed only by a declared shift (M-1 re-measurement, owner pick on §13.6 (8)'s panel, calibration run §13.9); no acceptance run treats an unset value as passed — a table with an empty cell fails to load; §4.7's granularity table, §4.9's greenery table and §13.7 cite it as "J-T".

Fallbacks that move a threshold (NF-S5): a fallback may change a mechanism (table value, weight, radius) and re-measure against the same threshold; a fallback that instead moves the threshold to a measured value is marked not achieved — the letter and measured value enter known-defects.json, the parity report and release notes, and are never cited as evidence an improvement was achieved (§15.2 O class); an owner pick on the threshold panel is not a fallback but the owner setting the number (provenance "owner-eye ⟨milestone⟩").

O18 (i) smooth field: p99 of |∇P| ≤ 0.5 per 100 m of the normalised prosperity field outside hard seams; confirmed M2b (B-CITY and a §13.6 strip at σ = 45 / 60 / 90 m); fallback σ rises one step (60 → 75 m) and re-measures; an owner pick of σ sets σ and the threshold is re-signed at that σ's measured p99 ("owner-eye").

O18 (j) plot-size variety: within-district plot-area CV ≥ 0.25 for districts with ≥ 30 plots; M2b; fallback: granularity rows' frontage CV rises 0.25 → 0.35 and re-measures; if still failing the floor becomes the measured p10 — not achieved.

O18 (h), O7 (f), S3 soft seams: across soft seams Δ median frontage ≤ 25 %, Δ median plot area ≤ 35 %, Δ median storeys ≤ 1; M2b; fallback: seam smoothing radius doubles and re-measures; if still failing the band becomes measured p95 + 5 points — not achieved.

O19 (d) canopy: tree nearest-neighbour p1 ≥ 0.5 × the class's mean crown diameter (orchard, avenue, garden), ≥ 0.3 × for woods; M2b (bench, §8.10's stamps); fallback: the class's stamp spacing range (table value, §4.9) raised until its lower end meets the threshold (scaled tiles' minimum distance is the entity's own spacing, so the shipped asset does not change).

O19 (g) city-zoom greenery: every green face ≥ 0.3 ha drawn at the city band with a short side ≥ 2 px; green/ground and green/paper pairs at or above §8.2's contrast floors; no option coupling drops the layer; M2b for ink and lit (the milestone building S12's greenery rules); fallback: the green role steps one value step from ground (style row) and re-checks.
O12 (a) legibility floors: minimum drawn feature ≥ 2 px; area-label cap height ≥ 7 px (§9.4); M1 (B-ZOOM and a §13.6 strip at 6 / 7 / 8 px); fallback: the owner's pick, with no pick 7 px stands.

O13 (c) name–feature consistency: a name referencing a feature type has that feature within 250 m; M1; fallback: the grammar's feature guard shrinks its radius 250 → 200 m and re-measures against 250 m.
O7 (b) water-dependent trades within 100 m of water; M2b; fallback: the placement score's water term weight doubles.

O14 (b) farmsteads: every farmstead within 300 m of one of its own fields and within 1 500 m of all; M2b; fallback: the hinterland unit's S10 re-sites a violating farmstead to its fields' area-weighted centroid (§4.9).

O14 (c) wood edges: edge straightness (chord ÷ path over 200 m windows) median ≤ 0.90; canopy fraction monotone in the wildness control; M3b; fallback: edge-noise amplitude rises by half and re-measures.

O14 (e) built / map area: settlement-perimeter area ÷ frame area (without margin) within 0.06–0.25 at every rung and population; M1; fallback: the frame side per rung is rescaled in ladder.json so the median ratio is 0.12 (a declared shift).

Block-level use mix (MFP-7): residential-only blocks ≤ 60 % in core districts; per-block use-mix entropy p50 ≥ 0.5 bits; ≥ 70 % of trade households live at their workplace; M2b; fallback: the live-in default share of craft and shop rows rises one step (§10.2).

Requested features (IMP-5): degraded delivery (tiers 4–5) on ≤ 5 % of requested features; M1; fallback: the F-* ladder whose degraded rung fires most gets 5 instead of 3 tier-3 attempts and re-measures; if still over, the band becomes the measured rate + 2 points and the top three causes enter known-defects.json — not achieved.

O16 (c) scripted tasks: one UI action where a reference needs a detour; recovery = one undo; every app response ≤ 1 s; confirmed M1 (link, SVG, coast side, variants), M2a (undo), M3b (the rest); fallback: a task over its action count gets a toolbar shortcut and repeats.

O2 (c) carry-over: edited entities kept or carried ≥ 95 % for local actions and re-derivation from S7 on, ≥ 80 % from S4–S6, ≥ 60 % from S1–S3 (§15.2); M3a (B-EDIT); fallback: §6.3's doubled anchor radii with the IoU test, then an edited building or plot without a successor re-imposes its last geometry as a drawn constraint.

S4 (d) square area (stage 2): typed squares (market, church forecourt, well square, bridgehead, crossroads) inside a district: 0.03–0.15 ha per 1 000 inhabitants over districts of ≥ 1 000 inhabitants; M5; fallback: square-sizing rows scaled so the median is 0.08 ha per 1 000 (declared shift) and re-measures.

Realism against real towns is measured by the corpus phase (§13.9), staged by the owner after the standalone generators; until then the base's realism evidence is the D-5 realism question and §13.5's P rows, and §15.2 says so.

Full verification rig ≈ 10–20 CPU-hours (12 000 B-CITY generations ≈ 1.6 CPU-h before the suite; 10⁵ oracle regenerations ≈ 8 CPU-h; 10⁶ fuzz inputs × ≈ 20 primitives ≈ 0.3–5.5 CPU-h), so it cannot gate a single change; three tiers each with a wall-clock budget on a stated runner (16-core x86-64 Linux; timings normalised by §12.1's calibration score).

PR tier (every change, ≤ 15 min on 8 cores): lint (determinism allowlist, units, dependency direction, repository path rule), type check, unit and contract tests; B-FUZZ 10⁴ random inputs per primitive + the whole constructive set; B-CITY-lite 50 seeds per rung × 4 water settings; B-EDIT 10³ sequences with the oracle once per sequence; stage-isolated goldens and placement digests on Node x86; every style sheet through §8.2 slot resolution at every band (0 unresolved, 0 ambiguous) and render keys across two B-CITY-lite seeds per rung; stamp-tile loaded hashes and seam check; licence, notices and deny-list scans; app scripted and accessibility tasks on Chromium.

Nightly tier (≤ 4 h on 16 cores): B-CITY 1 000 seeds × 4 water × 3 rungs with the invariant suite and §12.3's max-clause screen; B-FUZZ 10⁶ per primitive; B-EDIT 10⁴ sequences; the O9 (c) faithfulness campaign (800 × 50, ≈ 12.5 CPU-min); the five-engine golden run (one PNG per LOD and preset, placement digests, stamp-tile asset rebuilt on five engines and loaded hashes in both workers, sliced-raster and sliced-placement census rows) and from M3a the five-engine GeoJSON with trees; visual regression and B-ZOOM; control sweeps at TOWN and CITY; option matrix; B-REF parity report.

Milestone tier (every milestone exit and weekly; ≤ 12 h on 16 cores): B-EDIT 10⁵ sequences; METROPOLIS control sweeps; the 20-epoch test; the parity report at five seeds per matched size; the D-5 renders incl. every earlier panel still provisional — not rated (§13.6 (7)); §12.3's pool comparison in the timing phase at every rung the milestone confirms; memory and document-size tests at every rung.

A tier whose normalised wall-clock exceeds its budget by more than 10 % fails with over budget; the answer is to split the job or make it faster, never to raise the cap — a budget changes only by a recorded decision; measurement at M0: the harness times each tier; fallback: if the PR tier exceeds 15 min, B-CITY-lite drops to 25 seeds per rung and random fuzz to 5 × 10³ inputs per primitive (the constructive set is never cut) and the nightly tier absorbs the difference.

Corpus calibration is staged by the owner after the standalone generators (base, neighbourhoods, buildings, village); the corpus lies outside this folder and is not read by this program; the base carries the interface now so the corpus phase needs one adapter and no other code.

facts.statement: CorpusAdapter {id, version, maps(): AsyncIterable<CorpusMap>} (written in the owner's staged phase); CorpusMap {id, source (archive, sheet, date), era, region, populationEstimate?, features: FeatureCollection — GeoJSON in metres: ways, blocks, plots, buildings, walls, water, greens with kinds}; CalibrationRun {id, corpus {adapter, version, maps[]}, metrics[] (§13.5 ids, same parity code), changes[] {table, rowKey, column, from, to, evidence[] (baseline ids)}, before, after: ParityReport, shifts: ShiftRecord[] (cause.kind calibration)}.

Calibration steps: (1) parity code computes every §13.5 metric on the adapter's maps research-side and writes baselines.json rows with reference corpus:⟨map id⟩, role target, referenceBuild = corpus version; (2) a CalibrationRun changes table cells only — every cell is {value, unit, provenance, calibratable} (§7.6) and each changed cell's provenance becomes {source: corpus, evidence, date}; (3) the run ships as a table-version bump inside an output-version bump with a shift record per moved stage (§13.3, §6.4) in plat/goldens/shifts/o<k>.json with the run id as cause, so every existing document replays under its own output version; (4) first re-signed: era and region presets (D-2), rung profiles (§1.1), granularity, site-plan and greenery rows (§4.7, §4.9), forms' signatures (§7.7), and §13.7 thresholds with provenance architecture or owner-eye where the corpus measures them.

Packages have one-way dependencies: the kernel knows nothing about towns, the model nothing about drawing, the drawing code nothing about how the town was made; the app sits on a headless library; new looks, templates, export formats, building generators and rule tables plug into named registries without touching the pipeline; everything lives in one repository plat/ that never reads research material (§17).

@plat/kernel: lattice, predicates, one arena per layer with the five levels as views (§2.2), role and owner tables, stored-reference resolution, batched transactions, kernel invariants, arrangement booleans/buffers/bands (§3.7), straight skeleton and validator (§3.8), obb/hull/lir, delaunay (delaunator), poisson (stamped ranked tiles built from a constant stream key at build time by plat/tools/stamptiles/, in a worker only as the fallback rebuild, §8.10), curves, index (flatbush / rbush / grid), noise, dmath (fdlibm 5.3 port), rng (xoshiro + 128-bit keys; rng.stream the one structured stream mixer of §6.1), concern registry.

@plat/model: schema (zod), addresses and lineage (§6.3), layers, entity registry (CI path-coverage test), lifecycle, provenance, document, serialisation (.plat, CBOR twin), migrations, Merkle model digest, core statistics record, control registry; label records LabelEntity and QuarterNode (§9.1) and the shared view vocabulary LodBand, Role, ZoomStop.

@plat/tables: rule tables, presets, style sheets, rung profiles (ladder.json, §1.1), work-limit coefficients (workLimits.json, §5.1 (5)), setting packs (§10.4) and the default keymap as versioned JSON with provenance; loaders; the override layer.
@plat/site: S1 terrain, hydrology, coast/lake/island outline routine, rivers by descent, islands, bank classes, water faces.

@plat/content: S2 sequential roster, demand, government and religion rows, S7b/S10a allocation, S10b placement, households and people derivation, relation-store schema, economy and personality schema stubs (D-32), naming engine + grammar.

@plat/layout: S3 siting, reservations and gate sites, S4 backbone, S5 growth and regimes, S6 grower/typing/fields/quarter merge tree, S7 fortification and water furniture, S7b claims, S8 infill (BentCutFabric), S9 corridors, S12a hinterland siting, the hinterland unit, S12b greenery; the StrategyRegistry and the ordering of registered StageDecls.

@plat/plots: S10 granularity law, per-frontage regions, joins/splits/alleys, boundary treatments; S11 site plans, packer, heights, footprint templates; the BuildingGenerator interface (outline / compose) + OutlineBuildingGenerator; assignment + placement solver.
@plat/hood (stage 2, built after the base): RingFabric / SquareFabric / StreetFabric and the neighbourhood LOD workflow; the interface lives in @plat/layout.

@plat/labels: S13a names (every node of the quarter tree), candidates and spines; S13b view placement over parameters the renderer passes in (ObstacleSource, RoleIndex) — never imports render; font-metrics reader; collision; furniture incl. the ruler and the emblem generator.

@plat/render: S14 columnar display-list builder, paint programs, style sheets, LOD, tile pyramid and tile worker (which runs S13b by calling @plat/labels), backends (Canvas2D, SVG, print tiles; WebGL2 tile compositor as fallback), shadow pass, decoration stamps over the bundled stamp-tile asset (§8.10), live layers, the tile worker queue of resumable raster jobs (§8.9).
@plat/edit: edit events, dry-run validation, undo and redo records, scoped regeneration, rebase, dependency audit, event migrations, warp kernels.
@plat/export: geojson, svg, png/tiles (streaming), vtt (Foundry-class scene JSON, dd2vtt), gltf/obj, cityjson, csv, permalinks.
@plat/sim (optional, M4b): relation store materialised, postings, occupancy and schedules, calendar, factions, events, economy, personality and the stat-block pack (D-32), over @plat/content ids.
@plat/api: the handle-based facade (§11.2), generation worker host, derivation pool, host bridge (§11.3) and DocResolver (§11.5), the headless CLI.

@plat/docs: the user guide (generated reference pages from control, entity and table registries plus written pages); known-defects.json; release notes generated from plat/goldens/shifts/ and the milestone records (§13.3), the D-5 statuses (§13.6) and the known defects.

@plat/testkit: B-FUZZ generators (random and constructive), invariant runners, cost-model tests, bench statistics and the parity CLI (reads baselines/baselines.json only), golden tooling with shift, cascade and milestone records and placement digests over plat/goldens/ (§13.3) and the one WaterSetting type, the O9 (c) faithfulness campaign (§13.2), the boolean and buffer oracles (Clipper2-WASM in Node, polygon-clipping), the clean-room scanner (§17), the D-5 seed list by H32 and the export command (plat d5 seeds, PNGs for §13.6), which read only the committed ftg-captures.json and ng-counts.json (§13.6 (2)).

Dependency order (lint-enforced): kernel ← model ← tables ← {site, content} ← layout ← plots ← labels ← render ← edit ← export ← api ← app; labels ← render (N-22): render tile worker runs S13b from labels, and drawn symbol extents and the display-list index reach it only as the parameters ObstacleSource and RoleIndex (declared by labels, implemented by render), so labels never imports render; shared types LodBand, Role, ZoomStop, LabelEntity come from model.

Further dependency rules: docs reads only the registries of model and tables; hood depends on layout/plots only through their interfaces; sim depends on content and model only; render never imports layout; nothing depends on app; no package imports a backend it does not need; every adopted runtime library is imported in exactly one adapter file of the one package using it.

Acceptance-letter classes: [C] conformance (holds by construction once the rule is built; proves the implementation follows the design; never cited as evidence an improvement was achieved); [P] parity (compared with a measured reference number in baselines.json by §13.5 band rule); [O] outcome (can show the result is better than the references, for a user or for realism); thresholds without a reference source have their numbers in §13.7.

Every acceptance letter is stated in full in §15.2, stage-2 letters included (NF-S4); letters an earlier draft dropped are restored with numbers (IMP-10); implementers read this matrix, never docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md, which is cited for traceability only (§17.1 (1)).

facts.statement: Who reads what: research seats (readers, measurers, the digest writer) may read findings, captures/, research/ and — under the standing ruling — reference/; implementer seats (anyone writing code, tables, style sheets, content, assets or tests in plat/) read only docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, the implementer digest in plat/docs/digest/, the plat/ repository, published algorithm papers and adopted libraries' public documentation; they never open research/, captures/, reference/, the findings, the critics, docs/confidence/, docs/improvements/, docs/CONFIDENCE.md, docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md or red-team files; citations are for traceability and an implementer follows them only into the digest; no code from TownGeneratorOS (GPL-3), the FTG Foundry module or any captured bundle is read for implementation, ported or paraphrased.

The implementer digest: a digest seat writes plat/docs/digest/ from the research — behaviours, measured numbers (each with its baselines.json id or finding reference) and the creators' stated ideas; no code excerpts, reference word lists, grammars, palettes, tables or identifiers; a separate checker seat reading only the digest runs the content scan on it and files a report; every digest change repeats the check; this document is held to the same rule (FTG-22).

Until M-1 builds the deny-list, every seat that writes this document (a fix-all integration seat, an amendment pass's apply and repair lanes, any finishing or repair seat) runs before its change lands: python3 docs/validation/bench/doc_checks.py --sections "⟨every section heading key the change touched⟩" from the project root — content checks (iii) and (vi) over the touched sections, the others over the whole document.

doc_checks (i) identifiers: whole-word, case-sensitive search for the backticked identifiers of research/findings/ftg-payload-visual.md §7.2 plus one further time-setting message name — 36 names read from the finding or held research-side, none copied into this document.

doc_checks (ii) colours: every six-digit colour value (#rrggbb or 0xrrggbb) looked up case-insensitive and hex-delimited in research/ (text files incl. JSON), captures/**/README*.md, captures/**/*.json, docs/confidence/, docs/improvements/, docs/CONFIDENCE.md and docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md.

doc_checks (iii) token 3-grams: lower-cased word tokens of the changed sections against every 3-gram of research/findings/*.md and of the string keys and values of every JSON file under research/ and captures/, in document order with numeric tokens dropped; a hit is a run of three or more consecutive shared 3-grams (five or more tokens in a row standing together in a source); a single shared 3-gram is ordinary phrasing.

doc_checks (iv) tables: outside fenced code (fences may be indented) every line starting with | ends with |, no other line sits between two table lines, and every row has its header's number of cells counting only unescaped pipes; inside a table a pipe in code is written \| (GFM splits cells at every unescaped pipe, even in a code span).
doc_checks (v) pointers: every §n and §n.m pointer resolves to a heading of this document.

doc_checks (vi) lists in any order: every JSON file under research/ and captures/ except the profiler's recordings (call censuses, coverage, idle, trace, draw and path records, run reports, metadata, session and index files) is read for its lists (a dict's keys, an array of strings, one field's string values across ≥ 3 records); a hit is a line of the changed sections holding ≥ 5 distinct whole words of ≥ 4 letters that are members of one such list, reported sorted.

Each hit is corrected before the change lands or reviewed into docs/validation/doc-checks-allow.tsv with its check, exact text and a written reason (capture-citation file name, measured number, creator sentence under 15 words quoted for traceability, ordinary phrasing, generic vocabulary in our own selection and order, pointer into another document); the script exits non-zero while any hit is unreviewed; the change does not land until it exits zero; the seat records its counts in its output file (fix-all integration log; amendment pass in docs/validation/amendments-applied.md and amendments-repair.md); from M-1 the hashed scan of (5) also runs over this document and replaces (i)–(iii) and (vi), while (iv) and (v) stay.

Calibration (executed): on §13–§17 after round 2 (pre-round-3 lines 6657–7826, md5 ca2e2066…, docs/validation/bench/fixall_scope_r4_calib_pre_r3_s13_s17.txt), 1 196 of 26 236 token 3-grams shared with the findings forming 47 runs of ≥ 5 tokens (45 distinct: §13 24, §14 4, §15 11, §16 6, §17 2); no run threshold 1–7 gives the 27 an earlier draft stated; on the round-3 text the same rule gives 53 runs; (ii) finds none of the document's 36 colour values in its sources; (iv) found exactly the one broken row VS2-1 names, and the cell-count clause exactly one more (J-I15); the round-4 JSON extension over 2 052 JSON files (≈ 30–45 s) adds 50 distinct run texts to (iii) and (vi) flags 8 lines of generic vocabulary, all reviewed into the allow file; of 429 one-line lists in FTG's content database, (vi) catches all 429 in either order while (iii) catches none of the alphabetised five-name lines and 210 in database order.

facts.statement: Repository boundary: the product is its own repository plat/ at the folder root outside research/, captures/ and reference/; a PR-tier CI rule fails any import specifier, fixture path, script path or build input resolving outside plat/ (symbolic links resolved); the product's CI never reads the research trees.

Reference numbers only through committed numbers-only files: research-side scripts (research/baselines/) measure the captures and write Baseline rows with provenance into baselines.json, committed into plat/packages/testkit/baselines/; the parity CLI reads only it; the D-5 panel is assembled research-side from product PNG exports and capture images, and "its only inputs to the product are two numbers-only files" in plat/goldens/d5/⟨milestone⟩/ — ftg-captures.json (capture ids, rungs, water settings, resident counts) and ng-counts.json (NG building counts) — which plat d5 seeds reads.

Content scan: research/baselines/make_denylist.py builds the deny-list from the creative data the findings and captures record (naming-grammar rule names and terminal words, Markov and corpus sample words, palette colours, FTG building-type, profession, item and service identifiers and names, FTG Foundry-module message and field names, texture and image file hashes); the list holds only salted SHA-256 digests — of single normalised tokens (lower-cased, diacritics stripped) not in §9.6's spell-check list, of token 3-grams in list order, of exact six-digit colours, of file bytes, and per recorded list the set of salted digests of its members' words of ≥ 4 letters.

@plat/testkit's clean-room scanner digests the same way every token of @plat/tables, assets, source string literals and comments and the digest in the PR tier; it flags as a list hit any line or table column holding ≥ 5 distinct words of one list's set; a hit fails the build unless a reviewed allow entry with a written reason is added (an authored roster sharing ordinary building or trade names is such an entry; the review decides whether the selection was copied).

At every milestone the checker seat runs a research-side palette audit: a shipped palette with three or more colours within ΔE2000 2 of one reference palette fails and is redesigned; every file in plat/assets names the script that generated it or its third-party licence (fonts); a file with neither fails the build.

Honest provenance: every table cell's provenance is one of own, ref:⟨reference⟩ ⟨behaviour⟩ (a measured or stated behaviour admissible as a calibration anchor — e.g. MFCG castle 0.75 compactness gate, FTG 40 m bridge spacing and 39 m tower spacing, NG's lane-width law, Poisson k = 50), owner, owner-eye ⟨milestone⟩, architecture ⟨date⟩, corpus or host; a number describing a behaviour is a fact; a list, grammar, palette or table is creative content, never reused.

The record: plat/docs/CLEAN-ROOM.md holds the rule, the seat ledger (which seat read which research file, from the lane logs), the digest checker's reports and the deny-list's generation record (date, sources, counts — never the tokens).

Sources of algorithms (published; each read in its published form, the seat ledger records which): Shewchuk predicates; snap rounding (Hobby; Guibas–Marimont; Hershberger); winding-number arrangement booleans; Bridson Poisson-disc; Felkel–Obdržálek and Aichholzer straight skeletons; Chaikin; Visvalingam–Whyatt; Parish–Müller growth; Lloyd relaxation; marching squares; priority-flood; Garbrecht–Martz flat resolution; fBm with ridged multifractal and domain warping (Musgrave in Ebert et al. 2003); xoshiro128** with Irwin–Hall normals; MurmurHash3 x86 128-bit and its 32-bit finaliser (H128 §6.2, RH32 §8.1, H32 §13.6) checked against SMHasher values; Krüger transverse Mercator in Karney's formulation to fourth order (§11.1); van der Corput radical inverse and Morton interleaving (§8.10); Ulichney void-and-cluster (§8.10); monotone-chain hull and rotating calipers (§3.1); centripetal Catmull–Rom and pinned-vertex Laplacian smoothing; Dijkstra and A*; Brandes betweenness; Kruskal; Lambert shading; CIELAB and CIEDE2000; D8 flow and accumulation (O'Callaghan and Mark 1984); exact EDT (Felzenszwalb–Huttenlocher 2012); three-pass box Gaussian (Wells 1986); Merkle tree (1987; D-28); Tracery-style grammar and n-gram Markov (ideas only, own grammar and corpora); power diagrams with area targets (Aurenhammer et al.) for §4.9 hinterland lots; Kahn topological sort with stage-id tie-break (§4.1, §4.12); SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4); for tests: Pearson χ² with Holm, Spearman, Moran's I, KS, SSIM, pair-correlation (Stoyan and Stoyan 1994), Shannon entropy, Jaccard index, Hausdorff distance; the round-4 list was checked by a scripted scan of 119 method names.

The creators' stated ideas admitted (with constants calibrated on our own measurements): twisted bisection, the casing idiom, skeleton labels, the proposal queue, dependency ratios, lazy people, integer centimetres.

Protocol names (FTG-22): the host bridge vocabulary is our own (§11.3) — concurrency token logHead (§2.9) carried as baseLogHead and currentLogHead; time is the view key time set by view.set; the simulation module advances it with sim.advance { hours } (§10.3, §11.3); schema-level ideas (event/command split, optimistic-concurrency token) are admissible; FTG module message, command and field names are not reused, are in the deny-list and occur nowhere in this document (check (i)).

Fonts are third-party OFL assets outside the clean-room rule; chose IM FELL Great Primer (OFL) as the default label face over a different serif chosen "for clean-room distance" because it is MFCG's label face and part of the ink look the owner adopted (D-1); EB Garamond and Cinzel ship as alternatives.

Fonts ship unmodified; CI reads each face's name table and refuses to subset a face declaring a Reserved Font Name; the OFL text ships in the notices file; label metrics are read from the bundled files (§9.2); bundled faces are TrueType-flavoured (glyf) as SVG's default text writes (§11.1); when the default face lacks smcp the family's OFL small-caps cut is bundled unmodified beside it (§9.2); an SVG export may embed a face unmodified as a data URI (§11.1); CI checks all three (§9.2).

Our own licence (D-22): until the owner chooses, plat/ is proprietary — "Copyright © the owner. All rights reserved." in its LICENSE file, no open-source licence; chosen over an open licence because it keeps every option (publishing later under any licence is one act; an open licence once granted cannot be withdrawn); flagged for the owner's veto.

What keeps every licence choice open: permissive-only dependencies checked over the production closure (§17.4); nothing copyleft linked or bundled; the notices file; the clean-room chain (§17.1); every file written by the program's seats for the owner; no outside contribution without the owner's written assent.

Licence checker: the allowlist — MIT, ISC, BSD-2/3, Apache-2.0, BSL-1.0, CC0, Unlicense, OFL (fonts) and Sun's fdlibm notice — runs in the PR tier over the transitive production closure of every shipped bundle (library, embed, app, CLI); dev-only exceptions each with a reason: @resvg/resvg-js (MPL-2.0), Playwright and its browsers (MPL/LGPL components), axe-core (MPL-2.0), the oracles, the validators and the spell-check dictionary; Inkscape and QGIS are GPL programs CI runs as external tools and never links.

Notices: CI generates THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt from the production closure (name, version, licence text, copyright lines) plus the fonts' OFL text and the fdlibm notice; every bundle ships it; the minifier keeps /*! */ banners.

Pins: exact versions in every package.json with the lockfile committed; no prerelease in the production closure; an upgrade is a reviewed change re-running the checker, §6.5's allowlist scan of vendored sources and the goldens; every adopted runtime library is vendored at its pinned version into plat/vendor/, scanned by the determinism allowlist (§6.5), with an audit record kept in @plat/kernel.

Dependency table: robust-predicates 3.0.3 (Unlicense; incircle and the adversarial orient2d test reference; adopt, pinned); booleans/buffers/bands on the arrangement (ours, §3.7, built); straight skeleton with validator (ours, §3.8, built); dmath (our port of fdlibm 5.3 from netlib with Sun's notice, no @stdlib closure; built); Clipper2 (clipper2-wasm 0.4.0, BSL-1.0; CI oracle; the pre-decided M0 fallback would ship it compiled to WASM as the single engine, §3.7; dev, shipped only if the fallback fires); polygon-clipping 0.15.7 (MIT; CI oracle; dev); delaunator, d3-delaunay (ISC; site sampling, medial axes; adopt); earcut (ISC; triangulation for fields, glTF and CityJSON meshes; adopt); flatbush, rbush (ISC, MIT; spatial indices; adopt); simplex-noise (MIT; noise base; adopt, determinism checked by vendored scan); d3-contour (ISC; marching squares for render-tile contours; adopt); cbor-x (MIT; compact twin; adopt); zod (MIT; schemas; adopt); @napi-rs/canvas 1.0.9 (MIT; Node CLI PNG; optional, CLI only); fast-check, vitest, Playwright, pixelmatch, ssim.js, Vite, esbuild, tsx, pnpm, TypeScript (MIT/Apache-2.0/ISC; dev); axe-core (MPL-2.0; dev, never shipped); @resvg/resvg-js (MPL-2.0 file-level copyleft; headless SVG rendering in CI; dev, never shipped); OFL fonts IM FELL Great Primer (default), EB Garamond, Cinzel (SIL OFL 1.1; style assets unmodified).
